title: What is derived state in a persisted Fabric object?
detail:
The dirty guard's cause (vg-026) is one field of a general question, and patching styles alone leaves the next per-character cache to arrive and be found by the user. SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES is an allowlist that already intends to do this job and is not applied on the way out. The spec should answer which Fabric properties are derived from telemetry or from rendering, how a serialisation excludes all of them, and whether the allowlist should be enforced at the boundary. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md. AND NOW THERE IS A SHARP INSTANCE OF IT, MEASURED, which is vg-026. The dirty guard compares a document key against one captured when the editor was built, and with no input at all 13 of the Starter 52 objects change between 0.4 and 1.9 seconds after load — every one a Textbox, repainted by the live preview pass. The document differs from itself with nothing touched, so every New asks the author to save work nobody did. That is what the allowlist was meant to stop and does not reach: the changed objects are bound text, and what the live pass writes is the same property the author edits. This row is therefore not an abstract design question any more — it is one concrete false prompt an author meets on the first Ctrl+N, and the fix belongs here rather than in the dirty guard. AND A SECOND SHARP INSTANCE, MEASURED, is vg-188: entering a group writes `subTargetCheck`/`interactive` on the group, both of which ARE serialized, so `isDirty()` flips with nothing authored and a save taken inside a group would persist editor-only reachability flags into the theme package. That row carries the diff and the Fabric evidence.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user, taken once on this question as it is filed on both vg-041 and vg-188: A SPEC NAMES THE DERIVED SET AND ITS ONE OWNER. Which Fabric properties are derived or editor-only, and how serialisation excludes all of them, is written down as a spec rather than patched instance by instance, so the Textbox repaint measured on this row and the group's subTargetCheck and interactive flags measured on vg-188 are two members of one class with one owner that strips them. Both rows move to that spec. COLLAPSED 2026-10-16 (§8.3). This row and `vg-188` ask one question — which Fabric properties are derived, and how a serialisation excludes them — and one ruling covers the pair. `vg-188` is the *measured instance* of the general question this row poses rather than a second finding: it names `subTargetCheck` and `interactive` reaching the serialized scene through `grouping-manager`'s reachability flags. One ruling, two rows marked; neither closes without the other.

title: The spec requires visible notch and safe areas, and no task or row owns them
detail:
FOUND IN REDESIGN PLAN 2 TASK 2 REVIEW. The redesign spec at section 2 requires "Device frame, notch and safe areas are visible and accounted for, because the display has them." No task in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-the-device-lens.md covers the notch or safe areas, the implementing agent declined them correctly as out of its brief, and the gap appears in NO backlog row and carries no "Discovered, not fixed:" trailer on the commit. Under AGENTS.md the trailer is the one path that survives compaction, so as shipped the requirement is simply lost. This is a controller error: the requirement was written into the spec without being given a task or a row. The device frame itself is an outline only and does not mask, which the reviewer confirmed is the honest direction - an author may pan artboard outside the screen and sees more than a device would rather than less. What is missing is the safe-area inset: a theme whose content sits under a notch or a rounded corner looks right in the editor and is cut on the device. That is exactly the preview-disagrees-with-the-phone failure this plan exists to remove, so it belongs with the device lens rather than as an orphan. RULED 2026-10-13: the row LEAVES PHASE 8 and is not built in this drain. It was seated there as a "row with a named single owner and no open ruling" and has neither, which this row's own text says -- the spec requirement was written "without being given a task or a row". THE MEASUREMENT: `DisplayLens` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/display-lens.ts:45-58`) carries exactly three fields -- `id`, `aspect`, `shape` -- and the interface's own comment refuses the fourth thing this would add ("**A shape, never a size.** No resolution... Fixing one here would be the redesign's own failure -- silently settling a second thing nobody asked about"). Building the safe area means settling what a lens's inset is per device and whether it masks or only overlays (the frame is outline-only and does not mask, which the row records a reviewer judged the honest direction). The requirement's EXISTENCE is settled by the spec; its SHAPE is not, and the shape is what the work is -- inventing one is the move this plan has had to undo before. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: this row is the first candidate for the device-lens work that follows the drain, where a spec can settle what a lens's inset is before anything renders it. SEVERITY: the row's own -- a spec requirement stays unbuilt one plan longer, against shipping device geometry nobody chose.
PARKED 2026-10-16: this row is applied rather than new work. Its own ruling of 2026-10-13 says it LEAVES PHASE 8 and is not built in this drain, and names it as the first candidate for the device-lens work that follows the drain — so the register records a real finding that is known and not scheduled, which is decision 0045's park, rather than a to-do. The census can now separate it from the work the drain owes. Nothing about the finding changed: the spec still requires visible notch and safe areas, and `DisplayLens` still carries only `id`, `aspect` and `shape`.

title: A text side handle does not snap at the portrait lens, so an author resizing text gets no guide at all
detail: FOUND BY THE SABOTAGE RUN AGAINST vg-137, and it is NOT a test reading the camera wrong - this one is the product. Set DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS to 9:19.5, rebuild, and tests/e2e/snapping.spec.ts "resizing geometry snaps a side handle onto a guide" lands 100.0 scene units from the line it was aimed 3 client px short of. 100 units is a quarter of the 600-tall artboard: that is not a missed snap, it is no snap at all, and at the default lens the same gesture passes. Measured on the same run where every other snapping test passes at both lenses, so the fixture, the gesture and the camera plumbing are all fine. CONFIRMED IT IS NOT THE TOLERANCE: vg-137s derived bound at this lens is 2.92 scene units and the landing is 100, so no tolerance question can be behind it. The gesture arrives as object:resizing on a canonical width rather than as a scale - Fabric gives a text box changeWidth side controls - and that path is the one that does not reach a snap line under this camera. Whether the side-handle resize path consults the camera at all is the thing to check, and it is a one-symbol question in the resizing side of snap-manager, not a test change. VERIFIED PRESENT ONLY AT 9:19.5; NOT VERIFIED ON ANY OTHER LENS, portrait is the one measured, and landscape is the default so the mainline gate is green and does not see it. This is the shape vg-137 fixed the test side of: a lens or a resize that moves the camera changes what the snapping path is asked to do, and this is where it shows. BROWSER PASS TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e): with DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS planted to `9:19.5` and rebuilt, and the PLANT PROVEN LIVE by reading the camera off the preview (zoom 0.2468 x 1672 = 412.6px, a portrait 9:19.5 rect inscribed in the 894px-tall stage), `npx playwright test snapping.spec.ts --grep "resizing geometry snaps a side handle onto a guide" --workers=1` PASSES - 1 expected / 0 unexpected in the run own JSON report - so the 100-unit miss does not reproduce at HEAD and the lens is not the explanation for it. The row stays open: one measurement of a defect against one non-reproduction is not a refutation.
owner: packages/editor/src/snap-manager (the resizing side of the gesture path)

title: A video frame in the host media spec is an intermittent that fails at the baseline too
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING DEVICE-LENS PLAN 2 TASK 5, in the full host suite rather than by driving the product. tests/e2e/host-media.spec.ts has a video-frame test that fails intermittently: 3 of 5 samples with the Task 5 commit f49f632b, 1 of 3 at its parent, and it fails at the clean baseline too, so it is NOT a regression from that task and NOT this plan's. MEASURED on both sides rather than assumed, per the repo rule that a single sample is not a measurement. A flaky spec in a suite that gates merges is a real defect whatever its cause, and the cause is not established: video decode timing under a loaded, shared box is the obvious candidate and has not been confirmed. Needs an owner and a determinism fix; the surface to look at is the video-frame readiness wait, not the assertion. SAMPLES TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e, --workers=1, one suite at a time): `npx playwright test host-media.spec.ts --grep "a playing video background reaches the glass panel over it"` is green in FIVE consecutive runs, 1 expected / 0 unexpected each in its own JSON report. Five samples of one case on one box is not a measurement of an intermittent and does not close it; the row still needs an owner for the readiness wait it names.

title: The host player units spec times out on the real host, and does so in isolation too
detail: FOUND AT THE DEVICE-LENS PLAN 2 BOUNDARY, in the full e2e gate run against a verified-current bundle. tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts, "hosted player over the real host :: shows a temperature in the units this PC chose, converting nothing else" times out at 30s. IT REPRODUCES IN ISOLATION - it was among the six of a prior 16-failure run that still failed when re-run alone - so this is a real defect and not machine load. NOT THIS PLAN'S: device-lens plan 2 touched the artboard clip, the display switch, the new-theme chooser, arc and wedge shapes, and the deliberate-bleed flag, and none of them touches unit formatting or the host player's reading pipeline. MEASURED CONTEXT: the same boundary run was 260 passed / 1 failed / 160 skipped against a pre-plan baseline of 236 / 17, so the suite is otherwise in good shape and this is the last red. The failure is a 30s TIMEOUT rather than a wrong value, which points at a readiness wait on the host stream rather than at the conversion itself - the same shape as vg-141, the host-media video-frame intermittent, and the two may share a cause on this box. Cause not established. Needs an owner: establish whether the host never delivers the reading or the player never repaints on it. BROWSER PASS TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e): `npx playwright test host-player.spec.ts --grep "shows a temperature in the units this PC chose, converting nothing else"` ran on the real host and PASSED in 5.8s (1 expected / 0 unexpected; the second copy in the report is skipped). The 30s timeout does not reproduce at HEAD. One green sample against a defect that reproduced in isolation is a sample, not a refutation, so the row stays open.

title: Every imported JPEG was placed on the canvas, but only some of them appeared in the layer panel
detail: Reported by the user on 2026-10-07 from hands-on testing, and restated by them the same day after an agent mis-filed it: they imported JPEG images only, not a mix of file types, and every one appeared on the canvas, but only some produced a row in the layer panel. The ones that did not were missing from the panel while present on the canvas. The user does not know whether it has been fixed since. THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED, which is why this is a row rather than a fix on the fly. What reading ruled out, each a real mechanism rather than a guess: not isPlaceable (asset-manager/panel.ts:232-236), because every JPEG is kind image and so is placeable; not the storage path, because placeImage (asset-manager/index.ts:60-91) declares and places together and importImage (image-manager/index.ts:105-115) calls canvas.add(image) at the root unconditionally, since placeImage does not set withoutAdding; not the listing filter, because isListed (layer-tree.ts:112) excludes only excludeFromExport objects, namely the artboard plate, the clip and the crop frame, and no import sets that flag; not a row cap or virtualisation, because layer-panel.tsx renders every row and contextRows (:231-240) builds a dimming set rather than a filter; and not a missing trigger, because bridge.ts:124-130 subscribes object:added and object:removed to notify(), which re-projects. Every mechanism readable says the row should appear, which is exactly why a reproduction is needed rather than more reading. What the reproduction has to vary: how many files were imported in one session, whether a group was entered or selected when each import happened, whether files went in one at a time or several quickly, and whether the document already held many objects. Worth noting for whoever takes it: no browser spec covers this path at all, because no case in tests/e2e asserts that a placed image produces a layer row, so nothing would have caught it and nothing will catch a regression. BROWSER PASS TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e, editor preview on 4174, --workers=1), driving the Add pane file section and comparing the document own image ids against the layer rows ids at every step. THREE VARIATIONS, ALL CLEAN: five JPEGs one at a time on a document already holding 60 objects (5 images, 5 rows, none missing); five picks with NO pause between them (5 images, 5 rows); and three imports with `group-cpu-card` ENTERED (3 images, 20 rows, none missing). A several-files-at-once pick cannot be made at all - the input carries no `multiple` attribute - so that route does not exist. The defect does not reproduce in any variation tried, and no browser spec still covers the path.

title: An unlanded plan removes the menubars Insert and View menus, and nothing queues it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5S PLAN AUTHOR and left for the controller by that plans Out of scope section rather than fixed inside it. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-editor-left-column-and-header.md is 19.8 KB of unlanded plan whose Task 4 removes the Insert and View menus from the menubar. That removal is one half of the superseded frontend redesign, which ruled those menus leave the header (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-frontend-redesign-design.md:383). AGENTS.md requires that exactly one plan is active and every other incomplete plan is queued, and STATUS.md names no queue entry for this one. It matters now rather than later because plan 5 gives insertGroups() a fourth rendering (the + popover beside the Add pane, the Insert menu and the canvas context menu), and this plan is the one that would take the second of those away. Merging it into plan 5 would be two plans at once, which AGENTS.md forbids, so it is neither executed nor merged here. ITS OWN STATUS IS UNESTABLISHED: whether any of its tasks landed under another plan is not measured, and neither is whether its remaining tasks are still the shape its file describes. The neighbouring bookkeeping defect is vg-152, the same archive-versus-queue rule applied to plans 1 and 2, which are closed but still live in the plans directory. MEASURED IN PART BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW, which is the measurement this row said was missing: the unlanded plans Task 3 is now actively false rather than merely unqueued. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-editor-left-column-and-header.md:229 says to create editor-shell/insert-popover.tsx, which plan 5 created at 577c44e5 with a different contract, taking an anchor ref that the older plans Produces does not mention. Worse, that plans verification says to delete insertMenuGroups, insertMenuEntry and the test inserts the same objects from the Insert menu as the Add pane offers (shell-layout.dom.test.tsx:209-216, :286, :843), and plan 5 deliberately keeps and extends all three. So restoring that plan as written would now delete tests that a closed plan made load-bearing. Everything else about that plans state remains unmeasured, and the row stays open. MEASURED BY TASK 9.3 (2026-10-13, base f6e3a705), and the row stays open because the measurement answers only half of it. The Insert half is now false: the Insert menu is gone — redesign plan 2 (`2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail`, archived by this task) trimmed the header, and `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx:1169` now asserts 'has no Insert menu', while the `insertMenuGroups`/`insertMenuEntry` helpers and their tests this row named as load-bearing are themselves gone. The View half stands: `editor-shell/shell-menu-bar.tsx` still renders File, Edit and View, the three View settings inside the View menu, so this plan's Task 4 — moving those beside the canvas and leaving two menus — is unlanded and unqueued. Task 1 (pane bar) and Task 3 (insert popover) landed then were reversed: `pane-bar.tsx` created e0171079, deleted c6ee8d32; `insert-popover.tsx` created 577c44e5, deleted 2eeb4516. Task 2 (scale tokens) landed. Whether the View menu leaves the menubar is a product decision the redesign owns and not this task's to take; the plan file is left in `docs/superpowers/plans/` and `plans/README.md` now names it as the one entry held out of the queue.

title: The settings page's disk dropdown is missing when the suite runs it under load
detail: FOUND AT PLAN 5'S CLOSE-OUT BROAD GATE, in the full browser suite rather than by driving the product. tests/e2e/host-settings.spec.ts:249, 'asks a theme's disk question once, and remembers the answer', failed with locator('select[data-group="system-disk"]') element(s) not found after a 5000 ms timeout, the spec itself taking 23.9 s. IT PASSES ALONE: re-run in isolation on the same rebuilt bundle with --project=desktop-host --workers=1, it is 1 expected / 0 unexpected in 21.4 s. Two samples, opposite outcomes, so the failure is environment- or ordering-sensitive and is NOT a defect this plan caused — plan 5 touched the editor shell, the card library, the layer projection and two docstrings in scene-fabric, and none of those is the settings page or its device enumeration. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and the two readings are a real cross-test interference (the desktop-host project shares one host app dir across host-media, host-player and host-settings, and the disk list is read live from the machine) or plain load (the select did not populate inside its 5 s window while the whole suite ran serially). The surface to look at first is what populates [data-group="system-disk"], and whether an earlier spec in the same project mutates the host fixture's directory. BROWSER PASS TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e): `npx playwright test host-settings --project=desktop-host --workers=1 --grep "asks a theme disk question once, and remembers the answer"` PASSED in 9.5s (1 expected / 0 unexpected). That is the third sample saying the case passes in isolation, which is the green half of the pair the row already records; it is not a measurement of the under-load failure, so the row stays open.

title: Entering a group marks the document unsaved, because the grouping manager's reachability flags reach the serialized scene
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT WHILE PLACING TASK 4.1 OF PLAN 7's second capture, from an `Unsaved changes` mark in the footer that the task's first capture does not have. Pre-existing and not plan 7's: `grouping-manager` predates the plan and plan 7 does not touch it. THE MEASUREMENT, TAKEN IN THE BROWSER AND PROBED STEP BY STEP: reading `.editor-shell-save-state[data-dirty]` after each act gives after-load `false`, after-enterLayer `true`, and `true` for every act after it (selecting a part, pressing `?`, `Delete`, `Control+z`, `Escape`). So the keypresses behind the sheet change nothing -- the deferral being proved -- and entering the group is what flips the marker. THE CAUSE IS MEASURED, not inferred: diffing `canvas.toJSON()` across `enterLayer` gives 8 changed paths, `objects[3].subTargetCheck`, `objects[3].interactive`, and `objects[4|5|6|8|9].objects`. Both of the first two are set by `makeSelectableThrough` (`grouping-manager/index.ts:92-97`) and **both are serialized by Fabric**. THE COMMENT THAT SAYS OTHERWISE IS NARROWER THAN THE CODE: `grouping-manager/index.ts:75-78` claims '`selectable`/`evented` are not in Fabric's `stateProperties`, so this never reaches a save', and at `:111-119` 'neither key is in Fabric's `stateProperties`, so it stays view state (SS67)'. The `stateProperties` claim is TRUE -- verified against `node_modules/fabric/dist/index.mjs`, whose `stateProperties` list is top/left/scaleX/scaleY/flipX/flipY/originX/originY/angle/opacity/globalCompositeOperation/shadow/visible/skewX/skewY, with neither key in it. But the comment reasons only about `applyReachability`, which sets `selectable`/`evented`; **`makeSelectableThrough` sets two different keys, `subTargetCheck` and `interactive`, and the comment never covers them.** So the guard the comment believes it has does not exist for those two. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE MARKER: if the author saves while inside a group, the reachability flags this manager set are written into the theme package, which is the same class as `vg-129`/`vg-130` -- editor-only state reaching a shareable artifact -- and SS67 says view state is never authored history and never a Fabric write. The six changed `objects` arrays are measured but NOT explained: the cause of those is not established, and they may be a consequence of the same flag write or something else in the path. THE FIX NEEDS A DECISION AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE: it is the general question `vg-041` owns -- which Fabric properties are derived or editor-only, and how serialisation excludes them -- and `vg-026` is that row's other measured instance, a text object repainted by the live pass. Filed as its own row rather than folded into `vg-041` because that is the pattern this register already uses for `vg-026`: the instance is independently fixable and independently verifiable, and the general row points at it.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user, taken once on this question as it is filed on both vg-041 and vg-188: A SPEC NAMES THE DERIVED SET AND ITS ONE OWNER. Which Fabric properties are derived or editor-only, and how serialisation excludes all of them, is written down as a spec rather than patched instance by instance, so the Textbox repaint measured on this row and the group's subTargetCheck and interactive flags measured on vg-188 are two members of one class with one owner that strips them. Both rows move to that spec.

RE-MEASURED 2026-10-15, WHILE PROVING `vg-023`'s ROUND TRIP. **One half of this row is stale and the other half stands, and they are two different key pairs.** The half this row measured — `subTargetCheck`/`interactive`, armed by `makeSelectableThrough` — is **no longer a leak**: `scene-fabric`'s `persist.ts` now strips both after serialization through `removeGroupEntryFlags`, and its own docblock says so, naming exactly this case. The half that survives is the pair `applyReachability` writes, `selectable`/`evented`, because `SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES` lists both by name (`persist.ts`, the constant read directly rather than inferred) alongside `locked`. So an author who saves while inside a group still writes editor-only reachability into the package, which is this row's subject and `vg-041`'s class. **THE COMMENT THAT MISLEADS IS STILL STANDING, and this is the part worth acting on: `grouping-manager/index.ts`'s `applyReachability` docblock justifies the write with "neither key is in Fabric's `stateProperties`, so it stays view state". That sentence is true and reasons about the wrong list.** `stateProperties` governs Fabric's default `toObject`; this project serialises through `canvas.toObject([...SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES])`, which adds both keys back explicitly — so the guard the comment believes it has does not exist. Task 12.4f edited that same docblock (it added the dim's paragraph) and left the false sentence in place, correctly declining to fix it: the ruling below makes the derived set a spec's business, so correcting one instance here would pre-empt the owner. The next reader of this row should read the comment as the instance of the defect rather than as its refutation. COLLAPSED 2026-10-16 (§8.3). This row is the measured instance of the question `vg-041` poses — which Fabric properties are derived from rendering, and whether the allowlist is enforced at the serialisation boundary — so one ruling covers the pair and it is recorded on `vg-041`. Marked rather than re-asked; neither row closes without the other.

title: No e2e fixture can raise a data gap and a composition gap together any more, because the player raises no crop notice at all
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT ON 2026-10-08, correcting plan 8 Task 2.3 before dispatching it, while checking whether the theme its ceiling test uses could actually raise the two strips the test's own comment named. THE MEASUREMENT, read from the seeded packages rather than assumed: `.e2e-host-app/themes/e2e-missing-sensor/theme.json` has artboard `{width:640,height:360,contentFit:contain}` and ONE object, a `Textbox` at `40,140` sized `420x60` -- entirely inside the artboard. `.e2e-host-app/themes/e2e-hosted/theme.json` has the same 640x360 artboard and four objects, the lowest a `Textbox` at `40,300` sized `420x60`, whose bottom edge is exactly 360. Neither bleeds, so neither raises `#yunari-crop`, and `showCropNotice` (`packages/player/src/chrome.ts:121`) is the only writer of that strip. THE PAIR THAT DOES NOT EXIST: a theme that both bleeds and binds a key no provider reports. The bleed fixtures (`HOST_BLEED_THEME_ID`, `HOST_BLEED_ALL_THEME_ID`, `e2e-bleed-*`) bind real keys, so they raise a composition gap and no data gap; the missing-sensor fixture binds an unreportable key and raises a data gap and no composition gap. SECTION 97's rationale -- that an unreadable sensor and a cropped object must be legible as different things, which is why two strips may be on screen at once -- is therefore not exercised as a pair by any browser test. WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT IN THE PLAN RATHER THAN HERE: Task 2.3's second test keeps its two-strip assertion, because the chrome ceiling is about total chrome height and not about which notices make it up, and its comment now says the pair is a data gap beside a TRANSPORT gap (`#yunari-connection`, drawn because the test aborts `**/ws`) instead of claiming a composition gap. Filed rather than fixed because closing it means adding a fixture to `tests/e2e/host-theme.ts` that is both bleeding and missing-sensored, which is a decision about fixture inventory rather than a change to the code under test.

RULED 2026-10-12: ADD the fixture — one document that both bleeds and binds a key the host cannot report. §97's rationale is that an unreadable sensor and a cropped object must be legible as DIFFERENT things, which is why two strips may be on screen at once, and no browser test exercises that pair today: Task 2.3's two-strip assertion passes with a transport gap standing in for the composition gap, which is a different pair. Fixture inventory is the test suite's own decision and this is the entry it is missing, against a requirement that already exists rather than a new one. It is a change to the evidence and not to the code under test, which is why the row was filed rather than fixed. CORRECTED 2026-10-18 BY TASK 25.7, and its ruled intent is now unexecutable. The ruling above (2026-10-12) was to ADD a fixture that both bleeds and binds a key the host cannot report, so that §97's pair could be exercised as two strips on screen at once. Task 25.7 removed the player's crop notice entirely, on the user's own "BOTH, EVERYWHERE" ruling (`vg-578`), so a bleeding document now raises NO strip at all: the pair this row exists to make testable cannot be raised on the player's surface any more. The remaining half is not a gap — a data gap on its own is already covered by the `e2e-missing-sensor` fixture. So the row's subject is gone rather than narrowed, and its disposition is a ruling the user owes: withdraw it, or re-point it at the surface where a composition gap is still legible (the editor's artboard panel, whose count stays and now excludes nothing). Recorded as pending rather than withdrawn, because withdrawal is the user's decision and not an agent's to take.

title: A theme install that loses the staging rename to EPERM fails a spec outright, and the cascade reads as unrelated defects
detail: FOUND AT PLAN 9 PHASE 1'S BOUNDARY, where it was the single largest reason a full browser-suite run was unreadable. THE MECHANISM: the e2e host installs a fixture by writing into `.e2e-host-app/themes/.staging-<random>.<fixture>` and renaming it onto the fixture's own directory. Under parallel load that rename intermittently loses with `EPERM: operation not permitted` on Windows, and the spec fails at the install: `the host accepted the fixture: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '...\.staging-muzerquni8dhlraixl.e2e-clip-parity' -> '...\.e2e-host-app	hemes\e2e-clip-parity'`. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SHRUG IS THE BLAST RADIUS, not the race. In one full-suite run that failure accounted for 17 of 21 unexpected results without appearing 17 times: every spec whose fixture did not install then fails somewhere else - five on a missing object (`no object with id authoring`, `no object with id mover`, `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'groupContext')`), three on `#status` never reaching the text the spec waits for - so ONE filesystem race presented as five unrelated defect classes across glass, clip, snapping and appearance specs. That is precisely the shape that gets misattributed to whatever diff happens to be in the tree, and it very nearly was here. THE SAMPLE THAT CLASSIFIES IT: re-running the same spec set with the box quiet left 4 unexpected, and `clip-parity` run entirely alone is 2 expected / 0 unexpected. So it is load- or handle-dependent and NOT a standing red; the remaining 4 were `vg-151` (known open) and `vg-196` (filed separately). The staging directory is left clean - no `.staging-*` survived either run - so nothing is wedged between runs. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the handle belongs to the host's own file watcher on the themes directory, to an indexer or scanner on this box, or to a previous run's host process that had not fully exited is not measured, and no other session's Chromium is implicated because none was on the box for the classifying run. THE FIX IS PROBABLY SMALL AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE: a bounded retry around the rename is the obvious repair, since the staging directory is the host's own and a lost race currently fails the spec outright with no attempt to recover. Worth pairing with whatever owns `themes/store.ts`'s install path, because `vg-174`'s LAN move work is in the same neighbourhood. title: Renaming an object is written in two places, they refuse differently, and the validity guard lives in a module the ownership map does not name
detail:
FOUND by a read-only architecture survey the user asked for ('does any domain manager need clean-up — same domain spread across a few managers, a domain under another owner that should be its own'), run on 2026-10-09 with docs/architecture/ownership.md as the yardstick. Verified from source. The validity RULE has one owner and is shared correctly — renderer-core/src/theme/object-name.ts:33 isObjectName — but that module has NO row in ownership.md, and by the map's own preamble a module owning a concept while appearing nowhere in the map is invisible, so nothing warns a reader not to decide it elsewhere. The two writers of the FACT disagree on the refusal path: editor-shell/bridge.ts:323-324 (layer-row rename) returns silently at :329, while selection-inspector/appearance.ts:339 reports through errorManager.warn('controls', uiCopy.inspectorFields.invalidName) at :319-325. They notify differently too: bridge fires nothing and relies on the session subscription (bridge.ts:148), while appearance.ts:345-350 fires object:modified itself. So typing a refused name has two outcomes depending on which surface it was typed in — one author action, two behaviours. NOT ESTABLISHED: neither writer was traced past the refusal branch. OWNER: unassigned; the name write belongs with the object's identity, and both surfaces should call it. SEVERITY: low — the name is refused either way, and the divergence is in what the author is told. CONFIRMED BY THE CENSUS (2026-10-12), after a review forced it to apply one standard in both places: this row's complaint stands. The code half is exactly as described -- the guard is now shared (bridge.ts:346 and view.ts:456 both call isObjectName), and the second writer moved from selection-inspector/appearance.ts to selection-inspector/index.ts:384. The unnamed-module half also stands: object-name.ts sits in renderer-core/src/theme/, and the registry's row for that names a DIRECTORY ("Theme semantic types/validation"), which does not name a module: the census states the rule as a row names a module when the file holding the guard is fixed by the row, which a *-manager/ directory does by pointing at its index.ts entry and which renderer-core/src/theme/ does not do for any of its eleven modules. The census applies that same standard to selection-inspector's own files too, so it is one standard rather than two, and not this row being right by luck. Consequence beyond this row, and the reason to keep it: several registry rows name directories, so the map's module-level coverage is thinner than its row count suggests.

READING 2026-10-13: the unnamed-module half is discharged — the ownership map now names renderer-core/src/theme/object-name.ts as the object-name rule's owner (dd308143). The divergence half stands and the row stays open against it: a refused rename returns silently at editor-shell/bridge.ts:341-352 and reports "invalid" at selection-inspector/view.ts:440-450.

title: The snap manager implements one acquire-hold-plan-verify protocol twice, split movement-versus-scale — the duplicated axis — rather than by the sub-domains that are genuinely separate
detail:
FOUND by a read-only architecture survey the user asked for ('does any domain manager need clean-up — same domain spread across a few managers, a domain under another owner that should be its own'), run on 2026-10-09 with docs/architecture/ownership.md as the yardstick. The largest structural finding of the set, and the answer to the user's companion worry that several files have crossed the 500-line signal. snap-manager/ is ~8,300 non-test lines across eight files and roughly 4,900 of them are ONE concept implemented twice, which the guards confirm as well as the shapes: the movement family's assertMovementHoldState/assertRawIntentMatchesBaseline (movement-snapping-resolver.ts:313-314) and assertAxisHold (:1315-1316) are mirrored by the scale family's checks in scaling/scale-projection.ts:95,117,156,186,187 and scaling/scale-snapping-runtime.ts:84-229. The parallel-for-parallel evidence: identical threshold records with identical values (movement-snapping-resolver.ts:81-87 with MOVEMENT_SNAP_VERIFICATION_EPSILON = 0.1 at :203 versus scaling/scale-snapping-resolver.ts:88-94 with SCALE_SNAP_VERIFICATION_EPSILON = 0.1 at :243); parallel frozen holds (FREE_MOVEMENT_HOLD_STATE :240 / FREE_SCALE_HOLD_STATE :265); runtimes exposing the same five-method protocol (movement-snapping-runtime.ts:75-190 startSession/getDuplicateStep/resolveMovementPlan/verifyMovementPlan/finishSession versus scaling/scale-snapping-runtime.ts:84-229 the same shape with resolveScalePlan/refineScalePlan/verifyScalePlan); and parallel candidate builders (movement-snap-candidates.ts:23-76 versus scaling/scale-snap-candidates.ts). GENUINELY SEPARATE and not the duplicated part: spacing (spacing.ts at 1302 lines plus spacing-chains.ts, spacing-patterns.ts, movement-spacing-correction.ts, movement-spacing-verification.ts) and pointer-to-multiplier projection (scaling/rectangular-scale-gesture-projection.ts at 985, scale-projection.ts at 726). WHY IT IS A MANAGER QUESTION: the axis the module is split on — movement versus scale — is the axis that duplicated, while the sub-domains that are actually distinct are not the split; that is why the family carries five files over 700 lines and three over 1,300. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the two protocols fold into one parameterised by axis without disturbing spacing and projection, which is the design question. The map's footer already names 'advanced snapping' as a review-only legacy candidate, so this is a candidate for a spec rather than a task. OWNER: unassigned. SEVERITY: low today (it works and is tested), high as the reason the editor's largest module family is the largest. SIZE CORRECTED BY THE CENSUS (2026-10-12): this row said "~8,300 non-test lines across eight files"; the census measured 30 non-test files, four of them past the 800 stop. The duplicated-protocol finding itself stands and the census confirms it -- only the size was unsourced.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: SPEC IT NOW. The one acquire-hold-plan-verify protocol implemented twice along the movement-versus-scale axis is specified before any re-shape, so the axis that duplicated is settled on paper -- spacing and projection preserved -- rather than discovered while moving 30 non-test files, four of them past the 800-line stop. The spec names which sub-domains are genuinely separate and which protocol is shared, and the re-shape lands from it. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-snap-manager-protocol-design.md

title: `editor-shell.css` styles `select` elements nothing renders: the inspector pair this row named is deleted, and the surviving arms trace to an unimported `settingsField`
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING PLAN 4 TASK 10 (2026-10-10, commit 80facf67) AND CARRIED AS A `Discovered, not fixed:` TRAILER IN THAT COMMIT; both terms were re-located BY RULE in 4a283864, which deleted the two `.editor-shell-panel select` terms beside them and so moved the lines. Located by rule rather than by line number (the finding's own instruction): `grep -n 'editor-shell-inspector' packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css | grep -i select` returns exactly two, in the shared selector lists `… button, … input, … select {` and `… input, … select, … textarea {`. MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: with an object selected in the built editor, `document.querySelectorAll('.editor-shell-inspector select')` is 0, `.editor-shell-panel select` is 0 and `.editor-shell select` is 0. The last `document.createElement("select")` the editor shell's own code holds is settings-field.ts:196, imported by controls.dom.test.ts alone (R68's consumer survey), so the terms style an element nothing renders. [CORRECTED 2026-10-12, see the amendment below: this sentence said "the only ... in the package" and that was false.] NOT DELETED IN TASK 10 because the rule there is delete-what-lost-its-OWN-last-consumer within that plan, and this pair's consumer left in plan 3; a cross-plan dead rule belongs in the register rather than in a sweep task's diff. AMENDED 2026-10-12 by Task 2 of the dead-code sweep and its independent review (report `docs/architecture/dead-selectors.md`, review `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-12-the-dead-code-sweep/task-2-review.md`). TWO CORRECTIONS, both to statements rather than to the measurement. (1) **The two `.editor-shell-inspector select` terms this row names are GONE at HEAD** -- `grep -n 'editor-shell-inspector' editor-shell.css | grep -i select` returns nothing, as does the `editor-shell-panel` twin -- so a fixer should not go looking for this pair. (2) The sentence above that claimed settings-field.ts:196 was the only `createElement("select")` in the package was **FALSE**: `packages/host/public/settings.html:197` and `:372` hold two more, inside `packages/`. The material conclusion survives: `settingsField` is imported by `controls.dom.test.ts` and `copy-defects.test.ts` only, while production imports only `isSettingVisible`/`settingsFieldsFor`. WHAT SURVIVES INSTEAD is four arms, located by rule as this row requires: `.editor-shell select` and the `select` arm of the `:is(...)` focus rule, both already covered by this row's own browser measurement (`.editor-shell select` = 0), plus `.yunari-field select` and `.yunari-field-row select`, which are dead by the static argument only -- `.yunari-field`'s producers (`number-field.ts:55`, `settings-field.ts:236`, `new-document-chooser.tsx:236`) render no `<select>` -- and have **not** been browser-measured. Retitle rather than close: closing would lose both the measurement debt on those two arms and the fact that they are dead by the same missing-importer argument this row owns. TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the browser measurement this row owed is taken on the built editor preview at base 7f88dff3. document.querySelectorAll('select') is 0 in every state read: the editor at boot with nothing selected, with a Rectangle selected, with the settings modal open on each of its three tabs, with the New-document chooser open (where .yunari-field is 1, so that class does render), and on the Add pane. .editor-shell select, .yunari-field select and .yunari-field-row select are 0 in every one of those states, and the dialog is not a descendant of .editor-shell (.editor-shell [role=dialog] is 0 with the modal open), so the .editor-shell arm cannot reach a dialog's select either. The measurement debt is discharged: all four arms are dead by measurement as well as by the row's static argument. NOT DELETED HERE, and that is the one act left: the four arms are a cross-plan sweep of editor-shell.css rather than a browser pass's act, and the cost of moving them is measurable: 18 live rows attribute a line to that file, 31 such citations across them, with 33 rows mentioning the file at all, so the delete belongs to whoever can carry those citations with it.

title: The spec's acceptance instrument for native controls cannot see the class it exists for
detail:

Counted, before and after.", and plan 4's Task 10 measured it with a grep for createElement("select"), <select and "range" under packages/editor/src. The spec's own sentence is unchanged, and rewording an Acceptance item is a decision about what done means, so this row records the debt rather than closing it.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D5's membership ruling covering vg-228, vg-267, vg-271, vg-274 and vg-286 together: TESTS JOIN THE GATED LIST. A test file that renders the shell is ratchet material, expressed as one rule in the checker rather than judged file by file -- today 11 test files are gated and 35 exist, and the four files carrying violations become checked. This row is the direction taken here: the Acceptance item is reworded to what the instrument proves rather than the debt being recorded. D5'S RULED WORK WAS ADOPTED BY NO PHASE, MEASURED 2026-10-13: `vg-228` carries the full measurement. In short: none of D5's five rows appears in any work phase's list, and the plan's closing rule (`2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:80`) lets a ruled row close only on the phase that lands its change, so this row is ruled and unclosable until a task adopts it. The blocker is its criterion rather than its scope -- see `vg-228` for the two readings and their measured costs. RULED 2026-10-13: THE CRITERION OF THE 2026-10-12 MEMBERSHIP RULING, asked as its own question and answered by the user: **EVERYTHING THAT RENDERS OR DRIVES THE SHELL**, expressed as one derived rule rather than a list. THIS ROW'S OWN QUESTION IS NOT THAT ONE and is not answered by it: `vg-271` asks whether the Acceptance item is reworded to what the instrument proves or the debt stays recorded, and that remains its own decision - named here so a session reading the cluster does not mistake the criterion for an answer to it. RULED 2026-10-14: REWORD THE ITEM. The Acceptance item is reworded to what its instrument proves rather than left requiring a comparison the controls instrument cannot make for the class it exists for, so the gap stops being a debt carried against a promise and becomes a statement of the instrument's measured reach. The row closes on the reworded item, with that scope written where the item is read.

title: The design-language fixture proves the shell's global focus rule, not the portalled control's own, because it nests the row inside `.editor-shell`
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 2'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over 64fea389..eba81b2a), WHICH CORRECTED THE FINDING ITS OWN FIX ROUND HAD FILED. WHAT THE COMMIT TRAILER CLAIMED (commit eba81b2a): that `components/ui/control-choice-row.tsx:54`'s `focus-visible:outline-*` classes are inert, because `.editor-shell :is(button, …):focus-visible` out-specifies them. MEASURED: the specificity half is true only for an element INSIDE `.editor-shell` - the shell rule is unlayered while the Tailwind utility lands in `@layer utilities` (built CSS: `.focus-visible\:outline-2:focus-visible` at offset 20264 inside `@layer utilities{` @7990, the shell rule unlayered at 39365) and its specificity (0,3,0) beats the class's (0,2,0). But the Appearance tab does not ship inside `.editor-shell`: the modal is a Base UI Dialog portalled to `document.body` (`components/ui/dialog.tsx:44-60`), a sibling of `#app` rather than a descendant of `.editor-shell` (`palette.ts:93-99`, `shell-layout.tsx:699`), so there the shell rule cannot match at all and the control's own classes are the SOLE focus treatment. The CSS author knew: `.editor-shell-settings-tab:focus-visible` and `.editor-shell-settings-panel:focus-visible` exist precisely because the dialog is portalled, and no equivalent rule exists for the choice row. ACTING ON THE TRAILER WOULD HAVE BEEN A DEFECT - deleting those classes as redundant strips the shipped product's focus ring, while the design-language fixture stays green because there the shell rule paints the outline. THE REAL FINDING IS THE PROOF-CONTEXT GAP: `control-fixture.tsx:145-175` mounts `ControlChoiceRow` inside the fixture's own `.editor-shell` (`:62`), and `design-language.spec.ts`'s new §4e case (`~:866-1030`) asserts a `solid` outline of at least 2px there - which the shell's global rule supplies. So §4e passes even when the control's own focus classes paint nothing, and cannot detect a regression in the treatment that actually ships on the portalled modal. The implementer's own red proof demonstrates exactly this: removing the shell focus rule reddened the case with `paints the browser's auto ring, not §5's solid outline`, while the classes were the thing under test. NOT FIXED HERE because the fix is a decision about how a portalled surface is measured (a second fixture outside `.editor-shell`, or a browser case on the real modal) rather than a one-line change, and this plan's Task 6 owns the capture. OWNER: whoever owns `components/ui/` and the design-language fixture's context.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174; the venue is `design-language.spec.ts`'s fixture case, and the second half is the shipped portalled modal): the fixture case passes in the same run (`the control set renders in the design language`, 4156ms), and on the shipped Appearance tab a focused palette card - a `ControlChoiceRow` - computes `:focus-visible` true, `outline-style: solid`, `outline-width: 2px`, `outline-color: rgb(114, 224, 192)`, `outline-offset: 2px`, while `closest(".editor-shell")` on it is null (its only dialog ancestor is the portalled `.editor-shell-dialog`). So the ring that ships is painted by the control's own classes, and the fixture's green reads that same visual fact through the shell's global rule instead. What §4e cannot see is the control's own classes going missing.

RULED 2026-10-15: **BOTH, and they answer different questions.** A second fixture mounted *outside* `.editor-shell` makes the control's own focus classes the thing that paints, so a regression in them reddens the case instead of being masked by the shell's global rule — that is the fast regression. A browser case against the real portalled Appearance modal asserts the ring that actually ships, on a surface `closest(".editor-shell")` does not match — that is the shipped-surface proof the fixture cannot give, because the fixture is a stand-in for the modal rather than the modal. **Neither substitutes for the other**, which is why this is both rather than the cheaper one: the fixture proves the treatment is present, and the browser case proves the treatment is reachable where it ships.

title: The layer row's attended state slot can intercept a press meant for the row, so a click on a name may reach its visibility or lock control
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over 50797965..b3805273). MEASURED, in the test harness: `tests/e2e/rebuild-driver.ts:206-222` presses a layer row through `.yunari-layer-name` at the element's LEFT END rather than at its default centre, and its own comment records why - the centre is intercepted, and five cases of `author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts` hung on it. The comment names the interceptor: the attended row's absolutely-positioned state slot (`editor-shell.css:1707-1712`, `position: absolute; right: 2px; top: 0; height: 26px`), which sits over the name because the name is `flex: 1 1 auto` (`editor-shell.css:1658`). WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this is a product-side hazard or only a Playwright fixed-point problem. A real pointer that hovers a row to click it has already revealed that row's state slot, so a press aimed at the row can land on the slot's own controls (visibility, lock) instead of selecting the layer - but nobody has measured the slot's width against the row's, or what a press at the name's centre actually hits in a browser. The CSS author calls the related shift deliberate: the attended row's name narrows by whatever its key does not take, "charged to the one row the pointer is on, and it is deliberate" (`editor-shell.css:1700-1708`). That states the SHIFT is intended; it does not say the slot may swallow a press aimed at the row. NOT FIXED HERE because the cause is not established and the fix, if needed, is a layout decision about the attended row rather than a test edit; the harness works around it, which also means nothing reddens if the layout changes. OWNER: whoever owns the layer row's layout (`selection-inspector/` and `editor-shell.css`'s `.yunari-layer-*` rules). TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the pointer measurement this row owed is taken on the built preview at base 7f88dff3, and the hazard is REAL at the desktop viewport. With a layer row attended (hovered) and its four-control slot drawn, the name's box reads left 120 / right 240.6 while the slot reads left 155 / right 277 — the slot overlaps the name by 85.6px — and document.elementFromPoint at the name's centre returns an SVG inside the slot's first button, where the same read 6px inside the name's left edge returns the name's own span. The cause is named: the room the :has rules reserve is written on .yunari-layer-bound (editor-shell.css:2188-2206), this row draws no bound at all, so nothing reserves it and the absolutely-positioned .yunari-layer-state (:2121-2134) covers the name. Three citations on this line corrected by re-measurement, as symbols and lines: the slot is .yunari-layer-state at editor-shell.css:2121, not :1707-1712; the name is .yunari-layer-name at :2072, not :1658; the deliberate-shift comment is at :2115-2120. STAYS OPEN: the fix is a layout decision about the attended row, which the row already says.

title: Two editor specs claim a fresh starter trips the dirty guard, which the session mechanism contradicts, while a third records the opposite sample
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I'S SECOND SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over b3805273..846e451c), which retired the same claim from a fourth file. THE CONTRADICTION: `tests/e2e/author-journey-display.spec.ts:231-235` and `tests/e2e/composition-panel.spec.ts:556-558` both assert that a fresh starter "counts as unsaved work", so opening another theme asks the dirty guard. The mechanism says otherwise: `editor-session.ts:1004-1020` asks only when `isDirty`, and `persistence-manager/index.ts:34,42` compares the current key against `#savedDocument` - the snapshot the session opened on, built at `editor-session.ts:498-501`. `editor-main.ts:233-238`'s `onNew` mounts a fresh session, so a document that has just been created IS its own baseline. MEASURED, by the implementer, against the built bundle during round 2: after Create a fresh editor shows zero `[role="dialog"]`, and Open library opens the chooser with no question - which is why the fourth file's comment (`tests/e2e/rebuild-driver.ts:132-138`) was corrected in `bdce766e`. WHAT MAKES IT A FINDING RATHER THAN A TYPO: `tests/e2e/reference-theme.spec.ts:490-492` records the OPPOSITE sample - five prompts in six save-then-Ctrl+N rounds on an unchanged starter. So at least one of the three is wrong, they disagree about product behaviour rather than wording, and nobody has measured which path differs (Ctrl+N against the menubar's New is the obvious candidate, and neither the session nor the specs distinguish them). WHY THE SPECS SURVIVE: `answerDialogIfShown` tolerates the absence of a dialog, so a spec asserting a prompt that never comes still passes - the tolerant call was the right one: the driver's absolute "asks nothing on the path every caller takes" is not what `reference-theme` observed. NOT FIXED HERE because establishing which claim is true needs a browser run per path, and the fix is to the claim rather than to behaviour. OWNER: whoever owns the editor's browser journeys (`tests/e2e/`) and the dirty-guard's own contract (`persistence-manager/`). TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the runs are taken on the built preview at base 7f88dff3, and the fresh-starter half of the contradiction is settled against the two specs. The dialog read is [role=dialog] — Base UI portals a div, not a native dialog[open], which is why a first pass read nothing from every path. A fresh editor, Control+n then Create: the size chooser opens and NO replacement question follows. A fresh editor, File then New theme then Create: same. A fresh editor, File then Open package: no dialog at all, and the file chooser fires, which is the guard having passed. So on a fresh starter the guard asks nothing on any of the three paths, and author-journey-display.spec.ts:231-235 and composition-panel.spec.ts:556-558 — both of which state that the starter, being unedited, counts as unsaved work — carry a premise this run refutes. reference-theme.spec.ts's five-prompts-in-six sample is a save-then-Ctrl+N state, which this run did not reproduce either way; the cell's --grep New collects TWO cases and not one, because Playwright compiles the pattern as a case-insensitive regexp: the unpiped --list exits 0 with four entries, reference-theme.spec.ts:380 (a fresh document is the reference composition, and New never touches the saved one -- the case that presses Control+n) and :2444 (a new background image is imported, and the artboard is repointed at it), each under desktop-chromium and phone-chromium, so neither case presses the menubar's New and the menubar path stays measured here rather than by the cell. STAYS OPEN: the fix is a claim correction in two spec files outside this task's file list, and correcting one side of a two-sided contradiction would leave the register claiming a disagreement the tree no longer carries.

title: A browser run at playwright.config.ts's default worker count reports 30s locator timeouts as failures at a clean HEAD, on this box
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 5 (commit 4698f233), while taking a browser baseline at 7d31622c with nothing broken. The same four specs, same commit, same built bundle: 4 failed / 23 passed at the default 10 workers, every failure a 30s locator timeout or `no control matches [data-yunari-palette-token]`; 27 passed at --workers=2. The four: keyboard.spec.ts:18 (locator.evaluate timeout), panel-labels.spec.ts:136 (locator.count timeout), panel-labels.spec.ts:208, shell-appearance.spec.ts:85 (locator.click waiting for visible/enabled/stable). CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED beyond "the machine": another session was busy on this box at the time (AGENTS.md, a long run holds the machine), and a single sample proves nothing about load or concurrency. It matters because a green suite read as red at the default worker count costs a false fix round: plan 5 Task 5's first browser baseline read exactly this way. ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT MECHANISM: vg-216 is two configs sharing test-results/ and deleting each other's traces; this is one run under load. What would settle it: run the same specs at 10 workers on an otherwise idle box, and if they still time out, bisect the worker count. CONTROLLER MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-11, WHICH NARROWS THE CAUSE RATHER THAN CONFIRMING THE ONE OFFERED: running the palette sweep (shell-appearance.spec.ts:97) ALONE at the default worker count, on an otherwise idle box at 7309eb1d, takes 8.6s and 8.5s in two consecutive runs, a whole run 12.1s - roughly 3.5x inside the 30s limit. So that test's own runtime is NOT what tips it over, and the most plausible inherent explanation is now falsified rather than merely untested. Plan 7 Task 2's fix round reported the same test timing out at 30,722ms with durations of 26.8s, 28.2s and 33.3s, and those figures did NOT reproduce: they were taken while this session was itself running Playwright against the same built bundle, which is exactly the contention this row's first paragraph names. The cause is therefore CONCURRENT BROWSER RUNS ON ONE BOX AND ONE BUNDLE, and two things follow - a red at the default count is worth nothing until the spec is re-run alone at the same commit (AGENTS.md already asks this, and this is the measurement that makes it cheap to obey), and raising this spec's timeout would not fix it, because on an idle box there is nothing to fix. TASK 2.3B'S READING ON AN IDLE BOX, 2026-10-12, WHICH IS THE GATE THIS ROW NAMES: the same three files (`shell-appearance.spec.ts`, `panel-labels.spec.ts`, `keyboard.spec.ts`) on the same built bundle, with no other suite, build or browser driving it, FAILED at `--workers=10` - this box's default, its 20 logical cores halved, which is what the absent `workers` key in `playwright.config.ts` leaves in force. 4 of the 19 desktop-chromium cases were unexpected, every one a `Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded` reading 30.7-34.1s: the keyboard modal-trap row, `no control is unnamed`, the palette sweep and the treatment-boundary row. THE FINDING REPRODUCES, so the three timeouts this row already carried are the same shape rather than another session's artifact. BISECT, same three files and the same built bundle on the same idle box, one count per run: 8 workers 3 failed (33.4s, 33.2s, 30.8s), 6 workers 1 failed (the keyboard trap, 31.4s), 5 workers none failed (19 passed, 19 skipped, 59.5s, reproducing the dead attempt's reading). Every failure sits 1-14% over the 30s limit, so the count is a load threshold on this box rather than a stable boundary, and the threshold is in the worker count rather than in one spec: this row's own controller measurement had the palette sweep at 8.6s alone, and it reads 34.1s here. THE CLAUSE THE READING FALSIFIES: the sentence above saying raising a timeout would not fix it because on an idle box there is nothing to fix is half wrong - the idle box DOES redden at the default count - so what remains is a decision about which count this suite is run at here, and a decision rather than a patch because `playwright.config.ts`'s own comment defends leaving `workers` to the default (a hardcoded count oversubscribes a small CI runner). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT NOW: that decision, on this line - pin a count for this box, or accept the default and re-run the named spec alone at the same commit before believing a red. ONE CAVEAT ON THE LIST ABOVE, which this row does not otherwise carry: the treatment-boundary row IS one of the four, and Task 2.3b rewrote that row's own setup in the very commit that took this reading -- its member sets are now derived from the stylesheet rather than named. So the row does not claim the derivation is innocent of those four reds. What rules it out is arithmetic rather than a measurement: one extra `page.evaluate` per test rather than per palette, per-palette work unchanged, and the arm reading 12.2 s alone against a 30 s limit. One sample of that arm alone at 10 workers on the BASE commit would settle it, and no such sample was taken.

title: The derived-palette ladder is asserted as order only, so a palette whose three surface rungs collapse to steps of 0.0001 keeps its ordering and passes every assertion
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 4 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-11) IN ITS OWN DELIVERABLE, reviewing `a3d2c407` at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/task-4-review.md` finding 4. MEASURED BY READING THE ASSERTION: `design-language.spec.ts`'s derivation case compares `--bg`/`--panel`/`--panel-2` by luminance ordering (`bg < panel <= panel2`), which is what the plan's Step 5 asked for - "the luminance ordering ... matches graphite's" - and the plan's Step 3 asks for more: "takes from graphite the relationships between roles: the luminance separation". A palette whose three surfaces sit 0.0001 apart satisfies the ordering and shares nothing of the separation, so the assertion that exists to keep six transcribed value sets from drifting apart cannot see a collapse. TASK 4's FIX ROUND TIGHTENS WHAT CAN BE STATED WITHOUT INVENTING A NUMBER: strict `bg < panel < panel2` for the five derived palettes, editorial's equal `panel`/`panel-2` named as the one licensed exception. What is left is the magnitude, and that is why this is a row rather than a constant: a floor of "at least X luminance" has no rule behind it in the bible, and picking one is the move this plan has already had to undo once (the `designLanguagePx` allowlist entry added to make a gate pass, R25). NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a magnitude floor is worth having at all, since a derivation is re-derived rather than edited, or whether the bible should state a minimum surface separation - section 4 gives the roles and no spacing between them. What would settle it: a bible rule naming the minimum separation between a ground and the panel above it, and then an assertion reading it. PLAN 7 TASK 6 SEARCHED FOR THE RULE AND FOUND NONE (2026-10-11). Read, and this is the search rather than the conclusion: section 3 (`design-language.md:64-109`, the spacing, radius and elevation tables) — **the file `db000c40` deleted on 2026-10-11 when the bible became the root `DESIGN.md`, so these numbers have no successor**; the sections are named rather than re-pointed because this sentence is the search record of 2026-10-11 and not a pointer to follow states no surface separation; section 4 (`:111-140`, the role table) gives the roles and no relationship between `--bg`, `--panel` and `--panel-2`; section 5 (`:141-206`) gives contrast ratios only (3:1, 4.5:1), which bind a boundary against its ground rather than the distance between two grounds; the drawing (`current/shell.html:17-18`) declares three literals with no stated relationship. No constant was added and this row stays open, because a magnitude floor with no rule behind it is the `designLanguagePx` move (R25) this plan has already had to undo once.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174; the venue is `design-language.spec.ts`, and the magnitudes are read off the live `:root` custom properties resolved through an element): the ordering case passes (`graphite's roles are the drawing's, and the other five keep its ladder`, 3404ms), and the magnitude the row asks about, measured as WCAG relative luminance, spans 40x across the five palettes that can be measured. panel minus bg / panel2 minus panel, with the three luminances: graphite 0.0036 / 0.0035 (L 0.0043, 0.0079, 0.0113); ember 0.1454 / 0.0581 (0.6428, 0.7882, 0.8463); moss 0.1307 / 0.0680 (0.7016, 0.8324, 0.9003); plum 0.1438 / 0.0652 (0.6511, 0.7949, 0.8601); editorial 0.1008 / 0.0000 (0.8815, 0.9823, 0.9823 - the licensed equal pair). light's `--bg` is `linear-gradient(145deg, #d8ebe4, #afd4d1)` and has no single luminance, so its bg rung is unmeasured here rather than estimated; its declared surfaces are `#eff9f2bf` and `#f8fffbdf`, both carrying alpha. A magnitude floor would bind graphite first: a threshold above 0.0036 reds it. RULED 2026-10-14: ASSERT THE VALUES. The three surface rungs are asserted against what the derivation produces rather than against each other's order, so a palette whose rungs collapse to steps of 0.0001 fails because the value is wrong rather than because it crossed a threshold — no magnitude floor is introduced, and the reason is measured: a floor above graphite's 0.0036 / 0.0035 would red the tightest legitimate palette, so a floor would need a per-palette constant and would still only catch collapse by accident. The values are available to assert because the derivation is the owner: the assertion reads the produced rungs, not a hand-copied table.

title: light is the one palette whose chrome is still translucent, so "chrome is opaque" holds in five of six palettes and light composites against a gradient ground
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11) while making the chrome opaque, and reported to the controller as the brief asked rather than settled here: "where a palette's chrome has no derivation to read that is a finding for me, not a literal invented here". MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER after the change, reading `getComputedStyle().backgroundColor` on `.editor-shell-rail`: editorial `rgb(255,253,247)`, graphite `rgb(18,22,28)`, ember `rgb(247,226,210)`, moss `rgb(228,239,217)`, plum `rgb(236,227,247)` - all opaque - and light `rgba(239,249,242,0.75)`. CAUSE ESTABLISHED: `.editor-glass` now paints the palette's own `var(--panel)`, and light is the only palette whose surface roles carry alpha at all - `--shell-surface: #eff9f2bf` and `--shell-surface-strong: #f8fffbdf` - while its `--shell-backdrop` is the set's only gradient, so no role light declares is an opaque surface and plan 7 Task 4's derivation (graphite's relationships: the luminance ladder, the edge's weight against its surface) produces none. It is not expressible in CSS either: deriving the composite needs `color-mix` over `--shell-backdrop`, which is a gradient and is invalid inside `color-mix`. CONSEQUENCE: the rail, both panes, the inspector and the header each composite 25% of the mint gradient behind them, so light's chrome contrast is not one composited value and its boundary ratio (measured 1.40:1, `vg-200`'s pin) moves with the ground. The treatment assertion in `shell-appearance.spec.ts` names light as its one exemption and reads the translucency it carries, so a value that lands reds the gate and the exemption has to be deleted rather than left to excuse a regression. NOT FIXED IN TASK 5: choosing an opaque light surface is a palette value decision, and the task that owns the derivation is the one that should make it.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174; the venue is `shell-appearance.spec.ts`, and the surfaces are `.editor-shell-rail`'s computed background per palette): five rails are opaque - editorial rgb(255, 253, 247), graphite rgb(18, 22, 28), ember rgb(247, 226, 210), moss rgb(228, 239, 217), plum rgb(236, 227, 247) - and light is rgba(239, 249, 242, 0.75), the field the browser reports for the declared `#eff9f2bf` surface, over the set's only gradient ground (light `--bg` = linear-gradient(145deg, #d8ebe4, #afd4d1)). No value moved. The treatment case is green in the same run (`chrome is flat and opaque, and the canvas clusters keep the glass`, 11894ms). RULED 2026-10-14: MAKE LIGHT OPAQUE. Light gains a declared opaque surface — the mint gradient composited into one value, measured from the composite the rail, both panes, the inspector and the header each produce today (25 percent of the gradient behind them) — so "chrome is opaque" holds in six of six palettes and light's boundary ratio stops moving with the ground under it. `shell-appearance.spec.ts`'s light exemption is then deleted rather than left in place to excuse a regression, which the row says is what the exemption becomes if a value lands. The new value is derived and measured rather than picked, because the derivation is the owner and the row's cause is that light had no derivation to read.

title: `current/shell.html` draws no Add-pane asset preview, so the surface the product renders at `file-section.tsx:189` is one no gate can check
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 7 (2026-10-11, as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `7efea17f`) and adjudicated by its task review rather than left as the implementer's observation. MEASURED: `current/shell.html:128-140` draws the Add pane's Asset group as a select, then `Import a file`, then Replace/Remove, and a case-insensitive search for `preview` in that file returns nothing, while the product renders an `img.yunari-asset-preview` carrying `data-yunari-asset-preview` at `panes/add/file-section.tsx:189-194`, styled at `editor-shell.css:1107`, and both `editor-shell-add-desktop-chromium.png` and `pane-add-desktop-chromium.png` show it. DISPOSITION: `drawing-stale`, not `fix` - pulling the product to the drawing would delete a real capability (the thumbnail and its hidden-when-unpreviewable rule), spec section 13.1 does not let a visual difference waive a required capability, and Task 9's own rule sends a capability the product has and the drawing lacks into the drawing, because a gate cannot check a surface the drawing never draws. The frozen original `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html` stays as it is; the repair belongs to `current/shell.html` and was in flight as Task 7's fix round 1 when this row was filed. CONSEQUENCE UNTIL IT LANDS: the plan's own completion condition (section 13: every difference fixed or backed by a cited rule) is not met, and the Asset group is the least-comparable region besides, because the 1280x720 capture clips `Import a file`, `Replace asset` and `Remove asset` below the fold where the 1180x1040 drawing shows them. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the repair should be paired with a reader row, since that needs machinery the parity table does not have today. THE DRAWING HALF IS DISCHARGED (2026-10-11, artefact 221bf1a1, Task 7 fix round 1): `current/shell.html` now draws the preview well between the Asset select and the `Import a file` row, in the drawing's own idiom, with the class it stands for named in a comment beside it - `height:120px;aspect-ratio:1672/941` taken from a live measurement of `[data-yunari-asset-preview]` on the built bundle (213.3x120 at the pane content's left edge, flush under the select), and a gradient standing in for the chosen picture. The frozen original is untouched and nothing was renumbered. The parity table re-ran green with the drawing changed and no row's answer moved (9 passed at `--workers=1`, re-run by the controller against `design-language.spec.ts` rather than taken from the report). WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY THIS ROW STAYS OPEN: the title's second clause is untouched - a surface the drawing omits is still one no gate can check. No reader row was built, and the reason is measured rather than laziness: the product's contract is `max-height:120px` with `object-fit:contain`, a bound and not a size, and the Add pane is `display:none` while Document is open, so a row would read no element. This class - a drawing that omits a surface the product renders - needs a surface-inventory check and belongs to `vg-304`'s family; the row stays open as that family's member rather than closing on the half that was repaired. REOPENED 2026-10-12 BY TASK 2.3a OF THE BACKLOG-DRAIN PLAN, on review: a close in this task was reverted rather than defended. THE INSTRUMENT EXISTS AND IS GREEN, AND IT STILL CANNOT CARRY A `verified`. What it proves: the surface this row names is named on all three sides — the component that renders it (`img.yunari-asset-preview` carrying `data-yunari-asset-preview`), the `editor-shell.css` rule that treats it, and `current/shell.html`, which draws the box beside the name. What it cannot prove, and this IS the class the row exists for: the list of surfaces it reads is HAND-WRITTEN AND ONE ENTRY LONG, so a product surface that is not on the list reddens nothing — the instrument re-asserts the one surface already found and cannot discover the next. AND THE DRAWING SIDE READS A NAME, NOT A DRAWN ELEMENT: the drawn box at `current/shell.html:134` is an anonymous inline-styled div with no class and no hook, so that side is satisfied by the `<!-- asset preview (.yunari-asset-preview) ... -->` comment at `:133` — delete the drawn box and leave the comment and the instrument stays green. DERIVING THE SET FROM THE PRODUCT WAS MEASURED AND DOES NOT CONSTRUCT: the panes render 73 distinct `data-yunari-*` hooks, 5 of them named anywhere in `editor-shell.css`, and NO checked drawing names any of them — the drawings are hand-authored HTML that names a product surface by its class, in prose beside the box, never by a hook on a drawn element. Measured 2026-10-12 by walking `src/web/packages/editor/src/panes/**/*.tsx` and testing each hook against the stylesheet and the six checked drawings; a derivation that required the drawing to name every hook would red the suite at 73 entries — or at 5, scoped to the hooks the stylesheet names — with no way to satisfy any of them. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an enumeration of the product's surfaces that the drawings can be held to — either the drawings gain a mechanical way to name a product surface, or a product-side registry of surfaces exists for the drawings to be checked against. The §8.11 path correction and the §8.2 line correction recorded above still stand and are unaffected: the surface is `src/web/packages/editor/src/panes/add/file-section.tsx:192-193`, and the `.yunari-asset-preview` rule is `editor-shell.css:1229`.

title: The settings drawing's frame is a fixed 560px while the modal is content-sized, so it measures 405px on Appearance and every drawn region inside it renders half-size — and no row reads a drawing's frame width
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 5 (2026-10-11, as the third `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `411dbe91`). MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:20` draws the modal's frame at `width:560px` fixed, while the product's `.editor-shell-dialog` is `min-width:340px; max-width:560px` and content-sized (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1311-1312`), so Task 5's report measures it at 405px on the Appearance tab, 507px on Keyboard and 393px on About. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT: the palette cards render about 58px wide against the drawing's about 120px, so the grid is the drawing's three columns while each card is half the drawn width and the drawn proportions are not reproduced anywhere in the modal. WHY NO GATE SEES IT: the one row on the frame reads its `border-radius`, and no row reads a drawing's width - the same gap `vg-292` names for another geometry and `vg-320` names for a drawing's value. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: it is the frame's geometry rather than the palette group's, and Task 5's outcome is the group; the plan's ten tasks name no frame width, and the three panels' content differs (Keyboard is already 507px), so taking the drawing's fixed width is a ruling about the modal rather than an edit inside it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the modal should take the drawing's 560px, or a width per panel, or whether a content-sized modal is right and the drawing is the stale one - the drawing's `width:560px` may simply be how a static drawing is authored rather than a property the product must match. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: that ruling, plus a row that reads the frame's width so the next divergence is visible. IT IS NOT THE SAME AS THE GLASS OR THE RADIUS: the modal's frame radius is a green row and stays green. PLAN 8 TASK 10 MEASURED THE PRODUCT SIDE, WHICH THIS ROW DID NOT HAVE (2026-10-11, b78ee264): the modal is content-sized today at 405px on Appearance, 507px on Keyboard and 393px on About, against the drawing's fixed `width:560px`; the Appearance pane's palette cards therefore render about 58px wide where the drawing draws about 120px, and the difference is visible in the committed capture beside the drawing. NO PREDATING RULE NAMES A DIALOG'S WIDTH: section 3's table is spacing, and the bible's two dialog rules are the title's type (section 2) and the scrim (section 3), so this is not licensed and stays open. REJECTED RATHER THAN ANSWERED, BY THE USER (2026-10-11), and this is the larger finding: 'Setting should not be a modal but a panel like add, composition.' The question was whether the modal takes the drawing's fixed 560px; the answer is that there should be no modal to measure, so this row's width question and the 405/507/393px measurements are about a container that is going away. Filed forward as `vg-330`, which owns the change and the drawing redraw. This row stays open only so the measurement is not lost; it closes when `vg-330` does.

RULED 2026-10-15: **CLOSES WITH THE PANE.** This row measures a content-sized modal against a drawn fixed 560px frame, and a pane has the shell's pane width unconditionally, so the mismatch it describes stops existing when `vg-330`'s spec lands. It closes on that landing rather than before it, and it does **not** narrow to the drawing: the drawing is redrawn in the same change.

title: No drawing in the checked set draws the `?` shortcut sheet, so one modal surface is outside the acceptance instrument and two plan-8 rulings leaned on that absence
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 7 (2026-10-11, while scoping the chord chip). MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/` holds six drawings - `controls.html`, `controls-light.html`, `settings.html`, `settings-keyboard.html`, `settings-about.html`, `shell.html` - and **not one of them draws or mentions the shortcut reference sheet**. `settings-keyboard.html` contains the word 'shortcut' because it is the Keyboard panel's own drawing; a search for the reference itself ('shortcut reference') matches nothing in the directory. The sheet is not a fringe surface: `shortcut-reference.tsx:36-45` renders `h2.editor-shell-dialog-lead`, one `section` per group and a `kbd` per row directly into the dialog, so it is the second consumer of the modal's shared rules and it is on the keyboard-only walkthrough (spec `:516-521`, 'open and close a popup', 'cancel shortcut capture'). TWO RULINGS LEANED ON THIS ABSENCE, both soundly: Task 7 scoped the chord chip to `.editor-shell-keyboard kbd` rather than moving the shared `.editor-shell-dialog kbd`, because moving it would move a surface no drawing governs; and `vg-319` defers the shared `h3` eyebrow for the same reason. Neither ruling is wrong - the point is that the instrument's hole became load-bearing twice without being named. WHY IT MATTERS: the sheet has behaviour proof (`vg-284` names what that proof misses) and no treatment comparator at all, so every pixel of it is unmeasured against the gold target - the same shape as `vg-314`, which names the Add pane's asset preview as a surface no gate can check.
