Spec `:506-507` is explicit that a visual difference cannot waive keyboard access or contrast, and those are exactly the properties a drawing is the instrument for. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a drawing of the sheet in `current/`, in Task 4's pattern for the Keyboard and About panels - or a ruling that the sheet's treatment is wholly inherited from the modal's drawing and needs a comparator of its own nowhere. NOT ESTABLISHED: which of those two is right, and whether the sheet is in scope for the drawing set at all - the plan's Out of scope assigns the shell and its clusters to plan 7 and says nothing about the sheet.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174, the `?` sheet opened by the shell's own dispatcher): the hole is still there and the sheet is live. Pressing `?` opens a portalled `.editor-shell-dialog` labelled "Keyboard shortcuts" carrying `h2.editor-shell-dialog-lead`, 5 group `h3`s, 20 `dl > div` rows and 20 `kbd`s - the modal's shared rules' second consumer, as the row says. It is compared against nothing: `docs/design/mockups/current/` holds six HTML drawings (controls, controls-light, settings, settings-keyboard, settings-about, shell), a grep for "shortcut reference" matches none of them, and "Keyboard shortcuts" matches only `settings-keyboard.html:244`, which draws the binding that OPENS the sheet rather than the sheet.

RULED 2026-10-15: **THE SHEET IS DRAWN.** A drawing of the `?` shortcut sheet joins `docs/design/mockups/current/`, in Task 4's pattern for the Keyboard and About panels, with its own capture and with `docs/design/mockups/README.md`'s count and table edited to match — the README states the set as six files with a table of exactly six, so a seventh drawing is a README edit rather than only a new file, and its literals enter the design-language instrument with it. **Inheritance was rejected on the evidence rather than on taste**: the run recorded on this row shows the sheet is the modal's shared rules' second consumer (20 `kbd`s, 5 group headings, one `h2`), so a treatment that is inherited is still a treatment nothing compares. **The two rulings that leaned on this absence are not overturned**, and the reason matters: they leaned on there being no comparator, not on a decision that none was needed, so the chord chip's `.editor-shell-keyboard kbd` scope and `vg-319`'s deferred eyebrow both stand.

title: Section 3's row-density rhythm is read by no gate: the drawings gate holds spacing to the step list and never to the 26/30/32 rule, which is where 75 corrected well insets would have shown
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 8'S REVIEW (2026-10-11). MEASURED: section 3's density rule (`docs/design/design-language.md:82-84`) — **the file `db000c40` deleted on 2026-10-11 when the bible became the root `DESIGN.md`, so these numbers have no successor**; the sections are named rather than re-pointed because this sentence is the search record of 2026-10-11 and not a pointer to follow gives the row rhythm 26, 30 and 32 - values that are deliberately NOT on the spacing step list at `:69` - and Task 8's widened drawings gate holds a spacing declaration to the step list alone, so a row drawn at the wrong density passes as long as its padding is a step. The scale where it would show: the 75 `5px -> 4px` well insets, because `control-well.tsx:52-56` pins `h-[26px]` in the product while the drawing expresses the same row through padding, so the drawn well height is font-metric-dependent - the `font` shorthand the drawings use sets no line-height - and the two sides can disagree with neither gate nor report examining it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawings and the product actually disagree on any row's height - the review that found this did NOT claim a break, only that nothing examines it. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: either a rule that the density values are outside the spacing arm's reach with a reason, or an arm that reads them (which needs a rendered height rather than a declaration, so it is a different kind of check from everything else in this gate). IT IS NOT vg-320, which is a drawing measured against the frozen original; this is a drawing measured against a written rule no arm reads. STILL OPEN AFTER TASK 2.3a OF THE BACKLOG-DRAIN PLAN (2026-10-12). The arm the row wants was attempted and not landed, and the reason is a measurement rather than a shortage of effort: §3's row rhythm is 26/30/32 and the product expresses it through `ControlWell`'s `WELL_HEIGHT`/`ROW_MIN_HEIGHT` density tables, but **no caller in the workspace passes `density="dialog"` or `density="settings"`** — every call site takes the default — so nothing renders at 30px for an arm to read, and a rendered arm built on the densities that do render would assert one number three times, which is the shape `vg-233`'s first pass closed on and the review refused. What the run established: the drawings gate is green over all six checked drawings with the field row at 26px in a panel reading its rhythm, and the deliberate decision §3 makes (26/30/32 are densities, not gutters, and are `design-tokens.mjs`'s `SPACING_PROPERTY` comment's reason for excluding them from the step list) still holds. What would close it: a rendered arm with a comparator for a surface's density, which needs at least one surface to render at the dialog density first. ONE CLAUSE CORRECTED 2026-10-13. This row reads the drawings' `font` shorthand as setting no line-height, which is true of the element rules and not of the files: the page furniture does state one - `settings-about.html:10`'s `font: 12px/1.45` on the page body, inherited by every drawn element - so a drawn row is not metric-dependent at the inherited ratio, only where an element overrides the size and keeps it. The ratio itself is off section 2's scale and is filed as `vg-440`; this row's subject, section 3's density rule (26/30/32) and the well-height disagreement it hides, is unchanged. ONE CLAUSE FALSIFIED AND CORRECTED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.5). The 2026-10-13 clause above reads the drawings' page furniture as stating a ratio — `settings-about.html:10`'s `font: 12px/1.45` on the page body, inherited by every drawn element — and that is no longer true: `vg-440` landed and the furniture now carries NO ratio (`font: 12px system-ui`), with every text-holding element stating its own size's companion instead. **So the well-height reading this row rests on has moved rather than been answered**: a drawn row is now metric-dependent only where an element states its own companion, which is the opposite of what the clause said, and the density question (26/30/32) is unchanged. Nothing else in this row is affected.

title: Settings is a modal today and the user has ruled it should be a pane like Add and Composition, opened from the rail's gear, with the settings drawing redrawn as a panel
detail:
FOUND BY THE USER (2026-10-11), reading the current mockup capture, in answer to the modal width question this round put to them: 'Setting should not be a modal but a panel like add, composition.' Three further sub-rulings came with it, each asked with a recommendation and each answered as recommended. (1) HOW IT OPENS: the rail keeps its FOUR slots -- Composition, Add, Tokens, Document -- and the gear opens Settings as a pane in the same area, exactly like Add and Composition; the pane's own header then names the surface, which is also this round's answer to `vg-328` (one name). A fifth rail slot was offered and declined: it would change the drawing's 46px rail and leave the gear redundant with the slot, which is two controls opening one surface. (2) THE DRAWING: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html` is REDRAWN without the scrim and the modal frame, as a pane at the shell's pane width. The user was told this edits the gold artefact and chose it anyway, because they had ruled the drawing is the acceptance instrument and a panel that is not drawn as a panel cannot be compared against anything -- Task 9's parity item could not be met for Settings at all. (3) SEQUENCING: after plan 6, not now. WHY IT IS A SPEC AND NOT A TASK: it touches the rail, the shell layout, `ownership.md` and the drawing, and AGENTS.md requires brainstorm then spec then plan for something of that shape; it also cannot run beside plan 6, because exactly one implementation plan is active at a time. WHAT IT INVALIDATES, recorded here so the future spec re-reads them rather than rediscovering them: plan 6 Task 8 Step 3's acceptance item -- 'the rail's gear opens the settings modal rather than a fifth pane' -- which is TRUE while Settings is still a modal and is superseded the moment this lands (that item is deliberately NOT corrected in plan 6, since plan 6 finishes first and the item is accurate for its duration); `vg-318`'s scrim measurement, which measures a container that will not exist; and `vg-322`, whose whole subject is the modal's width. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the spec and its plan landing, with the redrawn drawing committed beside the shipped pane and a PARITY row on the pane's frame so the next divergence is visible. PARKED BY THE USER (2026-10-11): 'Let's park the settings becomes a pane spec.' The row stays OPEN and nothing is queued against it; the sequencing sub-ruling above is unchanged, and what it invalidates stays invalidated until a spec is written. RULED 2026-10-14: UNPARKED. The spec is commissioned — settings becomes a pane opened from the rail's gear, the settings drawing is redrawn as a panel, and the pane's frame gains a PARITY row so the next divergence is visible. Two rows whose subjects this invalidates are to be revisited inside that spec rather than before it: `vg-318`'s scrim measurement measures a container that will not exist, and `vg-322`'s whole subject is the modal's width. The row's own closing terms stand unchanged — the spec and its plan land, with the redrawn drawing committed beside the shipped pane.

RULED 2026-10-15 (two answers this spec inherits): **THE THREE TAB HEADINGS BECOME A VERTICAL LIST inside the pane** — a pane holds a list that the fixed 560px modal could not, and the shell already has list chrome to draw it with, so the pane is not the modal with a different frame. **AND THE PANE'S NAME IS `Editor Settings`,** which the pane's own header carries in both the redrawn `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html` and the product. `vg-328` is the ruling this inherits: the pane's header names the surface, so one name covers the gear, the pane and the drawing.

title: The palettes carry one accent and the user has asked for a second highlight, orange for graphite, whose role is an attention or in-flight state and must be defined before any colour is chosen
detail: FOUND BY THE USER (2026-10-11), looking at the current mockup capture: 'graphite needs another highlight/accent color, like orange, on top of the current pallete (other themes to follow once we define the role of this color).' THE ROLE WAS ASKED AND ANSWERED FIRST, because a colour chosen before its job is a colour that will be used for the wrong thing: it is an ATTENTION or IN-FLIGHT STATE -- something that is neither the primary action nor destructive, such as unsaved or unpublished changes, a reading that is stale or awaiting the author, or a pending operation. Two alternatives were offered and declined: a second colour for emphasis with no state meaning, and re-hueing graphite's existing --shell-accent to orange instead of adding a role. WHAT THE ROLE REQUIRES BEFORE ANY HEX IS PICKED, and each is a decision rather than a lookup: a name that says the JOB and not the hue (--attention, not --orange); a bible section 4 clause saying when it may appear, since section 4 already rations --accent to at most one accent-filled element visible and a second colour with no stated job is exactly the competition that rationing exists to prevent; and a rule keeping it off the same element as --accent, so the two can never both claim a surface. IT IS NOT GRAPHITE'S ALONE: the user's own framing is that the role is defined once and the other five themes follow, so the output is a section 4 role plus a per-palette value in each of the six, not a graphite-only token. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the section 4 clause and the six values, which is spec work rather than a task, together with whatever gate reads a state colour -- the contrast instrument measures text and boundaries and has no state-colour row today. RELATED: `vg-330` is the other change the user asked for in the same sitting, and both are sequenced after plan 6.

title: The one control that renders a chart setting descriptor has no production caller, and its module doc names a consumer that does not exist
detail:
FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of plan 6, which recorded it as out of that plan's range; it is not a plan-6 finding. `settingsField()` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/controls/settings-field.ts` has ZERO production callers: read in node across `src/web` (dist excluded), all twelve of its call sites are tests - one in `copy-defects.test.ts:138` and eleven in `controls.dom.test.ts`. Its module doc at `settings-field.ts:13-14` reads "The inspector's per-kind column mounts that same rendering, so the loop is this control rather than a second copy of it". The call sites were removed deliberately, not lost: `f254259b` (2026-10-06) added the file, then `4dc220c6` (2026-10-09) - "a chart's fields are React views, not DOM", plan 3 Task 3a - turned `chart-manager/panel.ts`'s descriptor loop into a view-model projection, and `settingsField` has had no production caller since. `SettingsFieldDescriptor` is referenced in production only by `settings-field.ts` itself and its owner `renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts`. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED for the doc half: whether the inspector's per-kind column was meant to be migrated to this control and never was, or renders descriptors by another route, the record does not settle, and this row does not guess which. Two fixes are possible and they are a design decision rather than a task: delete the now-unused control, or migrate the column to it. Checked for duplicates first: the archive's three `settings-field` mentions are `vg-145` (a gauge end angle), `vg-121` and `vg-122` (unreachable descriptor keys), and none owns this.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: MIGRATE THE INSPECTOR'S PER-KIND COLUMN TO IT. The module doc names a consumer that does not exist and the doc was right about the intent -- the column is re-pointed at settingsField rather than the control being deleted, so the descriptor route becomes the control's real caller. BLOCKED ON A CONFLICT WITH THE REDESIGN'S SETTLED ARCHITECTURE, FOUND 2026-10-13 BY THE CONTROLLER, WHILE LOOKING FOR THE NEXT UNBLOCKED PIECE OF THE REDESIGN'S SIXTEENTH ACCEPTANCE ITEM -- WHICH NAMES THIS ROW AS ONE OF THE `fix` DIFFERENCES THAT DISCHARGES IT, SO THE CONFLICT IS ON THE CRITICAL PATH RATHER THAN BESIDE IT. The ruling above directs that the inspector's per-kind column be re-pointed at `settingsField`. **Measured: `settingsField()` returns an `HTMLElement`**, built from `addEventListener`, `setAttribute` and DOM nodes (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/controls/settings-field.ts`), so re-pointing a React column at it puts an imperative DOM island inside that column -- which is exactly what the redesign's Acceptance forbids ("Every editor surface is React, including chart fields ... no imperative UI island survives under a React wrapper") and where ADR-0039 draws the boundary. `4dc220c6` (2026-10-09, "a chart's fields are React views, not DOM") is the commit that deliberately removed the call sites, so **the ruling as written reverses a decision the redesign was built on rather than restoring one**. The half of the ruling that has moved is its premise: it rests on the module doc's claim that "the inspector's per-kind column mounts that same rendering", and `4dc220c6` superseded that intent. **NOT TAKEN IN EITHER DIRECTION, DELIBERATELY.** Deleting the control for a React view is not what was ruled; re-pointing the column is what was ruled but contradicts the redesign's own acceptance clause. A controller's licence covers code and architecture correctness, not the reversal of a user's design ruling, so the two readings need the user's word. Task 6.5b declined this same close on 2026-10-13 for the adjacent reason (a rendered-surface rewrite that would reverse `4dc220c6`), and Phase 6's close recorded the row open rather than resolving it. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT:** either the ruling is re-read as "the descriptor route should have a **React** owner", which makes the work a control in `selection-inspector/` and lets `settings-field.ts` retire unused; or the imperative island is accepted on purpose, in which case the Acceptance section's React clause gains a named exemption beside ADR-0033's. Either answer is small; guessing it wrong is a rendered-surface rewrite in the wrong direction. RULED 2026-10-14: THE RULING IS RE-READ AS "THE DESCRIPTOR ROUTE SHOULD HAVE A **REACT** OWNER." The work is a control in `selection-inspector/` that renders the descriptor as React, `settings-field.ts` retires unused, and `4dc220c6`'s removals stay removed — ADR-0039's boundary holds because the new owner is React rather than the imperative island the earlier reading would have put in a React column. The Acceptance section's React clause therefore needs no exemption here. Cost if this reading is wrong: a rendered-surface rewrite in the wrong direction, which is exactly what the row waited for the word on.

RULED 2026-10-15: **THE DESCRIPTOR ROUTE GETS A REACT OWNER.** The work is a control in `selection-inspector/`, and `settings-field.ts` retires with it. This reverses `4dc220c6`. **One consequence stated so it is not rediscovered:** the sixteenth acceptance item's React clause therefore stands absolute and gains **no** named exemption — ADR-0033's exemption is not extended to this case, because the case is being fixed rather than licensed.

title: The settings drawing light preview bar is the one bar no gate reads, because its ground is a gradient rather than a solid colour, so a wrong light ground passes every row
detail:
FOUND BY the task-1 review round of 2026-10-11 (finding 2, reviewed commit 6da1716a). THE RULING OPERATIVE SENTENCE IS NOW MET FOR FIVE OF SIX BARS: mockup-values.ts carries one colour row per solid-ground palette - editorial, graphite, ember, moss, plum - each reading a bar background-color in current/settings.html against the product .editor-shell-palette-swatch[data-shell-palette=...]. THE RESIDUAL IS light: its bar (current/settings.html:82) paints background:linear-gradient(145deg,#d8ebe4,#afd4d1), and no row reads it, so repainting it to any other gradient reddens nothing. WHY THAT IS NOT A GATE - the reason this is a row rather than a test: the five rows key on background-color, the light bar declares the background shorthand, lookup (mockup-values.ts:364) matches property names exactly and returns the drawing silence for a property it does not declare, colourValue (:514) answers null for a gradient, and a length comparator cannot read a colour - so a sixth row of the same shape would fail on a drawing that is currently correct. OWNER: whoever owns the drawing preview bar; the instrument is the mockup-values.ts comparator set. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either the light bar declares a solid background-color like the other five, in which case a sixth row is the same shape and the drawing becomes a worse depiction of a product whose light ground really is a gradient; or the reader grows a comparator that resolves a gradient first stop and compares it with the product --shell-backdrop, which needs a ruling on which stop of a multi-stop gradient is the ground. The second is the honest solve and is a decision, not a silent choice. NOT A DUPLICATE: vg-310 is light translucent chrome, and vg-321 (now withdrawn, archive) is the ruling this residual belongs to - its own detail already named light a backdrop gradient.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE LIGHT PALETTE'S BAR BECOMES A SOLID background-color LIKE THE OTHER FIVE. One ground per palette and one rule in the reader, so the drawing is corrected to the shape the other five already have rather than the parity reader growing a gradient comparator plus a ruling on which stop is the ground. This does not absorb vg-322, which still owns which role a palette preview ground bar depicts. MECHANISM REFUTED 2026-10-16, at Phase 20's open, by the controller: the ruling's action does not produce its own outcome. The ruling makes the DRAWING's light bar solid like the other five, but the product side is what the reader compares against, and .editor-shell-palette-swatch paints background: var(--shell-backdrop) (editor-shell.css:973-976), which under light is the gradient linear-gradient(145deg, #d8ebe4, #afd4d1) (:420's block) - so the product's computed background-color is rgba(0,0,0,0) and a colour row for light would fail on a surface that is correct, which is exactly what tests/e2e/mockup-parity.ts:437-450 already says. Making only the drawing solid therefore cannot give one rule in the reader; it moves the mismatch to the other side. The only reading that satisfies the ruling's own outcome is that the LIGHT PALETTE'S PRODUCT GROUND becomes a single solid colour and the drawing follows - and that is the one decision the ruling explicitly declined to make, in its own words rather than the parity reader growing a gradient comparator plus a ruling on which stop is the ground. So the row stays OPEN and Phase 20's Task 20.5 is not dispatched until the light palette's ground colour is decided. ONE STALE CITATION TOO: tests/e2e/mockup-parity.ts:443 cites editor-shell.css:281 for light's ground, and :281 sits inside graphite's block (graphite's selector is at :278); light's block is at :420. PARKED 2026-10-17: held at Phase 20's close on the user's word. Task 20.5's ruling asks that only the drawing be made solid, and that cannot give the "one rule in the reader" the ruling's outcome needs, because the product's light swatch paints a gradient — so only making the product's light ground solid achieves it, and that is what the ruling refuses. The row stays `open` because the defect is real and the choice is a design decision rather than a measurement.

title: DESIGN.md's front-matter `fontFamily` is owned by nothing: no CSS token declares it, `--sync` ignores it, and the design.md linter does not require it
detail:
FOUND BY the design-md final review (2026-10-11). Every one of the six typography entries in DESIGN.md's front matter carries `fontFamily: "system-ui, sans-serif"`, and nothing owns that value. `editor-shell.css`'s `@theme static` block declares no `--font-*` token -- the stack is written inline at the use sites -- so `--sync`, which reads only the `spacing`, `rounded` and `typography` groups, never compares it. And the format does not require it: a copy of DESIGN.md with every `fontFamily` line deleted lints 0 errors / 0 warnings under `@google/design.md@0.4.0`, so the spec's step-1 claim that `fontFamily` is required by the format's Typography is not borne out. The value is therefore a transcription that no gate keeps honest and no rule forbids changing -- neither a second owner of a CSS value (the front matter's other groups are locked to the CSS) nor an enforced transcription. IT IS CORRECT TODAY; it will silently lie if the UI stack changes. THE CONTROLLER'S RULING: unresolved, and closing it needs a decision rather than a patch -- either the shell gains a `--font-*` token the front matter can be synced against (making it a real transcription like spacing/rounded/typography, the same shape the rest of the front matter has), or `fontFamily` is declared `omitted` with a reason (the format's own mechanism, already used for `colors` and `components`) so its absence is documented rather than silent. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one of those two landed, with the front matter and the CSS agreeing afterwards.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE FRONT MATTER AND THE CSS AGREE, RATHER THAN fontFamily BEING DECLARED OMITTED. The shell already declares its display stack per palette (--shell-display), so the front matters fontFamily syncs against the shells default display stack: --sync compares them and the design.md linter requires the key, which makes one fact declared once instead of a field no consumer reads. COST IF WRONG: a DESIGN.md front-matter field that must be kept in step with a CSS declaration, which is exactly what --sync exists to check. MECHANISM REFUTED 2026-10-16, at Phase 20's open, by the controller: the ruling's inference does not hold. Measured at 58be6688, --shell-display is declared eight times (bare :root at :70 as the default, ui-serif Georgia Times New Roman serif; the dark base at :171 and graphite at :290 as system-ui sans-serif; :219, :343, :373, :403 and :441 as ui-serif) and its three consumers are display surfaces (:773, :1238, :1651). The six typography entries this row is about are the TEXT SCALE, and the CSS declares that scale as size and line-height only (--text-2xs through --text-xl at :498-506) with no family at all; :root's own comment at :60-68 calls the pair it holds a display face and a flatness flag. So the six entries are not a transcription of --shell-display, and syncing them against it would make the normative document declare the serif display stack as the family of six UI text steps, which the CSS does not say. TWO MECHANISMS SURVIVE AND THE CHOICE IS A DECISION ABOUT WHAT DESIGN.MD NORMATIVELY SAYS, so it is not taken here: (a) the shell gains a token for the stack those six steps actually inherit and the front matter transcribes that, which is this row's own first option; or (b) fontFamily is dropped from the six entries and --sync requires only fontSize and lineHeight, which the ruling explicitly refused. THE ROW STAYS OPEN and Phase 20's Task 20.6 is not dispatched until this is answered; the annotation is on the plan's Task 20.6. AND THE FRONT MATTER IS NOT SOURCED FROM THE CSS AT ALL, which the same reading found: DESIGN.md's own section 2 (Typography) declares the three families, the first being UI sans (the system-ui stack), Everything a person reads as language - labels, menus, headings, panel copy - and the six typography entries carry exactly that string. --shell-display is a DIFFERENT fact: the palette's display face, serif under editorial, graphite, ember, moss and plum and system-ui under light and the dark base, and section 2's table names no serif family at all. So the front matter transcribes section 2's prose rather than any CSS token, and the ruling's target is the wrong owner. THE TWO SURVIVING MECHANISMS ARE THEREFORE: (a) the shell declares a token for the UI sans stack and --sync compares the front matter against it, which also gives section 2's first family a CSS owner; or (b) the front matter stays a transcription of section 2 and the design.md linter requires the key to equal section 2's declared UI sans string, which is a prose-to-front-matter check rather than a CSS one. Neither is the mechanism the ruling names. A THIRD FINDING COMES WITH IT AND IS NOT THIS ROW'S: section 2 names no serif family while --shell-display applies one to chrome headings at three sites, so the CSS declares a face the normative table does not list - reported here rather than filed, because whether the display face belongs in section 2's table is a question about the document's own completeness. PARKED 2026-10-17: held at Phase 20's close on the user's word. Task 20.6's ruling targets `--shell-display`, which is the headings' face, while the six front-matter `typography` entries are the text scale the CSS declares as size and line-height alone — so syncing them against it would make the normative document declare the serif display stack for six UI text steps. Two mechanisms survive and what decides between them is what `DESIGN.md` normatively says about typography, which is the user's call rather than a task's.

title: The manager ownership review asked for on 2026-10-09 was deferred to plan 3's close, that condition has long passed, and its seventeen rows are still open
detail: FOUND BY THE USER on 2026-10-09, NOT on 2026-10-12 -- this row was first filed an hour ago saying the latter, and it was wrong. The correction matters because the earlier text would read as a fresh finding and duplicate the seventeen rows this work already produced. THE ORIGINAL REQUEST, 2026-10-09, in two parts. First: "Does any domain managers need some clean up? I.e. same domain ownership spread across a few managers. A domain under another manager needs to become a manager of its own. Etc". Then, an hour later: "One question I forgot to ask earlier. Maybe you've already considered it. It's the reverse direction, does any manager turned out to be too small/narrow of a concept to stand on it own and should be folded into another?" WHAT PROMPTED BOTH, in the user's words: "the fact that we now have several files crossed the 500 lines threshold". WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so nothing here is re-found. A read-only survey was run against docs/architecture/ownership.md and filed SEVENTEEN rows, vg-232 through vg-248, all 2026-10-09, all still open and none archived three days later. The user then said "File the manager issues in the backlog for now then", and the cleanup was DEFERRED to plan 3's close with the ordering recorded in STATUS.md (commit 47d47d32). vg-240 was named at the time as the row with real drift risk and the likeliest to be pulled forward. THE DEFERRAL CONDITION HAS PASSED. Plan 3 closed, and so did the whole redesign programme; the registers were never revisited, which is why the user had to re-raise this on 2026-10-12 and again to ask whether it was tracked. So this row is the DEADLINE for that deferral rather than a new finding. THE REVERSE QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED -- measured on 2026-10-09, and the answer was NO. layer-manager (68 lines), deletion-manager (62) and object-lock-manager (129) were each read in full, and each owns a decision nobody else owns: Fabric's membership trap in ownerOf; "a removal that found nothing is not a deletion"; and the transform-flag derivation including that undo revives a locked object at Fabric's defaults. error-manager is 59 lines with 13 importers, a service by nature. That read instead surfaced the INVERSE defect, filed as vg-247: the locked predicate has no owner, so object.get("locked") is read in eleven non-test places across eight modules in two polarities. THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT THE LINE COUNT, and the survey said so at the time. ownership.md carries its own test: for each row, find the code that would reject a wrong value for that concept -- the guard, the validator, the refuse -- and ask whether it lives in the module the map names. A guard in an unnamed module is a missing row or a wrong owner. That is what found vg-232 through vg-246; a line count never would have. THE SIZE MEASUREMENT, for reference and NOT as the criterion. On 2026-10-09 it was 35 source files over the 500 signal and 15 over the 800 stop out of 264; at HEAD on 2026-10-12 it is 32 and 12, so it has improved slightly. snap-manager remains the largest single domain at eight files and roughly 7,000 lines, of which five files are past 500 and four past the stop. font-trios.generated.ts at 28,284 lines is GENERATED and exempt, and editor-shell.css at 2559 already belongs to vg-274. CARRIED BY the dead-code sweep plan as Phase 4, Tasks 8 and 9, which now name the guard instrument, the passed deferral and the answered reverse question rather than treating any of them as open. SIZE CORRECTED BY THE CENSUS (2026-10-12): this row said snap-manager was "eight files and roughly 7,000 lines, of which five files are past 500 and four past the stop". docs/architecture/manager-census.md measured 30 non-test files, four of them past the 800 stop. The size is not the finding and not the fix, and this row cites the census's FILE counts rather than its line totals: a top-level and a recursive count differ by more than a factor of two in that directory, and a line total depends on whether a file's trailing newline is counted as a line, so two figures can both look authoritative while measuring different things. The census also demotes snap-manager to LAST of ten candidates: one external production module reaches it (editor-session.ts, established from the code by the census review), so its fix is a protocol re-shape needing a spec, not an extraction.

title: The authored box's minimum dimension is decided in two places, and consolidating the writers applied one of them to the resize path
detail: FOUND BY Task 9 candidate rank 4's review (2026-10-12). Commit dd7c3365 moved the three writers of yunariText.box onto writeAuthoredBoxDimension, and the owner's `value < 1` / non-finite refusal (authored-box.ts:203, pre-existing, deliberate and documented there) now applies on the text-manager resize path, which previously wrote unconditionally. THE DELTA: a resize whose `target.width * scaleX` falls below 1 now returns without writing, so the authored box keeps its previous width while Fabric's width moves -- a silent no-op rather than a visible refusal. Reachability is NOT ESTABLISHED: it needs a text object carrying a non-1 scaleX, because Fabric floors its own width at 1 and only the scale can push the product under; the review derived that from vendored Fabric 7.4.0 and the editor's resize controllers but did not execute it, and no test fires the sub-unit input -- text-manager's resize specs run at scaleX 1 and widths 170-120. THE SECOND SITE: selection-inspector's funnel floors the same dimension with MIN_DIMENSION = 1 (index.ts:272, per-kind-column.ts:281), which serves all geometry and so cannot simply move to the text owner. The two floors agree today and neither is wrong; the open question is which site owns the box's minimum, and whether `< 1` is the right floor for a path a user drags. One browser check settles it together with vg-233 -- scale a text object, drag a side handle, compare yunariText.box.width against width * scaleX. SEVERITY: low, because the affected input class is a text object under about two scene units wide. MEASURED 2026-10-12 (Task 2.1, the one browser check this row asked for), in editor.spec.ts's 'resizes a scaled text by its side handle, and reopens the box it wrote': the starter wordmark is scaled to scaleX 0.7432 by a real corner drag and its mr handle is then dragged to a scene x of left + 0.4 -- a requested rendered width under one unit. THE REFUSAL DID NOT FIRE AND THE BOX WAS NOT SKIPPED: the box was written 460 -> 26.485, and the edge landed at a rendered width of 20.427 (Fabric width 26.485), so no sub-unit width was ever produced for the value < 1 guard to refuse. The drag's landing is 20.0 scene units away from where the pointer asked to put it (62.4 units on the widened drag that follows it, in the same case). RE-RUN 2026-10-12 after commit 6cec8acf fixed the resize path's stored units (it now writes the box unscaled): the same sub-unit drag writes 460 -> 35.637 and lands at a rendered width of 27.228 -- the pre-fix numbers times 1/scaleX -- so a sub-unit width is STILL never produced and the refusal is still not reached, now 26.8 units from the ask, and the widened drag that follows lands within 1.31 units. REACHABILITY IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and the 'silent no-op' this row describes is not reproduced. The landing-versus-request disagreement is filed as vg-393; this row's own question -- which site owns the box minimum -- is untouched by the run and stays open on it.

title: An in-app store where authors submit themes and anyone can browse and download them
detail:
RAISED BY THE USER on 2026-10-12 as a brainstorming exercise: not accepted work, and the user does not intend to start it soon. DESIGN RECORD: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md, Status draft. SHAPE AGREED IN CONVERSATION: GitHub is the whole backend, so nothing is run and nothing is paid for. The catalogue is item.json files in one public repo; identity is the author's GitHub account reused for everything; a submission is a pull request; the review instrument is the diff, which a theme being JSON makes readable; merging lists the item; a login added to a verified-authors list makes that author's own PRs auto-merge, and that auto-merge must be scoped to the author's own catalogue path or one compromised account rewrites the store's CI; media rides on release assets, which carries a native download_count. THE EXCHANGE UNIT ALREADY EXISTS, which is why this is small: §139, ADR-0004 and 0017 fix the validated package ZIP as the portable artifact, §141 fixes validation, and host/src/themes/store.ts already enforces 32 MiB per asset and 128 MiB total, on save and on load, so the store defines no format, no validator and no size policy. IDENTITY IS SKIPPABLE: browsing is a static index.json and downloads are plain URLs, so neither needs a token nor an API call, favorite COUNTS still render anonymously because the Action bakes them into index.json, and sign-in is a just-in-time prompt on the heart only. VIEWS ARE DROPPED: GitHub exposes no free per-item view count, so 'most viewed' is not a sort and sorting is created, updated, downloads and favorites. MEDIA: video is expected to be common and rides inside the package, so an unbounded video is what would break a zero-cost host; the existing size cap needs a companion duration cap (proposed 30s) and resolution ceiling (proposed 1920 long edge) or an author cannot predict the outcome, and a publish-time normalizer holds the envelope. OPEN, each needing a decision rather than a patch: hosting the bytes (release assets versus an object store with zero egress), the ffmpeg source for the normalizer (a probed system binary versus a bundled static build carrying GPL parts such as x264), index.json freshness, who inspects imagery for moderation, and removal semantics. UNVERIFIED: every free-tier limit the design leans on, listed in the spec, because a false one changes the architecture. NAMING: the owner ruled on 2026-10-12 that the existing editor-to-phone publish route is renamed so the store owns the word; 'activate' was the suggestion but collides with keyboard-activation in editor/src/viewport-manager/navigation.ts, cast and go-live are the clear candidates, and the rename is a family spanning the route, the published store in host/src/server.ts (a watched path) and publish-loop.spec.ts, so it can land alone before any store work. WIDGETS ARE OUT OF SCOPE: widget packages do not exist yet because §139 defers them until they have an authoring workflow, so the widget store needs its own spec.

RULED 2026-10-15: **SCHEDULED AHEAD OF THE TRIAGE, and it enters a phase** rather than waiting for one. The user set the order: this row and `vg-405` outrank the 95 rows no phase carries, because they are the two the user raised themselves. This one is a feature with a spec rather than a fix.

RULED 2026-10-15 (brainstorming, before the spec is revised): **THE STORE CARRIES THREE KINDS, AND THE SPEC IS SCOPED AS STOREFRONT-NOW, KINDS-FOLLOW.** The user's own words: the store should carry **dashboard themes, widget presets and editor themes**. The spec that follows covers the catalogue, the submission and review flow, identity and the client surface **kind-agnostically**, and specifies the theme package as the only kind v1 ships; widget presets and editor themes each get an addendum when their own artifact is designed. **This supersedes this row's own `WIDGETS ARE OUT OF SCOPE` sentence and the draft spec's scope line**, which both said the widget store must be a later spec that the theme spec must not pre-empt — the later spec still exists, but the storefront is now specified once for all three rather than three times. The reason the split is affordable: of the three kinds **only the dashboard theme has an exchange unit today** (ADR-0004/0017/§139/§141 plus `host/src/themes/store.ts`'s bounds), and the draft spec's leverage claim — that the store defines no format, no validator and no size policy — is true only while that is the only unit.

**A WIDGET PRESET IS A THEME ENVELOPE MINUS THE ARTBOARD**, defined by the user on 2026-10-15: a scene **subtree** plus its `bindings`, `globals` and `assets`, and no artboard. That is deliberately larger than the alternative reading (a subtree plus bindings alone) and it is the cheaper one, because it reuses the envelope's own sections and therefore its validator and its bounds rather than inventing a second format for a second kind. `card-library.ts`'s insertable cards are the authoring-side precedent — one Fabric `Group` over its parts, with readings in the envelope's `bindings` and a `provenance` key — and §139 still defers widget packages until an authoring workflow exists, which is what the addendum waits on.

**AN EDITOR THEME HAS NO ARTIFACT AT ALL TODAY, and that is a design decision rather than a gap:** §35 states that editor-shell theming is separate from authored dashboard theme globals, so an editor theme is a token set for the editor chrome, not a scene. Its addendum therefore has to settle what the artifact is before the store can carry it, and nothing about the dashboard theme's package shape answers that.

RULED 2026-10-17 (six decisions from the spec review): **THE STORE INTERFACE SHOWS ONLINE AND LOCAL THEMES TOGETHER**, and the spec revision is arranged around that. (1) One surface for the catalogue's online themes and the local ones — made here or imported offline. (2) IMPORT LANDS IN THE LIBRARY: a new host route writes a package into the theme library, so the local list is exactly the library; the host validates with `readThemePackage` because it owns the folder; the id is the envelope's own when valid and free, else name-derived, else suffixed, and import never overwrites. (3) THE TWO HALVES ARE TABS — local and online; a downloaded theme is a local theme, so the two views of one fact are never on screen together, and that cost is accepted. (4) THE THIRD MODE IS THIS PC: devices, display and theme questions rebuilt in the shell, with its Themes section and `library.html`'s activate job moving to the store's local tab, so one surface owns the theme list; `Editor Settings` keeps the editor's chrome, the two names no longer conflict because the subjects are disjoint, and `settings.html` and `library.html` stay served for a browser with no editor open. (5) ACTIVATION IS PER-DISPLAY FROM THE START, so `active-theme.json` becomes a per-display map and `/api/themes/active` changes shape with it rather than being built single-theme and reworked. (6) PER-DISPLAY ASSIGNMENT IS ITS OWN SPEC AND LANDS FIRST; the store consumes its assign action. **THE THREE-MODE TOP BAR IS FOLDED INTO THIS SPEC**, superseding the 2026-10-15 ruling that it needs its own spec. **NEW OWNER: INSTALL PROVENANCE** — nothing links a library folder to the catalogue item it came from, so `theme-origins.json` in consumer state beside `active-theme.json` and `theme-answers.json`, keyed by library id and swept on removal, is what lets the surface say Installed and offer an update; deliberately not a stamp inside `theme.json`, which would change the exchange unit, the validator and the package. **CLOSURE CONDITION CHANGED:** the row closes on the storefront plus the dashboard theme, not on all three kinds as Phase 24's acceptance says; the two addenda become their own rows. The spec now carries an acceptance section and a six-phase landing order, A (shell plus local tab) through F (media caps). RULED 2026-10-17, SECOND PASS (two more decisions from the spec review, both the user's). **THE STORE IS SEARCHABLE AND FILTERABLE BY FOUR FACETS** — author, colour mode, the sensors a theme reads, and author-declared style tags. Three are DERIVED from the document, not authored: author from `metadata.author`, which `ThemeStoreEntry` already carries via `entryFor`; colour mode from the artboard's resolved `PalettePaint` (a solid by its own relative luminance, a gradient by the mean of its stops, `backgroundMedia` or a mid-band luminance unclassified, and unclassified themes stay reachable under any); sensors from `bindings[*][*].semanticKey`, labelled by `describeSemanticKey`'s own descriptor, which is the same source `requiredDeviceGroups` reads for its different question. Style tags are the ONE addition to the theme format: `metadata.tags`, a CONTROLLED list owned in renderer-core's theme modules beside `bleed.ts` and `glass.ts` and mirrored into the schema and `envelope-keys.ts`, authored in `panes/document/metadata-fields.tsx`, up to five per theme. Free text was rejected because a facet that cannot be enumerated is not a facet: sci-fi, scifi and science fiction would arrive as three tags with one theme each. Consequence named rather than discovered: `metadata` is `additionalProperties: false`, so a build older than this one refuses a tagged theme as an unknown field; v2 gains the field with no version bump, and the outcome to avoid is a tagged theme reported as corrupt. **Within a facet the values OR and across facets they AND, EXCEPT sensors, which AND** — the user's own example (show all themes that have CPU and GPU usage) is one selection that must not return a CPU-only theme. **NEW OWNER: THE FACET RECORD** — one derivation in renderer-core, the only Fabric/DOM-free layer both producers can import, called by the host for a library theme and by the catalogue's Action for a merged one; never authored, never stored in `theme.json`, and `index.json` carries it per item so the author's `item.json` does not. **THE STORE IS A GALLERY GRID, PAGED** — the grid replaces the row list in both halves rather than being a second view of it; paging is client-side because the local half is a folder and the online half is one static `index.json` fetched whole, with sharding `index.json` named as the upgrade path; the pager is a composition of §5's icon buttons and a mono readout around a per-page well; the page size persists in the shell's localStorage on the `editor-shell/palette.ts` precedent, while the filter and the sort are a query and do not; a changed filter returns to page one. **NEW PHASE G** carries the tag vocabulary, its editor control and the Style facet; it needs only A and lands before C so the first generated `index.json` already carries tags. **NEW OPEN QUESTION 7** is the vocabulary's contents, which the user's examples seed but do not settle. **DESIGN.md §5 grows ONE control** — a checkbox choice row, since rule 7 describes a radio group — and nothing else, because the facet button, the cell, the pager and the per-page well are all compositions of vocabulary §5 already names. RULED 2026-10-17, THIRD PASS (five more from the spec review, all the user's). **STYLE TAGS ARE LOWERCASE, PICKED RATHER THAN TYPED, AND THE FORMAT VALIDATES SHAPE RATHER THAN MEMBERSHIP** — this SUPERSEDES the second pass's sentence that the vocabulary is owned in renderer-core and mirrored into the schema and envelope-keys.ts, and its phrase a CONTROLLED list. A tag is `[a-z0-9-]`, one to twenty-four characters, at most five per theme, and there is NO enum, because a tag the vocabulary does not yet know has to be writable before the vocabulary can grow to include it. The author chooses from the tags that already exist; a new one is proposed only when nothing fits, and the submission carries the proposal and the theme that uses it in one diff, so the reviewer approves the word and its first use together — the only review that can catch a near-synonym. The Style facet enumerates the tags present in the catalogue, so the vocabulary IS the catalogue's own content and no second file can fall out of step with it. Cost named rather than discovered: a theme may carry a tag whose count is one. **NEW FACET: SHAPE** — orientation, aspect ratio and pixel size, three readings of `artboard.width` and `artboard.height`, so nothing new is authored. Orientation is landscape, portrait or square by exact comparison. Aspect ratio is bucketed to a published set by log-ratio distance, and a theme further than the tolerance from every bucket is `Other` rather than the nearest wrong bucket. Pixel size is exact, and the facet offers only the sizes more than one theme declares, with the rest under `Other` and the exact size on the modal. **SHAPE AND SENSORS ARE AND WITHIN THE FACET; AUTHOR, COLOUR MODE AND STYLE ARE OR** — the second pass said sensors was the only exception and shape is the second; inside Shape the three groups are AND with each other and OR within themselves. **THE GRID IS RESPONSIVE BY CSS, NOT BY BREAKPOINTS** — `auto-fill` with a content-derived 240px minimum and no invented breakpoints, because §7.8 binds (measure at the real width, reduce columns only for an observed overflow) and §7.7's proof is 1280x720, 1440x900 and 200% zoom; the phone layout stays `vg-172`'s recorded limitation and is not claimed here. The one non-automatic decision is that the facet row wraps rather than dropping a control. **THE PAGER IS NUMBERED** — a step back, the five pages nearest the current one, a step forward, first and last always reachable, an ellipsis for what is skipped, and seven pages or fewer showing them all. The current page takes the same chosen treatment as every other chosen thing in this store (raised background, `--text` numeral) and never an accent fill. **RULING 9: AN ITEM OPENS A DETAIL MODAL** — one modal for every kind, since `kind` is already the seam; elevation level 3 like the settings modal; it holds the preview at the theme's own ratio (the one place a portrait artboard is uncropped, which is what makes `Other` acceptable in Shape), the description, the derived facets spelled out, the tags, the counts and state, and the same commands the cell offers — one command reached two ways rather than two owners. Closing it restores the page, the filter and the sort unchanged. **NEW OPEN QUESTION 8** is the aspect-ratio bucket set and its tolerance, which nobody has measured. Drawings: the store mode is four files — the two galleries redrawn, plus `store-facets.html` (Shape open, three groups, `Other`) and `store-detail.html` (the modal). **FOURTH PASS, same day, two more items from the user.** (a) **The cell is one box and both halves use it** — same width, same height, one anatomy stated once: the picture at `aspect-ratio:2/1`, the name, the author, a 26px facts band, a 10px inset. The badge moves into the facts band because beside the name it would make the two halves’ cells different heights. The minimum is **272px**, derived from the online half’s busiest band and rounded up to a multiple of 8 — derived rather than picked, since a minimum chosen for the local half alone is a grid that overflows the moment the catalogue’s cells arrive in it. (b) **RULING 9 IS AMENDED: the modal is a viewer, not a two-column panel.** It is **960px** wide against the settings modal’s 560; the preview is a **fixed stage** the theme is *contained* in, letterboxed against a ground darker than the modal — which **SUPERSEDES “the preview at the theme’s own ratio”**, because a stage sized to the theme makes the modal change height as a person steps between themes. The facts are **pills in three groups (Reads, Shape, Style) under §2’s eyebrow**, which SUPERSEDES “the derived facets spelled out” as one 30px row per fact; a proposed tag says so on its own pill; the name, the author and the kind are one caption line carrying the version and the change date, with **no title bar** — the close control floats over the stage’s corner; and the actions are written in words because a footer has the room and the glyph was only ever a space saving. **No accent fill in that footer**: none of the four verbs is *the* act, and Delete is `--hot` text. Drawings: `store-detail.html` redrawn as the viewer, and both galleries now draw the one shared cell. Spec sections rewritten: “The gallery, and paging” and “The item’s own surface”, which also gains the version, the change date and the provenance line. **FIFTH PASS, 2026-10-18.** **RULING 10: THE ITEM KIND IS AN EXTENSION POINT.** The user asked that the store architecture be expandable, since more kinds may arrive. New spec section “Adding a kind, and what keeps it cheap”, and five things the first kind must leave open: (1) **the wire value and the display word are different** — `item.json`’s `kind` is a stable identifier (`dashboard-theme`, `widget-preset`) and the badge reads `uiCopy`’s word, so an older client still has something true to print, which is why the skipped-kind line quotes the identifier; (2) **one handler table per kind, and the missing row IS the degradation rule** — written as a lookup rather than a branch so a second row is data; (3) **a kind gets its own store, not a `kind` field on this one** — `host/src/themes/store.ts` is the *theme* store, one file name and one validator, and `readStoredOrAbsent` answers a non-theme folder as **absent**, so a second kind under that root would be omitted from `list()` silently rather than refused; `createThemeStore(directory)` already takes its directory, so a kind is a second call, and the local half reads through the set of registered stores — **that one hop is the ruling’s whole cost at phase A**; (4) **the facets a kind has are its own and the ones it lacks are absent, not defaulted** — a widget preset has no artboard, so no orientation, ratio, size or derivable colour mode, and it matches no selection in them, the rule the sensors facet already carries; (5) **`item.json` splits into a storefront-owned header (id, kind, name, author, version, dates, counts, thumbnail, facet record) and a kind-owned body the storefront never reads into.** It designs no second kind and no second format: open question 6 still owns the two addenda. Phase A’s acceptance line gains the kind-source clause, and ruling 9’s own text is amended in place to the fixed stage, which the fourth pass had left stale. Drawing: `store-browse.html`’s skipped-kind line now quotes `widget-preset` rather than a display word.

title: Escape out of a layer rename drops focus to the document body, so a keyboard author loses their place
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4'S REVIEW of the keyboard walkthrough plan (2026-10-12), MEASURED rather than read: the reviewer's probe on the committed bytes printed `PROBE-AFTER-ESCAPE BODY|`, where the walk expected to still be on the row it was renaming. WHAT: with a composition row's rename field focused, Escape cancels the draft and the field unmounts, and focus is left on `document.body` -- nothing returns it to the row. The next Tab therefore restarts from the top of the document instead of continuing from the author's place. WHY IT MATTERS: section 13.1's keyboard-only walkthrough requires focus to be where an interaction left it, and this is the one sub-step in the assembled walk where it is not; the helper that drives it re-tabs from the document root under a bounded press count, which works and is not the behaviour a keyboard user gets to rely on. It is NOT in the assembled §13.1 walk: that walk's field interaction is the inspector's ControlText, whose Escape leaves focus in the field, and the rename cancel lives in the plan's separate Task 4 test. WHAT IT COSTS the plan that found it: the walk is less continuous there than it reads, and Task 5 must not assume it resumes in place -- recorded in that plan's ledger. NOT FIXED THERE ON PURPOSE: the walkthrough plan's Out of scope reads "No new focus management. If a region is unreachable, this plan records it; changing the shell's focus order is its own change with its own spec." A register row is that record. OWNER: whoever owns the composition row's own focus -- the rename field is opened by Enter or F2 on a treeitem and is unmounted by the cancel without a focus return. WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT SHOW: whether the same cancel-by-Escape inside a settings row or a dialog does the same; only the composition row was driven.

title: Two plans' parity comparisons no longer exist, and the acceptance item that requires them has no wording for that
detail:
FOUND BY the counted acceptance pass of 2026-10-12, which walked every item of the design-language spec's Acceptance section and found this the only one not discharged. WHAT: that section's last item requires every plan's parity capture to exist beside its mockup in docs/design/mockups/ with every difference either fixed or backed by a cited rule. Plans 6, 7 and 8 have captures (shell-capture-add.png, shell-capture-graphite.png, shell-capture-glyphs.png beside shell.html; settings-capture-graphite.png and settings-capture-editorial.png beside settings.html, registered in docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md). Plans 1 and 3 do not: current/controls.html and current/controls-light.html have no capture beside them, no .superpowers/sdd/ workspace survives for either plan, and the archived acceptance ledger in docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy.md records in its own words that Plan 1's ten differences no longer exist anywhere. WHY IT MATTERS: the item cannot be met or refused as written, because for those two plans the thing it asks to be checked is gone; the verdict the archived ledger records for the item (met) was taken on the capture half only and never addressed this half. WHAT IT NEEDS: a decision rather than code -- either reproduce the comparison from each capture and the commit body that carried it, or narrow the item's wording to the plans whose reports survive. OWNER: whoever owns the spec's Acceptance text; the item is the spec's, so the decision is the user's. WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT SHOW: whether any of plan 1's or 3's differences were in fact fixed later under another plan's name; only that no record of the comparison survives to establish it. THE CAPTURE HALF IS NOW PLACED FOR EVERY DRAWING, MEASURED 2026-10-13, WHICH CHANGES WHAT THIS ROW OWNS BUT NOT WHAT IT ASKS. The paragraph above said `current/controls.html` and `current/controls-light.html` have no capture beside them; they do now. `controls-capture-graphite.png` and `controls-capture-editorial.png` sit beside those two drawings (`988d1788`), placed from the registered action `the control set renders in the design language` (`captureVisualReview(page, testInfo, "control-set")`, `design-language.spec.ts:1410`) and registered in `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md`. **And the same pass closed the modal's third sheet**: `settings-keyboard.html` and `settings-about.html` had no capture either, though the one action already photographs all three tabs, so `settings-keyboard-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` and `settings-about-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` were added beside their drawings and the existing two were re-shot, because the committed six were taken 2026-10-11 (`f7078e93`) and the dialog moved under them on 2026-10-13 (`69e6e7f1`'s `dl > div` padding, `7a92d0fe`'s dialog section-2 body role) — the Appearance and About renders are now 2px shorter and the Keyboard render 6px narrower than the committed bytes (`e412c98d`). **So as of `e412c98d` every drawing in `docs/design/mockups/current/` has a capture pair beside it** — six drawings, twelve PNGs — and the first half of the acceptance item is met for every plan whose matching mockup is one of them. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, AND IT IS THE ROW'S ACTUAL SUBJECT.** The item says *each plan's* completion report carries *its* capture, and the prose attributes captures to plans 1, 3 (`988d1788`), 6 (`shell-capture-glyphs.png`), 7 (the shell pair) and 8 (the three settings pairs). **No durable record names a capture for plans 2, 4 or 5** — their completion reports died with their `.superpowers/sdd/` workspaces, and the register holds no row for it. Whether their captures were the shell and settings images already beside those drawings, or were never distinct, is not recorded anywhere this repository keeps. **WHAT IT NEEDS IS UNCHANGED**: a decision rather than code — either reproduce plan 1's and plan 3's comparisons from each capture and the commit body that carried it, or narrow the item's wording to the plans whose reports survive, and settle whether plans 2, 4 and 5 are inside that wording at all. NEAR ROWS: `vg-436` (the `controls-light.html` naming question, which this row's own paragraph names by that filename); `vg-434` (references that resolve to nothing); `vg-316`, `vg-319` (the open `fix` differences that keep the item's second clause unmet regardless of the capture half). THE OPEN QUESTION THIS ROW NAMED IS NOW ANSWERED, 2026-10-13: the row said "whether their captures were the shell and settings images already beside those drawings, or were never distinct, is not recorded anywhere this repository keeps". **They were, and the mapping is now recorded.** **THE PLANS, FROM THE SPEC'S OWN TABLE** (`2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md:396-405`): 1 the control set, 2 the shell and rail, 3 the inspector, 4 the panes, 5 settings and appearance, 6 iconography and copy, 7 shell parity, 8 settings parity. **WHAT EACH DRAWING ANSWERS FOR.** `controls.html` and `controls-light.html` draw plan 1's set, which plan 3's column is built on. `shell.html` draws plans 2, 3 and 7 at once: its Position, Paint and Spends sections are the inspector's (`grep` finds those words in it and finds Composition, Tokens and Document in no drawing at all), and it is the drawing both parity plans were pulled to. The three settings sheets draw plans 5 and 8. **SO THE CAPTURES EXIST FOR PLANS 2, 4 AND 5, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ROW COULD NOT ESTABLISH.** Plan 2's surfaces are `shell-capture-graphite.png`; plan 4's Add pane is `shell-capture-add.png`, and its other three panes are the `pane-composition`, `pane-tokens` and `pane-document` files in `docs/evidence/screenshots/`, which sit beside no drawing because no drawing draws them; plan 5's surfaces are the six settings files. Plan 6's glyph work has no drawing of its own either, and `shell-capture-glyphs.png` is its evidence. **WHY THE RECORD READ AS IF THEY DID NOT EXIST.** `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md` already carries drawing-adjacent passages, and they name plans **1, 3, 6, 7 and 8**. Plans 2, 4 and 5 are named in none of them, so a reader pairing captures to plans finds those three absent and concludes the evidence is gone. **That paragraph is now written**: the README records which surfaces each of the six drawings and their eleven captures show, explicitly not as a claim that a plan's own report names its capture. **WHAT THE RULING THEREFORE TURNS ON, WHICH IS NARROWER THAN THE ROW FIRST PUT IT.** It is not "reproduce plan 1's and plan 3's comparisons or narrow the item", although plans 1 and 3's own comparisons are still gone with their workspaces. It is **whether the item counts a capture that shows a plan's surfaces when the durable record attaches that capture to a later parity plan instead** — the situation for plans 2, 4 and 5, whose surfaces are photographed and drawn but whose own reports never named the image. Plan 4's three undrawn panes and plan 6's missing drawing are the residue the item still cannot reach at all: for those, there is no matching mockup to carry a capture beside. THE WORDING QUESTION HAS A NORMATIVE RULE ON ONE SIDE, FOUND 2026-10-13: `docs/design/mockups/README.md` is not only a description of the set -- it carries a rule for keeping it current, under **Keeping them current**: "**The current files are refreshed when the set of surfaces changes.** A pane, a tab, a section or a rail slot that appears or disappears is drawn -- in the original's treatment, never in a treatment of the product's devising." **So the undrawn panes are not merely unreachable; the drawings' own rule requires them to have been drawn.** Composition, Tokens and Document are shipped panes and they are named in no drawing (`shell.html` draws the shell and the Add pane, and the three panes' captures sit beside nothing). Scope stated exactly: that sentence names a pane, a tab, a section and a rail slot, so it binds plan 4's three panes and **does not** bind plan 6's glyph sheet, which is not one of the four things the sentence lists. **What that makes the decision.** The item's residue for plans 4 and 6 is not "narrow the wording or leave it open" but a three-way choice the repository's own documents frame: (a) draw the three panes, per the README's rule and in the originals' treatment, and the captures then have a matching mockup to sit beside -- the item's second clause becomes reachable for them; (b) narrow the item to the drawings that exist, on the reading that the acceptance instrument is the six current files and the README's refresh rule is a maintenance duty rather than an acceptance one; or (c) leave both as they are and carry the residue. **And (a) is deliberately not taken by this session**, because a drawing is the acceptance instrument rather than a description of one: the README's own warning is that a mockup which no longer matches is worse than none because it is believed, and the user's ruling of 2026-10-10 made the drawing the target the product is pulled to. Authoring three new targets is the ruling owner's act, not a session's. **Verified beside it, so the capture half is not doubted later**: `docs/design/mockups/current/` holds six drawings (`shell.html`, `settings.html`, `settings-keyboard.html`, `settings-about.html`, `controls.html`, `controls-light.html`) and eleven captures -- `shell-capture-graphite/add/glyphs`, `controls-capture-{graphite,editorial}`, and a pair for each of the three settings panels -- so every current drawing carries a capture. The two unpaired PNGs a reader might expect to have drawings, `inspector-controls.html` and `inspector-language.html`, are **originals**: the README freezes them as "the record of the first cut, not the target", so no capture is required beside them and their absence is correct rather than a gap. THE SECOND CLAUSE'S RESIDUE IS EVERY PLAN'S, MEASURED ACROSS ALL EIGHT ON 2026-10-13, AND IT IS NOT THREE ROWS. The spec's discharge paragraph counts plan 8's three, which is right for plan 8 and understates the clause, because the clause reads "every plan's parity capture ... every difference it lists". Walked plan by plan, five of the eight list a difference whose owner is an open row today, and plan 1's ten have no owner recorded at all. PLAN 1 (the control set) - ten, OWNER UNKNOWN: `1f991845`'s body is the only trace ("Ten differences are listed in the task report"), and `docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy.md:759-768` records that they "no longer exist anywhere". PLAN 2 (the shell and the rail) - four: its 25-row table (`archive/2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail.md:731-757`) puts rows 7, 17, 18 and 22 on `vg-227`, `vg-222`, `vg-225` and `vg-230`, and rows 19, 24, 25 name `vg-231`, `vg-217` and `vg-226`, all `verified`; nine further rows are adjudicated "deliberate, deferred to a later plan" (plans 3, 4, 5), which is a claim about those plans and not a row state. PLAN 3 (the inspector) - none: its four differences survive in `9ee1fc21`'s body, each owned by a drawing, a cited section rule or that commit, and the one item its report called a difference is withdrawn there as a parity match. PLAN 4 (the panes) - five: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-the-panes/task-12-report.md:62-136` numbers 32 entries and puts four on `vg-269`, `vg-260`, `vg-265` and `vg-270`, and one (`vg-230`) on a shell-level row added in fix round 1. PLAN 5 (settings and appearance) - none: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/task-6-report.md:339-371` lists eleven differences, ten recorded deliberate and one fixed in-plan. PLAN 6 (iconography and copy) - none: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy/task-9-report.md:127-150` lists eleven, one fixed in-plan and one "no difference". PLAN 7 (shell parity) - two open among its own `fix` rows: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/adjudication.md:58` and `:92-97` name A11 `vg-217` (verified), A12 `vg-230` and A17 `vg-222` among the `fix` rows another owner holds, and hand 13 more to the next plan; its residual list (`task-7-report.md:205-219`) names `vg-308`, `vg-310` and `vg-274`. PLAN 8 (settings parity) - three: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-11-settings-parity/adjudication.md:82-102` numbers 19 rows and its row 19 is the Close, owned by `vg-316`; `vg-319` and `vg-322` sit in the spec's list beside it. THE DISTINCT OPEN OWNERS: `vg-222`, `vg-223`, `vg-225`, `vg-227`, `vg-228`, `vg-230`, `vg-260`, `vg-265`, `vg-269`, `vg-270`, `vg-316`, `vg-319` and `vg-322`, with `vg-308`, `vg-310` and `vg-274` from plan 7's residual list. Every one was read as `state: open` in `docs/product/backlog.jsonl` on 2026-10-13, parsed line by line, and none appears in the archive; `vg-223` and `vg-228` are the two plan 2 files as owned elsewhere rather than visible in its captures. `vg-254` is open in the same neighbourhood but its plan files it as a `Discovered, not fixed` item rather than a drawing difference, so it is not counted. AND EVERY ONE OF THOSE ROWS IS A ROW THE ACTIVE DRAIN'S PHASE 1 SESSIONS TAKE - `vg-222`, `vg-223`, `vg-225` and `vg-227` in D3; `vg-228` and `vg-274` in D5, already ruled 2026-10-12; `vg-260` in D6; `vg-230` in D10; and the browser-pinned `vg-308`, `vg-310`, `vg-319`, `vg-265` and `vg-270` in the Phase 1 follow-up session at Task 2.5 Step 4 - EXCEPT TWO: `vg-316`, which Phase 2 ran in Task 2.4 and could not close because what it needs is a DESIGN.md decision (`vg-441`), and plan 1's ten, which no row carries. WHAT THAT DOES TO THIS ROW'S ASK: the wording decision is still the user's, and it is now ORDERED rather than parallel - the item's second clause cannot be met before the drain's Phase 1 ruling sessions run, and the plans 1-3 narrowing is the one half no other plan will move. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether plan 2's nine "deferred to a later plan" adjudications were in fact discharged by plans 3, 4 and 5 - the later plans changed the shell and the modal materially and plan 2's own report is optimistic on several, but those owners are named as plans and not as rows, so no row state can settle it. BOTH HALVES OF THIS ROW WERE RE-MEASURED ON 2026-10-13, AND THE PROSE ABOVE IS NOW HISTORY RATHER THAN A GAP. FIRST, PLAN 1'S COMPARISON IS RE-MADE. Its ten differences are still gone, but its drawing and its capture are both current, so a read-only census re-derived the comparison from `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html` and the shipped control set (brief `dispatch-a658c22eac7f428fd.md`, drain workspace; read-only, no file touched). Only two checks against that drawing survive in the tree at all — `tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:913-934` (two `PARITY` rows reading the label column's width) and `design-language.spec.ts:2540-2552` (two `productRows` reading the plain-DOM button box's padding against `controls.html:112`). The re-made census places every drawn element in one of four classes. IMPLEMENTED: the field row's 74px label column and `flex:1` cell, the well's `--panel-2` fill with a 1px `--edge` and `--radius-md`, the slider's 36px well with its 3px accent track, the refusal line under the toggle, and the plain-DOM boxes' 12px control text (the D9 fix). OWNED BY AN OPEN ROW: the well's horizontal padding (`vg-202`, three-way between product 6px, drawing 8px and §3's 4px) and the segmented control's whole treatment (`vg-301`). RULE-BACKED, i.e. the DRAWING is the stale side and no work exists: seven differences where a cited § clause requires what the product already does — the eyebrow's colour (`controls.html:29` draws `--faint`, §2 (`DESIGN.md:144-147`) makes an eyebrow muted), the field row's label-to-value gap (`:36` draws 10px, §3's step table gives 8 between a label and its control), the select value's family (drawn `system-ui`, §2 makes values mono), the chevron mark (§5's well-with-chevron entry specifies a `▼` in `--faint`), the slider's track and thumb radius (drawn 2px and a circle, neither on §3's radius ladder), the toggle's resting boundary (§5 rule 6 brightens the toggle's border), and the read-only row's label family (`:177` draws the label in mono, §2 says labels are sans). UNOWNED: five, filed as `vg-443`, `vg-444`, `vg-445` and `vg-446` — with the honest boundary that this was a declaration-level pass and says where it cannot settle a question: a value the product inherits rather than declares, a shorthand the drawing writes that has no counterpart (the 26px row height arrives through `padding` plus a `font` shorthand, which `mockup-values.ts` refuses by design), and the drawing-local `--value` token, which has no §4 role. SECOND, PLAN 2'S TWELVE DEFERRED ADJUDICATIONS ARE NOW CHECKED AGAINST THE PRODUCT. Plan 2's table defers twelve differences to plans 3, 4 and 5 (tally at `archive/2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail.md:768-771`). NINE LANDED, each verified in the product rather than in the later plan's report: the pane re-cut to 246px (`editor-shell.css:988`, `7bdd4ea0`), the header palette chip's move into Settings (`64fea389`), the printed `⌘⇧P` (`shortcut-manager/index.ts:77`, `3fe3f22e`), the rail-foot settings gear (`rail.tsx:85-102`, `13984ab9`), the Add pane's diagram tiles, glyph tiles and text row (`add-pane.tsx:127`, `:171-182`, `:139`, `96099ba8`), Assets absorbed into Add (`c8dc0b1a`), and the inspector's empty state and five sections (`f1a35b82`, `cdd6ecc0`). **THREE DID NOT LAND**, and two of them are owned by no row: the Add title bar's count (`vg-269`, which plan 4 declined and filed — already one of the open owners this row lists), and the two copy differences filed as `vg-445`. **So the 'not established' sentence above is established, and what plans 1 and 2 leave in the second clause is a named list rather than an unread claim.** ONE CAVEAT THAT STANDS: the re-made census is not plan 1's own list — it is a comparison taken now, so it must be read with its method beside it, not as the ten differences the deleted report held. DISPOSITION CORRECTED 2026-10-13, because the sentence above is one step stale. It says the census's five unowned differences were "filed as `vg-443`, `vg-444`, `vg-445` and `vg-446`", which is not what happened to them. Of the five: TWO WERE FIXED rather than filed — the subject's name weight and the section count's family and colour, both already stated by the drawing (`controls.html:24`, `:30`) and required by §2's mono list and title weight and by §4's `--faint` role, landed with their red-proved browser case; ONE BELONGS TO `vg-441` — the plain-DOM control box's label colour, which is a property of the control §5's closed vocabulary does not name; and TWO ARE `vg-444` — the read-only rows' dashed dividers and the section headers' trailing rules. `vg-443` and `vg-446` are findings the census surfaced rather than members of that five: the serif family the count inherited, which a declaration-level pass could not settle and a browser then measured, and the case whose name asserts §7.4 while its assertion pins a literal that names no place. Recorded rather than left, because the earlier sentence would let a reader count four rows against five differences and conclude one was lost. ONE CENSUS ENTRY CORRECTED 2026-10-13, ON THE SAME EVIDENCE THAT CLOSED IT. The re-made plan-1 comparison called the read-only row's omitted dashed divider *unowned*; it is rule-backed — `selection-inspector/column.tsx:191-194` records the product's reason and cites it ('no well, no border, because a border means editable (DESIGN.md §5.1)'), four lines above the JSX the census read. The census read declarations and structure; a product note that states why a declaration is absent is a source it did not weigh, and that is the failure mode this correction is recorded against rather than quietly fixed. The same pass implemented the one hairline that had no such note (the section header's trailing rule), so `vg-444` closes with one half implemented and one half backed.

RULED 2026-10-15: **A CAPTURE THE REGISTER ATTACHES TO A LATER PARITY PLAN COUNTS FOR THE PLAN WHOSE SURFACES IT SHOWS.** The item is therefore met on this clause rather than narrowed: what was lost was plans 2, 4 and 5's own *reports*, and their surfaces are photographed and the captures resolve, which is what the item asks for.
