title: The inspector's write funnel is unreconciled: its writers left selection-inspector/index.ts, but the dispatch and the closure state it reads stayed behind
detail:
FOUND BY Phase 0 of the backlog drain (2026-10-12), filing the residual spec section 3.2 states for vg-255. WHAT CLOSED, AND WHY THAT LEAVES A QUESTION: vg-255's subject was a line count -- `selection-inspector/index.ts` past AGENTS.md's 800-line stop -- and its own AMENDED note already recorded that commit `3e8c9523` had taken the file back under the stop (822 -> 736) while the archived plan's own 540-line constraint still stood. The file is 707 lines today, so the close holds. THE QUESTION THE CLOSE DROPS, in that row's own words: splitting the write funnel out 'means deciding where the write path lives and how it reaches `described` and `targetRevision`, which are closure state the funnel reads at call time'. THE SPLIT HAPPENED; THE FUNNEL DID NOT MOVE WITH IT: the writes now live outside `index.ts` -- `writePanelField` and `writeShapeGeometryField` in `selection-inspector/panel.ts`, `writeGlassField` in `selection-inspector/glass.ts`, `writeMark` in `selection-inspector/bleed.ts`, and the run and binding writes in `selection-inspector/run-edits.ts` -- while the state they are asked from stayed in the closure. WHAT REMAINS UNRECORDED: the revision-and-lock refusal is `view.ts`'s `editRefusal`, read against the live target inside `createSelectionInspector`'s `edits.commit`; the dispatch that picks a writer by `fieldId` (the `panel-` and `glass-` prefixes and the shape-geometry fall-through) is that same function; and the state that makes the read correct is the closure's `let described` and `let targetRevision`, which each writer receives second-hand as an argument rather than reads. So the per-kind writers are named owners and the funnel that asks them is not, and nothing decides whether the next converted field adds another branch to `edits.commit` or moves the funnel out. `docs/architecture/ownership.md` names the writers (`panel.ts`, `glass.ts`) and the directory, and says nothing about the dispatch or the closure state. WHY IT MATTERS: it is vg-255's question one refactor later -- the file is under the stop because leaves were extracted, not because the shape was decided -- and `panel.ts` is now 751 lines, close to the same stop. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/selection-inspector/` (`createSelectionInspector` and its closure state); the decision is a design one, and `docs/architecture/ownership.md` is where a ruling would land. WHAT SETTLES IT: a recorded decision on where the write funnel lives -- in the closure, in a module of its own, or in the per-kind writers -- and how it reaches `described` and `targetRevision`. NOT A RUNTIME DEFECT: vg-255's reviewer found no behavioural problem, and none is claimed here.

PARKED 2026-10-16: the writers are out (`panel.ts`, `glass.ts`, `bleed.ts`, `run-edits.ts`) and the `fieldId` dispatch with the `let described` / `let targetRevision` closure state stayed in `selection-inspector/index.ts`. It waits on where the funnel lives — in the closure, in its own module, or in the per-kind writers — which is an ownership decision the map's `selection-inspector` rows do not settle. Parked rather than closed because the finding is real and the register's policy is that a real-but-low-value finding is parked rather than forgotten, and parked rather than left plain because the triage's job is to say what each row waits on.

title: Entering and leaving a selection inside a scaled or rotated group moves its members, so align and distribute measure a displaced scene
detail: FOUND BY THE USER (2026-10-12), reported as `Alignment and distribution inside a group is broken, they got transported to outside of the canvas`. THAT REPORT IS TWO DEFECTS, and the one below is the half the user's phrasing does not name. The other half -- a grouped selection aligned in a group whose transform is a pure translation -- is FIXED in the same commit as this row (`arrange.ts`'s `move` measured in canvas coordinates and wrote in the parent's plane, so a group's translation was applied twice; red-proved at `expected 934.5 to be close to 434.5, received difference is 500`). THIS ROW IS WHAT REMAINS, and it is not `arrange.ts`'s to fix by choosing a plane. MEASURED in jsdom (`arrange.dom.test.ts`'s sibling probe, since deleted): a `Group` of two `Rect`s at `left: 200, top: 120, scaleX: 2, scaleY: 2, angle: 30`, wrapped in a real `Canvas`, then `new ActiveSelection([a, b], { canvas })`, `canvas.setActiveObject(selection)`, `canvas.discardActiveObject()`. The anchor's `getBoundingRect().left` reads 86.051 before the selection exists and 293.678 after only the discard -- with the object's OWN state identical either side (`left: -65.5`, `top: -20.5`, `angle: 0`, `scaleX: 1`) -- so what moved is the group's own transform, not the child's. Re-selecting restores 86.051, so the pair round-trips and nothing is permanently lost; what breaks is that `applyArrange` measures and moves INSIDE that displaced window, so an align that is arithmetically correct in the state it can see lands 22.487 units out in the state the author sees (`expected 86.05067210423853, received 108.53778516388122`). WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT PART OF THE FIX: the cause is inside Fabric's `Group._enterGroup`/`_exitGroup` + `ActiveSelection` interaction for a parent whose matrix has a linear part, which is reachable from `grouping-manager` and from Fabric upstream but is not reachable from `arrange.ts`; the owner is a design decision, and the fix may be to stop discarding the selection at all. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the app reaches this state as shipped -- a pure-translation group does not, and a rotated or scaled group was NOT exercised in a browser, only in jsdom, and the browser run is what Phase 2 holds. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a browser reading of a rotated or scaled group's members before and after entering the selection (the displaced reading above), then the fix at whichever owner that establishes, with the same numbers re-taken.

title: The context menu's horizontal anchor arm allows a 2px drift where the placement it asserts is tighter than that
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 2.4a task review (2026-10-12), as observation 6 of ten, and filed rather than fixed because the fix widens an assertion that a red proof stands on. WHAT THE ARM IS: `tests/e2e/editor-context-menu.spec.ts` adds a case asserting the canvas menu opens where the pointer is, as `Math.abs(menu.popupLeft - point.x) <= ANCHOR_X_PX` with `ANCHOR_X_PX = 2` (`:108`), and a second-use arm at `:341` and `:351` asserting a second click moves the menu by the same distance. THE REVIEW'S NUMBER: it reports the measured offset as 1.4-1.8 px, leaving 0.2-0.6 px of headroom, and calls it flake risk of the `vg-141`/`vg-143` class. THAT NUMBER IS NOT REPRODUCED HERE, and the row says so rather than restating it as measured: the run reports this task left behind carry no numbers on a green run (an assertion's values appear only when it fails), so the controller could not re-derive 1.4-1.8 from any artifact on disk, and the review did not record where it read it. THE FIRST THING THIS ROW OWES IS THEREFORE THE MEASUREMENT ITSELF. WHY IT MAY MATTER ANYWAY: `ANCHOR_Y_PX` next to it is 8, and the case's own docblock says the failures it exists to catch are 'hundreds of pixels wide' -- a popup at the window's corner reads left ~ 0 -- so the arm does not need 2 px of discrimination to do its job, while a threshold that close to the placement it measures is a false red waiting for a second device pixel ratio. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: read the popup's actual placement rule (the menu's own offset, not a sample) and either widen the horizontal tolerance toward the vertical one, keeping a red proof that a corner-anchored popup still reddens the arm, or record that the 1.4-1.8 reading was wrong and the arm has real headroom. NOTE: the case's red proof was taken at `83072e99` against the 2 px threshold, so widening it invalidates that proof and it has to be re-taken -- which is why this is a row and not a drive-by edit.

PARKED 2026-10-16: the measurement the row says it is owed is **already on disk, in the spec's own docblock** (`tests/e2e/editor-context-menu.spec.ts:100-104`): "three clicks at different x put the popup's left edge 1.4–1.8px right of the click and its top a constant 5.64px above it (2026-10-12, `chromium`, 1280×1000)" — so the number is recorded, dated and attributed, and what remains is the decision rather than the reading. It waits on a tolerance decision and a re-taken red proof, and the two are one act: the case's red proof was taken at `83072e99` against the 2px bound, so widening `ANCHOR_X_PX` toward the 8px vertical invalidates it and it has to be re-taken in a browser. title: The inspector's geometry funnel refuses a non-finite value but still commits a coercible one, where the branch above it refuses an unreadable path
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 2.4b task review (2026-10-12), observation 8, while the task was adding a finiteness guard to that same branch. WHAT THE TASK DID: the Line-endpoints branch of `writeShapeGeometryField` in `selection-inspector/panel.ts` wrote `object.set(key, Number(value))` unfenced, and Task 2.4b added a `Number.isFinite` refusal, which is how `vg-376` closed. WHAT THAT DOES NOT COVER: `Number` coerces before the guard can see it, so `Number("")` is 0, `Number("  ")` is 0, `Number("0x10")` is 16 and `Number("1e5")` is 100000 -- every one finite, every one committed. The sibling branch in the same function refuses an unreadable value outright through `parsedPath`, and the React control's own `parse` refuses those four inputs too, so the funnel is the one caller that disagrees with both. WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT A DRIVE-BY FIX: whether the funnel's contract is 'a finite number' or 'a complete number' is a decision, and the two callers the funnel feeds do not agree today; guessing it would change what an author can type. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: decide the contract, then either refuse everything `ControlNumber.parse` refuses or record that the coercion is intended. NOT A LIVE REGRESSION: the guard is strictly tighter than the write it replaced, so nothing this row names was reachable only before it.

PARKED 2026-10-16: the Line-endpoints branch does `Number(value)` then `Number.isFinite`, so `""`, `" "`, `"0x10"` and `"1e5"` all commit, where the sibling `shape-path` branch refuses through `parsedPath`. title: Nothing in the repo re-shoots the captures beside the drawings, and three of the five predate the chrome weight collapse
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 2.5 OF THE BACKLOG DRAIN (2026-10-12) while re-shooting vg-341's seven, not by a failing test. WHAT: nothing in the repo re-shoots the five PNGs that sit beside the drawings in `docs/design/mockups/current/` (`shell-capture-add.png`, `shell-capture-graphite.png`, `shell-capture-glyphs.png`, `settings-capture-graphite.png`, `settings-capture-editorial.png`), and three of the five predate Task 2's weight collapse (`ef81b183`, 2026-10-11) by the test vg-341 uses - their last-touch commits are ancestors of it: `shell-capture-graphite.png` at `7efea17f`, and `settings-capture-graphite.png` and `settings-capture-editorial.png` both at `b78ee264`. THE ONE THAT IS ESTABLISHED: `shell-capture-graphite.png` is byte-identical to the pre-re-shoot `shell-palette-graphite-desktop-chromium.png` (sha1sum `1998cbf2ff05a8788687ff23d3498120bc3ef98b`), so the README route is a literal copy of the evidence frame, and when Task 2.5 re-shot the seven the evidence frame moved to sha1sum `1c0eb8ad9a469888afc64e8e0948522ff935755a` while this copy kept the old bytes - a whole-shell capture whose subject is the chrome the collapse rewrote. THE ONE THAT IS NOT: for the settings pair `b78ee264` is ancestry only. The collapse did rewrite the modal's three tab glyphs (`settings.tsx`'s `SETTINGS_TAB_GLYPHS`), but at size 14 the vocabulary's weight is 1.7 (`icons.ts`'s `glyphWeight`), the same weight the file already carried, so that hunk is not evidence their pixels moved, and neither image was read against the chrome's pixels. Stated as measured, not as established. THE README'S CLAIM: it says both drawings-adjacent shell captures are 'produced by the registered actions above' (the graphite one by `captures each palette's own surface`), but running exactly that action writes only into `docs/evidence/screenshots/` - the capture helper's default directory - and leaves the drawings-adjacent file untouched; a grep of `src/web/tests` and `scripts/` finds no writer for that name at all. So the production route the README documents is a copy step nobody wrote down, which is how the set goes stale without a run failing. NOT FIXED HERE: refreshing the three means either a manual copy of the evidence frames into the drawings directory or a capture-directory override, and which of those the parity instrument means is a decision about the drawings set (vg-390 is the neighbouring question). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: each stale capture re-shot, plus either the README's production step written down or a spec that writes the file.

MEASURED SINCE FILING, same session, on the shell pair's siblings: `shell-capture-add.png` (`f069e56c`) and `shell-capture-glyphs.png` (`f7078e93`) postdate the collapse commit by ancestry, which is not the same as being right - neither was read against the chrome's pixels, so no claim is made about them here. THE DRAWING-SIDE SET IS TWELVE FILES ACROSS SIX DRAWINGS, AND ALL TWELVE ARE CURRENT AS OF 2026-10-13, THOUGH THE MECHANISM THIS ROW IS REALLY ABOUT IS UNCHANGED. **The set grew from five to twelve.** The row counted five PNGs beside the drawings; six drawings now carry a pair each. Added: `controls-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` beside `controls.html` and `controls-light.html` (`988d1788`), and `settings-keyboard-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` and `settings-about-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` beside the two comparator sheets plan 8 Task 4 added (`e412c98d`). **Eight of the twelve were stale and were re-shot from the actions' own output rather than copied.** The settings six (`e412c98d`) and the shell three (`9b25aecb`). Each was measured before it was replaced, and the two families failed differently, which is worth keeping because it is how a stale capture is recognised: **the settings modal's moved in geometry** — the fresh Appearance and About renders are 2px shorter and the Keyboard render 6px narrower, read off the IHDR (312/224 against 314/226; 498 against 504) — while **the shell's moved in pixels at identical dimensions**, `shell-palette-light` being 1280x720 in both at 415108 bytes against 421995. The causes are the 2026-10-13 commits: `69e6e7f1`'s `dl > div` padding and `7a92d0fe`'s dialog section-2 body role for the modal, `7a92d0fe`'s dark-base tokens, `d0c67844`'s canvas clusters and `8b1b9106`'s rail for the shell. **The controls pair is the exception, and it is the useful one.** Its fresh capture is byte-identical to the images already committed, so the fixture page's rendering did not move under the same commits that moved the shell — which is what makes this staleness a per-surface fact rather than a global one, and why re-shooting everything was not the conclusion. **The `docs/evidence/screenshots/` copies were refreshed wherever a drawing-side file was**, so the two copies of each capture agree. **WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS THE ROW'S OWN SUBJECT.** Nothing in the repo re-shoots these; every one of today's was manual, run under `YUNARI_CAPTURE` with `YUNARI_CAPTURE_DIR` pointed at the drawings' directory. And no gate notices a stale image: the drawings gate enumerates `*.html` and skips a PNG beside a drawing without reading it. **The rest of the committed corpus was not measured** — the same shape applies to any capture shot before the 2026-10-13 chrome fixes, and which of the sixty-nine files in `docs/evidence/screenshots/` those are is still an open measurement. NEAR ROWS: `vg-435` (the gate that does not run `design:check`, the same class of a rule the repo believes is enforced); `vg-390` (the acceptance item whose evidence these captures are); `vg-436` (the drawing name one of the refreshed pairs sits beside). SECOND MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-13 -- THE CORPUS WAS SAMPLED RATHER THAN LEFT UNMEASURED: of the sixty-eight PNGs in `docs/evidence/screenshots/`, **thirty were re-shot and six were verified current; thirty-two are still unmeasured**. **METHOD, because the method is the finding.** Every capture action was re-run on a bundle built from HEAD with `YUNARI_CAPTURE=1` and `YUNARI_CAPTURE_DIR` pointed at a scratch directory outside the repo, then each output was compared against the committed file with `cmp` **after an existence check**. That check is not decoration: `cmp` fails on a missing file exactly as it fails on a changed one, and the first pass at the inspector column read three captures as stale when the scratch directory simply did not hold them -- they were in three other tests. Anyone repeating this must check existence first or they will manufacture staleness. **WHAT CAME BACK STALE, AND IT IS NEARLY EVERYTHING THAT PREDATES 2026-10-13.** The thirty re-shot: the settings modal's six (`e412c98d`), the shell's eight (`9b25aecb`), `pane-document` and the inspector column's three (`26dd3661`), and the editor spec's twelve (`559d3346`). Two signatures, and both are how a stale capture is told from a corrupt copy -- **the modal's moved in geometry** (IHDR 312/224 against 314/226, 498 against 504) and **everything else moved in pixels at identical dimensions** (the shell 1280x720 both, 415108 against 421995 bytes; `editor-toolbar` 392276 against 399286; `editor-inspector-chart` 276x1281 both). The cause is the 2026-10-13 chrome work: `69e6e7f1`'s `dl > div` padding and `7a92d0fe`'s dialog section-2 body role for the modal, `7a92d0fe`'s dark-base tokens, `d0c67844`'s canvas clusters and `8b1b9106`'s rail for the rest. The editor spec's twelve were all written by one commit, `f069e56c` on 2026-10-12, so they were a single day stale. **WHAT CAME BACK CURRENT, WHICH IS THE USEFUL NEGATIVE.** Six: `control-set-desktop-chromium`, `control-set-editorial-desktop-chromium`, `pane-add`, `pane-composition`, `pane-tokens` and `editor-inspector-card`. Each is byte-identical to a fresh run, and each renders a surface the 2026-10-13 fixes did not touch -- the control fixture page, three of the four rail panes, and the card-shaped inspector column. **So this is a per-surface staleness, not a global one**, and re-shooting the whole corpus blind would have been the wrong conclusion even though nearly everything sampled was stale. **THE THIRTY-TWO STILL UNMEASURED, NAMED SO THE NEXT PASS IS A LIST RATHER THAN A SEARCH**: `composition-panel-{document,starter,two-hundred}`; `editor-reference-{capture,dpr2,journey,new,overlap}`; `editor-snap-resize` and `editor-snap-resize-ctrl`; `keyboard-{armed-row,reference,tooltip}`; `host-theme-thumbnail-desktop-chromium`; `player-reference-desktop-host`; `publish-loop-live-publish`; and fifteen more editor captures (`artboard-gradient`, `assets`, `background-media`, `chart-creation`, `glass-authoring`, `live-text`, `palette-reassignment`, `palette-solid`, `panel-authoring`, `starter-backdrop`, `starter-cpu-card`, `text-reads`, `type-preset`, `type-reassignment`, `zoom-readout`). Most belong to specs other than the editor shell's, so they need their own runs and their own projects -- `player-reference` is `desktop-host` and `publish-loop-live-publish` is `own-host`. **WHAT REMAINS THE ROW'S OWN SUBJECT.** Nothing re-shoots any of this automatically; all thirty of today's were manual. No gate notices a stale image -- the drawings gate enumerates `*.html` and skips a PNG beside a drawing without reading it. **And the sampled result is an argument for the mechanism rather than for thirty more manual passes**: at thirty of thirty-six stale, the periodic re-shoot is the load, and whether it becomes a checked instrument or a scheduled act is the decision this row has always been asking for. COVERAGE, NOT ONLY STALENESS, MEASURED 2026-10-13. Re-shooting the registered Add pane capture (`editor-shell-add` / "captures the shell with the Add pane open and nothing selected") to place it beside the change that gave the pane free control boxes their own type, the fresh frame was inspected and shows NONE of the changed region: the Asset group draws its Import, Replace and Remove boxes below the pane fold, and the capture is a viewport frame, so the drawing `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html` carries three controls the frame registered for the same state does not show. The re-shot file was therefore left uncommitted, its pixels differing only by re-encode. That is a second face of this row: a capture can be current and still compare nothing for a region the drawing draws, and no gate reads either property.
MEASURED 2026-10-16 (Phase 15, Task 15.5): THE DOCUMENTATION HALF LANDED AND THE TITLE'S CLAIM IS STILL TRUE, SO THIS ROW STAYS OPEN. **What landed.** The README's claim that both drawings-adjacent shell captures are "produced by the registered actions above" was **verified false by running the action**: `captures each palette's own surface` writes `shell-palette-graphite-desktop-chromium.png` into `YUNARI_CAPTURE_DIR`, which defaults to `docs/evidence/screenshots/`, and never writes the drawings-adjacent name. The README now states the copy step and carries the eleven name pairs, and its three false passages are corrected. **The other eight drawings-adjacent captures had drifted from their evidence twins** — the settings six by 8px of dialog height (408x312 and 394x224 against the current 408x304 and 394x216), the controls pair by pixels at identical dimensions — and all eleven pairs are byte-identical again, verified by the controller with `cmp` over the README's own table. **Why it stays open.** The title's claim — *"Nothing in the repo re-shoots the captures beside the drawings"* — is **still exactly true**: the copy is now written down, which is one of the row's two stated ways to close, but writing a step down is not an instrument, and the row's own second measurement said the periodic re-shoot is the load. **The mechanism is `vg-287`'s and Task 21.3's** ("the capture registry owns a freshness check"), so this row is homed there rather than closed on documentation. **And a measurement that narrows what a freshness check can be.** Two runs of `captures the settings modal's three tabs` on one bundle produce **different bytes at identical dimensions**, so `cmp` is not a valid staleness test on that surface — a byte-diff scanner would report that capture stale on every run. A check has to key on geometry or on the recorded commit rather than on bytes. MEASURED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 21.3, which discharged this row's MECHANISM half and not its re-shoot half. **The instrument now exists and reports**: `scripts/capture-freshness.mjs` reads the registry's recorded sha and surface paths and exits 1 on a capture whose surfaces have moved, so the row's own question — *whether it becomes a checked instrument or a scheduled act* — is answered on the instrument side. **What is left is the act, and the first live run measures how much of it: 11 registered captures, 11 stale, 0 broken.** Every one is moved by `editor-shell.css` (17 commits, newest `7874e879`) and by `editor-shell/` and `components/ui/`, because Phase 20 retired ten tokens and moved the elevation ladder. **So the row's title is still true and its closing condition is still unmet**: nothing in the repo re-shoots them, and a re-shoot needs built bundles, one worker, `YUNARI_CAPTURE=1`, and then the drawings-side `cp` for each of the eleven. **Whether a re-shoot becomes a scheduled act is undecided and the scanner deliberately does not decide it** — it reports, and who acts on the report is a scheduling ruling rather than an instrument's. OWNER: whoever owns the capture actions, which `0061` records are Playwright titles in `src/web/tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` rather than a registry file.

title: serialiseScene strips every object's derived `styles` table unconditionally, while `authoredOnly` keeps it on a run-less object as authored — so an imported package whose text carries Fabric's own per-character styling loses it silently on the next save
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 5.1 (2026-10-13), by its task reviewer, while the strip that closes vg-129 was being verified. Two owners state contradictory models of the same key. `scene-fabric/src/persist.ts`'s `removeDerivedTextStyles` deletes `styles` from every object at every depth, because vg-129 measured that nothing reads it back; `editor/src/persistence-manager/index.ts`'s `authoredOnly` deliberately KEEPS `text` and `styles` on an object with no `yunariText.runs`, with the comment 'An object without runs owns its `text` and `styles`, so they are kept there and a real edit is never hidden'. For a product-authored document the two never disagree, because the only writer of `styles` is `fabric-text.ts` computing it from runs. They disagree for a package the product did not author: an imported or hand-edited theme whose run-less text object carries Fabric per-character styling passes the validator (scene objects are not key-enumerated - `KNOWN_KEYS` covers endpoint bags only), revives with the styling visible, and loses it on the next save with no report, unrecoverably. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED for the foreign path: no imported-package case has been driven. The decision owed is which model is true - if `styles` is unrevivable state wherever it appears (vg-129's finding) then `authoredOnly`'s comment and its `styles` branch are stale and should be amended; if a run-less object's `styles` is authored, the strip must be scoped as `removeDerivedTextClips` is, by `yunariText` presence, and an imported styling must survive the round trip. D7's `vg-041`/`vg-188` ruling owns what a derived property is in general, and this is that question at one key.

PARKED 2026-10-16: `scene-fabric/src/persist.ts`'s `removeDerivedTextStyles` deletes `styles` at every depth unconditionally, while `authoredOnly` keeps `text` and `styles` when `yunariText` is undefined — the contradiction reproduces. It waits on which side is the rule: amend `authoredOnly` so styles are unrevivable everywhere, or scope the strip by `yunariText` presence. Parked rather than closed because the finding is real and the register's policy is that a real-but-low-value finding is parked rather than forgotten, and parked rather than left plain because the triage's job is to say what each row waits on.

title: `grouping-manager`'s `ownerGroup` spells the group-holder fact a third time, in a `Group | undefined` shape the new `holderOf` contract cannot take
detail:

title: `arrangeEligible` re-derives the arrange refusal from a pure `ObjectTarget` while the same module also asks `canArrange`, so eligibility is a second owner of one decision — the shape `vg-365` closed, one layer up
detail: FOUND BY TASK 6.2 (2026-10-13), which closed `vg-365` and hit the same shape in the module it was editing; it could not file a row then, because its dispatch owned only its own two. `object-actions.ts:234-239`'s `arrangeEligible(target.memberCount, target.locked, id)` returns `count >= arrangeMinimum(arrangeVerb(id)) && !locked`, and the module's own filter asks the other owner instead: `:100-101` calls `gate.canArrange(id.slice("arrange:".length))`, which is `arrange.ts:46`'s `canArrange(editor, action)` — the function `applyArrange` itself guards with (`arrange.ts:25`). Two answers to one question inside one file, kept in agreement by hand. WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX, and why it is the same design question `vg-365` left open: `canArrange` needs the live editor and a real `FabricObject`, while `arrangeEligible` is a pure function of the Fabric-free `ObjectTarget` (`memberCount`, `locked`), which is what the action list can compute without a canvas. That is exactly the asymmetry `vg-365`'s row records as the reason its 'ask the manager that refuses' remedy was unavailable, so this row and that one should be settled together rather than twice. SEVERITY: unknown until measured — the two paths' answers were not compared on any input, and the row does not claim they disagree today. Established: the restatement exists, and a change to `canArrange`'s refusal does not reach it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any current input makes the two disagree, and whether `arrangeMinimum`'s count rule is the same eligibility question as the gate's or a third condition that belongs to the action list alone. title: the ownership map's "Whether an asset is still referenced" row names only the canvas half, while `editor-session.ts` answers the envelope half and the only place the two meet is an `||` in a pane
detail: FOUND BY TASK 6.2 (2026-10-13) as an unfiled concern and confirmed by the controller before filing; its dispatch owned only its own two rows. `panes/add/file-section.tsx:155-158` guards asset removal with `assetReferencedBy(editor.canvas.getObjects(), id) || isReferenced?.(id) === true`, and the two operands answer from different modules: the first is `asset-manager/index.ts:439`, the walk `sceneObjects` now owns (`:421`, Task 6.2's fix), and the second is `editor-session.ts:825`'s `#holdsAsset`, built into the panel at `:430` and consumed through `new-object-panel.ts:65`. THE TWO ARE NOT DUPLICATES, and this was checked rather than assumed: `#holdsAsset`'s own docstring says it reads the envelope's asset references -- `artboard.backgroundMedia.assetId` and each `globals.typePresets` face -- and that "the canvas walk the asset panel does cannot see either", because neither is a Fabric object. So the split is real and deliberate. WHAT IS UNOWNED IS THE UNION. `docs/architecture/ownership.md:99` claims the concept ("Whether an asset is still referenced -- the reference that decides a deleted asset can go") and names only `assetReferencedBy` and `sceneObjects`; the envelope half is answered one module away and joined at a call site. NOT A ONE-LINE FIX and not fixed on the fly: the cause spans two modules (`asset-manager`, `editor-session`), so more than one owner could fix it, and where the union lives is a design decision -- a second `isReferenced` source registered by the envelope, one `assetInUse(document, canvas, id)` the pane calls, or the map row naming both halves as one concept. ESTABLISHED: the guard, both operands, and the map row's silence on the second. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any input today makes the union wrong (none known), and whether `#holdsAsset` is reached by any caller other than the panel. title: the at-any-depth scene walk is spelled nine times: `sceneObjects` owns it for the reference question while eight other modules recurse through `Group` for their own
detail: FOUND WHILE REVIEWING TASK 6.2 (2026-10-13): its report and `vg-367`'s archived `check` called `sceneObjects` "the one walk of every object at any depth", and the reviewer falsified that. `sceneObjects` is the one walk *the reference question* reads, and that half of the row is genuinely fixed; the recursion itself survives in at least eight other modules, each for a different question: `scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts:297-311` (an id -> object map), `clipboard-manager/index.ts:72` (an id list), `chart-manager/index.ts:391` (a write pass over every object), `scene-fabric/src/glass.ts:741`, `palette-references.ts:41` and `:80`, `object-type.ts:45` and `:77`, `fabric-text.ts:392`, `card-library.ts:626`. title: themes/store.test.ts 'holds read and write to the same asset count' times out at 20359 ms inside the full suite and passes alone

title: The asset panel is a list of files, and assets are placed objects: insert belongs in the Add pane and replace on the selection
detail:
Raised by the user on 2026-10-07, ruling that the Assets pane should not exist. The argument, which the code supports: an asset is not a document object with its own identity to browse — it becomes a layer when it is placed, and the layer tree shows scene objects, not files. Measured here: the layer tree has no asset concept at all (no reference to assets in editor-shell/layer-tree.ts), and replace exists only inside the panel (asset-manager/panel.ts:28-37 build the replace input and button, :174-186 the replace path). So the user is naming two moves rather than one deletion — insert already has a home in the Add pane, and replace has none on the selection today and would be new work on the object context menu or the dock toolbar. Both the import path and the reference-count question (assetReferencedBy) have to survive wherever replace lands, or a file the theme still uses becomes removable. EXTENDED 2026-10-07 after the user reported from earlier testing that some assets appear as layers and some do not, and asked why the asset needs a place of its own when an asset already is a layer object. Measured, and it answers the report exactly: asset-manager/index.ts:21-31 defines four asset kinds — image (png/jpg/jpeg/webp), svg, video (mp4/webm) and font (woff2/woff/ttf/otf) — and isPlaceable at asset-manager/panel.ts:232-236 accepts only image and svg. So importing a file does two different things chosen by its type, silently: a PNG is declared and then placed, dropping an object on the canvas, while an MP4 or a font is declared only and appears in the asset panel and nowhere else. Import never says which of the two happened. On why a separate place exists at all: the relation is not one-to-one and has three cases. One asset to many objects — assetReferencedBy at asset-manager/index.ts:415 walks every object at any depth precisely because of this, and remove refuses while any of them holds the id. One asset to zero objects — a video or a font can never become an object, because no object kind exists for them, so the layer tree has nothing to hang management on. And one asset to no object at all — Artboard.backgroundMedia at renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts:133-138 is assetId plus fit on the artboard itself, which is what the reference theme full-bleed photograph is. Cases two and three are why a panel exists; case one, the common one, is what this row already rules should move onto the layer. Consequence that has to be decided with the removal: remove, including its refusal while referenced, is reachable only from that panel today, so without a home for it a font imported once can never be deleted.
EXTENDED 2026-10-10 BY PLAN 4 TASK 12 (the plan's closing comparison). WHAT LANDED (the insert half): the Add pane renders insertGroups() as its own React surface (panes/add/add-pane.tsx, Task 3, 96099ba8), so a card unit, a primitive, a chart family and Text are placed from the pane; and the declared-asset list this row requires to survive the move is inside Add — the file path is the pane's (panes/add/file-section.tsx, Task 4, c8dc0b1a) with the control set's select (Task 10, 80facf67), before which the row's own panel is gone: createAssetPanel was deleted and grep -rn createAssetPanel over src/web/packages/editor/src and src/web/tests returns nothing. WHAT DID NOT (the replace half, which is why the row stays open): a selection-scoped replace does not exist on any surface. Re-pointing one chosen object's image to another file was never the panel's byte replacement — the panel swapped a declared asset's bytes for every use of it — and no dock action, context-menu entry or inspector field offers the selection-scoped form today. It is a new capability, not a behaviour to preserve, so §2.3's no-drift constraint forbids building it inside this rewrite. Remaining work when it is taken: place the action where the selection's own actions live (the dock toolbar or the object context menu), and keep remove and its refusal reachable for the asset kinds that can never become an object (video, font), which is the consequence this row already states.

RULED 2026-10-13: THE ROW STAYS OPEN, and the `verified` close that briefly archived it is withdrawn. Its insert half was discharged by an earlier plan, but its replace half -- re-pointing a placed object at a new asset -- is still unmet at HEAD, and this row's own detail says so in as many words. What Task 8.2's seat landed is real and is kept: `panes/add/file-section.tsx`'s header now names where the capability belongs (the selection inspector, on `selection-inspector/crop.ts:9`'s own rule that a control over the selected object lives there), and `file-section.dom.test.tsx` gained a case pinning that replace swaps an asset's bytes under its id instead of declaring a new one. **A close is the machine-read claim that the named problem was addressed, and this one was not addressed -- recording a gap is not building the capability**, which is the same line drawn at `vg-175`. Building it needs the placement decision this row's own text describes -- where `remove` lives, and what happens to the asset kinds that can never become an object -- and spans the files the nearest selection-scoped control (crop) already spans, so it is not a file-safe seat in this phase. The interim `check` and `artefacts` are dropped with the close; `vg-117`'s close is unaffected.

title: The dialog's glyph-button hover raises --edge to --shell-accent where DESIGN.md §5 rule 6 raises it to --muted, and no row owns the call
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 8.3A'S SEAT AND CONFIRMED AS UNOWNED BY ITS INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-13), which swept both registers for `affordance`, `accent border`, `hover border`, `rule 6`, `.editor-shell-dialog > button` and `border-color: var(--shell-accent)` and found no owner. NEAR ROWS: `vg-316` (the control's fill, live), `vg-319` (the dialog's `h3`/`dl` roles), `vg-325` (the drawing's own parity). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on whether accent-on-hover is the dialog's intended affordance — in which case `DESIGN.md` §5 rule 6's first clause needs the exception written into it, since today the product and the rule disagree — or a one-line change to `border-color: var(--muted)`. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css`, with `DESIGN.md` §5 if the exception is the answer. SEVERITY: low — a live, user-visible divergence from a normative rule that reads as owned while nothing owns it.
PARKED 2026-10-16: measured at HEAD, this is **not one stray line** — the accent hover is a repeated, documented pattern, and the decision is which side of it is the rule.

- **The divergence.** `editor-shell.css:1708` raises `.editor-shell-dialog > button:hover`'s resting `--shell-edge` to `--shell-accent`, where `DESIGN.md:509` §5 rule 6 first clause says "Hover raises `--edge` to `--muted`".
- **The pattern.** The same accent hover is at `:1446` and `:1452` (the inspector's labelled controls), `:1455` (the panel's asset buttons) and `:1900` (the keyboard-action button) — four sites, not one.

It waits on the user, and on nothing else: either the labelled-control accent hover becomes a `DESIGN.md` clause (and the four sites are conformant), or §5 rule 6 stands as written and the four sites move to `--muted`. **This is a visible change to the editor's look either way**, which is why it is not taken here. title: The host's library listing keeps an empty theme name where the editor falls back to the id, so one theme is named two things
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 8.2A'S FIX-ROUND RE-REVIEW (2026-10-13), WHILE CHECKING `vg-218`'S CLOSE. `vg-218` CLOSED THE EDITOR'S SPELLING AND ITS `check` CALLED THE HOST'S A FIFTH SPELLING OF THE SAME FALLBACK. IT IS NOT THE SAME FALLBACK, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS OBSERVABLE. THE TWO SPELLINGS, BOTH READ AT HEAD: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/bridge.ts:128` is `return identity.name || identity.id;` and `src/web/packages/host/src/themes/store.ts:555` is `name: envelope.metadata?.name ?? id,`. `||` FALLS BACK ON EVERY FALSY NAME AND `??` ONLY ON NULL/UNDEFINED, SO ON `metadata.name === ""` THE EDITOR NAMES THE THEME BY ITS ID AND THE HOST NAMES IT BY THE EMPTY STRING -- the same theme appearing as its id in the editor and as a blank row in the host's library listing. THE EMPTY STRING IS REACHABLE, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: `schema/theme-document.schema.json:30` gives `name` `"maxLength": 200` AND NO `minLength`, so a theme with `name: ""` validates -- and the same schema sets `"minLength": 1` on the palette and typePreset names at `:72` and `:79`, so a floor was deliberately applied where one was wanted and deliberately omitted here. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the repair is not a substitution but a decision. Either the host adopts `||` (`vg-218`'s reading), or the schema gains a `minLength` and the empty name becomes unsaveable -- and the second is the stronger claim, because it fixes the reachability rather than the symptom, while touching saved-theme validation and every fixture that writes a theme. NEAR ROWS: `vg-218` (editor spelling, ruled 2026-10-13; its `check` is corrected by this pass and no longer calls the host's `??` the same fallback). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on whether an empty theme name is a name at all, and then either the host's spelling or the schema's floor. OWNER: `src/web/packages/host/src/themes/store.ts` with `schema/theme-document.schema.json`. SEVERITY: low -- a blank entry in a listing, on input no UI produces today.

title: `reuseExistingServer` lets a browser pass run against a preview server left over from a previous session, so the bundle under test can predate the change
detail:
FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-13) WHILE CLEARING THE MACHINE FOR TASK 8.3D, AND IT WOULD HAVE SILENTLY INVALIDATED THE PHASE 8 CLOSE. `src/web/playwright.config.ts` sets `reuseExistingServer: true` on all three `webServer` entries (the player preview, the editor preview and the real host). THE MEASUREMENT: a listener on port 4174, PID 83448, `vite preview packages/editor --port 4174 --strictPort --host 127.0.0.1`, started 2026-10-12 09:17:30 and STILL LISTENING TWENTY-ONE HOURS LATER. It was spawned by an earlier Playwright run and never reaped. `AGENTS.md` requires that affected bundles be rebuilt before a browser pass, and this is why that rule is not sufficient on its own: THE REBUILD IS INVISIBLE IF A STALE PROCESS KEEPS SERVING THE PREVIOUS BUNDLE. Playwright would have reused that server and tested a bundle built before every editor change made on 2026-10-13 -- including the destructive-mark CSS that took three review rounds -- and reported GREEN. That is the exact false-verified shape this drain has already been caught by twice, and here nothing in the output would have hinted at it. IT IS NOT ONLY A TEST-CORRECTNESS PROBLEM: the same live process held native `.node` bindings open, which is what made `npm ci` fail with `EPERM` on unlink -- once on a rolldown binding (task 8.3d's seat) and once on `@tailwindcss/oxide` (the controller). `ci` deletes before it installs, so that failure LEFT THE TREE WITHOUT ITS DEPENDENCIES; `npm install` recovered it. All three symptoms are one cause, and the cause is a process nobody reaps. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the repair is a decision with more than one defensible answer -- stop reusing servers (`reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`, paying a startup per run), have the harness reap survivors before it starts, or make staleness detectable (a build stamp the config compares against the bundles on disk). Each trades differently between run time and the risk of a green run that proved nothing. NEAR ROWS: none -- the three `EPERM` reports this wave treated as environmental are this row. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on whether a browser run may reuse a server it did not start, and then the config change and a way to notice a stale one. OWNER: `src/web/playwright.config.ts`, with whoever owns the test-run hygiene in `AGENTS.md`'s verification rules. SEVERITY: high in kind and invisible in effect -- nothing fails, and the thing that is wrong is the evidence itself.

PARKED 2026-10-16: all three `webServer` entries in `src/web/playwright.config.ts` still set `reuseExistingServer: true`. It waits on which hazard is worse: stop reusing (`!process.env.CI`), reap survivors before the run, or make staleness detectable with a build stamp — each trades a false green against a slower run. Parked rather than closed because the finding is real and the register's policy is that a real-but-low-value finding is parked rather than forgotten, and parked rather than left plain because the triage's job is to say what each row waits on.

title: The editor's vite config names no CSS target, so lightningcss may drop an unprefixed declaration and ship only a vendor-prefixed one the browser cannot use
detail:
FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-13) WHILE RETIRING `vg-311`, WHICH NAMED THIS CAUSE AND WAS NOT ITS SUBJECT. `vg-311` RECORDED A SYMPTOM: the built stylesheet carried only `-webkit-backdrop-filter` while `editor-shell.css` declared both forms, so a cluster's blur computed to `none` in a Chromium where `CSS.supports("backdrop-filter", "blur(1px)")` is true and `CSS.supports("-webkit-backdrop-filter", "blur(1px)")` is false. That symptom is GONE because the blur declarations were deleted outright, not because the emit was fixed. THE CAUSE STANDS: `src/web/packages/editor/vite.config.ts` sets no `css.lightningcss.targets` and the workspace has no browserslist, so lightningcss chooses the prefix set itself and is free to emit only the aliased form of any property it considers prefixable. `vg-311`'s own text draws the line: "a configuration gap rather than a stylesheet one". WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A LINE IN THAT CHANGE: setting a target rewrites the whole built stylesheet for every package, and which browsers the editor supports is a support-matrix decision, not a styling one -- `vg-311` refused it for the same reason and so does this. WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY: the failure mode is invisible. title: A glass-delta case measures itself against a repaint floor the editor no longer produces, so it fails on its own match-set guard rather than on glass
detail: FOUND BY PHASE 8'S CLOSE (2026-10-13), AND IT IS THE ONE FAILURE OF THAT CLOSE'S BROWSER PASS THAT IS BOTH REPRODUCIBLE AND THIS WAVE'S. `src/web/tests/e2e/glass-lifecycle.spec.ts:25` (§ the glass panel adds no repaint of its own) fails with `expect(measurement.withPanelMin).toBeGreaterThan(10)` reading **4**, and the full run read **3**. MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: in the full suite the case is red; run alone at the same commit, serial (`--workers=1`), it is still red at 7.2s -- so it is not load. Run against the phase's base `614265de` with the wave's 18 production files reverted it **passes**, so this wave is its cause. THE CAUSE IS NAMED IN THE FILE'S OWN HEADER: "the editor runs a 30 Hz chart-refresh loop of its own, so an idle editor repaints about 22 times a second whatever glass is doing ... Measured, not assumed: every one of those 22 requests stacks to `LiveRuntime.refresh` and `ChartManager.refresh`." Commit `97264e6c perf(charts): a chart is drawn when its reading moves, not every frame` (row `vg-107`) deleted exactly that: `ChartManager.refresh()` no longer ends in an unconditional `canvas.requestRenderAll()`, so an idle editor with static readings now requests almost nothing. WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A PATCH IN THAT CLOSE: the product is behaving as `vg-107` intended -- an identical reading should not repaint -- so what broke is the **instrument**, and repairing it is a measurement decision with more than one defensible answer. The `> 10` guard is not decoration: it is the match set that stops the case passing vacuously, because with both windows at ~0 renders the delta `withPanelMin - withoutPanelMin` is trivially 0 and `compositesInOneFrame === 1` still holds. Options, none obviously right: drive a repaint the test owns each round (a rAF loop or a scene mutation), assert composites-per-editor-repaint with the floor taken over a window the test forces, or give the fixture readings that actually move so the family->pull path has something to draw. Each changes what the case proves. NEAR ROWS: `vg-107` (its cause, verified 2026-10-13); `vg-196` (`display-fabric`'s repaint check times out, a different file and mechanism). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on how a repaint-marginal property is measured over a demand-driven renderer, and then the case rewritten to that shape -- with the `> 10` guard replaced by something that cannot be satisfied by a still scene. OWNER: `src/web/tests/e2e/glass-lifecycle.spec.ts`, with whoever owns what a canvas repaint is attributed to. SEVERITY: medium -- nothing in the product is wrong, but a gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate, and this one is the only browser instrument for glass's frames.

title: A second colour parser lives in `renderer-core` with a different contract, so the ownership map's single 'shared colour parsing' row names only the editor's half
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-13 while self-reviewing `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-colour-and-gradient-rebuild-design.md`, which had written the unification the wrong way round. **The duplication, measured.** `export function parseHex(input: string): Rgba | undefined` sits at `editor/src/components/ui/colour-maths.ts` beside `parseColour`, `toHex`, `rgbaToHsva` and `hsvaToRgba`, and **`export function parseHex(color: string): [number, number, number] | undefined` sits again at `renderer-core/src/charts/fill.ts`** — same name, same job, different return type. The editor's module is imported by exactly three files (`colour-picker.tsx`, `gradient-editor.tsx`, `colour-picker.test.ts`), so neither is shared with the other. **Why the map's row does not cover it.** `docs/architecture/ownership.md` names the editor's file as the owner of 'shared colour parsing — hex, rgba and hsva conversion, and the refusal that returns `undefined` for a value that is not a colour', which is the row `vg-246`'s close added. That row is scoped to the Editor section, so `renderer-core`'s copy appears in no row at all — the same failure mode `vg-246` reported, one layer down and still true after its close. **`vg-246` is not a duplicate of this and did not measure it.** Its own detail ends with **NOT ESTABLISHED: 'whether colour-maths.ts is the right owner (it is a components/ui helper, which may be why it was never promoted) or whether other colour parsing exists that the survey did not find'** — and it closed `verified` against `dd308143` on the narrower check, that the map promotes the de-facto owner and drops the Known-ownership-gaps bullet. The map row is real; the second implementation is the half its own text left open, now measured. **The direction that cannot be built, which is what the spec had to correct.** The obvious unification — the editor's module owns it and `fill.ts` consumes it — is an upward import: `renderer-core` imports nothing from `editor` (measured), and the editor bundles `renderer-core` from source through a Vite alias, so that direction is a cycle. Any single-owner resolution therefore moves the primitive **down** into `renderer-core` and leaves the editor's richer conversions consuming it, or scopes the claim to the editor and records `fill.ts`'s tuple parser as a deliberately separate contract for chart fill strings. **Owner and cost.** Whoever owns the map decides, and the spec's decision currently takes the first: primitive down, `colour-maths.ts` keeps `Hsva`/`rgbaToHsva`/`hsvaToRgba`/`toHex` and consumes it, `fill.ts` retires its copy, and the ownership row moves with the primitive. The cost if that is wrong is a package-boundary move of one small pure module plus a row rewrite; the cost of leaving it is a third parser the next colour surface will write.

PARKED 2026-10-16: the decision the row asks for is already taken in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-colour-and-gradient-rebuild-design.md`, which states the direction that can be built (the primitive moves down into `renderer-core` and `fill.ts` retires its copy) and the one that cannot (an upward import is a cycle); measured 2026-10-16, both `parseHex` definitions are still in place, so the work is real and unscheduled. It waits transitively on that spec's review, the same shape as `vg-322`'s park on `vg-330`: the row's decision lives in a document the user has not read yet, so the work cannot enter a phase before it. title: No check compares a drawing's drawn type to the product's, and none reads a pane surface's rendered type either, so the shell's plain-DOM control boxes are type-checked by neither route
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-13, measuring why `vg-274`'s one surviving D9 value cannot be closed with a check. **THE TWO ROUTES AND WHAT EACH REFUSES.** (1) The declared-versus-drawn comparison (`src/web/tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts`, the `productRows` block) reads a declaration out of the product's stylesheet and a declaration out of a drawing and compares the two strings. It carries those boxes' `padding` today - `.editor-shell-panel [data-yunari-asset-import]` and `.editor-shell-inspector [data-yunari-run-add]`, both against the one box `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:112` draws. It cannot carry their TYPE: the drawing states that box's type as the shorthand `font:400 12px system-ui`, and `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:392-399` refuses to answer a `font-size` question with it, deliberately, with the reason in its message ('this row reads the longhand, so a shorthand is a value it cannot see and would read as the drawing's silence'). Reading the drawing's whole `font` instead and comparing strings does not work either, because the product's idiom is a scale token (`var(--text-sm)`) where the drawing writes literals. (2) The scale route (`design-language.spec.ts:2846-2862`) compares a RENDERED value against a declared scale token, which is the shape that fits this row ('control text is section 2's `--text-sm` 12px'), and it needs the element rendered. Those boxes render inside the Add pane's file section and the inspector's action rows, and the surfaces that test reads are a whitelist in the spec itself (`:2790-2795`: the shell, `settings`, `settings-keyboard`, `settings-about`, `sheet`, `fixture`), so a row on a pane is not merely unread - it is rejected by a guard that exists to stop a typo being skipped by both tests. **WHY IT MATTERS, AND WHAT IT WOULD HAVE PROTECTED.** The value is live: the two rules declare no `font-size` and so inherit the shell root's `var(--text-md)` 13px (`editor-shell.css:687-689`, `:1317-1328`, `:1353-1363`), where section 2 gives control text `--text-sm` 12px and the same drawing's own instances state 12px (`docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:137`, `:140`). A third rule of the same shape, `.editor-shell-panel .yunari-layer-rename` (`:1332`), is in no drawing at all, so its correct size is a question no instrument can ask either. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT.** Either a shorthand-aware reading in the declared-versus-drawn block - which is a decision about `mockup-values.ts`'s stated refusal rather than a repair of it - or a pane surface registered in the scale route; either, plus the declarations themselves. **OWNER**: the parity instrument's owner, because each candidate changes how the acceptance instrument reads rather than what the product renders. NEAR ROWS: `vg-274` (the value this instrument would protect), `vg-437` (this file's line-height half, whose instrument is a source contract rather than a parity row), `vg-441` (the same rules' fill, whose gap is in DESIGN.md). NARROWED 2026-10-13: THE VALUE IS FIXED, THE DRAWING COMPARISON IS STILL ABSENT. The type this row described is now stated by the three rules and asserted in a browser by `tests/e2e/add-pane.spec.ts`'s 'the pane's file controls take control text, not the shell's 13px base', so what remains is not the value but the route. Neither candidate has moved: `mockup-values.ts:392-399` still refuses to answer a `font-size` question with the `font` shorthand the drawings write (`controls.html:112` writes `font:400 12px system-ui`), and the scale route still reads a whitelist of surfaces (`design-language.spec.ts:2790-2795`) that names no pane, so a scale row for a pane element is rejected by a guard rather than merely unread. **What that leaves uncaught is a change on the drawing's side**: a redrawn box whose type moved would redden nothing, because the product's declaration is pinned by the pane's own spec and not by the drawing it is measured against. The declaration half is no longer open; this row is the instrument half alone.
MEASURED 2026-10-16 (Phase 15, Task 15.1), AND THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE WAS FALSE. **The refusal this row describes did not exist.** It says `mockup-values.ts` deliberately refuses to answer a `font-size` question with the drawings' `font` shorthand, "with the reason in its message". Measured before any edit: `SHORTHANDS_SETTING` named no font longhand at all, so `mockupDeclaredOrNull(controls, BOX, "font-size")` returned `null` — the drawing's *silence*, which the parity table reads as `0`. So the instrument was not refusing; it was answering a `font-size` question about a `font`-shorthand box with the drawing's silence. **The refusal is now real**, which is the half of this row that landed: `SHORTHANDS_SETTING` maps `font` to `font-size`/`font-family`/`font-weight`/`font-style`/`line-height`, and a `font-size` question against a shorthand throws rather than reading silence. **What the shorthand still refuses is the comparison, not the reading, so this row stays open.** The drawing writes `font:400 12px system-ui` and the product writes `var(--text-sm)`, so making the longhand readable does not make the two comparable. **Both candidate routes are now narrower than the row states, and one is closed off.** The surface whitelist it cites (`design-language.spec.ts:2790-2795`) is gone with that file's split; the only surviving one is `design-language-parity.spec.ts:410-422`, which is `PARITY`'s own `surface` union — so candidate 2 is now "register a pane surface in that union", and the Add pane is `display:none` while Document is open, which would make such a row `unresolved` rather than unread. Candidate 1 remains a decision about the instrument. **So this row's subject — that no check compares a drawing's drawn type to the product's — is still exactly true, and the instrument now says so rather than implying otherwise.** Closing it `verified` on this commit would claim a comparison that was not built.

title: The inspector's and the panel's section headings render in a serif display face in six of eight declarations, where §2 gives headings UI sans and every drawing draws sans
detail:
FOUND BY RE-MAKING PLAN 1'S PARITY COMPARISON (2026-10-13, read-only; the census is on `vg-390`), and confirmed at the rule. WHAT: `.editor-shell-panel h2, .editor-shell-inspector h2` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1142-1151`) sets `font-family: var(--shell-display)` alongside `font-size: var(--text-md)`, `text-transform: uppercase` and `letter-spacing: 0.14em`. `--shell-display` is `ui-serif, Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif` at six declarations (`:70`, `:199`, `:323`, `:353`, `:383`, `:421`) and `system-ui, sans-serif` at two (`:151`, `:270`), so in six palettes the heading block is serif. WHY IT REACHES TEXT THAT LOOKS LIKE IT DECLARES ITS OWN TYPE: the section header's children — the eyebrow span, the count span and the `Read-only` marker — set their own size, weight and tracking but no family (`components/ui/inspector-section.tsx:69`, `:75`, `:81`), so the family is inherited from the h2. WHAT THE RULE SAYS: §2's family table gives UI sans 'Everything a person reads as language | Labels, menus, headings, panel copy' (`DESIGN.md:123`) and confines theme fonts to 'Inside the artboard only; never in chrome' (`:125`); no clause grants a chrome heading a display face, and `DESIGN.md` names no serif family anywhere. WHAT THE DRAWINGS SAY: every current drawing draws those headings in `system-ui` (`docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:29` and `:169`), and the user's ruling of 2026-10-10 makes the drawing the acceptance instrument. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: `--shell-display` is declared *per palette*, which reads as a deliberate palette-level identity rather than an oversight, and that puts this row beside `vg-441` — a chrome property no clause of `DESIGN.md` names in either direction, so neither the product's face nor the drawing's can be called wrong by a cited rule. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a §2 clause granting a chrome display face, in which case the drawings are the stale side; or dropping `font-family` from that rule, which is the direction §2 and all six drawings already agree on. ALSO RECORDED, because it is a trap rather than a live difference: the rule's own `--text-md` 13px and `.14em` tracking are inert today only because every child span states its own size and tracking, so any bare text added to an `h2` would take 13px uppercase serif tracking. MEASURED IN A BROWSER 2026-10-13, WHICH IS WHAT MOVES THIS ROW FROM A READ TO AN OBSERVATION. The class changes that fixed the *count*'s family (`inspector-section.tsx`'s section-count span now states `font-mono` and `text-faint`) were red-proved in `inspector-sections.spec.ts` before the rebuild, and the failure prints exactly the inheritance this row describes: `expect(...).toMatch(/mono/i)` received `"ui-serif, Georgia, \"Times New Roman\", serif"` for `[data-yunari-section-count]`'s computed `font-family`. So the count was rendering in the h2's display face, on a build made from this tree, in the default palette. THE FIX MOVES ONLY THE COUNT. The eyebrow span and the `Read-only` marker still declare no family (`inspector-section.tsx:69`, `:81`) and so still inherit `--shell-display`, and the subject's name in `inspector.tsx` now states its weight but no family, so it takes the shell's sans — which means this row's remaining subject is two elements in the same header, not the whole block: §2 assigns headings to UI sans, all six drawings draw sans, and six of eight `--shell-display` declarations are serif.

PARKED 2026-10-16: six of the eight `--shell-display` declarations are serif and the h2 rule still applies the serif face, while the eyebrow span declares no family. It waits on `DESIGN.md` rather than on CSS: add a §2 clause granting the chrome a display face, or drop `font-family` from the h2 rule — the row is a design-language gap, not a stray declaration. Parked rather than closed because the finding is real and the register's policy is that a real-but-low-value finding is parked rather than forgotten, and parked rather than left plain because the triage's job is to say what each row waits on.

title: A fake drive's capacity drifts, because `disk.total` and `disk.data.total` end in `total` and are answered by the fallback profile
detail:

The same shape reaches a drive: any vocabulary key whose last segment is `total` has no entry in `PROFILES`, so it falls to `FALLBACK_PROFILE` (min 0, max 100, period 37 s, unit ""), and a capacity that drifts across 0..100 is nonsense in the preview. title: Three of Phase 13's landed items have no browser case, so a regression living in the stylesheet is invisible to every check
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 13.5'S IMPLEMENTER and carried in its commit trailer (`677ff7bf`), 2026-10-15, while writing the two cases the phase owed and checking what the other items already had. **The three:** item 2 (`vg-459`, the layer kind marks and the add pane's tiles) and item 9 (`vg-466`, the inspector header's kind glyph and the rule above its first section) are pinned by jsdom cases alone (`kind-mark.dom.test.tsx`, `icons.test.tsx`, and the inspector's own dom suite); item 6's positive half (`vg-463`, "the inspector leads with the eight") is pinned by a jsdom case of its own (`selection-inspector/index.dom.test.ts:895`, asserting the column's eight `aria-label`s against `uiCopy.arrangeLabels`) and by no browser case either — nor by a capture: `editor.spec.ts:1880` photographs the layer panel, not the lead. **Why jsdom is not the gap being claimed, and the gap is narrower than "untested":** those cases do read a rendered DOM, so the *structure* the fix landed is pinned. What they cannot read is a computed stylesheet cascade or a painted surface — jsdom applies no external CSS — so **a regression that lives in `editor-shell.css` reverts any of the three with every check green.** That is the same shape as `vg-195` and `vg-284` (both archived, both `verified`): a browser surface whose only assertion was the one that could not see the defect. **The order this was found in matters:** the phase's acceptance is rendered evidence, and 13.5's Step 4 pass gives each of the three *one* reading. One reading taken once is not a case that pins them — nothing runs the next time someone edits that stylesheet. **What an owner needs:** one browser case per item, in the spec that already owns its surface — `shell-appearance.spec.ts` for the marks' weight and family, `inspector-sections.spec.ts` or `design-language.spec.ts` for the header. title: A gesture inside a group snaps to nothing, because both snapping paths refuse a group child for its plane
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.4d (`vg-123`) as an unfixed by-product of its own work, and carried in that commit as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer; materialised here by the controller. THE FINDING: a drag or a resize of an object **inside a group** reaches no snap candidate at all, on either path, and the cause is the plane each path assumes rather than the candidate set. **Measured by Task 12.4d, which was trying to make a part-inside-a-card resize the assertion its ruling named and could not.** (1) THE SCALE PATH refuses before any candidate is read: `isSupportedScaleTarget` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/snap-manager/scaling/scale-snapping-controller.ts` returns false when `target.group !== undefined || target.parent !== undefined`, so `beginGesture` never starts a session. Proved **load-bearing rather than over-broad** by relaxing the guard on the unmodified tree: the gesture then ran and wrote canvas-plane geometry into the child's group plane, landing the part at `1646.72` instead of ~`958`. (2) THE MOVEMENT PATH refuses every step: `assertRawIntentMatchesBaseline` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/snap-manager/movement-snapping-resolver.ts` requires `intent.bounds` to be `baseline.bounds` translated by `intent.position - baseline.position`, and a group child's `position` is group-plane while its `bounds` are canvas-plane — so it throws `Movement raw intent must be a translation of the gesture baseline` at every step, the throw is swallowed by the guard in `createSnapManager`, and the drag lands raw. **The candidate set is nevertheless correct, which is what isolates this from `vg-123`:** a probe of the built bundle read the sources at gesture start during a part drag as `["right-card@700","right-card-part@960","mover@300","loose-source@900"]` plus the artboard, so the part beside the dragged one **is** offered and the drag still does not snap. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR A RULING ALREADY MADE: `vg-123`'s ruling asked that its instrument — a resize of a part inside a card — become the assertion the work is fixed against, and that clause **cannot be met while this stands**; that task delivered the widening, left the instrument a recording, and proved the row's own title through a dragged card instead. So this row is the residue of a ruled clause, not only a new bug. WHY A ROW AND NOT AN ON-THE-FLY FIX, on the test's third clause rather than its first: the cause is named to symbol, but **the fix needs a design decision this task could not take** — which ancestor transforms are safe to write a movement or scale plan through — and the scale half is not small: `sendPointToPlane` is **not exported from `fabric/es`**, so converting a plan's anchor into the group plane means hand-rolled matrix work rather than the one-line conversion it looks like. It also spans two controllers and the resolver, none of which `vg-123` owned. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a decision on the plane question, then a plan written through the ancestor transform, with the part-inside-a-card resize finally snapping **and drawing its guide** — at which point `snapping.spec.ts`'s nested instrument can become the assertion its own comment says it is waiting to be. NEAR ROWS: none found — the live register holds no row naming `isSupportedScaleTarget`, `assertRawIntentMatchesBaseline` or the snapping plane question, and `vg-123` is the row whose ruling this blocks rather than a duplicate of it. NOT VERIFIED: the arithmetic of the two probe readings above (`1646.72`, and the candidate list) is the implementer's own; the controller verified only that both refusing symbols exist and read as described.

CORRECTED 2026-10-15 BY TASK 12.4d'S FIX ROUND (commit `7d3b3afa`, the review's F4 and F3). title: repeatsEnclosingBounds' epsilon can only match a child that adds no stroke, so a stroke-carrying part still offers a duplicate of its group's centre line
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.4d's fix round R1 (`vg-123`) as an unfixed by-product of its own work, and carried in commit `7d3b3afa` as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer; materialised here by the controller. THE GAP: the dedupe that `vg-123`'s widening added — `repeatsEnclosingBounds` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/snap-manager/index.ts` — compares a part's box with the nearest enclosing box already offered on all four edges at `SNAP_SOURCE_BOUNDS_EPSILON = 1e-9`. **Measured by R1 with `util.enlivenObjects` on the very JSON the specs author, and the result is that the dedupe fires on almost no real shape:** on `snapping.spec.ts`'s own `source("group", …)` the group box is 80×80 at (100,200) and the child's is 81×81 — the child's `getBoundingRect()` includes its own stroke — so the boxes differ by a stroke, the epsilon cannot absorb it, and the part **is** offered. The same holds for the nested fixture's card (group 400×200, part 61×81) and the starter's card (`cardGroup`, 360×200 against a panel 362×202). It fires only where a child adds no stroke and the group is fitted to it or declares its box: `new Group([rect])` yields the child's own 81×81, which is the path the unit case `offers a part repeating its group's own box once, as the group` exercises — so the dedupe is not dead, it is narrower than the hazard it was written for. WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS: `vg-123`'s report gave the dedupe the job of preventing "two candidates at one coordinate with different identities", the shape a count cannot see. **On a stroke-carrying part that hazard is still open** — the part duplicates its group's centre line and offers that group's edges shifted by a stroke — so the widening ships with a dedupe that does not dedupe the cases the fixtures actually contain. WHY A ROW AND NOT AN ON-THE-FLY FIX: widening the epsilon to absorb a stroke is a behaviour change and a design decision (how much of a stroke counts as the same box, and whether a shifted edge is the same edge), which R1 named rather than took; the code is unchanged and the scope is written into `snap-manager/index.ts` beside the function. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a decision on whether the dedupe compares declared boxes, stroke-inclusive boxes, or centres, then the comparison changed to match and a unit case on a stroke-carrying part that asserts the group's line is offered **once**. NEAR ROWS: `vg-123` (the widening this dedupe belongs to, whose own title is about a card snapping into a neighbouring card and which is unaffected), and `vg-524` (the two snapping refusals, whose movement half R1 re-measured in the same round — a different mechanism, filed separately). NOT VERIFIED: the report's own claim that the dedupe's *narrow* job is safe — that a fitted single-part group's part may be dropped without losing a line the group does not already offer — is R1's probe, not the controller's; the controller verified only that the epsilon and the function exist and read as described.

CORRECTED 2026-10-15, FROM ITS OWN INDEPENDENT REVIEW. **The duplicate is not one shape but three, and the row's sentence describes only the first.** The review measured each authored shape rather than the spec's own JSON alone: on `source("group", …)` — the shape this row quoted — the child sits at local 0, so a stroke-carrying child duplicates the group's **centre line** exactly. On the starter's cards (`cardGroup`) the child fills the card, so the exact duplicate is the **shared left/top edge** and the centres sit half a stroke apart. On the nested fixture's card (`openNestedFixture`) the group and the part share **no coordinate at all**. So the hazard is real and shape-dependent, and a fix must be written against the shapes rather than against the one this row named. **Two wording defects the review also found are corrected here:** the commit is `7d3b3afa` (this row and `vg-524` both said `7d3bafa`, which resolves to nothing — a sha that does not resolve is the one defect a reader cannot work around), and `snap-manager/index.ts`'s new note says the dedupe "fires only on a child that adds no stroke", which the case it cites contradicts: `new Group([sole])` has `strokeWidth` 1 and both boxes measure 81×81, so it fires. What is true is that it fires when the **enclosing box equals the child's**, which a fitted group satisfies whether or not the child carries a stroke.

PARKED 2026-10-16: the dedupe still compares stroke-inclusive boxes at a `1e-9` epsilon, so a stroke-carrying part is still offered as a snap source. It waits on the comparison: widen the epsilon to absorb a stroke, or compare declared boxes or centres — the row's own scope note is the corrected wording, so what is missing is the rule. title: backlog-check never tests whether a path inside a check still exists, so a verified row can cite a deleted file and stay green
detail:
FOUND WHILE applying §8.11's path corrections (agent, 2026-10-16).

WHAT: `scripts/backlog-check.mjs` enforces two things about a `verified` row's `check` — that it names a word from the row's own title, and that the row's `artefacts` resolve to commits that are ancestors of HEAD — and it does not test the third: whether a path the `check` names still exists. `vg-155`'s `check` named `file-section.ts` and `file-section.dom.test.ts` while the files are `panes/add/file-section.tsx` and `panes/add/file-section.dom.test.tsx`, and the 528-item checker stayed green the whole time. WHY IT MATTERS: the `check` is the row's proof of close, and the rule that a check must name a word from its title is deliberately lexical, so a check whose subject moved satisfies it by naming the same *word* at a path that no longer exists. The sha half cannot cover it — `artefacts` proves the commit is real and on the mainline, which is a different question from whether the file the check names is still there.

NOT A MECHANICAL FIX, which is why this is a row rather than an edit: a naive rule ('every path-shaped token in `check` must resolve') would red on legitimate checks, because some of them cite ledger files under `.superpowers/sdd/`, which is gitignored and so absent from `git ls-files` — `vg-328`'s check cites `adjudication.md` and `task-2-report.md` that exist on disk and in no tracked tree. So the decision is what counts as a check's path, and whether an untracked path is permitted, tolerated with a warning, or refused. A second decision follows: whether a `check` may cite a bare basename, which `vg-109` does (`index.dom.test.ts:1501`, unambiguous only because the row's `owner` names the directory).

DISCOVERED, NOT FIXED, in the §8.11 commit: filed rather than fixed because the fix needs that design decision, not because it is hard.

PARKED 2026-10-16: the checker still tests only the title-word rule and the sha rule, and nothing in `scripts/backlog-check.mjs` tests whether a path named inside a `check` still exists; the row's own trigger examples are now repaired, so what remains is the missing rule rather than a live bad citation. It waits on which unit the rule takes: require path-shaped tokens to resolve against tracked files, tolerate untracked ledger paths with a warning, or refuse them — a rule over prose needs its unit defined before it can be written.
