title: The player's pagehide tears down its whole mount under { once: true }, so a display restored from the back/forward cache is frozen until a reload
detail: FOUND BY TASK 17.1'S SEAT (2026-10-16) while fixing `vg-510`, and raised as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `7132ddf8` rather than folded into it: it is the same event pair in a second package with a different owner, and the editor's remedy does not transfer. **THE EDITOR'S SHAPE AND THE PLAYER'S ARE NOT THE SAME SHAPE.** `vg-510` was a stop with no re-arm, and the fix is a `stop`/`start` pair beside a one-way `dispose` (`chart-refresh.ts`) plus `pageshow` beside `pagehide` (`editor-main.ts`), following `DraftAutosave.start`/`stop`. **The player tears its whole mount down on `pagehide` under `{ once: true }`**, so what a restored display would have to re-arm is not a loop but a mount — and the listener is gone after one firing. **WHAT A RESTORED DISPLAY SHOWS**: nothing that updates. A bleed display or a wall display frozen into the back/forward cache and restored (a browser tab restored, a kiosk waking) keeps a torn-down mount until something reloads the page, which no code in the product does. **WHY A ROW AND NOT A FIX HERE**: *reload the page on `pageshow`* and *re-arm the mount* are different products, and the row's own task was scoped to the editor's boot and draft lifecycle. **Reload-versus-re-arm is an unmade ruling**, and it is a bigger one than it looks: a reload discards whatever state the author left on the display, while a re-arm has to rebuild a mount that was written assuming it happens once. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT**: a ruling on whether a restored display reloads or re-arms, and the player's `pagehide` handling changed to match. NEAR ROWS: `vg-510` (closed 2026-10-16 — the editor's half of the same pair), `vg-410` (the player's own mount path). OWNER: `src/web/packages/player/src/main.ts`. **COUPLING FOUND 2026-10-18 by Task 25.2's independent review, and it bears on whatever this row is ruled to do.** The availability notice now owns a three-state lifetime with one timer (`player/src/chrome.ts`), and `main.ts`'s `pagehide` handler tears down fonts, `chartRefresh`, the resize observer, the publish follower, the live source and the scene handle — it never touches chrome state, and the package has no `pageshow` listener at all. So a timer pending at `pagehide` is never cleared and the notice's state survives teardown. TODAY THAT IS INERT, and the review established why rather than assuming it: the timer's callback is three assignments plus `removeStrip`, which holds no mount, handle or canvas reference, so it cannot fire into a torn-down mount; and because `pagehide` is `{ once: true }` and nothing re-arms the mount — this row's own subject — nothing calls `showAvailabilityNotice` again, so the stale state is never read. **IF THIS ROW IS RULED "RE-ARM THE MOUNT", THAT STOPS BEING TRUE**: a display restored from the back/forward cache would carry state `dismissed` from before the park and stay silent about a sensor that is still failing, and a stale `up` timer armed before teardown could remove a strip raised after the restore. Whoever rules this row decides chrome teardown with it, or the re-armed display gets a silent gap.

title: The autosave's dirty flag is one flag for one autosave, so a document switch compares the incoming document's dirtiness against the outgoing document's answer and nothing gates the transition
detail: FOUND BY TASK 17.1'S SEAT (2026-10-16) IN THE GAP BETWEEN THE PLAN'S TASK 17.1 STEP 3 AND THE ROW THAT TASK CLOSED, and raised as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `93219354`. **The plan's Step 3 symptom is not what `vg-512` was about and nothing has fixed it** — Step 3 reads *the draft's single slot is written whenever the document is dirty with no transition gate, so a theme switch can persist the outgoing document's draft over the incoming one's*. `vg-512` is a draft the build could not **read**; a document switch is a draft the build can read and does not. **The controller rewrote this row's mechanism after reading the store, because the first draft of it stated the direction wrongly.** **THE MECHANISM, READ AT `93219354` AND NOT MEASURED.** `draft-store.ts`'s `startDraftAutosave` holds **one** `dirty` flag — *the document's own answer, as this autosave last read it* — and `writeNow` reads `input.document()`, whichever document is open **now**. There is no gate on the document changing: the flag is the autosave's memory of one document and the getter names another, so the tick after a switch compares the incoming document's dirtiness against the outgoing document's remembered answer. **WHAT THAT WOULD DO, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE PLAN NAMES ONLY ONE.** Incoming document clean with the flag still true — the transition out of dirty fires and `store.clear()` wipes the slot, which held the **outgoing** document's unsaved draft. Or the incoming document dirty, and it writes the outgoing draft's place full of its own. **The plan's Step 3 states the second as *persist the outgoing document's draft over the incoming one's*, which is the opposite direction from what the getter read at the tick implies** — one of the two phrasings is wrong and which is not established, so both are recorded rather than one being smoothed. **THE AUTOSAVE DOES SURVIVE A DOCUMENT SWITCH, ESTABLISHED BY READING THE TWO CONSTRUCTIONS RATHER THAN BY MEASURING A SWITCH.** `startDraftAutosave` is constructed **once**, at `editor-main.ts:99`, and `start()` is the module's own entry — `void start()` at `:583` — so a document switch does not re-boot and gets no fresh `dirty`. The getter it reads, `draftDocument()`, pulls the session's **current** document on every call rather than holding one, so after a switch the two halves of `writeNow` name different documents and the flag is stale. **WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED IS THE OBSERVABLE OUTCOME**: which branch fires depends on the incoming document's dirtiness at the next tick, and a freshly opened document is normally clean — which is the `clear()` branch and the one that loses the outgoing draft — but nothing here has watched a switch tick. **So the defect is real in mechanism and its symptom is unmeasured**, and the two candidate symptoms are the plan's Step 3 direction and its opposite. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT**: read the switch paths against `startDraftAutosave`'s construction and say whether the autosave survives a document change; if it does, gate the flag on the document (or reset it when the document changes), and if it does not, the plan's Step 3 is discharged by that reading and this row closes with it. NEAR ROWS: `vg-512` (closed 2026-10-16), `vg-040` (one slot), `vg-511` (closed 2026-10-16 — the announcement mechanism). OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-main.ts` with `draft-store.ts`. SEVERITY: unknown until the discriminator above is measured, and the failure it would cause is silent data loss, which is why it is not parked.

title: host-player's palette case reads ink 496 against a floor of 500 in the ordered desktop-host run and passes alone, so the floor is one sample away from a load-sensitive red
detail: FOUND BY TASK 17.2'S SEAT (2026-10-16) while running the ordered `desktop-host` suite for `vg-505`, and raised as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `b9db79f7` and `b2d558ba`. **MEASURED**: `tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts:550` — *the display paints its charts in the theme's own palette* — read ink **496** against a floor of **500** in the ordered run, and **passed twice alone**. So the case sits four pixels under its own threshold when the machine is busy, and four pixels is not a margin a rendering assertion can hold across loads. **WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX**: the number is a **floor on a painted-pixel count**, and the two ways to make it robust are opposite products of the same question — lower the floor until it is not load-sensitive (which weakens what the case proves) or make the reading not depend on how much of the frame has painted when it is taken (which is `vg-495`'s shape, fixed the same day by polling for a painted frame). **Which is right depends on what the 500 was measured to exclude**, and the row that set it is not established here. **THE ADJACENT PRECEDENT IS IN THE SAME SUITE AND WAS FIXED THE SAME DAY**: `vg-495`'s red was a pixel read racing the first paint, and its remedy was to poll for a painted frame rather than to move the threshold. **A reader taking this row should check whether 496 is an unpainted-frame reading before touching the number**, because lowering a floor to hide a race is the failure mode this repo already has a row about. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT**: one ordered-suite sample that shows whether the 496 is stable or drifts, then either the poll or a floor whose margin is stated against what it excludes. NEAR ROWS: `vg-495` (closed 2026-10-16), `vg-505` (closed 2026-10-16 — the task that found this), `vg-147`, `vg-532` (the load-shape family). OWNER: `src/web/tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts`. SEVERITY: low — a test-only flake, and no product behaviour is in question.

title: Two more e2e specs carry their own frame-decode helpers after frame-diff.ts became the shared owner, so three instruments read a capture three ways
detail: FOUND BY TASK 17.2'S SEAT (2026-10-16), after its last commit rather than before it, so it carries no `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer and is filed here instead. **THE STATE**: Task 17.2 moved the frame measure into `tests/e2e/frame-diff.ts` so that one instrument serves both the frost-extent and the stretch questions. **Two callers still hold private copies of the same three functions**: `tests/e2e/glass-shapes-visual.spec.ts` carries its own `createCanvas`/`loadImage`/`luma`, and `tests/e2e/glass-probe.ts` its own in-page `luma`. **WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN TIDINESS**: `vg-516` is a row about **two harnesses reading the same frost differently**, and it closed by establishing that a rim difference came from the cache rather than from the method. **A third and fourth copy of the decode is how that class of finding comes back** — the two copies differ in where they run (one in the page, one in the harness), which is exactly the axis that made `vg-516`'s two readings disagree. **NOT FOLDED INTO THE TASK THAT FOUND IT**, because the shared owner landed in the same commit series and the two remaining copies are in specs that task did not otherwise touch — folding them in would have widened a four-row task into a refactor of two more specs with no red proof to offer. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT**: both copies replaced by `frame-diff.ts`'s exports, with each spec's readings unchanged before and after — which is the check, because a decode refactor that moves a number is a different change than the one intended. NEAR ROWS: `vg-516` (closed 2026-10-16 — the method-dependence row), `vg-542`. OWNER: `src/web/tests/e2e/`. SEVERITY: low, and it is a duplication rather than a defect.

title: An invalid value's reason is sticky when the author edits back to the value already held, because the control declines to report a commit that changes nothing
detail:
FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-16) reviewing Task 18.1's commit `ee82150a`, and it is a defect the new channel makes visible rather than one it introduces. THE CAUSE, READ FROM THE SOURCE RATHER THAN INFERRED: `ControlText`'s `commit` does `setDraft(null); if (blocked || next === value) return; onCommit(next);` (control-text.tsx), so a draft that equals the authored value reports nothing to the caller — and `invalid` is a pure prop the control cannot clear. The Tokens pane sets it in `onCommit` and clears it only in `put`, which a declined commit never reaches. SO THIS IS REACHABLE: type `not-a-colour`, blur (the field is refused, `aria-invalid` true, the reason names it), then type the colour the document already holds and blur — the field shows a valid colour while `aria-invalid` is still true and the reason still names the value that is no longer there. A screen reader is told the field is invalid and told why, about a value the field does not hold. THE STICKINESS IS PRE-EXISTING — the pane's bare `

` was equally sticky — but it was silent then and it is announced now, which is the whole point of `vg-263`, so the row that landed the channel is where it surfaced. NOT FIXED IN THAT TASK because the fix is a design decision rather than an edit and more than one owner could take it: either the control learns to report a draft it declined to commit (an `onDraftChange`, or an `invalid` the control may clear), or the caller learns to clear on every blur — and the second is not available while `ControlText` withholds the event. EITHER WAY IT IS THE SAME QUESTION the channel just answered one level down: who owns a refusal the author can repair, given that repairing it to the value already held is not a commit.

title: A refused number carries two vocabularies in one editor: the inspector says why, the settings path says only that the value cannot be applied
detail: RAISED BY TASK 18.1's IMPLEMENTER (2026-10-16) as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `ee82150a`, and materialised here because that is what the trailer is for. THE MEASUREMENT: `uiCopy.controls.notANumber` reads `not a number` and `uiCopy.controls.atMost(n)` reads `at most 16384` — the inspector's controls, now that `vg-264` moved them into the copy table — while `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` still reads `That value cannot be applied. Enter a number in range.` and is read by exactly one site, `editor-shell/controls/number-field.ts:87`. BOTH ARE SHIPPED AND REACHABLE: `number-field.ts` is the editor shell's own control set, reachable from the settings path, so one editor tells an author two different things about the same refusal depending on which numeric control the surface happens to use. **`vg-264` DID NOT DISCHARGE THIS AND ITS CLOSE SAYS SO**: that row's subject was hardcoded English, which is gone, and its ruling deliberately moved `ControlNumber`'s copy into the table rather than unifying the two wordings — the row's own detail named the drift as 'one editor now carries two vocabularies for one refusal', and after the fix the count of vocabularies is still two, only both of them owned. NOT FIXED HERE because the direction is a design decision and neither side is obviously right: the specific message (`at most 16384`) tells the author what the field will take, the generic one tells them what to do, and a control that shows a bound at rest may not need the specific refusal at all. WHICH SIDE MOVES IS THE QUESTION: either `number-field` gains the specific refusals, or the shell's generic wording is adopted as the set's and the inspector's five specific strings are retired. The second would be a real loss of information on a control whose bound the author cannot otherwise see.

title: preset-list's delete-type button composes the shared plain-button token with text-hot, so two conflicting colour utilities on one element are resolved by stylesheet order
detail: RAISED BY TASK 18.2's IMPLEMENTER (2026-10-16) as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `f5788e86`, and materialised here because that is what the trailer is for. THE MEASUREMENT: `panes/tokens/preset-list.tsx:450` renders `className={`${plainButtonClasses} text-hot disabled:text-faint`}`, and `plainButtonClasses` already carries `text-text` (control-well.tsx:121) — so one element holds two `color` utilities and which one wins is stylesheet order, not source order. The `disabled:text-faint` is now redundant with the token it composes, for the same reason. THE SAME HAZARD IS WHY `paint-list.tsx:450` WRITES `text-hot` INLINE RATHER THAN COMPOSING, so the two delete buttons in one pane express the same idiom two ways and neither is obviously the owner's. **NOT FIXED IN THAT TASK BECAUSE IT IS A DECISION, NOT AN EDIT**: either the shared token gains a variant axis (which is the signal its own comment names for promoting it to a component), or the two delete buttons get their own token, or `text-hot` becomes a parameter of the plain-button idiom. **AND IT IS NOT MERELY TIDINESS**: the hazard is that a future edit to either utility silently changes which colour wins, which nothing in the tree measures — no test reads the resolved colour of either button.

title: A slider gesture that ends with neither a commit nor a cancel leaves the previewed value in the document with no history entry, so no undo step covers it
detail: RAISED BY TASK 18.5's IMPLEMENTER (2026-10-16) as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `6508ac42`, and materialised here because that commit is the only durable record of it. FOUND WHILE GIVING the selection column's sliders a preview (`vg-254`): the preview writes the document as the pointer moves and records nothing, the release commits exactly one value, and `Escape` puts the press's start value back — so a gesture has exactly two exits. **A third exists and neither of them is it**: if the press is held while the selection moves, the field the gesture started on is gone, and the previewed value stays in the document with no history entry, which means the author has a value they did not commit and cannot undo in one step. **Narrow and hard to drive** — it takes a non-pointer act during a held press, which is why it was filed rather than fixed. **THE REPAIR IS A DECISION RATHER THAN A PATCH**: whoever restores the start value has to be chosen when the gesture's object has changed under it — the funnel, which still holds the revision and the field id; the control, which holds the start value in a ref; or a cancellation on the selection change itself, which is a third exit the control set does not have. Each answer puts the restore somewhere different, so this is not a missing call. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the value survives a re-publish at all, since the column re-publishes on a selection change and the preview deliberately does not re-publish the column — the two have not been measured together. OWNER: whoever owns `selection-inspector/index.ts`'s write funnel with whoever owns `components/ui/control-slider.tsx`'s gesture state.

title: A preset bound to a packaged face keeps its family and weight fields editable, so an author can type a family that contradicts the face the preset carries
detail: RAISED BY TASK 19.1's IMPLEMENTER (2026-10-16) as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `055c7ecc`, and materialised here because that commit is the only durable record of it. FOUND WHILE WIRING THE FACE FIELD (`vg-268`), which is the task it was found in — it is filed rather than fixed because the fix needs a decision about who owns the contradiction, not because it is hard. **MEASURED, and the controller reproduced each half**: `editor-document.ts:563`'s `applyPresetFace` writes **three** things — `value.family`, `value.weight` and `value.face.assetId` — while `panes/tokens/preset-list.tsx` leaves the family field (`:273-279`) and the weight field (`:295-303`) editable with no disabling and no read-only state. So after an author applies a packaged face, typing a different family leaves the preset carrying a `face.assetId` that contradicts its own `family` and `weight`, and nothing in the UI says so. **THE MISSING HALF IS NAMED BY THE CATALOGUE PLAN AND WAS NEVER BUILT**: that plan's Task 7 specifies `unbindFace` alongside the face application, and **`unbindFace` exists nowhere in `packages/editor/src` or `packages/host/src`** — the same unbuilt task that left `/api/font-favorites` with no editor-side reader until `favorites-client.ts` was written. **THE DECISION THIS NEEDS**: either the two fields become read-only while a face is bound (with `unbindFace` as the way out, which is what the plan specified), or editing either one unbinds the face silently, or the face is re-resolved from the typed family and weight. Each answer puts the authority somewhere different — the control set, the document write, or the catalogue — so it is not a missing prop. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: whether the renderer resolves the face or the family when the two disagree, since `face.assetId` and `family` are both read on the paint path and the precedence was not measured. OWNER: whoever owns `editor-document.ts`'s type-preset writes with whoever owns the Tokens pane's preset fields.

title: The font picker's trio list renders all 379 trios unwindowed, so the inspector costs 1058 Tab presses to leave and the shell walk cannot reach the pane past it
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER AT THE PHASE 19 CLOSE (2026-10-16), diagnosing the browser suite's fourth red. `host-walkthrough.spec.ts:516` (§13.1's nine interactions in order, on the real host) fails at step 5 with `nothing matched in 200 presses`, thrown by `walkthrough-focus.ts:310` from `enterGroup`'s `tabUntil(page, (focus) => focus.region === "pane")`. MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: with `TAB_BOUND` raised to 2000 and that case's clock raised to 600 s the walk passes (exit 0, 4.4 m) and prints its own census — rail 6 and 53 presses, step 2's pane 5, step 4's inspector 34, STEP 5'S PANE 1058, step 6 102. So the pane IS reachable in one forward sweep and that sweep is 1058 presses long against a budget of 200; `tabUntil` additionally refuses to continue past an element it has already marked, so a larger bound is the only way across and the budget is not merely tight. CAUSE BISECTED, NOT GUESSED: the case passes at `b2c4f1e7` (pre-Phase-19) and fails at `055c7ecc` (Task 19.1) and at every commit after it, each bisect point rebuilt with `npm run build` and `npm run build:fixture -w @yunari/editor`. Task 19.1 mounts `FontPicker` on a text object's face field (`selection-inspector/font-face-field.tsx`), and `font-picker.tsx:355-376` renders `visibleTrios` in full — 379 trios, each drawing a favourite button and a row button, so 758 tab stops — while the face list directly above it (`:336-354`) is windowed to `WINDOW = 15`. Step 4 (`editFieldThenCancel`) leaves focus on the inspector's name field, so step 5's forward sweep must cross the whole picker before it can leave the inspector at all. NOT FIXED ON THE FLY, because the correct behaviour is not already specified: the `WINDOW` docblock gives the face list's reason as `FontFace` objects to keep, not tab stops, so the trio list is unwindowed by design rather than by oversight; and the picker carries no `role`, no `tabIndex` and no key handling at all (a grep of `font-picker.tsx` for focus, Key, tabIndex and role= returns nothing), so there is no keyboard model to extend. The fix is a decision about the picker's keyboard model for a 379-row list — window it as the faces are windowed, or give it a roving tabindex / listbox model — which is a spec rather than a task. THE WALK'S FIXED BUDGET IS THE SAME FINDING'S OTHER FACE and is deliberately not split into its own row: `TAB_BOUND = 200` is a constant no measurement derives, and raising it would hide this defect rather than fix it. Nothing in the six Phase 19 rows is wrong about this: the regression is the mount doing what its own ruling asked.

title: The product's segmented chips hug their own text where all three drawings give them equal shares, so the product's chip width is not the width the drawings draw
detail: FOUND BY THE SEAT IMPLEMENTING PHASE 20'S TASK 20.8 (`vg-554`), which scoped it out deliberately and filed it as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `e4785eaa` with both values rather than correcting it. MEASURED IN A BROWSER, palette settled: the product's chips are `flex: 0 1 auto` and hug their labels — **34.1px for "Left" and 48.1px for "Center" in a 170px group** — while all three drawings give every chip `flex:1`, so each is an equal third of the container. WHY THE SEAT SCOPED IT OUT, AND WHY THAT IS DEFENSIBLE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT: Task 20.8's subject is the control's composed TREATMENT — colour, spacing, radius, type, elevation and hairline — and a flex distribution is none of those, so correcting it would have been the seventh declaration the brief told the seat to stop and report rather than extend into. WHY IT IS STILL A ROW: the drawings are the checked target and the README describes `current/` as the column as it renders, so a reader who draws from it gets chip widths the product does not produce, and the divergence is invisible to every instrument — `mockup-values.test.ts` compares declared values and has no row over a flex factor. Homed as Phase 20's Task 20.9 with `vg-555`. CORRECTED 2026-10-17: THE DRAWING IS THE SIDE THAT HOLDS, and this row's original framing had it backwards. Task 20.9 removed `flex:1` from all 33 drawn chips to match the product, on the controller's brief and on the phase Outcome's sentence 'the drawings agree with the product where they had invented or drifted'. The seat flagged the counter-reading in its own commit and it is the one that governs: DESIGN.md §5 is silent on a chip's width, so `docs/design/mockups/README.md:102` applies and reads 'Where the written rules are silent, the drawing governs and the product is the defect'; `:124` is unconditional and reads '**The treatment is the target and is never redrawn from the product** … When the product differs, the product is the defect'; and `:119` forbids drawing a surface 'in a treatment of the product's devising'. The removal is reverted in `e0e7624b`, so all 33 chips draw `flex:1` again and the drawings differ from `d407c090` by the twin's two fill values and nothing else. WHAT THE FIX IS NOW: a product change, not a drawing change — `control-segmented.tsx`'s `Toggle` declares no flex and resolves to `flex: 0 1 auto`, so the chips must take an equal share of the group. THAT HAS NO HOME IN AN OPEN PHASE, because the phase that owned the editor's control set (Phase 18) closed on 2026-10-16 with all twelve of its rows `verified`, and Phases 20-24 own tokens and drawings, scripts, tests, the host and the user's two. NO INSTRUMENT CAN CATCH IT EITHER WAY: all eleven chips in a drawing share two attribute forms (four pressed, seven unpressed), so no `[style*="…"]` selector settles one chip, and `PARITY` carries no row over a flex factor. The README's own tension is filed as `vg-557`. PARKED 2026-10-17: held at Phase 20's close on `vg-557`. The fix is a product change to `control-segmented.tsx` — its `Toggle` declares no flex, so the chips must take an equal share of the group — and whether the product is the side that moves at all is what `vg-557` asks. It also has no home in an open phase, because Phase 18 owned the editor's control set and closed on 2026-10-16 with all twelve of its rows `verified`.

title: The drawings README calls `current/` both the target and the editor as it renders today, and where they differ those cannot both hold
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER 2026-10-17 WHILE DISPOSING TASK 20.9'S `vg-556`, whose direction turns on which sentence governs. `docs/design/mockups/README.md:3` reads '**`current/` is the target.** The editor is being rebuilt towards the original visual direction as those six files draw it'; `:10` reads 'The editor as it renders today, in the original visual direction'. THE TWO ARE ONLY COMPATIBLE WHILE THE DRAWINGS AND THE PRODUCT AGREE, and the whole point of the parity instrument is that they do not: `:95-102` exists because a phase photographs the built editor beside the mockup and lists the differences. The rest of the README then picks the first reading everywhere it speaks — `:124` '**The treatment is the target and is never redrawn from the product** … When the product differs, the product is the defect'; `:102` 'Where the written rules are silent, the drawing governs and the product is the defect'; `:119` a new surface is drawn 'in the original's treatment, never in a treatment of the product's devising'. THE PLAN ADDS A THIRD VOICE AND PICKS THE OTHER ONE: Phase 20's Outcome says 'the drawings agree with the product where they had invented or drifted', and Task 20.9 was briefed and implemented on that sentence before it was reverted in `e0e7624b`. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN AN EDIT: which sentence governs decides the direction of every drawing correction this repo makes — whether a divergence is fixed in the product or in the drawing — so it is a design decision about what the drawings are for, and `:119` shows the Outcome's reading is not even always available, because a surface the three originals never drew (the segmented control is one) has no original treatment to copy and the product's is the only concrete source left. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the user's word on whether `current/` is a specification the product is measured against or a depiction of the product. `vg-556` is the live case and `vg-558` is a second one in the same table.

title: The editorial twin's remaining table declarations contradict the product's own editorial aliases, and two of them cannot be transcribed at all
detail: FOUND BY TASK 20.9'S SEAT (2026-10-17) as the wider half of `vg-555`, reported rather than corrected, and measured by the controller against the product. The product's editorial palette block aliases DESIGN.md §4's whole vocabulary per palette, so it declares the drawing's own names: `--edge: var(--shell-edge)` (`#14120e`), `--edge-2: color-mix(in srgb, var(--edge) 55%, transparent)`, `--faint: color-mix(in srgb, var(--muted) 68%, transparent)` and `--accent: var(--shell-accent)` (`#14120e`). `docs/design/mockups/current/controls-editorial.html:20-21` declares `--edge:#e4ddcb`, `--edge2:#f0ead9`, `--faint:#8a8272` and `--accent:#0d7a6a`, so all four contradict the block, and `README.md:46-49` makes that a stale file rather than a style: where the current set and DESIGN.md disagree, DESIGN.md wins. THE FIRST THREE ARE STALE VALUES FROM THE ORIGINAL `inspector-language.html`, which is the light-palette column and is never edited again; `vg-436` measured the same thing and named the accent as matching no palette's accent at all. WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY A COPY, and this is the part that makes it work rather than a find-and-replace: `mockup-values.test.ts:243-248` requires every `SHELL_ROLES` token in the drawing to match `/^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/`, so `--edge2` and `--faint` may not carry the product's `color-mix(…)` expression and must be resolved to the opaque colour the mix produces over that ground, which is a measurement rather than a transcription. `--accent` IS THE ONE THAT NEEDS THE USER'S WORD RATHER THAN A RULING ALREADY TAKEN: `vg-436` renamed this file and said 'the drawing's token table stays editorial; nothing is redrawn', having already measured that `#0d7a6a` is neither editorial's ink nor `light`'s `#1c6b4f`, so the accent was left knowingly and its correction would change what the parity instrument checks for that row — the exact cost `vg-436` declined to pay. `--well`, `--well-edge`, `--kind`, `--value`, `--knob` and `--knob-edge` name no §4 role and are not this row's subject. OWNER: `docs/design/mockups/current/controls-editorial.html` together with the product's palette block as the authority it is read against.

title: `STATUS.md`'s bullets are unbounded in length, so the diary the bullet cap exists to stop now lives inside them
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER 2026-10-17 while replacing the file's `Last completed change` at Phase 20's close, and filed rather than fixed because the repair is a design decision rather than an edit. MEASURED: `STATUS.md` is 30,628 bytes over 61 lines; nine of its sixteen bullets exceed 400 characters and the longest is 4,960 characters on one line (`STATUS.md:31`, the active-plan bullet), with 18,874 of the file's bytes inside bullets. THE RULE IT DEFEATS IS AGENTS.md'S OWN, and the rule states its reason: "**The limit is bullet count, not line count** … and **one item per line, never wrapped**. A line cap was being gamed: each pass kept every fact and only re-wrapped the prose, so the file grew into a diary while every edit wasted tokens compressing it. Bullets bound how much there is to say; the one-line rule bounds each item, and forces the choice of what to drop at the moment of writing rather than in a rewrite pass." THE LETTER HOLDS AND THE PURPOSE DOES NOT: `scripts/check-status.mjs` counts bullets per section (`:85`) and rejects a wrapped continuation line (`:93-95`), and it has no cap on a bullet's own length — its self-test at `:146` is named "accepts a long file within the bullet limits" and `:119`'s comment reads "length alone must not fail". So one item can absorb every fact the rule exists to make the writer drop, which is what happened: the diary did not leave, it moved inside the bullets. WHY THE COST IS PAID EVERY SESSION: AGENTS.md opens with "**Start with `STATUS.md`** — a fresh session continues from it alone", so the whole 30 KB is read at every session start, and the file no longer functions as a status — `:31` alone is a phase-by-phase history of the whole plan. WHY IT IS FILED AND NOT FIXED: the cause is named, but the repair is not one owner's — it needs a decision on whether the checker gains a per-bullet length bound (and whether that warns or fails), and on how the nine long bullets are compressed without dropping a fact a later session needs, since the register, the plan and the ledger are the only other places those facts live. That is AGENTS.md's file-it set: the fix needs a design decision and more than one owner could make it. OWNER: `scripts/check-status.mjs` together with `STATUS.md` itself and the AGENTS.md rule that bounds them.

title: The redesign spec numbers its own sections §1–§13, so its own §2, §6 and §7 still claim `DESIGN.md` markers
detail: FOUND BY TASK 21.2'S SEAT (2026-10-17) while declaring the citation source set, and raised as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `c536b25a` rather than folded into it. **THE SAME SHAPE `vg-352` WAS ABOUT, ONE DOCUMENT OVER.** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md` numbers its own sections `§1`–`§13`, so a `§2`, `§6` or `§7` inside it is its own section and still reads as a claim on the matching `DESIGN.md` marker — exactly what the new `CITE_SOURCES` set removes for `requirements.md`. **WHY IT WAS NOT EXCLUDED, AND THE ARGUMENT IS THE ROW'S OWN**: the spec genuinely cites the bible (`§5`, `§7.1`, `§7.8`), so leaving it out of the set is the over-exclusion `vg-352` names as the risk — a set that omits a document that really does cite `DESIGN.md` turns a passing check red. **`vg-352`'s own detail and its ruling disagree about this document and the disagreement is recorded rather than smoothed**: the detail names the spec as a *foreign-numbering* document (`§1`–`§13`) whose numbers must not count, while the ruling names the redesign spec as a member of the set. Task 21.2 resolved toward the ruling, because excluding it is the named risk, and recorded the residual in `docs/decisions/0060` and in `CITE_SOURCES`' own docblock as a **known limit, stated so it is not rediscovered as a defect**. **DORMANT, AND WHY IT IS STILL A ROW**: the measurement Task 21.2 took found **0 of the 18 markers claimed only by one area**, so no marker is currently satisfied only by the spec's own numbering, and the failure needs a marker's genuine citations to be removed while the spec's own section number stays. That is the same dormant shape `vg-352` had. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: a rule for a document that is both about the design language and self-numbering — a declared prefix or an explicit marker convention for its own sections — rather than a decision about membership, since membership is settled and the number is what leaks. OWNER: `scripts/design-md.mjs`'s `CITE_SOURCES` and the spec's own numbering, together.

title: The evidence README states that each capture's two copies are the same bytes and stay that way, and nothing checks it
detail: FOUND BY TASK 21.3'S SEAT (2026-10-17) as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `6952bad4`, while extending the same README's copy table with the freshness columns. **THE CLAIM IS THE README'S OWN**: `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md` says *"The two copies of each capture are the same bytes and stay that way; a drawings-adjacent file that has drifted from its twin is a copy nobody refreshed, not a second render."* Nothing in the repo compares the pair, and the new scanner deliberately does not — it reads the recorded sha and the surface paths, never the copy's bytes, because a byte comparison of two *renders* is ruled out by the recorded measurement that two runs of one capture differ at identical dimensions. **THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT CHECKS AND THAT IS THE POINT**: a capture's render is not reproducible byte-for-byte, but a *copy* of a committed file is — so the copy check compares the drawing-adjacent file to the evidence file, both already on disk, and needs no browser and no render. `vg-402` established one direction of this by hand: `shell-capture-graphite.png` was byte-identical to the pre-re-shoot `shell-palette-graphite-desktop-chromium.png` at sha1sum `1998cbf2ff05a8788687ff23d3498120bc3ef98b`, and when Task 2.5 re-shot the seven the evidence frame moved to `1c0eb8ad9a469888afc64e8e0948522ff935755a` while the copy kept the old bytes. **THE COPY STEP IS MANUAL AND DOCUMENTED**, which is why the claim can be false without anyone noticing: the README's own two-step refresh ends in a `cp`. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a `cmp` over the eleven pairs, as a case in `scripts/capture-freshness.mjs`'s self-test or as its own check — it is cheap, needs no browser, and is a different instrument from the freshness one. OWNER: `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md` and `scripts/capture-freshness.mjs`, together with the eleven pairs the table already lists.

title: The three shell captures' surface sets omit the package that paints the stage they show, so a `scene-fabric` change leaves them reported fresh
detail: FOUND BY TASK 21.3'S SEAT (2026-10-17) while bounding each capture's surface paths, and recorded in `0061`'s limits and in the README's prose rather than guessed at. **THE THREE SHELL FRAMES ARE VIEWPORT SHOTS, NOT SCOPED ONES** — the spec's `captureVisualReview` call carries no `scope`, so the frame is the whole shell including the stage, and the stage's pixels come from `scene-fabric`, which paints the artboard and its objects. **The declared surfaces are `editor-shell/`, `panes/`, `components/ui/`, `card-library.ts` and `ui-copy.ts` — none of which is `scene-fabric`.** So a change to the renderer that visibly moves the stage leaves `shell-capture-add.png`, `shell-capture-graphite.png` and `shell-capture-glyphs.png` reported **fresh**, which is the unsafe direction: the instrument's whole purpose is to notice staleness, and this is a hole in it rather than a conservative choice. **WHY IT WAS NOT BOUNDED**: the stage shows a *scene*, and which of `scene-fabric`'s files a given capture's scene reaches depends on the data the capture mounts, so the honest bound is not a directory list. The seat recorded it rather than writing a plausible list, which is the right half of the trade. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: either a coarser but honest declaration — the package, as one path — or a rule that a viewport-scoped capture names its renderer explicitly; and note that `scene-fabric` is already on the reuse gate's watchlist, so a wrong bound there is expensive in a second way. OWNER: `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md`'s `Surfaces` column and the three shell captures, with `0061` as the note that records the limit.

title: One document holds three instruments and only one of them is a script, so the other two are pasted `node -e` commands that nothing runs
detail: FOUND BY TASK 21.4'S SEAT (2026-10-17) while deciding where the selector instrument lives, and reported as a deliberate omission rather than folded into the task. **THE SAME DOCUMENT, TWO KINDS OF INSTRUMENT.** `docs/architecture/dead-selectors.md` describes three passes: the selector reachability check (§2), a composition pass (§4) and an attribute-value pass. Task 21.4 turned the first into `scripts/dead-selectors.mjs`, with a `--self-test` chained into `gates:self-test` and a live run left as a command; **the other two are still `node -e` one-liners pasted into the prose** (two occurrences remain — §5's *"The composition search"* and §6, *"The second instrument: the attribute values"*), which means they run only when a reader copies them out of a markdown file by hand. **WHY IT WAS NOT WIDENED HERE**: the ruling on `vg-380` names the class direction and nothing else, and widening two further passes would have been a scope decision taken by an implementer rather than by a ruling — the same argument that kept `data-*` on the spelling reading and is recorded in `0062`. **WHY IT IS STILL A ROW**: the document's own stated virtue was *"no script to keep in step with the file it reads"*, and `0062` decided against it for one of the three passes. The document resolves that honestly for the selector pass — *"**The instrument is a script and this document is its reasoning.**"* — and **says nothing about the status of the other two**, so a reader cannot tell whether they are instruments that should be run on a schedule or illustrative one-offs shown once. A pasted command is also un-runnable by a gate, which is the whole reason the first one moved. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: either the same treatment (two more modes on `scripts/dead-selectors.mjs`, or two sibling scripts), or one sentence in the document stating which passes are instruments and which are illustrative — the second is cheap and is the honest minimum if the passes are not worth running on a schedule. **Check the occurrences before trusting this row**: three `node -e` strings are in the file and one of them is prose describing the history, not a command. OWNER: `docs/architecture/dead-selectors.md` together with `scripts/dead-selectors.mjs`.

title: Documents cite line numbers into source files and nothing re-resolves them, so this is the fourth instance of a shape three archived rows each fixed once
detail: FOUND BY TASK 21.5'S SEAT (2026-10-17) as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `c76b9445`, and raised as a class rather than as its four sites because the class is what recurs. **THE INSTANCE THAT SURFACED IT**: `docs/architecture/dead-code-candidates.md`, `docs/product/triage/triage-B6.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-12-the-dead-code-sweep.md` and `vg-386`'s own `detail` all cite line numbers into `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs`, and **they were already off by three at HEAD before Task 21.5 touched the file** — `:705` for `if (prodConsumers.length > 0) continue;`, actually `:708`; and `:531`/`:542`/`:724` for `usesIn`/`usesOutsideDeclaration`/`const ownUses`, actually `:534`/`:545`/`:727`. Task 21.5's change adds 49 and 85 lines of further drift on top, and every future edit to that file adds more. **THE CLASS IS ALREADY THREE ROWS OLD AND EACH WAS CLOSED BY FIXING ONE SITE**: `vg-371` (two comments in `tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts` citing `editor-session.ts` lines that no longer point at the code they name), `vg-432` (a settings DOM test citing `readStorage` by a line that lands on a JSX comment) and `vg-517` (`load-failure.ts`'s `showLoadFailure` comment citing `main.ts` lines that have moved) — all three `verified` in the archive, all three fixed by re-pointing the numbers, none by making the next one impossible. **A line number is a citation that rots on every edit above it, and the repo already has the instrument that could see it**: `scripts/check-doc-references.mjs` resolves a reference into `docs/superpowers/plans/` (decision `0048`, filed as `vg-434`), so the shape exists and simply does not cover `file:line`. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: a rule on whether a citation names a line at all (the cheaper answer — cite the symbol, as the commit-message convention already requires) or whether the resolver gains a `path:line` form that checks the line still contains what the citation says it does. The second is an instrument and the first is a convention; the three closes suggest the convention was never stated, because each fix re-pointed the number rather than removing it. **CHECK THE FOUR SITES BEFORE TRUSTING THE OFFSETS ABOVE**: they were measured at `c76b9445` and the file has changed since. OWNER: `scripts/check-doc-references.mjs` together with the four citing documents and `docs/engineering/`'s citation convention.

title: A decision note's `Paths:` claim is never checked, so 10 claims across 9 notes name files that no longer exist
detail: FOUND BY THE SUBAGENT IMPLEMENTING TASK 21.10 (2026-10-17) AND NOT PART OF IT, filed from its commit trailer. MEASURED AT `a5a2d0ab`. Method: for each `docs/decisions/NNNN-*.md`, take the backticked repo paths on its `- **Paths:**` line and any continuation line, resolve each from the repo root and test it. **63 numbered notes carry 150 claims; 10 of them are dead, across 9 notes and 5 distinct paths** — `renderer-core/src/theme/validate.ts` (notes 0003, 0022, 0023, 0028, 0041), `renderer-core/src/theme/serialize.ts` (0041), `editor/src/selection-inspector/style.ts` (0030), `editor/src/editor-shell/qr-code.tsx` (0032) and `editor/src/components/ui/popover.tsx` (0036, 0037). **THE COUNT IN THE TRAILER DISAGREES WITH THE RECOUNT AND THE RECOUNT IS THE ONE THAT REPRODUCES**: the trailer says 11 notes and names 5 paths "and six more", while the controller's pass finds 10 claims in 9 notes and 5 distinct paths, twice, by two parsers. **THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE SAME SHAPE AS `vg-544`'S, ONE LIST OVER**: a claim on a path that does not exist can never refuse anything, and a path later re-created at one of these names inherits a licence written for a different decision — which is half of why `vg-544`'s watchlist entry was inert, since `0030` still claimed a file `aa5edf96` had deleted. **WHY IT IS NOT DISCHARGED BY `vg-544`'S FIX**: Task 21.10 added an integrity case proving *every watchlist entry names a path that exists*, and that case reads `WATCHLIST`. **Nothing reads the notes' own claims**, so the class is closed on one list and open on the other. **THE FIX IS NOT PRESCRIBED HERE AND HAS A REAL DECISION IN IT**: a check needs a rule for the entry shapes the notes already use — a directory claim, a bare name — before it can be turned on, and `backlog-check.mjs` reads the register while the reuse gate reads `WATCHLIST`, so a claim is a third list with no owner. OWNER: `scripts/` (a check) and `docs/decisions/` (the notes themselves). SEVERITY: low per claim, and it compounds the way `vg-544` did. FILED, NOT FIXED, and the reason is the register's own rule: the fix is not the task being done, and it spans a list whose owner is not established.

title: The dead-code sweep's own report names its source as a file with an unresolved import, because an inline fixture string is read as a real specifier
detail: FOUND BY TASK 21.8'S SEAT (2026-10-17) as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `b7b5c29d`, and filed from it. MEASURED AT `b7b5c29d` IN THE SWEEP'S OWN `--json` REPORT. `unresolvedRelativeSpecifiers` carries six entries and the first is `{"from": "scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs", "spec": "./x"}` — **the sweep reporting its own source as a file whose relative import it could not resolve, where no such import exists.** **THE CAUSE IS THE SELF-TEST'S OWN FIXTURE**: the `readsOutsideDeclaration` check holds an inline string containing a `from "./x"` shape, the scan reads the sweep's own `scripts/` directory, and the literal is taken for a real specifier. **THE FIELD'S OWN TEXT IS WHAT MAKES IT A DEFECT RATHER THAN NOISE**: the report's own note and the field's docblock say each entry names a file whose importer is hidden from the analysis, so a false entry is a claim about a file that is not true — and it is a claim the sweep makes about itself. **THE FIX IS THE SHAPE TASK 21.8 ALREADY INTRODUCED**: an `importFrom(names, spec)` helper builds a fixture's import line from its parts, so the literal never appears in the sweep's own source. The seat used it for the new fixture and did not retrofit the older inline one. **PRE-EXISTING AT THE BASE, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED**: the report is byte-identical between `07dd4676` and `b7b5c29d`, verified by the controller with a `git worktree` at the base and `cmp`, so Task 21.8 neither caused nor fixed it. OWNER: `scripts/`. SEVERITY: low — one wrong entry in a report nothing gates on, and it costs a reader who trusts the report one false belief about the sweep's own imports. FILED, NOT FIXED, and the reason is the register's own rule: it is not the task being done, and the sweep's report is the artifact the task itself was measuring.

title: Starter template navigation can reopen the latest saved theme, and the user cannot select starter for phone publishing
detail: Reported by the user on 2026-10-17 while opening the editor and testing publish-to-phone: starter is no longer the initial theme and cannot be selected for phone publishing. Exact URL, replacement theme and selection surface are not yet established; controller asked whether selection means editor File/Open or phone theme list. SOURCE MEASUREMENT at ca9dbd45: boot-theme.ts intentionally resumes latest saved document on bare /editor/, the policy archived vg-060 owns; host/public/theme-list.js starter-template entry links that same bare /editor/, so selecting the starter entry can resume saved work rather than explicitly requesting starter. Route mismatch established in source; user's exact runtime cause and end-to-end reproduction remain unestablished. Phone publishing requires stored library identity, and editor-session.ts refuses a document without library base; do not bypass asset-safety contract.
