title: `tsconfig.e2e.json` resolves Node's types through the host's private install path, so a hoisting change reddens `typecheck` for no source reason
detail: FOUND BY TASK 22.3'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW on 2026-10-17 and filed by the controller rather than fixed in that task, because the durable fix is a manifest decision the task's brief reserved. `src/web/tsconfig.e2e.json` names `"types": ["./packages/host/node_modules/@types/node"]`, and the reviewer established with a fresh `npm ci` in its own worktree that this is not an artefact of the implementer's junctioned `node_modules`: `@types/node` is installed only under `packages/host`, there is no `node` entry under `src/web/node_modules/@types/`, and there is no repository-root `node_modules`, so the obvious `"types": ["node"]` does not resolve from `src/web` today. The program does load the types — 61 files under that path appear in `--listFilesOnly`, and `Buffer` type-checks in the specs. FAILING SCENARIO, with the failure shape reproduced against a scratch config: any hoisting change — a `@types/node` version bump that unifies with a transitive dependency, a lockfile or registry change, a different npm major — makes the relative entry resolve to nothing, and `npm run typecheck` exits 1 with `error TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for './packages/host/node_modules/@types/node'`, for a reason unrelated to any source change. THE DURABLE OWNER is a root `devDependency` on `@types/node`, which also needs the licence check and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` plus `docs/engineering/dependencies.md` updates that any new shipped dependency requires. NOT ESTABLISHED: which npm change would actually break it on this box, since the current layout is measured rather than predicted. OWNER: `src/web/tsconfig.e2e.json`, `src/web/package.json`, `src/web/package-lock.json` (via `npm install`, never hand-edited).

title: Each display client holds its own theme and its own theme-specific settings
detail: RULED 2026-10-17 while the user reviewed the theme store spec: the app is to serve multiple display clients, each with their own theme and that theme's own settings, and the store's activation is built per-display from the start rather than against the single-theme model and reworked later. TODAY THERE IS ONE THEME PER HOST: `host/src/settings/active-theme.ts` stores a single id in `active-theme.json`, `/api/themes/active` reads and writes that one, and `host/public/library.html` chooses the theme your displays should show. `host/src/settings/theme-settings.ts` keys its answers by theme id alone, so an answer cannot belong to one display's use of a theme. WHAT THIS OWES: its own spec, which LANDS FIRST because the theme store's local tab assigns a theme to a display and cannot be built against a model that does not exist; then the per-display map replacing `active-theme.json`; the `/api/themes/active` shape change; and the answer key becoming theme-and-display rather than theme. WHAT IT DOES NOT OWN: the theme store spec consumes this spec's assign action and does not restate its model, and the mode that shows a display and which theme it has belongs to that spec's Host settings mode. Filed by the store spec's revision, which names this spec as the first thing its own work owes.

title: Phase 24's acceptance for vg-388 asks for all three kinds while the theme store spec ships one
detail: FOUND 2026-10-17 by the agent while reviewing the theme store spec. `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md`'s Phase 24 acceptance reads that vg-388's store carries all three kinds as specified rather than the theme half alone, and its failure modes say reading vg-388 as the theme half only is superseded by the 2026-10-16 revision. **The revision superseded the scope line, not the shipping set**: `2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md` still ships the dashboard theme only, with a widget-preset addendum and an editor-theme addendum, because only the dashboard theme has an exchange unit today (ADR-0004/0017, sections 139/141, and the bounds in `host/src/themes/store.ts`). So the row cannot close on v1 as the plan words it. The spec's own acceptance section now records the closure condition as the storefront plus the dashboard theme, with the two addenda as rows of their own. WHAT IS LEFT IS THE PLAN'S OWN TEXT, which is a contract and not the spec's to edit: its acceptance line and its failure-mode line must be propagated together, or vg-388 stays open against work that is finished. Needs the user's word, because it changes a row's closure condition.

title: The chart refresh loop re-arms requestAnimationFrame every frame, so a display set to 1 fps still wakes the process ~60 times a second
detail: FOUND BY AN AGENT on 2026-10-18 while designing the host's own monitors (`vg-574`'s spec, the local-monitor section), and filed rather than fixed because it is not that task. THE DEFECT, read from source: `scene-fabric/src/chart-refresh.ts`'s `tick` calls `frames.requestFrame(tick)` on EVERY frame and only then tests whether the rate interval has elapsed — `if (lastRefreshMs !== undefined && nowMs - lastRefreshMs < 1_000 / rate) return;`. So the loop is a busy animation-frame loop whose body is usually an early return. At `ChartRefreshRate = 30` that is ~60 wakeups a second to paint 30 times; at rate 1 it is still ~60 wakeups a second to paint once. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: a rAF loop that never stops keeps the page from going idle, which keeps the compositor and the GPU process resident and stops the browser from reaching its own low-power states. This product's whole subject is a machine's load, so a display that wakes a process 60 times a second to decide to do nothing is the app becoming the thing it reports on. THE MOUNT SITES, both verified: `player/src/main.ts` calls `startChartRefresh(refresh, 30, ...)` — the player is what runs on a wall display, and it starts at the *higher* rate — and `editor/src/editor-main.ts` calls it with a rate the author can set through `setChartRefreshRate`. THE FIX IS SMALL AND NOT OBVIOUS, which is why it is a row and not a one-liner: at rate 1 the loop should be a `setInterval` so the browser can idle between updates, while rAF stays right for 30 because a 30 fps repaint wants frame alignment. That means the scheduler has two modes rather than one, and `setRate` has to switch between them without dropping or double-arming a timer — which is exactly what `chart-refresh.test.ts` already exercises for the single-mode version and would need extending for two. UNMEASURED: the actual wakeup count and the power difference were read from the source, not profiled, and the relative cost of this against engine baseline, device pixel ratio and GPU residency is unknown. A profile of one wall display at rate 1 is what should decide the change rather than the reading. RELATED: `vg-577` (the player as a PWA) is where a display's own idle behaviour would be settled, and `vg-576`'s keep-awake is the opposite pressure — a display that must not sleep while showing a theme that must not spin.

title: The design-token and CSS-size checks read only .ts, .tsx and .css, so a literal moved into an .html file is invisible to both while one of them claims otherwise
detail: FOUND BY TASK 25.3'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW on 2026-10-18, while deciding whether that task had evaded a gate or merely placed its CSS correctly. THE MEASUREMENT, which is what makes this a defect rather than a worry: `scripts/design-tokens.mjs`'s remainder walk reads `src/web/packages/*/src` with suffixes `[".ts", ".tsx"]` only (line 452), so `index.html` is read by no half of that gate — yet the same script's own comment at line 430 says the rule holds "wherever it lives". Running the gate's `check()` over the player's `index.html` produced **9 violations the gate cannot see**: eight introduced by Task 25.3 (`#000` for the dimmer, `#e8ecf3` three times, `#14161c`, `#3a2a00`, `#c3cde3` and an `84px`) plus one pre-existing `#000`. The ceiling was met by moving eight literals out of a file the gate reads and into one it never reads, not by consuming a token. The placement itself is legitimate and was ruled so — `index.html` already owned the player's chrome CSS, the player loads no token stylesheet at all, and the plan named the file — but the gate's guarantee is narrower than its comment claims, and the next reader will believe the comment. THE SAME BLIND SPOT IN A SECOND CHECK: `packages/player/scripts/check-size.mjs:68` counts only files whose extension is `.css` inside `dist`, so the player's CSS budget reported `CSS 0.0 KB` for a commit that added eight colour literals and an inline stylesheet to `index.html` — the budget cannot see the styles it is budgeting. WHAT IT OWES: either the two checks read `.html` as well, or the comment in `design-tokens.mjs` stops promising more than the walk delivers and the player's budget says which files it covers — and whichever is chosen, the answer is written where the next reader meets it. MINOR, same review, not worth its own row: the browser case's `lanAddress()` picks the first non-internal IPv4 and fails rather than skipping when that is a VPN or Hyper-V adapter, which is correct here (`192.168.2.56` first) and fragile on another box. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether either gate was written with `.html` deliberately out of scope, since neither says so. OWNER: `scripts/design-tokens.mjs`, `src/web/packages/player/scripts/check-size.mjs`.

title: The chart's overscan gutter is a quarter inside the axis range, so the newest sample sits inside the visible right edge on a fifth of frames
detail: FOUND BY TASK 25.4'S PER-FRAME PROBE while measuring `vg-571`, and filed rather than carried because it is a different owner with its own decision note to write. THE CAUSE, AS AN INDEPENDENT REVIEW MEASURED IT: the baseline is geometry, not the axis label. `scene-fabric/src/chart-object.ts`'s `_overscanWidth` (line 283) sizes the extra canvas it blits past the visible surface from `option.grid.left` and `option.grid.right` (lines 300-304), while the axis is laid out over the visible surface PLUS that gutter, so `xAxis.max` lands about 24 px inside the 32 px gutter (measured `pxMax` 1950 against the crop edge at the visible width 1926) and the delay band the gutter means to hide is exposed by that much whatever any label does. THE FIRST READING ATTRIBUTED THIS TO THE LABEL AND WAS WRONG: it claimed ECharts widens the plot to contain the last axis label (`outerBoundsContain: "axisLabel"`) and that the label's width is what moves the inset. Measured, `pxMax` equals `canvasWidth − grid.right` (1958 − 8) on 90-92 % of steady frames — no label inset applied at all — and at that geometry the crop edge is already `axisMax − 767 ms` with 20.2/20.0/22.8 % of those frames exposing the newest sample; the label's own widest frames sit at +93/+97 ms and so REDUCE the exposure rather than creating it. THE MEASUREMENT, from `tests/e2e/live-chart-edge.spec.ts` on the built player bundle at 412x839 against the real host: the crop lands at `axisMax − 767 ms` median against the 1 000 ms the code assumes, with per-frame p05 −767 ms and p95 −357 ms; the newest sample is inside the visible right edge on about a fifth of steady-state frames (19.8/21.0/26.6/24.9 % across four readings), by up to 285 ms (≈4.5 CSS px) and 1 244 ms (≈19.5 CSS px). WHAT THE FIX OWES: the engine's own grid rect rather than `grid.right`, since recomputing the layout here would be a second model of one ECharts already did; solving for the fixed point gives a gutter of about 40 px rather than 32, which puts the crop edge back at `axisMax − 1000`. `scene-fabric/src/chart-object.ts` is a REUSE-GATE MECHANISM BOUNDARY in `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`, so the decision note claiming that path lands before the first write. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the ≈19.5 px worst case is one frame or a repeating state, since the readings cover four runs; and whether the left edge's own residual is worth a second look — 16-19.5 % of steady frames hold no sample at or below the axis minimum, which is the host's cadence rather than the window, since measured cadence runs p50 1005-1026 ms and max 1869-3243 ms against the 1 000 ms `DEFAULT_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_MS` declares. READER: `tests/e2e/live-chart-edge.spec.ts`, which writes JSON to `%TEMP%/yunari-live-edge/` and, after the Task 25.4 review, runs only with `YUNARI_EDGE_PROBE` set; nothing else in the repo reads it, so re-run it here rather than trusting a stale reading. OWNER: `src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/chart-object.ts`.

title: The player's brightness control dims the picture because no browser can set a phone's panel brightness, so real device control needs a native player app
detail: FOUND BY THE USER on 2026-10-18, correcting the control Task 25.3 built: "By brightness control slider I meant control the phone screen brightness, not artificially dimming the Artboard". ASKED TO CHOOSE what the control should become, they answered: keep the picture dimmer for now, and record a native player app as the path to real device control. WHY THE WEB CANNOT DO IT: no browser API sets a display's panel brightness, and a PWA is still a page, so installation and a secure origin change nothing — `vg-580` and Task 25.6 do not unlock it. Measured on this box rather than assumed: TypeScript's DOM lib (`lib.dom.d.ts`) has ZERO brightness members, its one match being SVG `mask-type` prose, while `wakeLock` appears three times — the standard surface has a wake lock and no brightness. (Live web search was unavailable in the session that checked, so this is the DOM surface plus that session's own knowledge, not a citation.) The real control exists only natively: Android's `WindowManager.LayoutParams.screenBrightness` or `Settings.System.SCREEN_BRIGHTNESS` with WRITE_SETTINGS, and iOS's `UIScreen.brightness`. WHAT THE WEB CONTROL STAYS AS: `display-controls.ts`'s dimmer is an overlay over the painted picture with a ceiling of 0.85, and `ui-copy.ts` already labels it 'Dim the display — an overlay over the picture, not the screen's own brightness'. The user ruled that it stays, so that wording is not to be softened into a claim of screen brightness, and the control is not to be presented as the feature that was asked for. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a native app is wanted as an objective at all, what it would be built with, and which other device-level controls it should own — the Screen Wake Lock API's refusals, and a dimmer that survives the page being hidden, are the named candidates. OWNER: none yet; a recorded objective rather than a planned task. MEASURED 2026-10-20 on the owner's Windows 11 box: the web platform has no brightness API to gate - Firefox's screen.mozBrightness is deprecated and pref-gated, and the WICG Screen Brightness API proposal was never shipped and could only ever increase brightness through an auto-released sentinel, never set a level - and the platform path on this machine is empty too: root/WMI WmiMonitorBrightness and WmiMonitorBrightnessMethods both enumerate zero instances for the one attached monitor (AOC P27QBB-RA), so a host-side DDC/CI helper would not move that panel through WMI today. Real brightness therefore needs native code on both sides: the OS API on a phone or tablet, and on a desktop either a monitor whose OSD enables DDC/CI or a native shell. TWO FOLLOW-UPS ASKED AND ANSWERED 2026-10-20, both native-only: (a) set max brightness - the W3C/WICG Screen Brightness API (screen.requestBrightnessIncrease) was never shipped in any browser and could only raise brightness through an auto-released sentinel, never set a level, so secure context is not the missing piece; (b) disable adaptive brightness while the player is focused - no web API exists, and the Ambient Light Sensor API only reads light. The native shape for (b) is a per-window brightness override rather than a system setting: Android WindowManager.LayoutParams.screenBrightness pins the window and reverts when it loses focus, which is exactly the temporary, focus-scoped behaviour asked for, with no WRITE_SETTINGS permission needed.

title: The player listens only to the host ResizeObserver, so browser chrome that overlays the layout viewport instead of resizing it would move nothing and could cover the composition
detail: FILED FROM TASK 25.5'S COMMIT TRAILER while measuring `vg-572`, and filed rather than carried because it is a different question from the one that task answered. WHAT WAS MEASURED: a height change driven with `page.setViewportSize` re-fits the display correctly and returns it exactly, and `player/src/main.ts` re-fits from the host `ResizeObserver` alone — nothing in the player watches `visualViewport`, `window.innerHeight` or any other signal. WHAT FOLLOWS, AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED: browser chrome that OVERLAYS the layout viewport rather than resizing it — the shape mobile browsers take while scrolling — would change no box that observer sees, so the composition would neither move nor make room for it, and the chrome could sit over the picture. Whether any phone actually does that, and whether it is visible enough to matter, is unmeasured: Task 25.5 drove a layout-viewport resize on desktop Chromium and says so. OWNER: `player/src/main.ts`.

title: `main.dom.test.ts`'s display-replacement case timed out at 20 s in one full gate run and passed in isolation and on re-run
detail: FOUND BY TASK 25.5'S SEAT during an `npm run gate` on 2026-10-18, and filed rather than fixed because the cause is not established: the case `replaces the display that was already drawn` in `packages/player/src/main.dom.test.ts` failed with `Test timed out in 20000ms`. The run it failed in took 153 s against 104 s for the gate run before it, the file passes in isolation, and the re-run is green — so the shape is a timing-sensitive case on a loaded machine rather than a reproducible defect, and the seat's own change was comments in a Playwright spec that `vitest` does not collect. NOT ESTABLISHED: which wait in the case is unbounded or under-bounded; whether another session or a browser suite sharing the machine is what pushed it over; and whether the 20 s budget is simply too small for this case under load. HOW TO MEASURE IT, because `AGENTS.md` warns that a long browser run holds the machine and that a single sample of a flaky spec is not a measurement: take the case's own timing distribution under load, and compare a previous sample of the same commit against a later one before changing anything. OWNER: `src/web/packages/player/src/main.dom.test.ts`. SECOND SAMPLE 2026-10-18, by the controller during Task 23.3's integrated-tree gate: the same case `replaces the display that was already drawn` failed again with `Test timed out in 20000ms` on the first of two `npm run gate` runs (exit 1, 264 files passed and 1 failed, 3505 of 3506 tests), passed in isolation immediately after (`npx vitest run packages/player/src/main.dom.test.ts`, exit 0), and the second gate run of the identical tree was green (exit 0, 265 files, 3506 tests). **Two samples of one case is what makes it a case rather than a busy box** — the first was Task 25.5's — and the measured shape is the same both times: red in a full run, green alone. The commit under test touches `renderer-core`'s envelope loader and comments in the editor, nothing in `packages/player/src/`.

title: `artboard-crop.ts`'s `outsideEdges` and `outsideBoxes` have no production consumer since the crop notice went
detail: FOUND BY TASK 25.7'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW while checking whether a live assertion had been deleted with a dead one, and filed rather than deleted because `AGENTS.md`'s own rule is detection before deletion and a survivor is cheap where a wrong deletion is not. WHAT WAS MEASURED: `scene-fabric/src/artboard-crop.ts` exports `outsideEdges` and `outsideBoxes`, and after the notice's removal the only readers left are the package barrel and one test — `outsideCount` is the sole production consumer of the counting work. The functions are not wrong and not unreachable from outside the package; they are simply unread by the product. WHAT A SWEEP OWES: one pass over the package's exports for anything else the notice's removal orphaned, so this is closed as part of a set rather than one symbol at a time. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the editor's artboard panel or a planned surface would want them, which is why they are a row and not a deletion. OWNER: `src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/artboard-crop.ts`.

title: Nothing points a display at the host's secure origin, because the surfaces that advertise how to connect belong to the pairing and display-session spec
detail: RULED BY THE USER on 2026-10-18, mid-flight during Task 25.8: "Leave the pairing & connection management to the other queued spec". Task 25.8's measurement had found the scheme hardcoded `http://` in six places, and the brief for its implementation half told the seat to move all six to https — which is pairing and connection management, and belongs to `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-per-display-themes-design.md` and its plan, the owners of the pairing route, the display sessions and `host/src/session/pairing.ts`. The seat was told to drop that work and to touch none of the six, not even to change the scheme. THE SIX, for whoever picks this up: `host/src/main.ts`'s printed URL, its LAN banner, its console pairing link and its revoke curl; `editor/src/hosting-client.ts`'s `displayUrl`; and `editor/src/editor-shell/publish-control.tsx`'s phone address. WHAT THIS ROW IS: the handoff, recorded so the split is visible rather than discovered. When the host serves a secure origin and nothing advertises it, a display following the printed link reaches the origin that cannot hold a wake lock and cannot register a service worker — the two capabilities the user ruled for. WHAT THE PAIRING SPEC NEEDS FROM TASK 25.8, to be filled in from its report: the certificate's SAN, how a changed DHCP address is handled, how a display is expected to obtain the CA root, and whether the host keeps serving plain http alongside. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether that spec's own plan already carries this integration, or whether it needs a task added. OWNER: the pairing and display-session surfaces named above. THE PROSE THIS SPLIT LEFT FALSE, found by the independent review of Task 25.8b: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-per-display-themes-design.md` (four places) and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-per-display-themes.md` (two lines) still assert the host is `http.createServer` with no TLS and that a paired display reaches it over plain http. The host now serves https beside http on the same port from a CA it mints itself (`docs/decisions/0070`, Task 25.8b). That prose is that spec's and is corrected with it, not from here: the controller left it alone rather than editing a plan another session owns. ONE MORE THING THIS SPEC OWNS, filed separately because it is a different failure: an installed display launches at the host's root with no session and is refused with 403 — `vg-588`. It was found by the independent review of Task 25.6, which is where the install landed.

title: An installed display launches at the host's root, which the host refuses: the app works offline and is refused online
detail: FOUND BY THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF TASK 25.6 on 2026-10-18, and it is the one thing that decides whether the user's request was met. The request was "Make the player a pwa webapp" for a phone display (`vg-577`); the install now exists, and what it installs into does not work. MEASURED, on a real host bound to the LAN with a persistent headed Chromium: `packages/player/public/manifest.webmanifest` sets `"start_url": "/"`, and `/` is refused to an unpaired reader by `host/src/server.ts`'s pairing guard with **403** `This display is not paired with the host.` A session is only ever an `x-yunari-session` header or a `?session=` query (`server.ts`'s `allowed()` — no cookie), so an installed launch, which is a bare origin navigation, carries none. The same launch with the network gone renders the cached shell and the player's own failure page — so the app is usable offline and refused online, the exact inverse of what a wall display needs. **Omitting `start_url` is not the alternative it looks like**: measured on Chromium 153.0.8010.12, a manifest without one reports `installabilityErrors: [{errorId: "start-url-not-valid"}]` and fires no `beforeinstallprompt`, so the design is forced and the fix is not in the manifest. NOT THIS TASK'S DEFECT: Task 25.6's brief required the implementer to say what the app launches into, and `docs/decisions/0071` says it plainly. WHAT IS WRONG IS WHERE IT WAS LEFT: the note hands the gap to `vg-587`, and `vg-587` did not carry it — its subject is the scheme in six advertising surfaces — so until this row the gap lived only in a decision note and a reader picking up the handoff would not have found it. OWNER: the pairing and display-session surfaces, with the per-display-themes spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-per-display-themes-design.md`) and its plan, which the user ruled on 2026-10-18 own how a display obtains and keeps a session. THE QUESTION IT PUTS TO THEM: what an installed app's first navigation carries, and whether a paired display gets a durable identity rather than a token in a URL — the answer decides `start_url`, which is why it is not being guessed here.

title: The display's service worker caches every asset it fetches and nothing ever evicts one, so the shell cache grows with every build
detail: FOUND BY THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF TASK 25.6 on 2026-10-18. `packages/player/public/sw.js` fixes its cache name at `yunari-shell-v1` and caches every `/assets/**` response it serves, and nothing bounds the set: the `activate` handler deletes only *differently named* `yunari-*` caches, so entries accumulate inside the one cache across every deployment. A wall display is a device that runs for months and is redeployed repeatedly, and each build adds a fresh content-hashed copy of the bundle — the reviewer measured `index-*.js` at 335 KB and `echarts-*.js` at 558 KB, and their source maps if ever fetched. The only eviction path today is renaming `SHELL_CACHE` by hand, which no trigger is tied to. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX IN TASK 25.6: the cause is established and the owner is one file, but the policy is a decision nobody has measured against — how often a display is redeployed, whether the shell should be versioned by build (the worker is plain JavaScript copied verbatim from `public/`, so there is no build hash in it today), or whether a simple bound on the number of cached entries is enough. NOT ESTABLISHED: how large the cache actually grows on a real display, since no display has been redeployed against it. OWNER: `packages/player/public/sw.js`.

title: A unit case in the theme store timed out under a loaded box and passes alone, which is the second file to do it
detail: FOUND BY TASK 22.6's SEAT on 2026-10-18, on a gate run taken while a headed browser suite was holding the machine. `packages/host/src/themes/store.test.ts`'s `ThemeStore asset bounds > holds read and write to the same asset count` failed with `Test timed out in 20000ms`; re-run alone on the same tree it passed, 57 cases in 2.19s, and the gate then exited 0. The file is untouched by that task's change. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN SHRUGGED OFF: this is the second file to redden this way, and the first is `vg-585` (`main.dom.test.ts`'s display-replacement case), which the same reasoning would have called load and left alone. Two files is the point at which 'the box was busy' stops being an explanation for one case and becomes a question about the suite's timeouts under `gate` — which runs 264 files through 263 spawned workers while a headed Chromium suite may be running beside it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the timeout is the case's own cost or the worker's startup under contention, whether 20 s is the suite's own budget or a default, and how often it recurs — one sample of a flaky case is not a measurement, and a second sample of the same commit is what would make it one. OWNER: `packages/host/src/themes/store.test.ts` and whatever owns the unit suite's timeout budget. SECOND SAMPLE, 2026-10-18, taken by the controller while integrating Task 22.8: the same case, `holds read and write to the same asset count` at `store.test.ts:1467`, timed out again on a `npm run gate` — `Test timed out in 20080ms`, with the other 3484 cases green and a re-run exiting 0. That is a second observation of the same case on a different tree and from a different session, so the flake is reproducible rather than one seat's bad luck, and the two samples now point at the case's own cost under contention rather than at anything the box was doing. The second run also narrows the shape: the suite reports 263 of 264 files passing with one file red, so a reader of a red gate should check this case first before reading the failure as a defect in whatever was just committed.

title: The copy reader reads no bare span and skips every button with aria-controls, so the publish popover's warning and its trigger word are owned by nothing
detail: FOUND BY TASK 22.9'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-18), by probe rather than by reading. Replacing `{uiCopy.publish.warning}` in `publish-control.tsx`'s `<span id="yunari-publish-warning">` with a literal leaves all three copy nets green, and so does a literal on the popover's trigger. **Two mechanisms, both in `ui-copy-readers.ts`'s `spokenIn`.** The warning is a bare `<span>`, and the reader's vocabulary is labels, accessible names, buttons, headings and definition terms — it reads no span. The trigger carries `aria-controls`, which Base UI sets on a popover's open trigger, and the button loop skips `button[aria-controls]` — **a skip with no stated reason anywhere in the file**, which is the shape `vg-417` warns about: a carve-out whose width no reader can check. It is wider than any reason it has, because it also drops a converted select's trigger, every tab and every disclosure button. **This is `vg-418`'s class left live in one of the four surfaces it mounted**, and Task 22.9 states the limit in `ui-copy-surfaces.test.ts`'s header rather than implying coverage, so the row is the owner. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: which element kinds carry words rather than readings — a span in a popover prints copy, a span in the publish live row prints a theme name — and which `aria-controls` buttons print a word rather than a chosen value. That is a decision about the reader's vocabulary, which is why Task 22.9 did not narrow the skip in a fix round. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: whether any other mounted surface's words are dropped the same way. NEAR ROWS: vg-418 (closed), vg-335, vg-417. OWNER: `packages/editor/src/ui-copy-readers.ts` (`spokenIn`). SEVERITY: low — a coverage hole in an instrument, proved by two green literal runs.

title: The copy walk calls every function with one argument, so a composed sentence over a dynamic value is collected by nothing and a surface printing one goes falsely red
detail: FOUND BY TASK 22.9'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-18), and it is `vg-417`'s exact shape one paragraph above that row's fix. `copy()`'s probe calls each function entry with **one** argument, so a function of two or more receives `undefined` for the rest and the sentence it composes is collected by nothing. Measured: `copy()` holds neither `panels.artboardOutside("A rule.", 3, 5)` (`"3 of 5 objects are now outside the artboard and will not be shown on a display. A rule."`) nor `draftRecovery.lead("My theme", "today")` (`"My theme was edited and not saved. This browser kept a copy written today."`), and both are rendered by real surfaces (`artboard-fields.tsx`, `draft-recovery-prompt.tsx`). **CONSEQUENCE, AND ITS DIRECTION**: the same safe direction `vg-417` has — a surface printing one goes falsely **red** rather than falsely green — which is why the row is low and why it still needs fixing. **WIDENING THE PROBE CANNOT CLOSE IT**, and that is the part worth keeping: a sentence interpolating the theme's own name can never equal a probe's output, so the net cannot be made to own these strings by passing more arguments. Task 22.9 therefore made `copy()`'s docblock state the limit — it had claimed the argument shapes "yield a superset of what they show", which `vg-417` had already falsified for keys and the review falsified for arity — and filed this row rather than pretending the claim. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: whether these two sentences move into the table as functions the surfaces call with the same values the probe would, or the net grows a comparison that tolerates an interpolated value. NEAR ROWS: vg-417 (closed), vg-591. OWNER: `packages/editor/src/ui-copy-readers.ts` (`copy()`). SEVERITY: low — latent, and it fails closed.

title: The selection lead's glass-refusal paragraph prints a table sentence outside the walk's shell root, so no copy net reads it
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 22.9'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-18), answering the question `vg-417` recorded as not established. **A surface does print a `glassRefusals` sentence today**: `selection-inspector/glass.ts` calls `glassRefused(kindOf(object))` and `selection-lead.tsx` renders it in a `

`, so a `document.body.textContent` read of the walk's own mounted tree contains "Text is not a panel, and there is no surface behind a glyph to frost." **No net sees it**, because the walk mounts the inspector outside the `shellRoot` its paragraphs are read from, and the carve-out that limits the read to the shell's own paragraphs states a reason ("data in paragraphs of their own") that does not describe a sentence from the table. **The consequence is the opposite of `vg-417`'s and that is the point**: with the keyed pass disabled only `ui-copy.test.ts` reddens, while the surfaces and panels nets stay green over a live surface printing a table sentence. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: whether the walk's paragraph read should follow the mounted tree rather than the shell root, or whether the refusal paragraph is a reading the net deliberately does not own. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: how many other paragraphs outside the shell root print table sentences. NEAR ROWS: vg-417 (closed), vg-335. OWNER: `packages/editor/src/ui-copy-surfaces.test.ts` (the walk's root) with `packages/editor/src/selection-inspector/selection-lead.tsx`. SEVERITY: low — a coverage hole, with a live instance found.

title: The library chooser's leads and its Delete label are literals beside the dialog rather than in the copy table, and Delete passes only because the table holds the same word
detail: FOUND BY TASK 22.9'S SEAT AND CONFIRMED BY ITS REVIEW (2026-10-18), on the library dialog that task mounted. `theme-library-dialog.tsx` holds `DELETE_LEAD`, `CONFLICT_LEAD_TEXT` and `DELETE_LABEL` as literals beside the dialog rather than in `ui-copy.ts`, and its `confirmWords` composes a lead with the theme's own name. **`DELETE_LABEL` is the live half**: it is rendered by the mounted chooser and the walk passes only because `uiCopy.actions.delete` happens to be the same word — change the button's word and the table's in one direction only and nothing reddens. **The reason the seat gave for the confirmation dialog not being mounted is too strong**, and the review said so: a composed sentence does not defeat the net as written, because the table already owns composed sentences as functions (`publish.live`, `statusBar.objects`, `draftRecovery.lead`). The real obstacle is that these strings were placed beside the dialog deliberately, by their own comments, so moving them is a decision rather than a fix. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: whether a dialog's lead is copy the table owns or a sentence the dialog owns, decided once for every dialog rather than per string. NEAR ROWS: vg-418 (closed), vg-338, vg-591. OWNER: `packages/editor/src/theme-library-dialog.tsx`. SEVERITY: low — one accidental pass and two unowned literals.

title: The shared editor preview reuses an existing server, so a browser proof on 4174 can be served by another worktree's dist and read green
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE VERIFYING TASK 22.10 (2026-10-18), by being fooled. `playwright.config.ts` starts the editor preview as `npx vite preview packages/editor --port 4174 --strictPort --host 127.0.0.1` with `reuseExistingServer: true`. A preview server left running by another seat — from another worktree, over that worktree's own `dist` — therefore answers the shared port, and a run started in the primary tree measures **somebody else's bundle**. **It produced a false green in the controller's own hands**: the red proof for `vg-438` was run against a `dist` built by `npm run build` alone, which has no `control-fixture.html`, and it reported `1 passed (2.9s)` — because a stale server from the seat's worktree (pid 27304, started 14:31) was serving that worktree's `dist`, where the fixture had been built. Killing the server and re-running the same command reddened correctly. **The config already knows this class**: it excludes the rebuild and display specs from this config precisely so they cannot arrive at the shared 4174 server, and the rebuild runs its own preview on its own port — so the hazard is a known one that the shared preview still carries. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: whether the shared preview should refuse a server it did not start (a lockfile, a build hash in the URL, or `reuseExistingServer: false` with the startup cost accepted), or whether a seat's own preview should never outlive the seat. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: how often this has already happened — any browser proof in this phase taken while another seat's preview was up is suspect, and nothing records which server answered. NEAR ROWS: vg-438 (closed), vg-216 (a shared artifact dir, the same class). OWNER: `playwright.config.ts` (the 4174 `webServer` entry). SEVERITY: medium — it silently invalidates browser proofs rather than failing them, and a proof is the product here.

title: readLanSource cannot tell a default route that was read from systeminformation's own fallback, so the tie-break warning is suppressed on a machine whose route query fails
detail: FOUND BY TASK 23.1'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-18), by refuting the implementer's own docblock. That docblock claimed a failed query yields `undefined`; **it does not**. Measured with `execSync` blocked so the platform query cannot run at all, `systeminformation.networkInterfaceDefault()` still returns a name — this machine answers `"Npcap Loopback Adapter"` — because before its platform block it has already picked a fallback from the adapters themselves (the lowest IPv6 `scopeid`, else the first non-internal one) and its `catch` is `util.noop()`. `""` comes back only when there is no non-internal interface at all. **CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THIS ROW'S OWN CLASS**: `readLanSource` maps `""` to `undefined` and passes any other name through, so on a machine whose route query fails **and** whose fallback name is a surviving candidate, `rankLanAddresses` reads that name as "the route decided it", returns `alternatives: []`, and `lanAddress`'s warning — the ruling's step 4, the one thing that makes a wrong pick findable without a phone — is silently suppressed. On the machine this was measured on the fallback happens to be virtual and therefore filtered, which is why it degrades correctly there and not in general. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: reading the default route where the host can tell success from failure — a routing-table read of its own, or a check that the returned name actually carries a default route — weighed against rung 7 (the ruling already chose the dependency over a hand-rolled parse). **NOT ESTABLISHED**: whether any real machine reaches this; the fallback path is proved from `systeminformation`'s source and by a forced failure, not by a machine whose fallback is physical. NEAR ROWS: vg-171 (closed), vg-597. OWNER: `packages/host/src/cli/net.ts` (`readLanSource`). SEVERITY: low — latent, and it fails toward the old behaviour rather than toward a wrong address.

title: Every GET /api/hosting runs netstat -r through execSync, blocking the host's event loop for 126-149 ms and spawning a child process
detail: FOUND BY TASK 23.1'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-18), measured rather than argued. `readLanSource` calls `systeminformation.networkInterfaceDefault()`, and that call is **synchronous inside the promise body** — it runs `netstat -r` through `execSync` — so it blocks the event loop while it runs. Measured on this box at **126-149 ms**, with a 0 ms timer scheduled first firing 129 ms late, plus a child process per call. **The cost is new**: before Task 23.1 `lanAddress()` read only `os.networkInterfaces()`. **How hot it is, measured rather than assumed**: `state()` is called on `/api/hosting`, and the editor reads that route once at construction (`shell-layout.tsx`, one `HostingStore` per page load), once after a toggle, and through `readSettled`'s bounded retries — the only `setInterval` in the editor is `draft-store.ts` — so it is not per-frame and the review found no polling. That is why this is a row rather than a rewrite, and why it is worth having: a page load stalls the whole host for a tenth of a second, and a toggle's settle loop can do it up to ten times. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: how long a route reading may be reused — a TTL cache, a read at bind time, or a read only when `move()` changes the binding — which is a decision about staleness in the very thing this feature exists to get right, not a mechanical fix. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: the cost on a machine whose `netstat -r` is slower than this one's, and whether `execSync` has any timeout (the review found none, so a wedged child blocks the loop forever and no `catch` can run). NEAR ROWS: vg-171 (closed), vg-596. OWNER: `packages/host/src/cli/net.ts` (`readLanSource`). SEVERITY: medium — a host that stops answering for a tenth of a second per hosting read, and a child process that can hang it outright.

title: Four e2e specs carry their own first-non-internal-IPv4 helper, so a virtual-adapter-first machine builds the wrong origin URL for the test host
detail: FOUND BY TASK 23.1'S SEAT AND CONFIRMED BY ITS REVIEW (2026-10-18), which also checked the list for completeness rather than taking it: a tree-wide search for `networkInterfaces` finds `net.ts` (the owner), `net.test.ts`, and exactly four specs — `host-media.spec.ts`, `host-player.spec.ts`, `host-pwa.spec.ts` and `host-secure-origin.spec.ts` — each carrying its own copy of the old "first non-internal IPv4" rule. Nothing in `scripts/`, no shared helper module. **The consequence is narrower than the trailer that filed it claimed, and the review said so**: each uses the address only to build an origin URL for a browser on the same machine, and the hosts are started with `--host 0.0.0.0`, so a virtual adapter's address is still reachable and the specs would likely still pass. The helpers name the wrong address; breakage is not demonstrated. **That is what makes it worth a row rather than a fix**: four copies of a rule whose owner is now `rankLanAddresses`, diverging silently the next time the ranking changes, in the specs that prove the host's browser behaviour. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: whether the specs import the host's own ranking (they sit outside every package, so the import would arrive untyped — the same constraint `AddGroup` and `SPACING_STEPS` already record) or keep a copy with a note naming its owner. NEAR ROWS: vg-171 (closed), vg-597. OWNER: `tests/e2e/host-*.spec.ts`. SEVERITY: low — a duplicate rule, no demonstrated failure.

title: closeIdleConnections() and the per-connection answering bookkeeping have no production caller left, so decision 0070's connection-pruning paragraph justifies a capability nothing invokes
detail: FOUND BY TASK 23.2'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-18), by searching rather than reading. Task 23.2 replaced the move's `closeIdleConnections()` with `closeAllConnections()`, and that was its only production caller: repo-wide, the method is implemented at `server.ts:474`, declared on `ListenableServer` at `cli/net.ts:18`, and called only from `server.test.ts`. **The review found the dead surface is wider than the method**: the `answering` set (`server.ts:401`, written at `:460` and `:463`, read only at `:476`) and the whole per-inner-server `request` bookkeeping at `server.ts:452` to `:471` exist solely for it. `handed` and `nameOf` survive, because `closeAllConnections` uses them. **And a decision now justifies a capability nothing invokes**: decision `0070-the-host-mints-its-own-local-ca.md`'s "The port owns connection pruning" paragraph is about pruning idle connections, which no production path does any more. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: whether the port keeps a pruning capability for a caller that has not arrived, or the method, its interface member, the bookkeeping and the decision's paragraph all go together — the second is the repo's default (`AGENTS.md`: deletion over addition), but removing a member a watchlisted file implements is a change worth deciding once rather than per task. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: whether any test outside `server.test.ts` drives the method, and whether the bookkeeping is load-bearing for anything else that reads the same set. NEAR ROWS: vg-174 (closed), vg-600. OWNER: `packages/host/src/server.ts` and `docs/decisions/0070-the-host-mints-its-own-local-ca.md`. SEVERITY: low — dead code and a stale decision paragraph, nothing failing.

title: Whether a display's SSE stream still ends gracefully after a move is unverified, because the move destroys the socket just after the stream is closed
detail: FOUND BY TASK 23.2'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-18), on the comment that task corrected. The PUT handler's `finish` callback ends every display's stream before the move runs, and its stated reason was that `close()` waits for them and `closeIdleConnections()` will not take one that is open. That reason died with the fix — the move now destroys every connection itself — so the loop's justification is weaker than it reads: `SseConnection.close()` is `response.end()`, and `closeAllConnections()` destroys that socket microseconds later. **The host's intent is still right** — a stream should end deliberately rather than be cut — but whether the `end()` reaches the display before the socket dies is not established, and the comment now says so rather than implying it. **CONSEQUENCE**: a display on a host whose LAN is toggled may see a torn stream rather than a closed one. Whether that is visible depends on the player's reconnect path, which is not read here. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: a browser reading of a display across a LAN move — does it get the stream's end, or a transport error it has to recover from — which is the same shape as the empty reply `vg-173` measured on the editor side. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: whether the player already tolerates it, and whether the `end()` is flushed before the destroy on this platform. NEAR ROWS: vg-174 (closed), vg-599, vg-173. OWNER: `packages/host/src/server.ts` (the PUT handler) with `packages/host/src/transport/sse.ts`. SEVERITY: low — a possible torn stream on a rare action, with the intent unchanged.

title: The runtime has no twin of either bound on `metadata.name`: it repairs an empty name rather than refusing it, and stores one over 200 characters
detail: FOUND BY TASK 23.3'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-18), while checking whether the ruling's "anything written from now on is refused" was met. **It is met by the published contract and not by the runtime, in both directions.** The schema refuses an empty `metadata.name` and one over 200 characters; `validateMetadata` in `renderer-core/src/theme/envelope-semantics.ts` reads only `version`, so both documents return `ok: true`, and there is no JSON-schema engine anywhere in the repo to run the published file (`ajv` appears nowhere in `package-lock.json`, and the only in-repo readers of `schema/theme-document.schema.json` are four test files). **Measured by the review, not reasoned**: `ThemeStore.write` with `metadata.name: ""` stored `name: "empty"` — the id, because `namedEnvelope` repairs rather than refuses — and a 201-character name was `ok: true` and stored as sent. So a tool that validates before writing refuses a document the host accepts, and the host silently renames a document the published contract calls invalid. **The product cannot produce either** through the Document pane (`compact` drops an emptied name, and `ControlText` only produces strings), so both need a hand-edited or foreign `theme.json` — which is exactly the input the migration exists for. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: whether the runtime owes the twin (a refusal at write, or a repair stated as the product's behaviour) or the schema is a contract for outside tools only. Evidence that would settle it: a case asserting what the host writes for a PUT carrying `name: ""` and one carrying a 201-character name. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: whether the editor's own save path can write a name over the bound at all, and whether any published consumer of the schema exists outside this repo. NEAR ROWS: vg-221 (closed). OWNER: `renderer-core/src/theme/envelope-semantics.ts` with `schema/theme-document.schema.json`. SEVERITY: low — nothing is lost; the disagreement is between a contract and a repair.

title: A corrupt display-clients.json refuses the write-back, but no surface names the file or the failure, so a person sees only an empty display list
detail: FOUND BY TASK 1.1'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-18), in the fix round that closed the data-loss path the same review raised. `readDisplays` no longer collapses a present-but-unreadable file into an empty list: `readOrThrow` in `packages/host/src/settings/displays.ts` makes every mutator refuse with an error naming the file and the underlying failure, the write is now a temp file renamed over the target, and a regression test proves the file is byte-identical after a refused write. **What is missing is the report.** Readers still fail closed — `list()`, `find()` and `authenticate()` answer empty or undefined on a file they could not read — so the host keeps serving, and the failure surfaces nowhere: `GET /api/pairing/sessions` answers an empty list, the host's own page draws no displays, and nothing says the file is broken or names it. The only caller that learns is a loopback caller who attempts a write, where the pairing route throws the store's error. **CONSEQUENCE**: a person whose settings file was truncated or half-synced sees their displays vanish with no explanation, and the first evidence is a pairing that fails. The data itself is safe, because the write is refused. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: a decision on which surface owns the report — the host page's existing `role=status` row-note pattern in `packages/host/public/theme-list.js`, a console line at startup, or a route — and whether a settings file that cannot be read should be reported when the host starts rather than when someone tries to write. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: how a person would currently discover the cause, and whether the other settings stores should report the same way. NEAR ROWS: vg-601 (the same shape in the theme runtime — a contract the runtime does not enforce), vg-590. OWNER: `packages/host/public/` (the display list surface) with `packages/host/src/server.ts`. SEVERITY: low — nothing is lost, and the state is reachable only from a corrupt or hand-broken file.

title: publish-loop.spec.ts's second case is order-dependent: its poll passes on the overlay the first case leaves behind, so the editor is closed inside the 400 ms debounce and nothing is published or cleared
detail: FOUND BY TASK 1.2'S FIX ROUND 2 (2026-10-18), while proving a restored QR against the editor's e2e pair. The case at `publish-loop.spec.ts:349` fails at `:402` with `Received: "e2e-publish-loop"`. The traces say why, and the mechanism is not the fix's: test 2's editor page issues **no** `/api/publish` request at all, because its `toBe(THEME_ID)` poll passes on the overlay test 1 leaves behind — neither tree's trace carries test 1's `pagehide` DELETE — so the page is closed inside the publisher's 400 ms debounce and nothing is published or cleared. The trace was read by the independent re-review at `src/web/test-results/main/publish-loop-the-publish-l-75b16-ay-back-on-the-stored-theme-own-host/trace.zip`: the editor page issued only `GET /editor/`, its assets, `GET /api/hosting`, `GET /api/themes` and `GET /api/themes/e2e-publish-loop` — zero PUTs — while the display page polled `/api/published` eighteen times. **TWO READINGS, and they are separable.** As a test defect, the case is order-dependent and passes for the wrong reason, so it proves nothing about the second publish it means to exercise. As a product question, the same trace says a publish followed by a close inside the debounce window is lost — which is what a person does when they click publish and shut the tab. **ATTRIBUTION IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the samples are why.** The base samples were `publish-loop` alone under the default config (3 passed, untraced) and the same with `--trace=on` (1 unexpected); the head samples were both specs under the default config (1 unexpected) and, by the controller on 2026-10-18, `publish-loop` alone under `--project=own-host` (`npx playwright test tests/e2e/publish-loop.spec.ts --project=own-host --workers=1` -> exit 1, expected 2, unexpected 1). So the case fails alone at the head too, and no two samples share their conditions: a matched run needs a base worktree with its own install and build, which was not spent on a red the trace already places outside the fix's flow. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: for the test, whether test 2 should wait on its own publish rather than on the overlay, and whether the suite runs with a shared page or a fresh one; for the product, a decision on whether the publisher flushes on `pagehide` or the debounce is accepted as a window where an action is dropped. Evidence for the second: a browser reading that clicks publish and closes the page immediately, then asks the host whether the theme changed. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: whether the base's untraced 3/3 means the ordering is timing-dependent rather than deterministic, and whether any other case depends on the overlay the same way. NEAR ROWS: vg-585, vg-590 and vg-595 (the suite's timeouts, a case that reddened under load, and the preview a proof can be served from). OWNER: `tests/e2e/publish-loop.spec.ts` with `packages/editor`'s publisher. SEVERITY: medium — a case that cannot fail for its own reason, and a possible lost publish behind it.

title: Two wire names still say sessions while they now mean displays: the list key in GET /api/hosting, and the pairing flag in /api/health
detail: FOUND BY TASK 1.3 (2026-10-18), which removed the session store and made a display's credential durable. **Nothing misbehaves** — the list under `/api/hosting` is the display list, and the health flag is a boolean about whether the LAN is open — but a reader of the wire has to learn that a key called `sessions` means displays, and the editor's hosting client reads those keys. **The spec deliberately keeps two other names**, and this row is careful not to reopen them: `?session=` keeps its name because renaming it is a wire change across the QR, the player and the host's own console with no behaviour in it, and the routes table keeps `/api/pairing/sessions` because that route carries the live one-time codes as well as the known displays. What the spec does not name, and what moved meaning silently, are the `/api/hosting` list key and the `/api/health` flag. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: which names the wire should carry — `displays` for the list, and whether the flag is `pairing` or something about the LAN — and whether that rename rides with Task 4.1's route work or stands alone as the naming commit the spec says this change is not. **NOT ESTABLISHED**: whether anything outside this repo reads those keys; a saved player bundle or an installed phone app holding an older bundle would break on the rename, which is the argument for doing it before the phase ships rather than after. NEAR ROWS: vg-603 (the editor's pairing client, which Task 1.4 rewrites). OWNER: `packages/host/src/server.ts` with `packages/editor`'s hosting client. SEVERITY: low — no misbehaviour; the cost is a reader's confusion and a rename that only gets harder once a player ships.

title: A tunnel would free a display from the local network, which the pairing spec declines as transport and which nothing else owns
detail: ASKED BY THE USER on 2026-10-18, mid-flight during Task 1.4 of the per-display plan: copying 9remote's Cloudflare-tunnel approach would also free a display from the same local network. YES, and that is the transport the spec declines rather than overlooks -- docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-per-display-themes-design.md:68-75 records that 9remote pairs to a cloud relay, so its one-time code is revoked at a Worker and its permanent key is a bearer credential for a service somebody runs, where Yunari's premise is the opposite: no server, no recurring cost, browsing that touches no API. Its own words are that 9remote's device management transfers whole and its device transport does not transfer at all. TWO UPSIDES BEYOND OFF-LAN REACH, both real and recorded nowhere: a stable public hostname is exactly what the section 'Finding the host after its address changes' prefers over an address, and a tunnel's publicly trusted certificate answers vg-587 without installing a CA root on each device -- the per-device setup step the same spec names as the cost it avoids. WHAT IT COSTS: the host becomes reachable from the internet, where today's model is loopback-equals-admin (allowed()), a LAN guard on /api/displays, and /api/pairing/claim deliberately reachable unpaired -- a tunnel puts that claim route on the public internet and makes Task 1.4's rate limiting and burn-on-mismatch rules the only thing standing between the internet and a six-character code. Plus a third party in the path, an account, a domain and a recurring cost, and the premise that browsing touches no API dies. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS LOCALLY: the host serves https beside http on the same port from a CA it mints itself (docs/decisions/0070, Task 25.8b), so the secure-origin half is partly met with no tunnel at all, and the spec's 'no TLS' prose is the stale text vg-587 already records. WHERE IT BELONGS: its own spec, not Task 1.4 -- a tunnel is a provider, a credential lifecycle, supervision, a fallback for when it drops and a rule for what a display does while it is down. Task 1.4's code route is needed either way: a tunnel changes how a display reaches the host, not whether it pairs. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the user wants this specced, queued or left declined, and no tunnel provider was read, so every cost above is reasoned from the premise and from vg-587 rather than measured.
owner: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-per-display-themes-design.md (the transport ruling); a new spec if the user takes it

title: The pairing card shows the code's expiry instant and no countdown, which the spec asks for
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES TASK 1.4, which left it as a Discovered, not fixed trailer. The spec's section Pairing a display that has no camera asks the card for a countdown as well as an expiry, and the 9remote study it transfers from shows a live countdown with an expired key rendered as dots rather than as a dead value -- the point being that a person typing six characters needs to see the window closing. What shipped renders the expiry instant through uiCopy.publish.expires ("Pairing expires 08:41 PM") and no ticking value, so the card tells the reader when the code dies but not that it is about to. Not fixed there: the task's brief named no countdown, and the route already answers expiresAt, so the fix is card-side only. Owner: packages/editor/src/editor-shell/publish-control.tsx. Cost of leaving it: a code can expire mid-typing with nothing on the card having warned, which the rate-limit and consume-on-match rules then make visible only as a refusal.

title: /pair/ with a trailing slash is not served, so a hand-typed pairing URL reads 403
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES TASK 1.4, which left it as a Discovered, not fixed trailer. The pairing page is served at /pair, and /pair/ falls through to the dashboard guard and reads 403 off loopback. Nothing the host generates hits it -- the QR and the console line both print /pair?code=<code>, and the route is exact-matched -- so this is the hand-typed case: somebody reading the address off the console and typing it, or a browser that appends the slash. Measured by the implementer's own run rather than reasoned. Not fixed there: whether the pairing page should answer its trailing-slash form is a routing decision the task's brief did not name. Related and not the same failure: vg-588, where an installed display launches at the host's root with no session and is refused. Owner: the /pair route in packages/host/src/server.ts.

title: The console's pairing link carries a code minted at startup and expires ten minutes later, with no way to re-read a fresh one
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES TASK 1.4, which left it as a Discovered, not fixed trailer. Task 1.4 restored the console's pairing link as /pair?code=<code> (the controller's ruling R8), because a code is the one secret that can be regenerated for a printed link where a stored credential hash cannot be re-printed. The code it prints is minted once at startup and expires after DEFAULT_PAIRING_CODE_TTL_MS, so a host left running overnight prints a link that is already dead, and the console has no second line and no key that would print a fresh one. The editor's card is the live path and reads the code on demand, so this is the console's one-shot convenience being stale rather than the feature being broken. Not fixed there: a re-print needs a console affordance -- a key, a periodic line, or reading the code route on demand -- which is a decision the brief did not name. Owner: packages/host/src/main.ts.

title: The first-run page names its icon at /settings/favicon.svg, which is loopback-only, so a paired display on the LAN is refused its own favicon
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES TASK 1.4'S FIX ROUND, carried as a Discovered, not fixed trailer. It was surfaced by the origin-named browser proof that round's M6 required: the proof ran against http://192.168.2.56:5393 rather than 127.0.0.1, and the LAN origin is what made the reader set visible. packages/host/src/server.ts:326 composes the first-run page with `<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/settings/favicon.svg">`. Everything under /settings is refused off loopback with 403 'Settings are available on this PC only.' (server.ts:1904-1908), and that guard tests the origin alone, so a session does not open it. The icon the bundle-asset exemption actually serves on the LAN is /favicon.svg (server.ts:1352, decision 0019). So a paired display whose library is empty reaches / from the LAN (its session satisfies the display guard at server.ts:1364-1369, which is what a paired reader has), is served the first-run page, and is then refused the icon that page declares -- the browser logs a 403 on a clean load, which is the exact failure the icon link exists to prevent. WHY THE TEST DID NOT CATCH IT: packages/host/src/document-favicon.test.ts:29-32 lists two documents, library.html and settings.html, and its served-from case at :84-88 asserts their href is /settings/favicon.svg; both of those are admin pages that only loopback ever reads, so the shared href is right for them. The composed first-run page is checked only for declaring an icon at all (:72-74), never for the href resolving, and its reader set is the one that differs -- which is the hole. FIX: the first-run page declares /favicon.svg, the path the exemption covers, and the served-from case names the composed page with its own expected href rather than sharing the two files'. Not fixed there: the file is outside Task 1.4's brief, and choosing between moving the first-run page's href and widening the exemption to /settings/favicon.svg is a routing decision on a watchlisted path. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any other LAN-reachable document declares a loopback-only asset; two documents and one composed page were read, not searched. Owner: server.ts's first-run page and document-favicon.test.ts.

title: host-media.spec.ts starts a second host against the app folder the project's host already holds, and passes only because the wipe deletes the live lock
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES TASK 1.5, carried as a Discovered, not fixed trailer. tests/e2e/host-media.spec.ts starts a second host against HOST_APP_DIR, which is the same app folder the project's own host already holds. That is the arrangement the host lock now refuses, and the one the per-display design calls broken -- one app folder is one host. It still passes, and only because tests/e2e/global-setup.ts's wipe deletes the live lock first, which is vg-615. What the spec needs instead is its own --app-dir plus --themes-dir HOST_THEMES_DIR, so the second host has a folder of its own and the packages it serves. Not fixed there: choosing the arrangement is a test-arrangement decision rather than a fix inside this task, and it interacts with the plan's own project host. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any other spec starts a host against HOST_APP_DIR; one spec was read, not searched. Owner: tests/e2e/host-media.spec.ts. NEAR ROWS: vg-615 (the wipe that admits it).

title: The e2e global-setup wipe runs after the host has booted, deleting the running host's lock and every setting it wrote
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES TASK 1.5, carried as a Discovered, not fixed trailer, with the sampling recorded rather than the conclusion alone. tests/e2e/global-setup.ts wipes and re-seeds the app folder, and its own docblock says the ordering it needs: 'It also has to finish before the host web server boots, since the host reads its themes directory at startup and serves what it found there.' The measured pair shows that ordering not holding: the host wrote its lock at 2026-10-18T14:08:40.76Z (pid 30560, port 4175) and the file read ENOENT at 14:08:41.09Z, 330 ms later. So a host that is already running loses its lock and every setting it wrote, which is what admits the second host vg-614 starts. Not fixed there: the ordering belongs to the e2e harness rather than to this task, and the fix has to keep the project host's folder intact while a spec starts another host. NOT ESTABLISHED: the mechanism -- whether Playwright starts the web server before globalSetup, or the host at port 4175 was started by something else -- because the sampling shows the ordering without naming its cause. Owner: tests/e2e/global-setup.ts.

title: A hostname that trims to empty is stored as an empty name, so the record is half-usable and rewritten on every run
detail: FOUND BY THE RE-REVIEW OF PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES TASK 1.5, as a pre-existing Minor on a line the fix round touched rather than one the fix introduced. host-record.ts:93's mint is `usableName(hostname()) ?? ""`, so a hostname that trims or slices to empty yields `name: ""`. The record is then written with an empty name and the next read treats it as half-usable and rewrites it; the id is preserved, so this is a stable state rather than a loop that loses data, but Task 1.6's `GET /api/host` would answer an empty name and the display list would show a host with no name. Not fixed there: choosing the fallback is a decision rather than a line -- `this-pc` is already reserved as `LOCAL_DISPLAY_ID`, so reusing that word as a host name is a naming decision -- and the path is not reachable on a normal machine, where `os.hostname()` returns something. NOT ESTABLISHED: what `os.hostname()` returns on a machine with no configured name; the code path was read, not run. Owner: packages/host/src/settings/host-record.ts (`usableName`, and the mint that calls it). TASK 1.6'S SEAT THEN HIT THE SAME LINE FROM THE OTHER SIDE, and filed it again: host-record.ts's docblock says the name is absent when the hostname says nothing, while the code persists the name as an empty string -- so the docblock and the code contradict each other as well as the reader. Both halves are one fix, which is why this row is the second report of it rather than a duplicate.

title: Nothing refuses a second local display pointing at the same monitor, so the launcher opens two windows on one screen
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES TASK 1.7, reported by its own seat as a trailer on commit d4ce6d92 rather than fixed there. A local display is a display record with `kind: 'local'` and no credential, and the monitor hint it stores IS its identity -- but `POST /api/displays` mints one per call without asking whether another local display already holds that hint. Task 1.8's reconcile pass ensures every attached local display has a window, per display, so two records on one screen mean two fullscreen windows started on it, one hidden behind the other and both polling. Recoverable rather than lossy: the owner removes the extra record from the display list in the editor. RULING R32 (controller, 2026-10-18): the create route refuses with 409 a monitor hint that an existing LOCAL display already holds, checked in the store that owns the list, so the record cannot be written at all; paired displays carry no hint and are unaffected. R32 is carried into Task 1.8's dispatch, which already edits server.ts and owns the launcher the gap harms. Cost if the ruling is wrong: an owner who wants two windows on one monitor cannot express it -- but the launcher starts a window fullscreen, so that case has no meaning to express, and reversing it is deleting the guard. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a hint can be held by a local display that is currently detached, in which case the refusal must not fire on a monitor the owner has unplugged and replugged under a different name. Owner: packages/host/src/settings/displays.ts (the store owning the list) and the `POST /api/displays` route in packages/host/src/server.ts.

title: The answers store has neither of its sibling's guards, so a corrupt file is overwritten and two overlapping writes lose one
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES TASK 3.1, reported by its own seat as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on commit d06b76c8. `settings/theme-settings.ts` and `settings/active-theme.ts` are siblings -- two consumer-state stores beside each other in the same folder -- and only the second has the two guards the first needs. (a) `readLevels`' catch turns an unreadable file into `{}`, and `write`, `removeTheme` and `removeDisplay` then save that emptiness, so a corrupt `theme-answers.json` is silently replaced by the answers the next write happens to carry: the file is written over what could not be read. `active-theme.ts` refuses instead, with `editable()` throwing `could not be read, so it was not written`. (b) No write is serialized. Every mutator is read-modify-write over the whole file, so two overlapping ones lose the earlier: the second reads a file the first has not saved yet and writes it back without the first's entry. `active-theme.ts` answers this with `writeExclusively` (a `writing.then(work, work)` chain), and it is worth noting that Task 2.1's review raised exactly this as an Important because 2.1 *introduced* the read-modify-write -- here it is pre-existing, because `write` already did `readFile_` then `save({ ...all, [themeId] })` before this task, which is why the seat filed it rather than fixed it. VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING: read from `git show 7000a7b5:.../theme-settings.ts`, whose `write` and `remove` both read the whole file and save it back. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether two overlapping writes are reachable in practice -- the answers route is loopback-admin and a person drives it, so the window may be theoretical where 2.1's was not; the fix is the same either way and is three lines plus the refusal. Owner: src/web/packages/host/src/settings/theme-settings.ts (`readLevels`' catch, and the `write`/`removeTheme`/`removeDisplay` mutators).

title: Deleting a theme leaves every display's answers for it, and `removeTheme` was written with no caller
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES TASK 3.2'S REVIEW, as an out-of-scope observation, and filed rather than fixed because it is not the task in hand. Task 3.1 split the answers store's single `remove(themeId)` into `removeTheme(themeId)` -- one theme, every display -- and `removeDisplay(display)` -- one display, every theme. Task 3.2 wired `removeDisplay` into the display DELETE route (`server.ts`, beside `displays.remove`) because the plan's Review Focus item 4 named it, and it left `removeTheme` callerless: a grep over the host package finds only the interface declaration (`theme-settings.ts:37`) and the implementation (`:201`). The theme delete route exists and is the obvious owner -- `server.ts:2041` calls `themeStore.remove(rawId)`, moving the folder to the OS trash -- so deleting a theme today trashes its folder and leaves every display's answers for it in `theme-answers.json` for ever. THE SAME ORPHAN CLASS THE SAME TASK JUST SWEPT, one axis over: a display's deletion now sweeps its theme entry and its answers, and a theme's deletion sweeps nothing. `removeTheme`'s own docblock says 'every display's answers for one deleted theme', so the intended behaviour is written down and simply not reached. NOT A DEFECT THE PLAN CHOSE: Review Focus item 4 named only the display's deletion, so the asymmetry is an omission rather than a decision. Fix is one line in the delete route plus the test, in the shape Task 3.2's own fix round used. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the answers are ever read again after the theme is gone -- `read` requires a theme id the caller passes, and a deleted theme cannot be chosen, so the residue is storage rather than behaviour; the swept display case had the same property and was still swept for consistency. Owner: the theme delete route in packages/host/src/server.ts, beside `themeStore.remove`.

title: A display that disconnects mid-stream crashes the host with an unhandled ECONNRESET
detail: FOUND BY THE PHASE 3 GATE OF PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES, when a scratch script opened two sample streams, read frames, and then died with an unhandled rejection instead of closing them. The host process exited: `Error: read ECONNRESET ... Emitted 'error' event on Socket instance`, `at TCP.onStreamRead`. REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY on the same commit by re-running that script: the host's `/api/health` answered 200 before and the port refused connections after. Three narrower attempts did NOT reproduce it -- a clean `AbortController` abort after two reads, `process.exit(0)` with two streams open, and a raw-socket `destroy()` mid-stream -- so the trigger is narrower than 'any disconnect' and is NOT ESTABLISHED beyond the one script shape. CAUSE, read from the source rather than inferred: nothing in the sample-stream path listens for an error on the socket or the response. `openStream` registers `request.on('close', drop)` and `request.on('error', drop)` only (`server.ts:2319`, `:2340`), and `SseConnection.close()` calls `this.response.end()` (`transport/sse.ts`), which on an already-reset socket emits an error on the Socket that nothing handles, so Node's default action is to throw and end the process. ATTRIBUTION ESTABLISHED AS PRE-EXISTING: a grep for `socket.on(`, `clientError` and `on('error'` across `server.ts` and `transport/sse.ts` finds only the two `request` listeners, and the Task 3.2 diff (ab359448..8f45a847) only ADDS request listeners before removing them again -- no socket or response listener existed before that task and none was removed by it. IMPACT: the host serves every display from one process, so one phone going to sleep, one browser tab closing, or one flaky Wi-Fi drop can take down the streams of every other display and the whole dashboard. It also makes any browser proof in this repository unreliable, which is how it was found. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the pre-3.2 code crashed identically -- the reasoning above is from the source, not from running the older revision. Owner: the sample-stream path -- `openStream` in packages/host/src/server.ts and `SseConnection` in packages/host/src/transport/sse.ts, which owns the response and so should own its errors. A regression test would open a stream, reset the socket mid-stream, and assert the host still answers.

title: The committed settings-theme-question capture can never be refreshed by the test that registers it
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4.3'S REVIEW of plan 2026-10-18-per-display-themes. `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md:183` registers the capture `settings-theme-question` against the test `captures the question a theme raises` (`src/web/tests/e2e/host-settings.spec.ts:367`). That test writes its file with the running project's name appended -- `host-settings.spec.ts:388` builds `-${testInfo.project.name}.png` -- and the spec runs under the `desktop-host` project (`playwright.config.ts:167-173`), so it writes `settings-theme-question-desktop-host.png`. The committed file is `settings-theme-question-desktop-chromium.png`, a suffix no current project produces, so a capture run cannot overwrite it: the registered evidence is frozen at whatever the page looked like when the project was named `desktop-chromium`, and nothing can tell it is stale. CAUSE ESTABLISHED by reading both the naming line and the project list; the mismatch is PRE-EXISTING (the file and the registration both predate this plan) and the staleness became visible because Task 4.3 added a display column to the settings page, so the committed picture no longer depicts the page it is evidence for. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether other registered captures carry the same dead suffix -- the same check should be run over the whole table rather than this one row. Owner: `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md` together with the spec that takes the capture. The fix is a decision first -- whether the table names a file or a test, since it currently reads as the former and the test produces the latter -- and then either deleting the orphaned PNG and re-capturing, or changing what the table names. A capture run needs `YUNARI_CAPTURE=1` and `--workers=1`.

title: The safe-area inset slot mapping is pinned nowhere, so a swapped top and bottom padding stays invisible
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4.5s ROUND-2 SCOPED RE-REVIEW of plan 2026-10-18-per-display-themes. The round added the first assertion anywhere that the safe-area inset is emitted at all (theme-chooser.dom.test.ts:218, toContain(env(safe-area-inset-bottom))), after finding that the existing case only compared the chooser strip against a putStrip reference and so could not catch the token disappearing from both. That gap is now closed for the BOTTOM slot. What remains: stripInset (src/web/packages/player/src/chrome.ts:220-224) maps side top to env(safe-area-inset-top) and side bottom to env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and nothing asserts that mapping. A grep of chrome.dom.test.ts finds no mention of stripInset, safe-area or padding, so swapping the two slots would satisfy the reference comparison AND the new assertion, because both would carry the swapped value. CAUSE ESTABLISHED by reading the function and the test file; the gap is PRE-EXISTING and was only made visible by the round-2 fix naming the regression precisely.
