IMPACT: on a notched phone the bottom strip would take the top inset and the top strip the home-indicator inset, so a persistent control sits in the safe area it was meant to avoid. Invisible on desktop, where both insets are 0. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any real device has been tested against either slot; no browser proof exists for this control. Owner: src/web/packages/player/src/chrome.ts, with the case going in chrome.dom.test.ts, which owns putStrip and stripInset. The fix is one case asserting both sides.

title: The chart refresh rate set has four runtime restatements and no runtime owner, so a third rate would be silently refused
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4.7'S TASK REVIEW OF PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES, and carried in that plan's close commit 26dd2ea5 as a Discovered, not fixed trailer. The set is {1, 30}. It is owned at compile time by ChartRefreshRate (src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/chart-refresh.ts:1, `export type ChartRefreshRate = 1 | 30`), but four runtime sites restate it by hand: publish-follower.ts:149 (`if (chartFps === 1 || chartFps === 30)`, the player refusing a malformed rate off the wire before it reaches setRate, where a 0 would make the cadence comparison < Infinity and freeze the display with nothing logged), displays.ts:289 (the same pair when reading a stored record off disk), and displays.ts:360 (`rateOrThrow`, the validating writer). A third rate -- 60 for a high-refresh panel is the obvious one, and the per-display spec already makes the rate a per-display fact -- would be refused at every one of them, and no type error points at any of them, because widening the union keeps every site compiling. CAUSE ESTABLISHED by reading the four sites. NOT A DEFECT TODAY: no third rate exists and nothing requests one. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the fix is a decision, not a line. A runtime predicate (isChartRefreshRate) has to live somewhere and the two candidates disagree about ownership -- scene-fabric owns the type and the refresh loop, while renderer-core is where the host's and the player's shared vocabulary already lives -- and it spans two packages and three files, so no single owner can fix it. Owner: undecided between src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/chart-refresh.ts and src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/. A regression test would assert that every runtime site answers alike for 1, 30, 60, 0, null and the string "30".

title: data-kind on a theme-list display row has no production reader, and the comment claiming it does survives in two files
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4.8'S TASK REVIEW OF PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES, and carried in that plan's close commit 7c74d82f as a Discovered, not fixed trailer. themeList writes row.dataset.kind = kind (src/web/packages/host/public/theme-list.js:281, so the rendered attribute is data-kind), and the only thing that reads it is the assertion pinning it, theme-list.dom.test.ts:227-231. Nothing else reads it: the cost warning table does not, because it reads the kind off the displays array instead (assignedKind at theme-list.js:313-314), and no e2e spec selects on it. CAUSE ESTABLISHED by grepping every reader in packages/host/src, packages/host/public and tests/. The comment above the write (theme-list.js:277-280) says the kind rides the row BECAUSE THE WARNING TABLE IS KEYED ON IT, which was true of an earlier design and is false now; the same false comment is duplicated in the test file at theme-list.dom.test.ts:224-226, where the 4.8 fix round corrected the source copy but not this one. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: two things are entangled. Removing the attribute also means removing its assertion and both comments, which touches a test file Task 4.8 never opened; and whether a page-facing module should expose a display row's kind at all is a small design question -- a page cannot ask a display what it is, so the attribute is a plausible affordance that simply has no user yet, and the project's rule is to avoid speculative surface. Owner: src/web/packages/host/public/theme-list.js for the attribute and its comment, src/web/packages/host/src/theme-list.dom.test.ts:224-231 for the assertion and the duplicate comment. A regression test is not applicable to a deletion; the check is that no selector in packages/ or tests/ matches [data-kind] afterwards.

title: host-player's determinism case is red in both whole-file samples, and it is the check vg-347 was verified by
detail: FOUND BY the broad boundary run of plan 2026-10-18-per-display-themes (commit 058b66de, re-run at 91ce63be), carried on the boundary's close commit as a Discovered, not fixed trailer. SUBJECT: src/web/tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts's case 'a paused clock on one chart > makes two frames of one chart byte-identical', which fails on Buffer.compare(first.shot, second.shot) returning non-zero. MEASURED, every exit code read from a file: ALONE, three runs, three passes (the boundary's round 0), plus one more pass taken independently by the controller after the boundary fix round (exit 0, 2 passed, --grep on this case and the re-find case). IN THE WHOLE FILE (desktop-host, --workers=1), exit 1, 33 passed, this one failed. IN THE WHOLE FILE AGAIN with this plan's new describe excluded via --grep-invert, exit 1, 30 passed, this one failed -- so the cases this plan added are not what loads it. Two red samples under load and four green samples alone is the comparison AGENTS.md asks for rather than a single sample. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FLAKE REPORT: vg-347 is archived verified, and its check names this exact case -- it requires Buffer.compare of two captures of one frame to be 0 (desktop-host, --workers=1), red-proved by leaving the clock running. That check is red in both whole-file samples, so the verification vg-347's state rests on is load-sensitive rather than reproducible in the command the check itself names. This row is the missing half of that record, not a duplicate of it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the non-zero compare is a real determinism defect that only appears under load or a harness artefact of the long run. No cause is claimed. The nearest open rows are vg-542 (same file, palette ink 496 against a floor of 500 in the ordered desktop-host run) and vg-143 (the host player units spec timing out on the real host, and in isolation too), so this is one member of a class the register already tracks rather than a new one. Also filed as GitHub issue 37. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the case green in the whole-file run, at which point vg-347's check is reproducible as written. A check would run host-player.spec.ts whole on desktop-host at --workers=1 and read the exit code.

title: Five display-management routes have no caller in any shipped surface, so a local display cannot be created or registered at sign-in by a user
detail: FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of plan 2026-10-18-per-display-themes (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-18-per-display-themes/final-review-report.md section C1), verified independently by the controller. POST /api/displays, PATCH /api/displays/:id, DELETE /api/displays/:id, GET /api/displays/monitors and POST /api/displays/autostart are served by src/web/packages/host/src/server.ts:1217-1440 and read by nothing: a scan of every .ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.html file under src/web/packages and src/web/tests finds no reference to /api/displays outside server.ts itself, server.test.ts and three request.delete calls in host-player.spec.ts. The controller's own scan of every route found one more in the same state that the review did not list: /api/pairing/sessions (GET/POST/DELETE, server.ts:1158-1167) is referenced only by server.ts and test files. Pairing itself IS reachable -- the editor's hosting-client.ts:91 reads /api/pairing/code and host/public/pair.html claims it -- so what is unreachable is creating a local display, listing monitors, registering at sign-in, listing or revoking a paired display, and renaming or removing one. WHY IT MATTERS: the user's ruling 13, quoted in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-per-display-themes-design.md:220-222, is that a local display must survive host app restarts and computer reboots; that is delivered by registerHostAutostart (schtasks /SC ONLOGON) and by the launcher's liveness reconcile, and neither can be turned on from any shipped surface. THE HANDOFF IS THE CAUSE, NOT THE PLAN: the spec hands the surface away at :17-19 and :215 -- 'where the assignment is drawn -- the store spec's Host settings mode and its local tab own that surface', and 'Adding one is a Host settings action' -- and the queued plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-theme-store.md never mentions autostart, monitors, the local display or sign-in in A.8, A.9 or A.10. So the per-display plan met its spec and the handoff target does not carry it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the store plan's A.8 is meant to grow this surface or a new task is owed. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a surface that creates a local display, lists monitors and turns on sign-in registration, and a check that the theme store plan's A.8 names it. Owner: the theme store plan's phase A for the surface, src/web/packages/host/src/server.ts for the routes. Also filed as GitHub issue 38.

title: /api/published's display.id is computed and sent to every client, and no client reads it
detail: FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of plan 2026-10-18-per-display-themes (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-18-per-display-themes/final-review-report.md section C2). src/web/packages/host/src/server.ts:1598 writes display: { id, theme, chartFps } into the /api/published payload; the follower reads only theme and chartFps (src/web/packages/player/src/publish-follower.ts:140). Every reader of display.id is an assertion in src/web/packages/host/src/server.test.ts (:1123, :1519, :1689, :1704, :1728, :2091, :4788). Same class as the open vg-625 (data-kind has no production reader and two comments say it does): a field the host pays to compute and no client consumes. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether display.id is intended for the theme store's display work, in which case it is a deliberate forward declaration rather than dead weight -- nothing at HEAD says so. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a client reading display.id, or its removal from the payload with the assertions re-pointed at display.theme. Owner: src/web/packages/host/src/server.ts for the writer, src/web/packages/player/src/publish-follower.ts for the reader that does not exist. Also filed as GitHub issue 39.

title: The theme-id pattern is hand-rolled in six places while the device-id pattern was consolidated to one
detail: FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of plan 2026-10-18-per-display-themes (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-18-per-display-themes/final-review-report.md section C3). /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/ appears at src/web/packages/host/src/settings/active-theme.ts:41, src/web/packages/host/src/settings/theme-settings.ts:43, src/web/packages/host/src/themes/store.ts:158, src/web/packages/player/src/theme-loader.ts:73, src/web/packages/editor/src/theme-library-client.ts:106, and as STABLE_ID_PATTERN in src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts:11. This plan's own 'one owner per concept' constraint consolidated the device id -- src/web/packages/host/src/settings/devices.ts:44 exports DEVICE_ID_PATTERN -- and left the theme id with six owners. Two of the six are in packages that cannot import each other (renderer-core stays Fabric/DOM-free, and the player may not reach editor code), so a single export cannot simply be imported everywhere; the consolidation needs a decision about which package owns the shape. NOT ESTABLISHED: which package should own it, and whether all six copies are meant to be one shape or are two shapes that coincide today. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one exported pattern with the other five importing it, or a written reason each site is deliberately its own. Owner: no single one, which is why this is a row rather than a fix. Also filed as GitHub issue 40.

title: The per-display fallback rule is implemented twice, in the host's server and again in its own page
detail: FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of plan 2026-10-18-per-display-themes (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-18-per-display-themes/final-review-report.md section C4). 'This display's theme, else the default's' is implemented in assignedThemeFor (src/web/packages/host/src/server.ts:879) and again in shownTheme (src/web/packages/host/public/theme-list.js). They agree today. Two implementations of one rule, in two languages, neither pinned against the other, is a divergence waiting for the next change to either. The host page cannot import the server's function, so this is not a one-line dedupe: it needs a decision about which side owns the rule and how the other reads it -- the page could be served the resolved theme rather than resolving it itself. NOT ESTABLISHED: which side should own it. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a case that drives both and asserts they agree, or the page reading the resolved value instead of recomputing it. Owner: src/web/packages/host/src/server.ts and src/web/packages/host/public/theme-list.js. Also filed as GitHub issue 41.

title: server.ts is 2689 lines against the 800-line stop, and this plan added roughly 700 of them
detail: FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of plan 2026-10-18-per-display-themes (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-18-per-display-themes/final-review-report.md section C5). AGENTS.md: '500 lines is a signal and 800 is a stop for normal source files.' src/web/packages/host/src/server.ts is 2689 lines; this plan added roughly 700 of them -- the three resolvers, the display routes, the pairing routes, the resolution order and the answers route's display. The file was already past the stop before this plan, so this is not a defect the plan introduced; it is the change that should have split it, and it is recorded so the next work in the file starts from the number rather than rediscovering it. NOT ESTABLISHED: where the seams are. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the route groups extracted into modules of their own, or a written reason the host's server is one file. Owner: src/web/packages/host/src/server.ts. Also filed as GitHub issue 42.

title: The dashboard starter palette token "bars" is named "Letterbox bars" and no longer paints the letterbox
detail: DISCOVERED, NOT FIXED in commit 28f2b14d (artboard: one background colour, and a media fit that names its box). That commit removed artboard.barColor, so the letterbox is painted by artboard.background and nothing references palette.bars any more. Its display name "Letterbox bars" (src/web/packages/editor/src/new-fabric-theme-globals.ts) therefore describes a job the token no longer has: what remains is that new-object-defaults.ts SURFACE_TOKENS lists "bars" as a surface a new object may take. Cause established; the fix is a decision, not a diagnosis - either the token is deleted from the starter palette (SURFACE_TOKENS still finds "background" first, which the palette has) or its display name is changed to describe the surface job, and no name has been agreed. Not fixed on the fly because AGENTS.md requires the correct behaviour to be already specified, and it is not. Related: the same commit left the blank starter painting its letterbox with palette.chartTrack, which is intended.

title: The shell's third mode is called Host while the machine and its local display are called This PC
detail: FOUND BY the scoped re-review of the A.1 fix round (b6428695), finding N3, recorded in .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-18-theme-store/review-A1-fix-r1.md. The user named the third shell mode Host (ledger ruling R100, 2026-10-19), but the host package still calls the machine This PC: host/public/settings.html is the page the mode shows and its h1 is This PC, the local display record is labelled This PC (theme-library-client.ts, and its tests), and the mode id itself is "this-pc". Two names for one machine, and nothing conflicts today only because the mode region is still empty - A.2 and A.8 fill it, and A.8 is the task that puts the host settings surface inside the shell. Needs a decision before then: rename the mode, rename the page and the display label, or keep both because one names a display and the other a surface. Filed rather than fixed because the correct behaviour is not already specified and the two candidate owners are in different packages. Also filed as GitHub issue 44 in this repo.

title: The publish popup prints an https address beside copy that still warns about plain http
detail: FOUND BY the task review of 9fc0adaf (https first, http kept as the fallback), findings 3 and 5. The control now renders https://<address>:<port> (editor-shell/publish-control.tsx) and two lines below it renders uiCopy.publish.warning, which still reads "Plain HTTP on your own network - trusted networks only, never the internet" (ui-copy.ts). The address and the warning disagree about what the reader is looking at. The same commit left a literal "Fallback http://<address>:<port>" string inside publish-control.tsx rather than in ui-copy.ts, because that file belonged to another seat at the time. Both need ui-copy.ts, so neither could be fixed in the commit that created them and neither is covered by the plan that owns that file. The fix is a copy decision: the warning should name the fallback it is about, and the literal should move to its one owner.

title: The host's bound-port case failed in one full-suite sample and passed in two others at the same commit
detail: FOUND BY TASK A.3'S SEAT during its full-suite run on 2026-10-20, and filed as GitHub issue 45 rather than fixed because the cause is not established. The case is packages/host/src/server.test.ts > answers the port it is actually listening on, not one it was given. SAMPLES: (1) the full suite at 8b2fe5e2 under parallel load, exit 1, Test Files 1 failed | 276 passed and Tests 1 failed | 3784 passed, the single failure being this case; (2) the same file alone, exit 0, 155 passed; (3) the full suite re-run at the same commit 8b2fe5e2, exit 0, 277 files / 3785 tests passed, which is the re-run against a sample of the same commit that the failing sample was taken on; (4) the full suite at 783ce5fb, the commit before it, exit 0, 276 files / 3775 tests passed. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether load is the trigger at all, since samples 1 and 3 are the same tree and the only known difference is what else the machine was doing; which step of the case is sensitive, the case binding a port and reading the port actually bound, so the window between those two is a candidate nothing here measures; and whether it has failed before, since no earlier run is recorded against this case. WHY FILED RATHER THAN SHRUGGED OFF: it is the third file to redden only under load, after vg-585 (player/src/main.dom.test.ts's display-replacement case timing out at 20 s) and vg-590 (host/src/themes/store.test.ts's asset-bounds case), and vg-590's own detail records that two files is where the box-was-busy explanation stops. The commit it was found on adds exports to the renderer-core barrel, and nothing in this case's path reaches them, so that change is not implicated - an argument from the diff rather than a measurement.

title: The published schema requires artboard.background to be a palette reference while the in-repo validator accepts a literal
detail: FOUND BY THE TASK REVIEW OF A.3 (8b2fe5e2, theme store plan), finding 6, and filed as GitHub issue 46 rather than fixed because the fix is a design decision. schema/theme-document.schema.json types artboard.background as a paletteReference - an object with a required ref matching ^palette.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ - so a local literal is not allowed. src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/theme/envelope-semantics.ts's validateStyleValue accepts either shape, reading ref or value and reporting style-value-ambiguous only when both or neither are present. BOTH SHAPES ARE REACHABLE: the editor's artboard control cannot author a literal (packages/editor/src/panes/document/artboard-fields.tsx, a literal is in no option of that control) but it preserves one it does not edit, so an imported document keeps it, and A.3's groundOf reads both branches because the validator permits both. NOT ESTABLISHED: which shape is intended. The fix is either the schema widening to admit the literal, or the validator tightening to refuse it - and the second rejects documents that load today. The row is load-bearing for A.3's colour-mode reading, which cannot be right about both.

title: The rule that a board with media behind it is unclassified is written twice, in two packages, so the ground and the colour mode can drift
detail: FOUND BY THE A.4b FIX ROUND, in the round that gave the ground a host-side derivation (R114). The rule is one concept with two readers: renderer-core/src/theme/facet-record.ts:104-105 reads `artboard.backgroundMedia` to answer `unclassified` for the colour mode, and src/web/packages/host/src/themes/store.ts:573 reads the same field to answer `undefined` for the ground. Both are correct today and both are one-field presence checks, so nothing is broken now; what is missing is an owner, and `docs/architecture/ownership.md`'s rule is one owner per concept. The host already depends on renderer-core, so the cheap shape is a predicate exported from renderer-core that both call. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the two answers should stay two expressions of one rule at all, or whether the ground's own absence rule is a separate fact about paint rather than about media. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a decision on where the predicate lives. Filed rather than fixed because it is not the task that found it and the fix needs that decision. REPORTED BY the round-1 scoped re-review as its note 4.

title: A theme whose ground is a CSS colour name is schema-legal and paints correctly, but the facet record calls its colour mode unclassified
detail: FOUND BY THE A.4b FIX ROUND 2's implementer, which hit it while fixing an unrelated fixture: its own test envelope used `color: "midnightblue"`, and the case asserting the ordinary colour-mode reading had been passing for the wrong reason. CAUSE ESTABLISHED: renderer-core/src/theme/facet-record.ts:162-164 `lightnessOf` reads a ground through `parseHex` alone, and `parseHex` (renderer-core/src/charts/fill.ts:152-155) accepts only 3- and 6-digit hex, so any other CSS colour answers `undefined` and `colourModeOf` returns `unclassified` (facet-record.ts:141). A named colour is LEGAL: schema/theme-document.schema.json:100 types a solid palette paint's `color` as `{"type":"string","minLength":1}`, the hand-maintained validator agrees (fabric-envelope-validate.ts:710, "A solid palette paint needs only a non-empty CSS colour"), and the editor's palette field accepts anything `CSS.supports("color", ...)` passes (vg-033, verified). CONSEQUENCE: such a theme is unfindable under Light or Dark and reachable only under "any", which contradicts the spec's derivation (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md:502-513, which reads the paint's own luminance and reserves `unclassified` for the genuinely ambiguous mid band and for a media-backed board). It also covers `rgb()`, `hsl()`, 8-digit hex and `transparent`, not just names. NOT ALREADY FILED: vg-439 is about the duplicated parser's ownership and vg-033 about the field accepting anything; neither names the record's answer for a legal document, which is this row. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether the record resolves a colour the way the browser does (a normalizer, or names resolved to hex at the point the paint is built) or the schema and validator tighten a solid's colour to hex — the first is the honest fix if any surface can author a name. Pre-existing in A.4a, not introduced by the fix round that found it.

title: A store listing that fails draws an empty surface and says nothing, so a failed load cannot be told from an empty library
detail: FOUND BY THE A.6 TASK REVIEW, and named by the implementer as one of three gaps it would not paper over. CAUSE ESTABLISHED: region.tsx:462-471 swallows the listing's rejection — `items` stays `undefined`, the body's state stays `"none"` (region.tsx:328,487), and the surface draws nothing at all. That is the right half of the answer: the empty-library sentence (R124) must NOT be shown for a listing that failed, because saying "you have no themes" to someone whose host refused the request is a fabrication of the same kind as answering a missing telemetry value with zero. WHAT IS WRONG IS THE SILENCE: the store's own copy has an empty-library sentence and an empty-filter-result sentence, and nothing for the third state, so a person cannot tell a store that failed to load from one that holds nothing. The editor has a notice owner for exactly this (`error-manager/`), and the A.6 review's judgment is that it is not reachable from this region — which is the design decision this row waits on. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a store notice belongs to the error manager, to the shell's own strip (§7.6), or to a state of the region's own body. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a decision naming the store's notice surface. Filed rather than fixed because it spans the region, the error manager and possibly the shell, and because the correct behaviour is not yet specified anywhere. Related: vg-640 is the other A.6-era gap in what the listing answers.

title: A save with no base is ungated, so writing onto a theme id the library already holds replaces it silently
detail: FOUND BY THE A.7 SEAT as its own finding 1, and reproduced by the controller against the source rather than accepted from the report. CAUSE ESTABLISHED: theme-library-client.ts's `save` sends `base` only when the caller has one, and host/src/themes/store.ts's `write` refuses a taken id only when a base was sent AND mismatched (`if (options?.overwrite !== true && options?.base !== undefined)`, store.ts:742), so a base-less PUT onto an id the library already stores replaces that theme's document and folder with no refusal and no undo. NOT SPECIFIC TO THE IMPORT, which is why it is filed rather than fixed in A.7: every blank theme carries the same id, so "New theme then Save to library" twice has the same shape, and any first save is ungated by construction. WHAT IT COSTS: the silent replace is data loss with no undo, which is the failure R131 believed a 409 prevented — the 409 cannot happen on a call that sends no base. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a protocol decision, either that a save must claim the id is free (the shape R136 gives the import's own host-side route) or that the library suffixes a taken id instead of replacing it; the two differ in what a client older than the decision sees. R136 closes this for the import route only, because that route holds the store and can make the claim in one step. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any shipped surface other than the import reaches a base-less save onto a taken id — the editor's save path was not traced here. Related: vg-388 is the theme store's own register row.

title: `glass-lifecycle`'s repaint floor is unreachable for a chartless fixture, so the case is red on an assertion it cannot satisfy
detail: FOUND BY THE A.7c SEAT while re-pointing the browser suite onto the store's open route, and reported rather than papered over: it refused to lower the floor, which is the weakening its brief forbids. CAUSE ESTABLISHED: the editor's loop calls `session.tick()`, whose text pass is due every 250 ms (four times a second) and whose chart pass repaints only when a chart's reading moves; the case's fixture (`GLASS_ENVELOPE` plus stripes, three objects) carries no charts, so four to five renders a second is its ceiling against an assertion of `withPanelMin > 10`. MEASURED in the same page: 3-5/s unfitted, **4.5/s with the product's own `zoomToFit()` forced** — so the camera is not the cause — and 21.5/s for the starter document (ten objects, with charts). THE CASE'S SUBJECT DID NOT CHANGE: A.7c re-pointed it from the picker to the store's route and the fixture bytes are identical, so this is not the re-pointing's doing. NOT ESTABLISHED: that the case has been red since `38cbfe3e` (2026-10-02), when the loop began calling `tick()` — that is inference from the commit and from the assertion's own comment naming `LiveRuntime.refresh` and `ChartManager.refresh`, and no older revision was checked out and run. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one run of the case at a revision before that commit. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the floor belongs to whoever owns that spec, and the property the case is about — the delta between the two windows, 4 against 5, `<= +1` — still holds, so the repair is to re-express the assertion around the delta or to give the fixture a chart, not to lower the number. Related: vg-604 is another editor-e2e case red for a reason this plan did not cause.

title: Oklab is the reference for the colour picker's interpolation upgrade path, which the spec records deliberately and does not build
detail: RAISED BY THE USER on 2026-10-20, sharing https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/ — Bjorn Ottosson's Oklab post — to be noted for the colour/gradient picker. WHERE IT LANDS: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-colour-and-gradient-rebuild-design.md's point 6, "Interpolation is not exposed", which already decides this: "Photoshop and Figma's shader surfaces offer an interpolation space and CSS now defaults to Oklab, but this repo's renderer draws CSS gradient strings in sRGB through ECharts and Fabric, so a control offering Oklab would promise something nothing honours". The spec records it as an upgrade path rather than building it, and this row is that path's reference, filed so the user's note is not lost. WHAT THE REFERENCE IS FOR: perceptual uniformity — interpolating in Oklab does not pass through the muddy greys an sRGB or naive linear-RGB blend does, and Oklch adds a hue channel with an even lightness for picking. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT ACTIONABLE, and this is NOT ESTABLISHED: the condition differs by renderer, so the upgrade is two different jobs. A DOM/CSS gradient can be honoured directly, because CSS Color 4 carries an interpolation space (`in oklab`, `in oklch`). A canvas gradient cannot: `CanvasGradient.addColorStop` takes no colour space, so Oklab interpolation there means interpolating the stops ourselves and emitting more of them. WHICH ONE THE PICKER'S GRADIENT IS — and whether ECharts' gradient option can carry a CSS colour-space interpolation at all — is the thing to establish before any of this is planned. NOT A FINDING: nothing is broken and the spec's decision stands unchanged; this is a pointer. RELATED: vg-405, the user's own finding that the picker and the gradient editor are barely usable, is what that spec answers; vg-439 is the second colour parser in renderer-core.

title: The two browser cases that drive the import picker assert a message prefix any failure produces, so they cannot tell a refusal's own reason from a crash
detail: FOUND WHILE REVIEWING THE THEME-STORE PLAN'S TASK A.7 (the re-done import route), 2026-10-20, by that task's reviewer, as an out-of-scope observation — not by that task, and not in its diff. THE FACT: `src/web/tests/e2e/reference-theme.spec.ts:756` and `:766` are the only browser cases that drive the import picker, and they assert only `toContainText("Could not import:")`. Any failure satisfies that prefix — a reader refusal, a 413, a 500, a transport error, a client-side throw that reaches the same status line — so the two cases prove a message appeared and cannot tell which. WHY IT IS NOT NOTHING: the rule A.7 implemented is that a refusal carries the reader's own reason rather than a generic sentence, and the host route does answer 400 with the reader's own text (`packages/host/src/server.ts:2172-2177`), covered at the unit level (`packages/host/src/themes/import.test.ts:185`, `server.test.ts:980-999`). So the ROUTE is covered; what is uncovered is the browser's mapping of that reason into the status line — exactly the half `packages/editor/src/theme-import.ts` owns now that the id rule has moved to the host. ALSO TRUE AND PART OF THE SHAPE: those two cases run against the editor preview, which serves no `/api` at all (`tests/e2e/store-library.ts:19-22`), so the import failure they exercise is a transport failure rather than a refusal. THE FIX NEEDS A DECISION, which is why this is a row and not a fix: the cases can assert the reader's specific reason, which needs the preview to serve a stubbed `/api/themes/import` or the case to move to a host-backed project, or they can stay transport cases and be renamed to say so. Both are reasonable and the choice is a scope decision. OWNER: whoever owns `tests/e2e/reference-theme.spec.ts`'s import cases. NOT FIXED HERE: not A.7's file, and the choice above is not an agent's to make silently.

title: The Host mode's display row cannot draw the checked drawing's second line, because no route answers a display's address or resolution
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING THE THEME-STORE PLAN'S TASK A.8 (this PC as a mode), 2026-10-20, and carried in that commit's own `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer rather than fixed there. THE FACT: the checked drawing `docs/design/mockups/current/host-settings.html` gives each display row a second line, `192.168.1.42 · 1280x800`, and nothing in the host's answers carries either value. `activeThemeMap` answers `{ id, label, kind, theme }` per display - an id, a label, a kind and the theme it shows - so the row A.8 builds names the display and its theme and stops there. Closing it needs a route read that does not exist plus a decision about whether that line is still wanted at all. WHY THE DECISION IS NOT OBVIOUS: the drawing marks its Displays section provisional itself, and the per-display model that owns display identity is the theme-store spec's neighbour, not this plan's, so adding an address and a resolution to a route is a decision about what the host publishes about a machine rather than a missing field. A display's address is also the kind of value that is wrong the moment a machine changes networks, which is a reason to want it and a reason to be careful about caching it. OWNER: whoever owns the host's display answers (`packages/host/src/settings/active-theme.ts` and the route that serves them). NOT FIXED HERE: A.8's brief required `server.ts` to be touched only if a route needs a read it does not already have, and whether this read is wanted is a product decision rather than a task gap.

title: The player's pagehide handler disposes the chart-refresh loop for good, so the back/forward-cache re-arm the module documents and the editor uses cannot happen there
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 while investigating vg-647 (a phone player's panels blinking), and recorded separately because it is a fact about the code rather than a guess about that symptom. THE ASYMMETRY: `scene-fabric/src/chart-refresh.ts` returns three lifetimes on purpose - `stop()`/`start()` for the page's own, `dispose()` for good - and its own comment says the pair exists "because a page frozen into the back/forward cache comes back - and a loop that could only be stopped came back dead (vg-510)". The EDITOR uses that pair: `editor/src/editor-main.ts:455` calls `chartRefresh.stop()` and `:465` calls `chartRefresh.start()`. The PLAYER does not: `player/src/main.ts` calls only `chartRefresh.setRate` (`:402`) and `chartRefresh.dispose()` (`:414`), and its `pagehide` listener is registered `{ once: true }` (`:406-429`). So on the player the terminal dispose is the only teardown, and a page restored from the back/forward cache is left with a disposed repaint loop, a disconnected `ResizeObserver`, a closed `liveHandle`, disposed controls and a disposed scene handle - nothing re-arms any of it, and `start()` after `dispose()` is documented to do nothing. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: that this causes vg-647. A restored page under this code would be dead rather than blinking, and the user's symptom is a blink, so the two do not obviously match and this row is not evidence for that one. It is also not claimed that the player is wrong to tear down permanently - a player page may be intended to end for good, and the editor's page is the one with a document worth keeping. WHAT IS CLAIMED: the module documents a two-way contract for a page that comes back, the editor honours it and the player does not, and nothing in the player says which of the two it means. Either the player's teardown should use `stop()` and re-arm on `pageshow`, or its `pagehide` comment should say that a restored player page is deliberately dead. OWNER: `src/web/packages/player/src/main.ts`.

title: Removing /settings's Themes section also removes that page's only display selector, so its Questions section can only answer for the default display
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 while preparing task A.10's brief, by reading the page rather than the plan. THE COUPLING: `/settings`'s Questions section asks a theme's questions for ONE display, and that display is `selected` (`packages/host/public/settings.html:137`, initialised to `"default"`), which is read at `:248` as `?display=${encodeURIComponent(selected)}` when the answers are fetched. `selected` has EXACTLY ONE WRITER in the whole page: the `onSelect` callback the page hands to `themeList` (`:182`), which is the display column the theme list renders. So the Themes section is not only a duplicate listing - it is also this page's display selector, and the column lives inside `themeList`'s own output (`packages/host/public/theme-list.js:310-415`, which R116 names as where the column and the cost note are built), so the column cannot be kept while the list goes. THE CONSEQUENCE OF A.10 AS WRITTEN: A.10's text (R116) removes `/settings`'s Themes section and says only that 'what leaves is the duplicate listing', which understates it - after the removal the Questions section is pinned to the default display, with no control to answer a theme's questions for another display. In practice the loss is modest rather than total, because `selected` starts as `"default"` and only changes when a consumer presses another row, so the page's behaviour on load is unchanged; what is lost is the ability to answer for a display other than the default. WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY A.10's TO DECIDE: `/settings` is the host's own page and R116 keeps both it and `/library` served, because they are what a phone or a browser with no editor open can reach, so dropping a capability from it is a product decision about what that page is for now that the editor shell has a This PC mode. A.8's region draws the unanswered slots the chosen display's theme leaves, so the editor half exists; whether the plain host page should keep per-display answers at all, gain a selector of its own, or hand that job to the editor is the user's call and is not decided here. RULED FOR A.10's PURPOSES (R153, ledger 2026-10-20): the Questions section STAYS, it answers for the default display, and the page SAYS which display it is answering for rather than silently answering for one. Cost if wrong: `/settings` answers for the default where the author expected the display they last pressed, and the fix is either one selector or one sentence - both cheap, and this row records the question so the wrong choice is visible rather than silent. OWNER: `packages/host/public/settings.html`, together with whatever decides that page's fate once the editor's This PC mode is the surface people actually use.

title: The shell's status footer is the editor's readout and renders in every mode, so the store mode shows document counts that are not its own
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 while adjudicating A.8's fix round, and filed rather than fixed there because that round's scope is the host mode. THE SHAPE: `editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx:641-649` renders `<footer id="status" className="editor-shell-status">` unconditionally - it is a sibling of the mode section, not a child of it - and its contents are the EDITOR's: `StatusReadout store={store}` reads the open document's object and selection counts, beside the host mark, the diagnostic message, the save state and the publish indicator. The header carries the three-mode switch and the mode region is chosen by `mode`, but the footer is not, so `themes` mode shows the same document readouts as `editor` mode. CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `store-mode/region.tsx` contains **no occurrence of `status`** at all, so the store mode publishes no status line and has no seam to reach the footer with - the footer is simply the editor's and renders everywhere. WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT A ONE-LINE FIX: what the store mode's status bar SHOULD say is a design question with no answer on disk - the host page's drawing answers it for `this-pc` only (`docs/design/mockups/current/host-settings.html:144-150`, a live display count on the left and the save state on the right, under a comment naming §7.6), and no drawing in `docs/design/mockups/current/` was read for the store mode while filing this. The shape of the fix is the same one R154 rules for the host mode - the region owns the content and the shell owns the placement, so the region publishes and the footer renders per mode - but the strings and the data are the store mode's own and are not established here. RELATION TO A.8: A.8's region drew its own `border-t` strip (`host-settings-mode/region.tsx:595-605`) as a workaround for this gap, and A.8's fix round removes that strip and builds the host mode's half of the seam; this row is the other half, plus the general statement that the footer is not mode-aware. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx` for the placement, `src/web/packages/editor/src/store-mode/region.tsx` for the content.

title: The shell's status strip drops the save state and the publish indicator in the Host mode, so an unsaved document is not announced while it is showing
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by the scoped re-review of task A.8's fix round 1, and recorded as a consequence rather than a defect because it is what the ruling and the drawing ask for. WHAT HAPPENS: task A.8 moved the Host mode's status line out of the region and into the shell's own `#status` footer (R154). The footer's `this-pc` branch renders the two host strings and nothing else - a live display count on the left and the save sentence on the right, which is exactly the drawing's bar (`docs/design/mockups/current/host-settings.html:144-150`). The editor and store modes are unchanged and still render all five children. SO THE LOSS IS REAL AND INTENDED: `SaveState` and `PublishIndicator` are not drawn while the Host mode is showing, so an author who has unsaved work and switches to This PC sees no save state in the strip. The mode switch's own dirty guard is what covers the document in the meantime, and nothing is lost or misrepresented - the values simply are not shown. WHY IT IS FILED ANYWAY, when the re-review called it 'an accepted consequence, not a defect': the SDD ledger that records it is deleted when the plan closes, so a note there is not a durable record; and the drawing is a static mockup of the host page, drawn before anyone asked whether a save state should survive a mode switch, so following it is faithful rather than obviously right. The question - should the strip keep the document's save state in every mode, or does a mode own its own strip - is a product decision and it is the user's. Cost if wrong: an author works in the editor, switches to This PC, and cannot see that the document is unsaved; the fix is to render the two editor readouts beside the host strings, or to keep them in every mode. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx`.

title: Assigning a theme from its own surface closes it, so the author is returned to the gallery rather than to the theme they were reading
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by task A.9's fix round 1, reported as its own concern 5 rather than discovered by a reviewer. WHAT THE FIX DID: the original review's finding 1 was that `ItemModal` and `AssignDisplay` are rendered as React SIBLINGS (`store-mode/region.tsx:706-720`), so Base UI's nested-dialog coordination never engages - one Escape closes both, and two scrims stack. Round 1 fixed it by closing the item modal as the choice opens, so the two never coexist. That is measured: jsdom proves the modal is unmounted. WHAT IT COSTS, and this is the finding: the author's place. Someone who opens a theme from the gallery, presses the cell's assign action, and finishes the assignment lands back in the gallery rather than on the theme they were reading. THE ALTERNATIVE, in the seat's own account: nest the two properly, which needs a `children` prop on `ItemModal`, a hoisted render site, and a browser to trust the result. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A ROUND: the trade is one measured behaviour (one dialog at a time, which jsdom can prove) against one source-derived and unmeasured defect (the stacking, which no browser has exercised), so swapping them is a product decision about the store's flow rather than a defect with a specified correct answer - and the nesting route needs a browser run that the served bundles cannot give, since they predate `4f82fcc3`. The question is whether an author who assigns from a theme should be returned to that theme or to the gallery. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/store-mode/region.tsx`, which renders both surfaces, together with `store-mode/assign-display.tsx`.

title: The chooser's write path for this PC's own screen is asserted nowhere, so pressing your own row and landing on that screen's dashboard has no test
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by task A.10's implementer, as its own concern 4 rather than by a reviewer. WHAT HAPPENED: A.10 moved the two cases whose subject is the theme list from `/settings` to the chooser. The chooser is served at `/` (`packages/host/src/server.ts:2554-2562`), and `/` is one-shot for the caller's own screen - `displayKeyFor` answers `this-pc` for a loopback browser, so a write that gives this PC a theme makes the next `/` resolve a theme and serve that screen's dashboard. A case that must still be the chooser after its write therefore has to press ANOTHER display's row. Both moved cases do exactly that. SO THE GAP: the write path for this PC's own screen - press your own row, the write lands, and the browser is handed to that screen's dashboard - is now asserted nowhere in `tests/e2e/host-settings.spec.ts`. It is not that the path is broken; it is that nothing measures it. `publish-loop.spec.ts` also drives `/` for a display, and whether it covers that hand-off was NOT checked - so the first step is to read it rather than to write a case. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A ROUND: the fix is a new case in a file A.10 had just restructured, and the honest first move is to find out whether another spec already covers the hand-off, which is a different question from A.10's own contract. Cost if wrong: the chooser's own-screen hand-off can break - a display that should have been handed to its dashboard instead stays on the chooser, or the reverse - and every spec stays green, because the only case that would notice was shaped to avoid the path. OWNER: `src/web/tests/e2e/host-settings.spec.ts`, with `src/web/tests/e2e/publish-loop.spec.ts` checked first.

title: The chooser logs one 404 per theme with no thumbnail, eleven on the e2e fixture, because the fallback requests an image that is not there
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by task A.10's implementer, as its own concern 5, and framed as 'observed, not this task's'. WHAT HAPPENS: the chooser at `/` and the store mode both render their rows through `packages/host/public/settings/theme-list.js`, which falls back to the theme's name when a theme carries no thumbnail - a fallback the module's own comment documents as normal, not an error. The cost is that the missing image is still REQUESTED, so every thumbnail-less theme costs a 404 in the console: eleven on the e2e fixture. NOT INTRODUCED BY A.10: it is pre-existing on both pages, and A.10 changed nothing about it - it was noticed because A.10's browser run inspected the rendered page and its network, which is where an observation like this comes from. WHY IT IS FILED ANYWAY: it is a real observable with a real (if small) decision behind it - whether the list should know a theme has no thumbnail before requesting one, or should keep requesting and treat the 404 as the fallback's trigger. The second is what it does today and it works; the first is quieter. It is also the kind of noise that hides a REAL 404 when one appears. Cost if wrong: an author debugging a genuinely missing asset scrolls past eleven expected 404s, and the expected ones are indistinguishable from the one that matters. OWNER: `src/web/packages/host/public/settings/theme-list.js`.

title: design:check's design:md half never runs while design-tokens is red, so the gate's own citation check is invisible from npm run gate
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by task A.10's implementer, as its own concern 6, and it is a finding about the instrument rather than about a surface. WHAT HAPPENS: `npm run design:check` short-circuits - while its `design-tokens` half is red it never reaches `design:md`, so `npm run gate` reports one red step and says nothing about whether the citation check would have passed. A.10's implementer ran `npm run design:md` separately and read exit 0 (lint clean, 367 citation sources clean), so nothing is hidden TODAY. WHY IT IS STILL A ROW: the short-circuit means a green `design:md` is not evidence `npm run gate` can produce, and the current baseline makes that permanent rather than momentary - `design:check` has been red at its `vg-626` baseline (remainder 20 against a ceiling of 19) since the per-display plan landed, so every gate run since has silently skipped one of its two checks. Anyone who fixes `design-tokens` and expects the gate to have been checking citations all along is wrong. It also means a `design:md` regression could land inside a period when the only command anyone runs is the gate. This is NOT a request to raise the ceiling - `vg-626` records that raising `remainderCeiling` is the one move the instrument exists to refuse. It is the smaller question of whether the two halves should run independently and report both. Cost if wrong: a citation error (a `§N` naming a marker that does not exist, which `design:md --cite` is built to catch) lands on `develop` with every gate run green, because the half that would have caught it did not execute. OWNER: the `design:check` script in `src/web/package.json` together with the design-token check it chains.

title: Two jsdom harnesses describe work the settings page no longer does, and one still injects theme-list.js the page never calls
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by task A.10's task review, finding 2. WHERE: `src/web/packages/host/src/settings-page.dom.test.ts:32-40` and `src/web/packages/host/src/editor-link.dom.test.ts:35-42`. WHAT IS STALE: both comments say the page 'calls the module's own resolution rule as well as drawing its rows through it'. A.10 removed the page's import of `theme-list.js` and every call to it, so `/settings` now does neither - the claim is true of `library.html` alone. WHAT IS DEAD: `settings-page.dom.test.ts` still imports `../public/theme-list.js` (`:6`) and still passes it as the `__themeList` parameter (`:121`), which the page's script no longer references; the harness's import-rewriting `.replace` (`:34-40`) now matches nothing on this page. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the comment is a reword, but the dead scaffolding is the harness's own mechanism - `editor-link.dom.test.ts` loops over BOTH pages and still needs the injection for `library.html`, so removing it from one file is a judgement about how the two harnesses should relate rather than a deletion. A.10's review called it safe to leave. Cost if wrong: the next person to change the settings page reads a comment describing a call that does not exist and either preserves dead scaffolding or re-adds a call the page does not want. OWNER: `src/web/packages/host/src/settings-page.dom.test.ts`, with `editor-link.dom.test.ts` checked for the shared shape.

title: The screenshot registry names an action the settings capture no longer performs, so its evidence line describes a press that does not happen
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by task A.10's task review, finding 3. WHERE: `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md:183` registers the capture's visible action as 'Choose a theme whose bindings need a device'. WHAT CHANGED: A.10 removed the theme list from `/settings`, and the capture's case now sets the theme through `PUT /api/themes/active` via the `request` fixture and presses nothing at all. WHY IT SURVIVED THE CHANGE: the capture is skipped unless `YUNARI_CAPTURE=1` (the run reported one skipped case), so the stale line was never exercised by A.10's browser run and no assertion could have caught it. WHY IT MATTERS: `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md` is the registry that says which actions have captured evidence, and its per-action line is what a reader uses to decide whether a screenshot still represents the surface. A line naming an action the capture does not perform makes the evidence claim unverifiable from the registry alone. Cost if wrong: someone reads the registry, believes a theme-choosing interaction is captured on `/settings`, and either re-captures a screenshot of a surface that no longer has the interaction or trusts a screenshot whose action has changed. OWNER: `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md`, with the capture's case in `src/web/tests/e2e/host-settings.spec.ts`.

title: The moved chooser cases reach `/` only when nothing is published, and the published store is in-memory with no reset in the spec
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by task A.10's task review, finding 4, as an observation rather than a defect. WHAT THE CASES DEPEND ON: the two cases A.10 moved to the chooser reach it only when `/` resolves no theme, which needs three things at once (`packages/host/src/server.ts:2523-2569`) - nothing published, nothing chosen for this PC, and more than one theme in the store. WHAT IS CONTROLLED: `resetStores` covers the chosen theme and the theme count, so two of the three are. WHAT IS NOT: the published store is in-memory and file-less (`packages/host/src/serve/published.ts:32-46`), so a publish left behind by an earlier spec in the same run would make `/` resolve that theme and serve a dashboard instead of the chooser. WHY IT IS FILED WHEN IT FAILS LOUD: the reviewer's own verdict is that it fails loud and can never read green - a case that lands on a dashboard fails its `h1` assertion rather than passing for the wrong reason. So this is a diagnosability gap, not a correctness one: the failure names a locator mismatch rather than the leftover publish that caused it. The reviewer's suggested fix is one line - `expect(h1).toHaveText('Choose a theme')` as the case's first assertion, so the precondition names itself. Cost if wrong: a case fails in a full-suite run, passes alone, and the reader spends a round looking for the defect in the chooser rather than in a publish another spec left behind. OWNER: `src/web/tests/e2e/host-settings.spec.ts`.

title: The cost note's post-write half is asserted nowhere, so nothing proves the note survives a write on any surface
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by task A.10's task review, finding 5. WHAT WAS LOST: the cost-note case in `src/web/tests/e2e/host-settings.spec.ts` used to assert that the note survives the write that follows it. A.10 moved the case to the chooser, whose successful write reloads the page (`packages/host/public/library.html:90-102`), so the post-write half became unreachable and the case now reads both halves of the cost table BEFORE any press. WHAT REMAINS: the discriminating pair is intact - this PC, a host monitor, is warned `/idle/`; the paired display is told nothing - and the row press still rebuilds rows in place (`library.html:85-88`), so half the original claim is retained. WHAT HAS NO TEST ANYWHERE: the other half. `packages/host/public/theme-list.dom.test.ts:612-650` covers the cost table at draw time only, so no surface now proves the note survives a write. THIS IS DISTINCT FROM vg-653: that row is the write path for this PC's own screen having no test; this is the note's own post-write persistence having no test, and either can be closed without the other. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A ROUND: the seat reported the loss honestly in the case's own comment, and restoring it needs a surface that rebuilds rows in place after a write, which A.10's review confirms does not exist - so the fix is a decision about whether such a surface should exist, not a case to re-add. Cost if wrong: a write that drops the cost note - leaving an author who has just assigned a theme with no warning about what it will do - is invisible to every spec. OWNER: `src/web/tests/e2e/host-settings.spec.ts`, with `packages/host/public/theme-list.js` as the surface that would have to hold it.

title: A full-suite run times out store.test.ts's asset-count case, and the same case passes alone in four seconds, so the gate reads red at random
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by the phase-A boundary seat, which ran the gate to produce the plan's closing evidence and got two different answers from the same commit. WHAT HAPPENED: the first `npm run test` sample failed one case - `src/web/packages/host/src/themes/store.test.ts:1850`, 'holds read and write to the same asset count' - on a 20-second timeout, under a run that spawns 286 workers. The file alone: 67 passed, 4.3 seconds, exit 0. The whole suite again: 286 files / 3902 tests, exit 0. So it is load-induced, and two samples of the same commit disagree. WHY THE CASE IS EXPOSED: it is not a pure unit test - it calls `store.write`, `placeOnDisk` and `store.read`, so it does real filesystem I/O, and a 20-second budget is generous for that alone and thin for it under a 286-way spawn on a machine another session may be sharing. THE MECHANISM IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and that is why this is a row rather than a fix: it could be the worker count, the timeout, contention on the disk, or something in `store.ts` that is slow only under contention. Naming which needs a measurement this boundary did not make. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FLAKE: the boundary's own first fact is the gate's exit code, and a gate that is red at random cannot be used as evidence - a future seat that samples the red half will report the gate red and be believed, and `AGENTS.md` already records that a single sample of a flaky spec is not a measurement. Cost if wrong: a real regression in `store.ts` hides behind 'it is probably that flake again', and the flake's own triage is spent re-establishing what this row already knows. OWNER: `src/web/packages/host/src/themes/store.test.ts`, with the timeout and worker settings in `src/web/vitest.config.ts` as the other candidate.

title: The facet-reachability spec covers one width and a narrow wrap, so two of the three sizes the plan names are proved by no spec
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by the phase-A boundary seat, as its concern 3. WHAT THE PLAN ASKS FOR: the boundary's first browser claim is the grid at 1280x720, 1440x900 and 200% zoom with every facet still reachable. WHAT THE SUITE HAS: `src/web/tests/e2e/editor-rail.spec.ts`'s case 'no width drops a facet' covers 1280 and one narrow wrap, and nothing else. So the boundary could pass its claim only by running 1440 and the zoom OUTSIDE the suite, which it did - against a five-theme fixture, all three sizes, five of five facets drawn inside the viewport, five popovers opening, and each facet with options filtering (Author 5 to 3, Colour 5 to 3, Sensors 5 to 2, Shape 5 to 3) and clearing. WHY IT IS STILL A ROW: that run is boundary evidence and not a regression test. Nothing in the suite fails if 1440 or a zoomed viewport starts clipping a facet tomorrow, so the claim the plan treats as acceptance is proved once and then unguarded. The fix is to add the two sizes to the existing case rather than to write a new one. Also worth recording: the 200% zoom is modelled as a 640x360 CSS viewport, which is the repo's own model and exercises layout rather than rasterisation - so a real browser zoom is still unverified by anything. Cost if wrong: a later change makes the facet rail clip at a width the plan named as acceptance, every gate stays green, and the loss is found by a person using the product at that size. OWNER: `src/web/tests/e2e/editor-rail.spec.ts`.

title: Three files sit past the 800-line stop and the oversize ratchet that would catch them runs in nothing
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by the final whole-branch review of the theme store's phase A, finding 3, and re-checked by the controller. `node scripts/oversize-files.mjs` **exits 1**: 717 tracked files, 125 past the 500 signal, 48 over the 800 stop, and **3 over the stop and not in the ceiling** - `src/web/packages/editor/src/store-mode/region.dom.test.tsx` (1376), `src/web/packages/editor/src/ui-copy-surfaces.test.ts` (821) and `src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/glass.dom.test.ts` (841). Two of the three are this phase's. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE THREE FILES: `npm run gate` chains only `oversize-files --self-test`, and CI runs only `gate`, so **the ratchet itself runs in nothing** - which is why three files could cross the stop without anyone seeing it. The instrument exists and is not wired in. ALSO FILED HERE, the review's finding 7, because it is the same measurement and the same fix: three source files sit past the 500 signal and short of the stop - `store-mode/region.tsx` (732), `host-settings-mode/region.tsx` (724) and `shell-layout.tsx` (797, up from 555), the last three lines under the stop. RULED: the files are to be **reduced, not accepted into the ceiling**. A ceiling entry is the move the instrument exists to refuse - that is `vg-626`'s rule for the token instrument, and it applies here for the same reason: an entry converts a finding into a permanent permission. The order matters and is the reason this is a row rather than a fix round: wiring the ratchet into the gate BEFORE the files come down would make the gate red for a new reason, which is worse than a ratchet that does not run. So: split or reduce the three, then add the ratchet to `gate`. Cost if wrong: the 800 stop stops meaning anything, and the next phase adds a fourth file the same way - silently, because nothing measures it. OWNER: the three files, with the `gate` script in `src/web/package.json` and `scripts/oversize-files.mjs`'s ceiling as the instrument.

title: The editor re-spells the host's assignable groups, so a fourth group would be dropped on both sides with nothing failing
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by the final whole-branch review of the theme store's phase A, finding 2's code half, and re-checked by the controller. WHERE: `src/web/packages/editor/src/host-settings-mode/client.ts:27-37` declares its own `ASSIGNABLE_GROUPS` (gpu, system-disk, data-disk) and `isAssignableGroup`; `:283-288` then filters the host's own `required` list down to it, so a group the host adds and the editor does not know is **silently dropped** rather than surfaced. The comment at `:23-26` already admits this in its own words - 'the routes filter to them on both sides, so a fourth would arrive at neither'. WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT A FIX: the comment also names the reason the obvious fix is unavailable - 'the editor has no dependency on the host package' - so importing the host's list is not open, and the real fix is a **shared owner** for the list, which is a design decision about which package holds it rather than an edit. Precedent says this shape gets fixed rather than tolerated: `vg-189` was the same defect for the host's own `settings/devices.ts` list, and `server.test.ts:4001` records that the groups became `ASSIGNABLE_GROUPS`'s there. The candidate owner is whatever the editor already depends on and the host can reach - the review notes that `renderer-core` is where the spec puts shared, Fabric-free domain facts, and that the colour mode already went there. Cost if wrong: the host learns a fourth slot, the editor drops it without a word, and the author sees a question they cannot answer with no error anywhere - the failure is silent on both sides, which is exactly what a second spelling of one list buys. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/host-settings-mode/client.ts`, with `src/web/packages/host/src/settings/devices.ts` as the incumbent spelling.

title: The copy-readers walk skips facet option rows, so the names those rows print are checked against nothing
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by the final whole-branch review of the theme store's phase A, finding 4. WHERE: `src/web/packages/editor/src/ui-copy-readers.ts:173` skips facet option rows when it walks the rendered surface for user-visible strings. WHY THAT MATTERS: those rows print **table-owned names** for Colour mode and Shape - the values come from a table rather than from `ui-copy.ts` - so the walk is the only thing that could catch a name drifting between the table and the surface, and it now steps over exactly those rows. The review names this as the same class as `vg-591`, `vg-592` and `vg-593`, which are the existing rows for strings that escape the copy readers' net. WHY IT IS A ROW: the fix is a decision about how a table-owned name should be walked - whether the reader learns the tables' shape, or the tables gain a reader of their own - and picking wrong widens the net over strings that are legitimately not copy. Cost if wrong: a facet option is renamed in its table and the surface keeps printing the old name, or the two drift apart, with `ui-copy.test.ts`'s walk reporting clean because it never looked. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/ui-copy-readers.ts`, with the Colour mode and Shape tables as the other half.

title: The theme store imports a Fabric-backed module for one pure string, when the shared layer the spec names is renderer-core
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 by the final whole-branch review of the theme store's phase A, finding 6. WHERE: `src/web/packages/host/src/themes/store.ts:15` imports `cssArtboardPaint` from `scene-fabric` - the Fabric-backed renderer layer - to produce one pure CSS string. WHY IT IS NOT A RUNTIME DEFECT: the review checked, and the import is **tree-shaken**: `dist/main.js` carries no Fabric as a result, so nothing breaks and no bundle grows. WHY IT IS STILL A ROW: it is an ownership question, not a size one. `AGENTS.md` puts `renderer-core` as the Fabric/DOM-free layer and `scene-fabric` as the one that may use Fabric, so a host-side store reaching into `scene-fabric` for a pure function inverts the dependency the architecture is built on - and it works today only because the bundler happens to drop the rest. The review notes the colour mode already went to `renderer-core`, which is the precedent for where a pure paint helper belongs. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: moving it means deciding whether `cssArtboardPaint` moves to `renderer-core`, is re-exported, or is duplicated - and `AGENTS.md` forbids re-export wrappers after a move except for package public barrels, so the choice is not free. Cost if wrong: a later change makes the import non-tree-shakeable, the host bundle gains Fabric, and the architecture guardrail is discovered to have been held by the bundler rather than by the dependency graph. OWNER: `src/web/packages/host/src/themes/store.ts`, with `scene-fabric`'s `cssArtboardPaint` and `renderer-core` as the two candidate homes.

title: A disabled ControlIconButton still advertises hover, so a control that cannot be pressed lifts its tone on the pointer
detail: FOUND BY the scoped re-review of the theme-store plan's phase A fix round (2026-10-20), as its observation 1, and reported as a row rather than folded into that round. WHERE: `packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-icon-button.tsx:112` writes `${tone} hover:border-edge hover:text-text`, and `hover:` applies whether or not the element is disabled — contrast `components/ui/dialog.tsx:17`, the same class of control with `enabled:hover:border-accent enabled:hover:text-accent disabled:text-faint`, whose own comment records that the `enabled:` qualifier is the deliberate half. CONSEQUENCE: hovering a disabled control lifts `--faint` toward `--text`, so a control that cannot be pressed answers the pointer. PRE-EXISTING AND COMPONENT-WIDE, not introduced by R164: the same control is used by `layer-panel.tsx:55`, `selection-lead.tsx:85` and `pager.tsx:196,219`. What R164 did was give the control its first disabled uses (`store-mode/gallery.tsx`, `item-modal.tsx`), which is what made the gap visible at all. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the cause is named, but the fix is a class-wide change to a shared control whose other call sites were not audited, and `--faint`-to-`--text` on hover is a visible tone change that this repo requires rendered inspection for rather than a className assertion. COST IF WRONG: a disabled control answers the pointer, which is the exact confusion R164 disabled those two cell actions to remove. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: auditing the four other call sites, then one `enabled:` qualifier, checked in a browser.

title: The architecture README's system diagram and Rendering boundaries table name neither the shell's three modes nor the editor-to-host import route
detail: FOUND BY the theme-store plan's phase A fix round and recorded in its commit `b561dcaf` as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer; materialised here because a trailer with no row is a finding with no home. The round repaired `docs/architecture/README.md:27-49`, which described a previous shape in a file that claims currency, and stopped there because that range was its scope. What is left is the file's system diagram and its Rendering boundaries table, which name neither the shell's three modes (store, host settings, and the default editor mode) nor the editor-to-host import route. The trailer's own judgement, kept rather than upgraded here: the modes are an editor-internal composition and the import route rides a relationship the diagram already draws, so no boundary the diagram states has changed. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: whether a package-internal composition belongs on a diagram of package boundaries is a judgement about what that file is for, not a correction to a wrong statement — and it is not the task that found it. COST IF WRONG: a reader takes the diagram for the whole shape of the shell and misses that the editor has three modes, which is the same class of drift the `:27-49` repair was made to stop. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on whether the diagram is a package map or a shell map.

title: The host-theme e2e fixture declares an opaque board behind a video and no test decodes that video, so the media-over-paint rule has no browser regression test
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 while fixing `vg-667` under decision 0080. WHERE: `tests/e2e/host-theme.ts`'s `videoEnvelope` declares `background: palette.bar` — an opaque `#101318` — together with a video asset, which is exactly the combination `vg-667` was about, and no spec that mounts it decodes the video or reads a pixel of it: `grep -rn videoEnvelope tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` matches nothing. The fixture shipped the trap and could not see it, which is why the defect survived a browser suite. WHAT IS MISSING: a browser case that mounts that envelope and proves the video reaches the display — the layered rule is now `scene-fabric/src/artboard-backdrop.ts` and its unit proof is `artboard-backdrop.dom.test.ts`, but nothing in the browser suite would notice the paint returning to the canvas. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: it is a coverage gap rather than a defect, it is not the task that found it, and writing the spec means deciding what a browser can assert about a decoded video frame (a pixel that moves) rather than about geometry. REPORTED BY the controller, from `vg-667`'s own detail.

title: Two glass.dom.test.ts cases set canvas.backgroundColor by hand as a stand-in for a canvas fill no surface paints any more
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 while fixing `vg-667` under decision 0080. WHERE: `src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/glass.dom.test.ts:591` and `:613` each assign `canvas.backgroundColor = "#000000"` before rendering a panel. Under 0080 no surface paints the artboard onto the canvas at all — the player clears it in `scene.ts`, the editor clears it in `editor-shell.ts`, and `persist.ts` restores that empty value over any fill a revived document brings — so the state those two cases set up is one the product never produces. The cases themselves are about the sample-size bound and are not wrong; their premise is stale, and a reader taking them as the shape of a real canvas is the cost. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: pass a `backdrop` to the stage fixture instead, which is how every other case in that file gets a base under the panel. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: it is a test-fixture observation rather than a defect, and it is not the task that found it. REPORTED BY the controller.

title: Five live sites still exclude src/web/.agent-scratch, which 0081's cleanup relocated out of the tree, so each is now an inert exclusion for a path that no longer exists
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 while building the scratch gate under decision 0081, in the same commit that relocated the directory. WHERE: `scripts/dead-selectors.mjs:38` (a SKIP list), `scripts/design-md.mjs:581` (a comment naming it as the example of captured residue), `docs/architecture/dead-selectors.md:107` and the two pasted command recipes below it (`:253`, `:323`, each carrying the same SKIP array), `docs/architecture/manager-census.md:315` and `:334` (the prose that explains the exclusion and why it was deliberate), and `.gitignore:81`. WHAT IS NOT DECIDED, which is why this is a row rather than a fix: whether an exclusion for a path that cannot now be created should be removed as dead compensation or kept as a second lock. The argument for keeping them is that the scratch gate refuses the path but a hook is one layer, and `.gitignore` should keep ignoring the name if it ever returns; the argument for removing them is that 0081's own note calls this compensation rather than cleanup, and five sites agreeing about a directory that does not exist is a reader's wrong turn. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: it is not the task that found it -- the task was the gate and the relocation -- and it spans four owners plus the ignore file. REPORTED BY the controller, from its own commit trailer.

title: The store's Shape facet files the product's own phone artboard under `other`, because 19.5:9 is not one of the published aspect buckets
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 while finishing the theme-store spec's pre-planning probes -- open question 8 asked for exactly this measurement, in as many words: the distance at which a theme falls to `Other` is a number nobody has measured. WHERE: `ASPECT_BUCKETS` (`renderer-core/src/theme/facet-record.ts:65-78`) publishes 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:10, 16:9, 21:9 and 32:9, with `ASPECT_TOLERANCE = 0.005` (0.5% in log space, `:87`). The product's own artboard ratios are 16:9, **19.5:9** and 4:3 (`editor/src/artboard-presets.ts:14-21`), and `artboardSize("19.5:9", "1080p", "landscape")` is 2340x1080 -- the phone shape the author-journey plan calls "the core workflow, not an edge case". MEASURED: 19.5:9 (2.1667) is 7.41% from 21:9 (2.3333) in log space against a 0.5% tolerance, so a phone-shaped theme's `aspect` is `other`. The reading is the shipped rule's rather than an approximation: a reimplementation of `aspectOf` reproduced all five expectations the shipped test asserts (`facet-record.test.ts:143-151`, `2350x1000 -> "other"` included) before its reading of 2340x1080 was trusted, and the reproduction is `C:\tmp\facet-repro.mjs`, outside the repo. **NO TOLERANCE FIXES IT, which is the part that makes this a set problem rather than a number problem**: the tolerance exists to keep a 2.35:1 artboard out of 21:9, 2.35:1 is 0.71% from it, and so any tolerance large enough to file 19.5:9 under 21:9 (>=7.41%) swallows the very case the tolerance was chosen for. A bucket is required. The comment at `:81-85` claims the tolerance keeps "every real display" inside; 19.5:9 is a real display shape, it is the one this product's own chooser offers, and it does not. ALSO, AND DECIDED SEPARATELY: 1920x480 (4:1), the shape of the TURZX panel in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-turzx-panel-displays-design.md:114`, is 11.8% from 32:9 and so is also `other` -- possibly the right answer for a 4:1 strip, but it should be decided with the panel work rather than fallen into. NOT ESTABLISHED: which set is right. Adding 19.5:9 changes the published `AspectBucket` vocabulary, the facet row's labels, the spec's own set at § "Finding a theme: the five facets" and the tests. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the fix needs a design decision rather than sitting inside one owner, which is this repo's own test for filing. REPORTED BY the controller. Filed as issue 50. RULED 2026-10-21 by the user, at the theme-store spec's acceptance: ADD BOTH -- 19.5:9 and 4:1 -- AND MAKE THE SET EASY TO EXTEND. The phone shape this product's own chooser offers and the panel's 4:1 strip are settled together rather than the second waiting on the panel work; and the owner requires a ratio to be addable as an entry beside the others rather than as a revisit of the rule, so `ASPECT_BUCKETS` stays data beside `aspectOf` and adding a bucket is one entry plus its label, not a change to `ASPECT_TOLERANCE`'s logic. The vocabulary change, the facet row's labels, the spec's own set and the tests still move together -- that half of the row stands.

title: `vg-214`'s no-poll ruling says a hosting push would ride a channel the editor already holds, but the editor's only connection is the live-mode sample stream
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by the Task 23.5 implementer while recording `vg-214`'s ruling as a stated boundary, and materialised from that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer by the controller, which re-measured every claim below. WHAT THE RULING SAYS: `vg-214`'s RULED 2026-10-12 paragraph ends "The channel already exists: the editor holds a live connection to the host, and the host is the only process that can observe its own `setLan` or a restart. So the ruling is a direction, not a feature: when the stale indicator is judged worth fixing, the host announces the change on that connection and the store re-reads; the editor never polls." MEASURED, and narrower than that reads: the editor holds exactly ONE connection to the host, the sample stream at `SAMPLE_STREAM_PATH = "/ws"` (`renderer-core/src/data/protocol.ts:25`), opened through `createEditorSource` (`editor/src/live-source.ts:25`, called at `editor/src/editor-main.ts:163`) and open only in `live` mode; it carries telemetry batches. Every hosting call is a one-shot request and answer over `fetch` — `hosting-client.ts`'s own header now states this, with `fetcher: typeof fetch = fetch` as the default (`:33`, `:36`, `:97`, `:119`) — and there is no `new WebSocket(` anywhere in the workspace's `packages/*/src` or `tests`. THE TENSION, which is why this is a row rather than a wording fix: the channel the ruling points at exists but is (a) a telemetry stream, so a hosting announcement would have to multiplex a second message kind onto it, and (b) absent outside `live` mode, so a fix riding it would leave the indicator stale in exactly the mode where a host is most likely to be reconfigured out of band. The ruling's own words rule out the obvious alternative — "a connection the editor already holds rather than a new one it opens" — so a fix has to choose between multiplexing onto the sample stream, opening a hosting channel the ruling's phrasing discourages, or leaving the boundary as the editor being the only in-session writer.
