NOT ESTABLISHED: which of those is right, and whether `vg-214`'s author meant the sample stream at all or assumed a general editor-to-host connection existed. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the cause is a ruling's premise rather than a defect in one owner, and correcting the premise or choosing the channel is a design decision, which is this repo's own test for filing. The ruling itself is NOT withdrawn and Task 23.5's record is accurate — it states the direction against the sample stream and says the editor never polls. REPORTED BY the Task 23.5 implementer; the row's own record is `docs/decisions`-free because no decision note was owed for that task.

title: The citation convention Task 23.8 stated has live violations: bare decision numbers are ambiguous between the `adr/` and `decisions/` series, and the sweep's scope is unmeasured
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by the Task 23.8 implementer's review, materialised from that task's fix commit (`82febbc5`) `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer by the controller. WHAT THE CONVENTION NOW SAYS: `docs/adr/README.md` states that `docs/adr/` is a closed series (0001-0010, stopped 2026-09-25), that its numbers are its own, that the two series collide across 0001-0010 with both holding a `0004` on a different decision, and that a decision must therefore be cited by its directory (`adr/0004` against `decisions/0004`) because a bare number is ambiguous. `docs/decisions/README.md` states the same convention and its own numbering (0001-0083, with 0006, 0034 and 0042 absent). MEASURED INSTANCES, both found by the reviewer reading rather than by any check that exists: (1) `src/web/packages/host/src/server.ts:624` cites `ADR-0018` bare - this one RESOLVES, because `adr/` stops at 0010, so it is ambiguous in form only; (2) `docs/decisions/0078-the-host-imports-a-package-and-mints-the-id.md:128` cites "0009, 0010, 0018, 0019 and 0043" bare, and here `0009` and `0010` exist in BOTH series, so a reader cannot tell which decision is meant - this is the ambiguity the convention was written to prevent, live in a decision note. NOT ESTABLISHED: how many other bare citations of 0001-0010 exist across `docs/` and `src/web`. The controller took one loose grep and abandoned it as too noisy to count (it matched `00004a` and `00001;`), so the sweep's scope is genuinely unmeasured, which is why this is a row rather than a fix. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: Task 23.8's Step 2 asked for the convention to be STATED, and stating it is what makes these instances wrong; sweeping every citing site is a separate pass whose size nobody has measured, and sizing it is the first thing the row's own work would do. NOT the same finding as the convention being unenforced by any check (`reuse-gate.mjs` watches note paths, not their READMEs) - that is recorded in the drain ledger as an observation both Task 23.7 and Task 23.8 produced, and is deliberately not a row. WHAT CLOSES IT: a measurement of how many bare 0001-0010 citations exist, then either a sweep that writes the directory at each site or a ruling that the convention governs new citations only.

title: server.test.ts's deleted-display case read 'no card assigned' in one full-suite sample, passed alone and in the next full run at the same commit
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by the Task 23.9 implementer while running the gate for a docs-only change, and materialised from that task's close commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. The failure is an assertion, not a timeout: `packages/host/src/server.test.ts:3926` read `expected 'no card assigned' to be 'gpu-0'` in 92 ms, inside the case `The assignment a display is served > does not leak a deleted display's answers to another display`. NOT ESTABLISHED: the cause. Two whole-suite samples at the same commit disagree — the first was red on this one case of 3918, the second green with 287 files / 3918 tests — and the file alone is green (157 tests, 13.4 s), so a single sample is not a measurement. RELATED BUT NOT THE SAME: `vg-637` records one full-suite sample failing the host's bound-port case and `vg-661` records a timeout of store.test.ts's asset-count case; this names a different case with a different symptom, so neither row covers it. The tree held a docs-only change, so no source behaviour is implicated.

title: The save path does not bound the theme.json it writes, so a save can store a document the read then refuses
detail: FOUND BY TASK 23.11 (2026-10-21), the seat that closed vg-409. The store's save path bounds a theme's ASSETS (ThemeAssetLimitError, thrown in themes/store.ts before the staging folder exists) but nothing bounds `serialized`, the theme.json bytes it writes at `fs.writeFile(path.join(staging, THEME_FILE), serialized)` — while readStored refuses any stored document over MAX_THEME_FILE_BYTES (32 MiB). So a save can report success over a document the store will not read back, against the promise write's own docblock makes about assets: what the store will not serve is never what it stores. CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT on the built host (2026-10-21, after 85c0b09d): a PUT /api/themes/<id> whose envelope carries 33 MiB in an unvalidated scene field answers ok:true with a base, writes a 34,603,295-byte theme.json, and the next GET /api/themes/<id> answers 413. The same request at BASE wrote the same file and the read answered 404 — the read side is what 85c0b09d changed, not the write. THE DECISION OWED: whether the save should refuse a document the store cannot read back, and if so whether that refusal is ThemeTooLargeError reused or a save-side error of its own. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any real document reaches 32 MiB through the editor's own UI, since an editor save carries what was opened. Filed rather than fixed: a different trigger from vg-409's, and the write path's bounds are a different owner's decision.

title: Nothing decides who looks at an item's thumbnail or background video before it is listed, so a valid package can carry objectionable imagery past the review gate
detail: OPEN QUESTION 4 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md`, carried as a row by the user's 2026-10-21 acceptance, which ruled the questions still open become rows rather than gates. WHAT THE REVIEW GATE CATCHES AND DOES NOT: the owner reading a pull-request diff catches a broken item -- a stale locale key, a missing asset -- and catches nothing about the pixels. A thumbnail is an image and a background is a video, and neither is read by any validator this repo has: the diff shows that a file changed, not what it depicts. WHAT IS OWED: a decision on who looks at those pixels and when -- at submission, at review, or after listing on report -- and the trust ladder makes it sharper, because a verified author's item auto-merges on green validation and is listed with nobody having looked at it at all. NOT ESTABLISHED: what the options are, which is why this is a row rather than a task.

title: Nothing decides what happens to a listed item that is later withdrawn, or whether its download counter survives the withdrawal
detail: OPEN QUESTION 5 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md`, carried as a row by the user's 2026-10-21 acceptance. WHAT IT ASKS: what a withdrawal does -- does the item leave the listing, keep its URL, keep its bytes -- and whether its download counter survives it. WHY IT IS BLOCKED RATHER THAN MERELY OPEN: the answer is downstream of open question 1, where the bytes live. If they live on the store's own release after a re-home, removal is enforceable because the store owns the asset; if they live on the author's fork it is not, because the author can delete them and break every listed copy. Open question 1 was DECIDED 2026-10-21 as deferred to phase D's plan, so this row is scheduled behind that probe rather than undecided in its own right. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a withdrawal should decrement, freeze or delete the counter -- the hosting answer constrains that but does not settle it.

title: A widget-preset package has a shape but no authoring workflow, so the store's second kind cannot ship before something can author one
detail: OPEN QUESTION 6, first of the two addenda, in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md`, carried as a row by the user's 2026-10-21 acceptance. THE SHAPE IS SETTLED: a widget preset is a theme envelope minus the artboard -- a scene subtree plus its `bindings`, `globals` and `assets` -- and the store plan states it in exactly those words. THE SEQUENCING IS NOT: `§139` defers widget packages until an authoring workflow exists, so the store cannot carry a kind nothing can produce. WHAT IS OWED: an authoring workflow for a widget preset, which is editor work rather than store work and is carried by no phase. This is why v1 ships the dashboard theme only -- it is the one kind with an exchange unit today.

title: An editor theme has no artifact at all, so the store's third kind has nothing to carry until a decision says what one is
detail: OPEN QUESTION 6, second of the two addenda, in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md`, carried as a row by the user's 2026-10-21 acceptance. THE GAP IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION: `§35` separates editor-shell theming from authored dashboard-theme globals, so an editor theme is not a dashboard theme's `globals` under another name, and nothing in the repo is a portable editor-theme artifact today. WHAT IS OWED: what a token artifact is -- whether it is the editor-shell design-token vocabulary as a named versioned set, a theme-envelope variant, or a third format -- before the store can carry the kind. This is the design question of the two addenda; the widget preset's is sequencing only and has its own row. NOT ESTABLISHED: which of those shapes is right, which is why this is a row rather than a task.

title: The editor offers no tag furniture by default, so an author working offline has nothing to pick and the first proposals have nothing to be measured against
detail: OPEN QUESTION 7 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md`, carried as a row by the user's 2026-10-21 acceptance. WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED: the ruling of 2026-10-17 fixed the mechanism and the ONLINE vocabulary, which is the catalogue's own content and so needs no separate list. WHAT IS NOT: which tags the editor offers before it has ever seen the catalogue. The user's own examples -- `futuristic`, `retro`, `modern`, `elegant`, `classic`, `nature`, `cityscape` -- are recorded in the spec as the seed rather than as the answer. WHY IT MATTERS: an author working offline has nothing else to pick from, and the seed is what the first proposals are measured against, so a poor seed shapes the vocabulary that follows it. The store plan's phase G carries this rather than shipping the field with an empty list.

title: The answers store's removal check walks the prototype chain, so removing a theme named like an inherited property rewrites the file it should have left alone
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by Task 2's reviewer in the theme-store plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-theme-store-origin-and-style.md`), while reviewing the new `theme-origins.ts`, which copied this file's shape. THE DEFECT: `theme-settings.ts`'s `removeTheme` guards with `themeId in level`, and `in` walks the prototype chain, so `constructor`, `toString` and `__proto__` all answer true against an empty object. `THEME_ID` is `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/`, which accepts every one of them, so the guard passes, `Object.values(all).some(...)` finds a hit in every level, and the function saves. WHAT THAT COSTS: `readLevels` answers `{}` for a file it cannot read, so the save writes `{}` over a file that was there — the one write the function's own comment says it exists to avoid. `removeDisplay`'s `display in all` has the same shape, as does the `levels[display] = level` assignment for a `__proto__` display key. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the store plan owns `theme-origins.ts`, which the reviewer found had both holes and which Task 2 fixed with `Object.hasOwn` and a prototype-safe map build; this incumbent file is a different owner and was not in the plan's scope, so fixing it there would have been a change nobody reviewed. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a person can reach it in practice — a theme id comes from the folder name, so it needs a folder literally named `constructor` or `__proto__` together with an answers file that cannot be read. The trigger is narrow; the write is still the wrong direction.

title: The store cell's origin badge and the modal's provenance line are plain spans, so no copy check reads either word
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by the controller of the theme-store plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-theme-store-origin-and-style.md`), working Task 4's review NOTE 2, which said the copy walk never reaches the badge or the provenance line because the store-mode stub carries no origin. CORRECTED the same day: this row first blamed the modal's line being composed into one text node by `[fromStore, catalogueId, version].join(readingSeparator)` - a real property, but not the cause, and it named only one of the two surfaces. THE ACTUAL CAUSE: `ui-copy-readers.ts`'s `saidIn` reads a surface through `spokenIn` plus `paragraphsOf`, and `spokenIn` reads exactly `label`, `[aria-label]`, `button`, headings and definition terms while `paragraphsOf` reads `p` elements. `gallery.tsx`'s badge and `item-modal.tsx`'s provenance line are both plain `span`s, which are none of those, so the walk cannot see either word however the line is composed. MEASURED, not reasoned: with an `origin`-bearing stub added so both surfaces render, substituting an invented word into the badge, and separately into the line, leaves `ui-copy-surfaces.test.ts` green (4 passed, exit 0) in both runs. A literal equal to a table value would pass anyway, since the walk compares against `copy()` - so the surfaces are unguarded against a wrong word and not merely against a novel one. WHAT THAT COSTS: the word these surfaces print is the one the phase was about, and it has already been wrong once - Task 4's round 1 drew *Installed*, the online half's word, and only a person reading the drawings caught it. `ui-copy.test.ts` pins the table's value but not its use, and `gallery.dom.test.tsx` / `item-modal.dom.test.tsx` compare against `uiCopy` values a literal equal to the table satisfies. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: closing it means either widening `spokenIn` to read plain spans - which loosens the net for every surface in the editor and would redden cases deliberately carved out today - or giving these two elements a readable shape (an `aria-label` or a `p`), which is a design decision about the cell's markup rather than a test edit. NOT ESTABLISHED: which of the two is right; the second is narrower and the first is a change to a shared reader. The invented-word probe was run with a stub origin that was then reverted, because adding it changes no measurement.

title: Three controls keep their own draft/commit path with no composing guard, so an IME's Enter commits a half-typed string
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by Task 7's fix round in the theme-store plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-theme-store-origin-and-style.md`), which inverted the guard that had let the same defect ship in its own new control. THE DEFECT: `components/ui/control-well.tsx`'s `useDraftCommit` is the one owner of DESIGN.md section 5's draft/commit decision - Enter commits, Escape drops, and the `composing` ref plus `event.nativeEvent.isComposing` together stop an IME's Enter from committing a string that is not finished. Three files keep a copy of that decision instead: `host-settings-mode/region.tsx` (its own Enter and blur, no Escape, no composing guard), `panes/composition/composition-pane.tsx` (an uncontrolled inline rename field with its own Enter, Escape and blur) and `selection-inspector/runs.tsx` (the run format field's own Enter and Escape, no composing guard). VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: a tree-wide search of `packages/editor/src` finds `onCompositionStart`/`onCompositionEnd` in `control-well.tsx` alone, so none of the three carries the guard. WHAT THAT COSTS: a person typing a run format or a theme name with an IME - Chinese, Japanese, Korean - presses Enter to end the composition and the control commits the half-typed string as the authored value. The original row for this class, vg-203, is archived, so this is a fresh instance rather than a reopened one. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the three differ in shape and none is a copy-paste of another. One field is uncontrolled, one has no Escape at all, and adopting the hook changes what blur does in each - and blur is deliberately the caller's, since the hook returns only `onCompositionStart`, `onCompositionEnd` and `onKeyDown`. Deciding per site whether leaving the field should commit is a design call, not a mechanical one, and it wants its own spec line. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any of the three is reachable by an IME user in practice - the rename field and the run format field both take free text, so the trigger looks ordinary rather than narrow. NOT LOST: the guard that would have kept them invisible now lists all three in `EXEMPT` with a reason each, and fails by default for any new control, so the set is enumerated and visible rather than unknown.

title: A popover paints the panel token at 75% opacity where the drawing fixes its own ground at 95%, so a cell's name reads through a facet menu
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by the boundary seat of the theme-store plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-theme-store-origin-and-style.md`) while rendering the Style facet's popover, and carried as that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer; materialised here by the controller. THE DEFECT: `editor-shell/editor-shell.css` defines `--shell-surface: #eff9f2bf` and aliases `--panel: var(--shell-surface)`, so the `bg-panel` utility paints a ground whose alpha byte is `bf` - 191/255, about 75% opaque. The facet popover draws with it, and `docs/design/mockups/current/store-facets.html` fixes that popover's own ground at `#12161cf2`, alpha `f2` - 242/255, about 95%. Under the popover the gallery's cells stay legible through the menu, so a theme's name and byline read as part of the facet rows. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: the drawing carries `#12161cf2` once, `--shell-surface` is `#eff9f2bf` at line 35 of the stylesheet, `--panel` is the alias at line 47, and the dark-scheme block overrides `--shell-surface` to the opaque `#12161c`, so the light scheme is the one with a see-through popover. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the cause is not established, and the seat says so. `components/ui/control-select.tsx` paints its own popup with `bg-panel` too, so this is either a second site with the same defect or evidence that `--panel` is simply the wrong token for a popover - and which of those it is decides whether the fix is one element's class or a design-language token, which is a decision the drawings and DESIGN.md own rather than a seat. It also spans more than one owner, which the repo's bug rule names as its own reason to file. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the 75% is deliberate for the elevation-2 shadow to read, in which case the drawing is the thing that moved and the token is right; and whether any other `bg-panel` surface has the same gap. NOT THIS PLAN'S: the plan added no token and no popover - the facet popover predates it, and the boundary seat found this by rendering a surface the plan's own change made reachable.

title: The accepted store spec still calls the library badge *Installed* at three lines, one of them Acceptance B, which names a word no surface prints
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by the final whole-branch review of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-theme-store-origin-and-style.md`, and carried as that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer; materialised here by the controller. THE DEFECT: the badge the plan shipped reads **From the store** - the drawing's word (`docs/design/mockups/current/store-themes.html`), with `store-detail.html` reserving *Installed* for the online half's footer button. The spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md`, accepted 2026-10-21 and therefore binding, still names the badge *Installed* at three lines: `:772` "a cell can say *Installed* and cannot say *installed from where*", which describes the cell's vocabulary; `:931`, the phase table's B row, "the origin record and the *Installed* badge"; and `:1236`, Acceptance B, "a theme installed from a catalogue item reads *Installed*, and the mark survives a restart because it is read from the origin record". `:1236` is the sharp one: an acceptance criterion naming a word no surface prints, so Acceptance B is literally unsatisfiable as written even though every behaviour it means is implemented and browser-proved. CHECKED LINE BY LINE, and NOT drift: `:803` (the section title) and `:807`/`:821` use *Installed* as the concept name for the provenance relation rather than as the badge's word, and `:468` (the detail footer's button) and `:1246` (Acceptance D) name the *online item's* state, which is what the drawing gives it. Those five are consistent with the drawing and need no change. ALSO AFFECTED: the plan uses the same word in its own prose - `:5`, `:24`, `:33`, `:63`, and Task 4's title at `:264` with its steps at `:266` and `:280` - while Task 8's Step 2 and that task's brief use **From the store**, so one plan document names one surface with two words. The plan is complete and will be archived; the spec is the binding artifact and the one that matters. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN AN EDIT: the user accepted the spec as drafted, and an acceptance criterion is their contract - re-wording one after the fact would leave the acceptance record describing a document they never read. The choice between moving the spec to the drawing's word and moving the badge back to *Installed* is theirs; the ledger's ruling that the drawings outrank the plan's prose is what makes the spec stale rather than the code wrong. NOT ESTABLISHED: which of the two the user wants. Nothing in the code turns on the answer - the word lives once, at `ui-copy.ts:662` (`fromStore: "From the store"`), read by `store-mode/gallery.tsx:165` and `store-mode/item-modal.tsx:328`.

title: ThemeOrigin is declared twice with nothing keeping the two in step, so a host-side rename renders `From the store · undefined · undefined` with every test green
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by the final whole-branch review of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-theme-store-origin-and-style.md` - the brief asked it to check this seam, and it found the two matching - and carried as that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer; materialised here by the controller. THE SHAPE: `host/src/settings/theme-origins.ts:15` and `editor/src/theme-library-client.ts:55` each declare `ThemeOrigin` with the same three fields, `catalogueId`, `version` and `installedAt`, all `readonly string`. The duplication is deliberate and documented on both sides: the editor package does not depend on `@yunari/host`, so each side reads the wire shape for itself. **The two match today** - checked field for field by that review and again here - and no third declaration exists. THE GAP: nothing keeps them matching. Neither package imports the other's type, so a rename on one side typechecks on both: `host/src/settings/theme-origins.test.ts` exercises the host's type, `tests/e2e/editor-rail.spec.ts:1854` builds its `BOUNDARY_ORIGIN` literal against the editor's type, and the e2e suite stubs `/api/themes` (`:1483`, `:1936`) rather than running the host, so no test carries a value across the seam. A host-side rename therefore renders `From the store · undefined · undefined` in the modal's provenance line, which joins those three fields, with every editor and host test still green. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the cheap guard is either a test that runs the real host and reads `/api/themes` - which the suite does not currently do - or a shared wire type the editor can import without taking the host dependency, and which of those is right is an ownership decision rather than a task. It is also not a defect yet: nothing has drifted. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether other editor-host wire shapes share the exposure. The editor's own docblock names `ThemeLibraryEntry` as the same deliberate pattern, which suggests the question is how many rather than whether - and if it is several, the answer is one shared home for wire shapes rather than a guard per type.

title: Neither half of the store mode draws the status bar its drawing fixes, and the local half's carries two catalogue facts
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by the controller of the theme-store plan while scoping phase C, and filed rather than fixed because it is not C's. THE GAP: `docs/design/mockups/current/store-browse.html:394-399` draws the online half's status line as `144 of 480 themes`, `1 installed` and `Sorted by downloads`; `store-themes.html`'s footer draws the local half's as `14 themes`, `1 update available` and `Store: 480 themes`. **Neither is built.** `store-mode/region.tsx` has no status row at all — it ends at the pager — and `ui-copy.ts` carries no copy for one: its only `status` block (`:475-481`) is the host page's display count and save answer, and the editor's other count keys (`objects`, `selected`) belong to the editor status bar rather than the store's. VERIFIED BY SEARCH, not assumed: the region's own body ends at `pageItems`/`PageSize` and the pager component (`store-mode/pager.tsx`) draws pages and a per-page well, no counts. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: two of the four facts are the **catalogue's** — `1 update available` and `Store: 480 themes` on the local half, `1 installed` on the online half — so the bar cannot be built before phase C's listing exists, and the local half's two make it a surface spanning both halves rather than one task's. It is the same shape as Export and Delete, which phase A drew disabled precisely because no task in that plan and no phase in the landing order owned them (R164, `cell-actions.ts`). NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the spec intends the bar at all. Its *The store mode* and *The gallery, and paging* sections do not mention one, so the drawings are the only authority for it — and the drawings are the design contract, which outranks a plan's prose. NOT THIS PHASE'S: C's row in the landing order (`:932`) names the online tab, `index.json`, browse, filter, sort and the modal's online facts, and no status bar.

title: Eleven other mutating loopback routes take an Origin from another page and state no Host check, so only the install route is guarded
detail: FOUND 2026-10-22 by the phase D whole-branch review and carried as `2bf41947`'s `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer; the fix that commit lands is scoped to `POST /api/themes/install`. THE SHAPE: `isLoopbackRemote` asks only where the socket came from, so any page in any origin can POST a `text/plain` JSON body to a loopback route without a preflight; the browser's `Origin` header is the one fact that page cannot forge, and `isForeignOrigin` (`server.ts:296`) now reads it plus a loopback `Host` for the install route alone. The routes the fixer listed as sharing the gap: `/api/displays` (POST, PATCH, DELETE), `/api/devices` (PUT), `/api/display` (PUT), `/api/published` (PUT), `/api/hosting` (PUT), `/api/font-favorites` (PUT), `/api/themes` (PUT save, DELETE), `/api/themes/import` (POST), `/api/themes/:id/answers` (PUT), `/api/themes/:id/thumbnail` (PUT), `/api/publish` (PUT/DELETE), and the `/settings` and `/editor` non-GET routes. `/api/pairing/*` is LAN by design and carries its own credential. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the install route was fixed because it is the first one with a destructive overwrite; retrofitting thirteen routes at once is a cross-cutting change with its own test surface, and doing it inside a fix round would have doubled that round's blast radius. NOT ESTABLISHED: which of the thirteen are actually reachable from a foreign page in a browser that sends `Origin` — a GET-only route cannot be, and a route that already requires the session credential is guarded by something else. The check is one helper and a call per route once that list is measured.

title: Six settings files still save by truncating in place while a reader can be mid-read, so a listing can flash empty and a crash can lose the whole file
detail: FOUND 2026-10-22 by the phase D fix round, reported rather than fixed per its brief, and carried as `2bf41947`'s `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. THE SHAPE: `writeFile(target)` truncates before it writes, so a concurrent `readFile` observes an empty or half-written file, and a crash between the two loses every entry. `theme-origins.ts` was fixed in `c226c75d` by writing `${file}.tmp` and renaming over the target, with `read` serialised behind the same write queue; the reported siblings are `active-theme.ts` (queued mutators, unserialised readers), `theme-settings.ts` (same save and no queue at all), `devices.ts`, `display.ts`, `hosting.ts` and `font-favorites.ts`. `displays.ts` and `host-record.ts` already write tmp+rename. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: six files under six different owners, each with its own read path and consequence, and the concurrency guarantee has to be tested per owner rather than shared wholesale. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether every one of them has a reader that runs concurrently with its writer — `theme-settings.ts` with no queue at all is the one with the clearest exposure.

title: An install refusal can reach the person as an operating system string with an absolute path in it
detail: FOUND 2026-10-22 by the phase D whole-branch review as its Minor 5, deferred by the fix round's brief and carried as `2bf41947`'s `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. THE SHAPE: every `stage: "package"` failure is answered 400 with the refusing owner's own `message`, and `install.ts` composes some of those from a store or filesystem error, so a person can be shown an OS sentence naming a path inside their profile; the editor's network arm separately shows `error.message` ("Failed to fetch"). WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the right sentence is the host's to compose and the mapping has to distinguish a validator's answer from a store's error, which means a copy table for the host package and a decision about what stays verbatim. NOT ESTABLISHED: which of the current messages actually carry a path — that needs one read per refusal site.

title: The install queue is keyed by catalogue id, so two items that slug to the same library id race the store's own free-name check
detail: FOUND 2026-10-22 by the phase D whole-branch review as its Minor 8, deferred by the fix round's brief and carried as `2bf41947`'s `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. THE SHAPE: `install.ts` serialises per `catalogueId`, but two different catalogue items can resolve to the same library id through `importIdCandidates`, and the loser's rename fails with the filesystem's own error and surfaces as the person's refusal instead of trying the next candidate. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the correct answer is either to key the queue by the resolved library id or to treat a rename loser like a taken id, and which one is right depends on whether `import.ts`'s candidate loop is the owner of that retry. NOT ESTABLISHED: how likely a collision is with the current catalogue — it needs two items whose package ids slug alike and two presses at once, which no fixture currently produces.

title: server.test.ts flakes on assignment cases: a deleted display's answers leak, or an assignment is sampled twice, in roughly one full run in three
detail: FOUND 2026-10-22 by the phase D fix round, which reported it and suspected it was pre-existing. MEASURED rather than argued, by the controller: at the fix round's head `a4fd917d` the suite failed 1 of 3 runs, and at the base commit `5e5be86f` in an isolated worktree it failed 1 of 4 runs, on the same case with the same message, `expected 'no card assigned' to be 'gpu-0'`. A second case, `samples once per distinct assignment, not once per connection`, failed once with `expected [ 1, 2, 2 ] to deeply equal [ 2, 2, 2 ]`. Both pass when `server.test.ts` runs alone. The phase D diff touches nothing in the assignment or display path, so this is pre-existing. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the cause is not established. The suspected shape is the Windows rename-open-reader race that `theme-origins.ts` documents in `c226c75d` — `displays.ts` writes tmp+rename and an open `readFile` makes the rename fail with EPERM — but that explains a 500, not an assignment sampled twice, so at least one mechanism is missing. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the two failing cases share a cause. A fix starts by making the sample deterministic, not by loosening the assertion.

title: The video caps ignore edit lists and presentation duration, so a short clip can present longer than the 30 s cap
detail: FOUND 2026-10-22 by phase F's scoped re-review as NF2. THE SHAPE: `readVideoFacts` reads `mdhd` and `stts` (media time) but not `edts/elst` or the `mvhd`/`tkhd` presentation duration, so a file whose edit list repeats or delays its media can present for longer than the sample table implies and still pass the 30 s cap. Not exploitable as a crash — the caps stay honest about media time — but the background loop the cap protects is presentation time. THE FIX: read `elst` segment durations when present and take the largest of media, edit-list and movie duration before comparing to the cap; add a crafted test the same way F1/F2's patches do. WHAT IT BLOCKS: nothing today, because no item exists in the catalogue; it matters when a submission is not authored by the app.

title: A theme package's credits.json does not survive the host library, so reopening a theme loses its attribution
detail: FOUND 2026-10-23 while landing the asset finder's Task 15 (credits at import). THE SHAPE: the editor now writes credits.json at save, and `readThemePackage`/`EditorDocument` seed the collection from it, but the host's library import (`host/src/themes/import.ts` → `writeUnderFreeId`) re-writes only envelope, assets and thumbnail, so the member is dropped on the way into a stored theme and `BootThemeOutcome` carries no credits. A theme opened from the library therefore starts with an empty collection even when its own package credited every icon it imported. THE FIX: persist the parsed credits beside the theme in the theme store (or write the original member through), return them from the library read path, and pass them into the editor mount as `credits` — `EditorDocumentSource.credits` already accepts them. WHAT IT BLOCKS: nothing today; the finder's import path is the only writer of credits so far and the feature is unreleased. Provenance: agent, during Task 15.

title: Biome lints and formats no .mjs script, so scripts/import-catalogue-item.mjs is outside the gate
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING TASK 5.1 OF THE R2 STORE BACKEND PLAN (import the catalogue item), while running the task gate. MEASURED: `biome.json` at the repo root sets `files.includes` to ["src/web/**/*.ts", "src/web/**/*.tsx", "src/web/**/*.json", "src/web/**/*.css"], so `biome check ..` from `src/web` reports `Checked 818 files` and never reads any `.mjs`. Handing it the two changed files reports `Checked 1 file` - the `.ts` test alone. It is the same include-replacement shape as archived `vg-149` (.tsx), which was left unfixed for a repo-wide reformat decision; this is the `.mjs` half of the same glob. WHAT IT COSTS: a task that edits a root or `src/web` script can name a biome gate while the changed file was never read, and the new `scripts/import-catalogue-item.mjs` is in that class. NOT FIXED HERE because the owning change is the `files.includes` decision already pending for `.tsx`, and the Task 5.1 controller ruling put the exclusion out of scope. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: after `*.mjs` joins the includes, append an unused variable to a `.mjs` script and see `biome check ..` exit 1 naming it.

title: Playwright's `reuseExistingServer` silently reuses another worktree's stale `vite preview` on a shared port, so a focused spec runs against a bundle that is not this tree's
detail: FOUND 2026-10-23 while executing Task 5.3 of the R2 store backend plan, recorded in `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-23-r2-store-backend/task-5.3-report.md`. THE SHAPE: the first capture rerun failed all four cases at `the routed session did not offer the Mine toggle`. Port 4174 was held by another worktree's `vite preview` (`background-media-becomes-a-layer`, PID 28516) whose built bundle contains no `/api/store/session` and no `data-yunari-store-mine`. The spec's Playwright config sets `reuseExistingServer`, so nothing tried to bind, no `strictPort` error was raised, and the run silently read that server's pages; the same spec that was green before went red and was green again once the server exited, with nothing in this worktree changed. The AGENTS trap warns only about `strictPort`, which cannot fire when reuse means no bind is attempted. WHAT IT COSTS: a browser run can report a red spec, or a green one, against code that is not this tree's, and the difference is invisible in the output. SUGGESTED FIX: fail before the run when a server already answers on a port this config needs (probe a path the spec requires, or a build marker), or set `reuseExistingServer: false` for the per-worktree configs and document the one-worktree-per-port rule in AGENTS. NOT FIXED HERE because the owning change is the shared Playwright configs, outside this plan.

title: Choosing a fixed pie total unmounts the editor before the value can be typed
detail: FOUND 2026-10-23 by Task 11 of the background-layer plan, in fix round 1, while rewriting the e2e cases that drove the removed Document-pane hooks. Not caused by that task: the crash reproduces with no background interaction at all. THE SHAPE: `fabric-envelope-validate.ts` refuses `settings.total = { kind: "fixed" }` with no `value`, which is the state the chart control writes first. `EditorShell.snapshot()` validates and throws, and `EditorDocument.isDirty()` calls it on every document-change poll, so the transient invalid document becomes an exception inside React render and the shell unmounts (`#app` emptied). `tests/e2e/inspector-sections.spec.ts` reaches it in the fixed-pie-total case. THE FIX is a decision, not a line: either `isDirty` tolerates an in-progress document that the loader would refuse, or the control writes a value with the kind. Not established when it began; the rule arrived with `1d26aac5`.

title: The background position controls stay enabled with no media and refuse after the fact
detail: FOUND 2026-10-23 by the background-layer plan's final whole-branch review. THE SHAPE: `backgroundColumn` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/selection-inspector/background-column.ts`) always projects bounds, both offsets and both flips, so a background with no `media` still shows the default values and accepts a draft; `writeBackgroundField` then returns `undefined` and the author sees `invalidValue` only after typing. Bounds and offsets also name a placement that has no picture to place. THE FIX is a UI decision, not a line: hide or disable the position section until a media is chosen, or keep it visible and let the first write create the media. WHAT IT BLOCKS: nothing. The refusal is safe; it is the affordance that is wrong.

title: selection-inspector/index.ts is 983 lines against the 800 stop and needs the background funnel extracted
detail: FOUND 2026-10-23 by the background-layer plan's final whole-branch review. THE SHAPE: `src/web/packages/editor/src/selection-inspector/index.ts` is 983 lines, past the 800-line stop in AGENTS.md. The background's own funnel lives inside the object inspector's file: `applyBackground`, the `background.*` routing inside `edits.commit`/`preview`/`cancelPreview`, `renderBackground`, and the `backgroundRevision`/`describingBackground` state. THE FIX: move that funnel beside the column that owns the fields (for example `background-edits.ts`, taking the document setter and the selection getter as ports), leaving `index.ts` to route a `background.*` id to it. WHAT IT BLOCKS: nothing today; every further column addition grows a file already past the stop.

title: The background's offsets carry no % cue, and SELECTION_KINDS no longer names the full union
detail: FOUND 2026-10-23 by the background-layer plan's final whole-branch review. THE SHAPE, two readings on one column: (1) `offsetField` in `selection-inspector/background-column.ts` sets `percent: true` on both halves, but nothing renders a unit, so the author reads `25` with no cue that it is a percentage; (2) `SELECTION_KINDS` (`selection-inspector/per-kind-column.ts:112`) lists the Fabric kinds only, and `SelectionKind` (`:121`) hand-unions `"background"` beside it, so the constant claiming to name every selection kind names six of seven. THE FIX: render a `%` suffix from the existing `percent` flag in the number and pair controls; and either add `background` to `SELECTION_KINDS` with the per-kind column answering a virtual arm, or rename the constant so it says it is the Fabric kinds. WHAT IT BLOCKS: nothing; both are the drift shapes that cost a second copy later. PROGRESS 2026-10-23: the percent cue landed in 220cb84 (ControlPair forwards a unit; the background offsets show "%"), recorded in decisions/0096. This row stays open for the SELECTION_KINDS half only.

title: Three decision notes claim 0093, so a bare "0093" is ambiguous
detail: FOUND 2026-10-23 while resolving the merge of `origin/main` into the background-layer branch, and carried as `4e00450`'s `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. THE SHAPE: `docs/decisions/` holds `0093-the-background-is-a-virtual-layer.md` (this branch), `0093-the-asset-finder-is-host-searched.md` and `0093-the-store-backend-is-one-worker.md` (both already on `main`), so the number names three decisions and prose that cites it cites all three; `0094-the-background-translates-and-mirrors.md` cites 0093 by filename, which is unambiguous, but a reader or a note that says only 0093 is not. NOT FIXED HERE because renaming a note changes what the archived plan and every prose reference resolve to, and the two `main`-side notes are owned by whoever wrote them; picking which of the three keeps 0093 is their call. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one owner renumbers two of the three (and their references) so each number names one decision.

title: Below the compact breakpoint the editor header is wider than the window, so the menubar and publish control render past the right edge
detail: FOUND 2026-10-23 while making `publish-header.spec.ts` green: at a 390px window the header's four regions (brand, the three-label mode switch, File/Edit/View, and the publish control) come to roughly 632px of min-content, so the publish trigger's box begins at x=390.1 and the whole control is outside the glass. What the case caught was its consequence rather than the row itself: the overflowing header widened `documentElement`, so a portalled popover clamped against the document and ended 13px past the viewport on CI's font metrics (0.3px locally). `editor-shell.css` now clips the header below the compact breakpoint, which stops the document widening but does NOT make the menubar or publish control reachable at that width — clipping is confinement, not a layout. NOT FIXED HERE because §7.1 fixes the header's contents and no ruling says which region a compact header keeps (dropping brand and menubar still leaves about 410px, and the mode switch alone plus publish is about 360). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on the compact header (which regions drop, or whether the editor refuses widths below the breakpoint), then the row's reachability asserted in `publish-header.spec.ts` alongside the popup's.

title: Nothing renders a theme's credits, so an imported attribution is written but never shown
detail: FOUND 2026-10-23 while executing Task 8 of the Wallpaper Engine plan. The credits member is landed and tested: theme-package writes and reads credits.json, the editor document carries the collection, and the Wallpaper Engine import adds one entry per item. Task 8 Step 5 asked for the credits to be rendered where a theme's details already render its other facts, but no theme-details surface exists: store-mode/item-modal.tsx renders a store listing's facts, not a package's contents, and the library and publish surfaces render neither. Choosing where a credit is drawn, and whether it names the Steam author, links the workshop page and shows the licence, is a design decision, so it is not invented here. The workshop URL is recorded in the package and is simply never drawn.
